title: MONUSCO Welcomes DRC-Rwanda Peace Agreement, Calls for Rigorous Implementation
excerpt: Kinshasa/Washington - On Thursday, December 4, 2025, MONUSCO welcomed the adoption in Washington of the peace agreement and the regional economic integration framework between the DRC and Rwanda, facilitated by the…
title_en: MONUSCO Welcomes DRC-Rwanda Peace Agreement, Calls for Rigorous Implementation
excerpt_en: Kinshasa/Washington - On Thursday, December 4, 2025, MONUSCO welcomed the adoption in Washington of the peace agreement and the regional economic integration framework between the DRC and Rwanda, facilitated by the…
body_en:
Kinshasa/Washington - On Thursday, December 4, 2025, MONUSCO welcomed the adoption in Washington of the peace agreement and the regional economic integration framework between the DRC and Rwanda, facilitated by the United States, praising the determination of Presidents Félix Tshisekedi and Paul Kagame.

The UN mission highlighted that this agreement - which includes a ceasefire, the disarmament of the FDLR, the withdrawal of Rwandan troops, and the return of refugees - provides a new opportunity to restore confidence, alleviate civilian suffering, and lay the foundations for lasting peace in eastern Congo.

In a statement, Bruno Lemarquis, acting head of MONUSCO, emphasized that the combination of this agreement with the one signed between the DRC and the AFC/M23 on November 15, as well as Security Council resolution 2773 (2025), offers hope for a shift from confrontation to political solutions, provided that implementation respects the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC.

The mission also welcomed the involvement of Qatar, the African Union (AU), the East African Community (EAC), SADC, and mediator Faure Gnassingbé, while calling for continued support and the promotion of inclusive dialogue.

In line with its mandate, MONUSCO will continue to support these efforts, particularly in civilian protection, ceasefire monitoring, disarmament of armed groups, and the stabilization of affected areas.

title: DRC Government Suspends "Save the DRC" Movement Linked to Joseph Kabila
excerpt: Kinshasa - On Monday, December 1, 2025, the Congolese government suspended all activities of the "Save the DRC" movement, created in October in Nairobi at the instigation of former president Joseph Kabila.
title_en: DRC Government Suspends "Save the DRC" Movement Linked to Joseph Kabila
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - On Monday, December 1, 2025, the Congolese government suspended all activities of the "Save the DRC" movement, created in October in Nairobi at the instigation of former president Joseph Kabila.
body_en:
Kinshasa - On Monday, December 1, 2025, the Congolese government suspended all activities of the "Save the DRC" movement, created in October in Nairobi at the instigation of former president Joseph Kabila.

Governors received instructions to strictly enforce this measure under penalty of sanctions, according to a telegram from Deputy Prime Minister of the Interior Jacquemain Shabani.

The ban, described as a "diversion" by Ferdinand Kambere, deputy permanent secretary of the PPRD, comes amid the platform’s opposition to the Kinshasa-led negotiations in Doha and Washington, which it considers a threat to national sovereignty.

This decision follows the suspension of the PPRD, confirmed on October 27, 2025, by the High Court of Kinshasa-Gombe, for "complicity with the AFC/M23 rebellion".

title: Federalism Debate: CDER Warns Against a “Dangerous Drift” Amid Crisis
excerpt: Kinshasa - The Current of Renewed Democrats (CDER), led by Jean-Lucien Bussa, has raised concerns over the resurgence of the federalism debate in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), recently reignited by former…
title_en: Federalism Debate: CDER Warns Against a “Dangerous Drift” Amid Crisis
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - The Current of Renewed Democrats (CDER), led by Jean-Lucien Bussa, has raised concerns over the resurgence of the federalism debate in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), recently reignited by former…
body_en:
Kinshasa - The Current of Renewed Democrats (CDER), led by Jean-Lucien Bussa, has raised concerns over the resurgence of the federalism debate in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), recently reignited by former Speaker of the National Assembly Olivier Kamitatu.

In a statement published on December 1, 2025, the CDER described the debate as “inopportune” given the ongoing security crisis, identity-based tensions, and the looming risk of balkanization.

The movement stressed that national unity must remain the priority, citing the partial failure of decentralization, which has at times been exploited for ethnic or regional interests. Steering the country toward federalism, the CDER warned, would constitute a “historical and moral crime.”

The party called on the political class to act responsibly, urging leaders to focus on security, national cohesion, and the well-being of citizens rather than engaging in debates likely to fuel internal divisions.

title: DRC-Belgium: Kinshasa and Brussels Strengthen Military Cooperation
excerpt: Kinshasa - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Belgium agreed to consolidate their military partnership during a meeting on Monday, December 1, 2025, in Kinshasa.
title_en: DRC-Belgium: Kinshasa and Brussels Strengthen Military Cooperation
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Belgium agreed to consolidate their military partnership during a meeting on Monday, December 1, 2025, in Kinshasa.
body_en:
Kinshasa - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Belgium agreed to consolidate their military partnership during a meeting on Monday, December 1, 2025, in Kinshasa. The talks involved Congolese Deputy Prime Minister for Defense Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita and his Belgian counterpart Theo Francken, accompanied by their respective chiefs of staff.

The two countries committed to intensifying collaboration in training, operational support, medical cooperation, and capacity building for the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC). The DRC also plans to appoint a defense attaché in Brussels in the near future.

Emphasizing Belgian support for security challenges in eastern DRC, Francken highlighted his government's commitment to developing cooperation, including through an increase in the defense budget.

The delegations later inspected joint European Union projects in Kindu, including the construction of a logistics complex, a brigade headquarters, and the reconstruction of the garrison military hospital, noting rapid progress on the works.

title: DRC-Rwanda: Peace Agreement Ratified in Washington to Turn the Page on Three Decades of Tension
excerpt: Washington - Presidents Félix Tshisekedi and Paul Kagame ratified the DRC-Rwanda Peace Agreement on Thursday, December 4, 2025, in Washington, marking a major step toward the pacification of eastern DRC after nearly…
title_en: DRC-Rwanda: Peace Agreement Ratified in Washington to Turn the Page on Three Decades of Tension
excerpt_en: Washington - Presidents Félix Tshisekedi and Paul Kagame ratified the DRC-Rwanda Peace Agreement on Thursday, December 4, 2025, in Washington, marking a major step toward the pacification of eastern DRC after nearly…
body_en:
Washington - Presidents Félix Tshisekedi and Paul Kagame ratified the DRC-Rwanda Peace Agreement on Thursday, December 4, 2025, in Washington, marking a major step toward the pacification of eastern DRC after nearly three decades of violence.

Based on the Declaration of Principles of April 25, 2025, the agreement commits both countries to mutual respect for territorial integrity, cessation of support for armed groups, and the creation of a joint security coordination mechanism. Under the accord, Kinshasa pledges to neutralize the FDLR, while Kigali must withdraw its troops from Congolese territory.

The agreement also provides for the voluntary return of refugees, guaranteed humanitarian access to vulnerable populations, and the establishment, within three months, of a regional economic integration framework.

President Tshisekedi reaffirmed his commitment to implementing the agreements "in all sincerity," calling for the same rigor from Rwanda." President Kagame welcomed an agreement “that contains everything necessary” to end the conflict, cautioning that its implementation may face ups and downs, while reaffirming Rwanda’s commitment to a stable and prosperous future.

title: Tshisekedi Assures U.S. and Rwanda of DRC Commitment to Dismantle Armed Groups
excerpt: Washington, D.C. - President Félix Tshisekedi has assured the United States and Rwanda that the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will fully implement the provisions of the peace and economic cooperation agreement…
title_en: Tshisekedi Assures U.S. and Rwanda of DRC Commitment to Dismantle Armed Groups
excerpt_en: Washington, D.C. - President Félix Tshisekedi has assured the United States and Rwanda that the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will fully implement the provisions of the peace and economic cooperation agreement…
body_en:
Washington, D.C. - President Félix Tshisekedi has assured the United States and Rwanda that the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will fully implement the provisions of the peace and economic cooperation agreement signed with Rwanda, including the dismantling of armed groups operating on its territory.

Speaking after the signing ceremony held in the United States on December 4, 2025, where he and Rwandan President Paul Kagame formalized the agreement, Tshisekedi reaffirmed his government’s commitment to peace and security.

“The DRC is committed to respecting, with full integrity, all the requirements of this agreement,” Tshisekedi said. “We will do so continuously, in the pursuit of peace and security for our people, and for the unity and sovereignty of our country.”

The Congolese leader expressed confidence that Rwanda would also honor the agreement, stressing that the two neighbors would work together in a spirit of mutual respect.

“We are moving toward a peaceful partnership based on mutual respect, non-interference, and a shared determination to combat armed groups, end all support for them, and build a true partnership,” he added.

Tshisekedi said the agreement places both countries in exceptional circumstances that could pave the way for lasting peace, while emphasizing that the DRC government would remain vigilant as it works with regional and international partners to fulfill its obligations.

“This Washington peace and economic agreement must serve our people,” he said, “and stand as a clear sign of our determination to close the chapter of confrontation and open a new era of cooperation and lasting peace in the region.”

The Rwanda-DRC peace agreement предусматривает the neutralization and dismantling of the FDLR and other affiliated armed groups, while Rwanda is expected to lift security measures it had previously put in place in response to regional threats.

The accord also outlines joint initiatives between Rwanda and the DRC, including:

Construction of the Rusizi III hydroelectric dam

Shared management of resources in Lake Kivu

The United States, which facilitated the agreement, said that full implementation would lead to sustainable peace and development in the Great Lakes region, delivering tangible benefits to citizens on both sides of the border.

title: United States-European Union: A Strengthened Commitment to Stability and Growth in the Great Lakes Region
excerpt: Washington - The United States and the European Union reaffirmed their shared commitment to promoting peace, security, and economic growth in the Great Lakes region on Thursday, December 4, 2025, placing the Lobito…
title_en: United States-European Union: A Strengthened Commitment to Stability and Growth in the Great Lakes Region
excerpt_en: Washington - The United States and the European Union reaffirmed their shared commitment to promoting peace, security, and economic growth in the Great Lakes region on Thursday, December 4, 2025, placing the Lobito…
body_en:
Washington - The United States and the European Union reaffirmed their shared commitment to promoting peace, security, and economic growth in the Great Lakes region on Thursday, December 4, 2025, placing the Lobito Corridor at the heart of their strategy.

This major project aims to connect the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to the Angolan port of Lobito. In a joint statement, Washington and Brussels emphasized that this strategic infrastructure will enhance regional connectivity, secure supply chains for critical minerals, and stimulate sustainable investment, while opening new trade opportunities between Central Africa, the United States, and Europe.

The two partners welcomed the progress in discussions between the Congolese private sector and the government, and expressed their willingness to explore financing options to synchronize the work with ongoing projects in Angola, maximizing the economic and geopolitical impact of the corridor, which they described as an essential catalyst for regional development.

title: Félix Tshisekedi Condemns Rwanda’s Violation of Washington Peace Agreement
excerpt: Kinshasa - The President of the Democratic Republic of Congo, Félix Tshisekedi, strongly condemned Rwanda for violating the peace agreement signed on December 4, 2025, in Washington, during a government meeting held on…
title_en: Félix Tshisekedi Condemns Rwanda’s Violation of Washington Peace Agreement
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - The President of the Democratic Republic of Congo, Félix Tshisekedi, strongly condemned Rwanda for violating the peace agreement signed on December 4, 2025, in Washington, during a government meeting held on…
body_en:
Kinshasa - The President of the Democratic Republic of Congo, Félix Tshisekedi, strongly condemned Rwanda for violating the peace agreement signed on December 4, 2025, in Washington, during a government meeting held on December 11 at the African Union City complex.

He accused Rwanda of intensifying military operations in South Kivu with the goal of seizing new localities, warning that this escalation aggravates an already critical humanitarian situation and constitutes a threat to the territorial integrity of the DRC.

President Tshisekedi called on national institutions to remain vigilant, urging the Ministers of the Interior and Defense to maintain full mobilization, while instructing the defense and security forces to remain on high alert.

In response to recent offensives by the AFC/M23, allegedly supported by Rwanda, particularly in Kamanyola, Luvungi, Katogota, and Uvira, he announced the upcoming convening of an inter-institutional meeting and an expanded High Defence Council to define, in full sovereignty, the necessary measures to guarantee the security of the population.

title: MONUSCO Mandate Renewal: United States Reaffirms Support to UN Mission in DRC
excerpt: Kinshasa - A few days ahead of the renewal of MONUSCO’s mandate scheduled for December 20, 2025, the United States reiterated its strong support for the UN mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo before the Security…
title_en: MONUSCO Mandate Renewal: United States Reaffirms Support to UN Mission in DRC
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - A few days ahead of the renewal of MONUSCO’s mandate scheduled for December 20, 2025, the United States reiterated its strong support for the UN mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo before the Security…
body_en:
Kinshasa - A few days ahead of the renewal of MONUSCO’s mandate scheduled for December 20, 2025, the United States reiterated its strong support for the UN mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo before the Security Council on December 12.

The US emphasized the need to equip MONUSCO with sufficient capacity to support the implementation of the Doha and Washington peace processes. The representative denounced the obstruction of MONUSCO’s work in Goma, occupied since early 2025 by the M23, accusing the Rwandan-backed rebellion of hindering the mission’s freedom of movement, supplies, and operational effectiveness, including through surface-to-air missiles and communications jamming operations.

He described as “regrettable hypocrisy” the support given by a Security Council member state to groups obstructing a UN peacekeeping mission, while reaffirming the United States’ commitment to agreements aimed at ending violence in eastern DRC.

Several other Council members, including France, China, Russia, and the United Kingdom, also advocated for the renewal and strengthening of MONUSCO’s mandate, particularly to support the ceasefire and help ease tensions between the DRC and Rwanda.

title: DRC-Rwanda Agreement: Félix Tshisekedi Denounces Violations and Reaffirms National Sovereignty
excerpt: Kinshasa - In his State of the Nation address before Parliament on December 8, 2025, President Félix Tshisekedi accused Rwanda of deliberately violating the ceasefire established by the peace agreement signed on…
title_en: DRC-Rwanda Agreement: Félix Tshisekedi Denounces Violations and Reaffirms National Sovereignty
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - In his State of the Nation address before Parliament on December 8, 2025, President Félix Tshisekedi accused Rwanda of deliberately violating the ceasefire established by the peace agreement signed on…
body_en:
Kinshasa - In his State of the Nation address before Parliament on December 8, 2025, President Félix Tshisekedi accused Rwanda of deliberately violating the ceasefire established by the peace agreement signed on December 4 in Washington, D.C.

According to Tshisekedi, Rwandan forces bombed several localities in South Kivu, including Kaziba, Katokota, and Lubarika, from Rwandan territory. While condemning these attacks, the President recalled the commitments under the agreement-including the withdrawal of Rwandan troops, the cessation of hostilities, and the creation of joint security mechanisms.

He reaffirmed the DRC’s commitment to the diplomatic path without compromising its sovereignty or the security of its citizens. Tshisekedi emphasized that the agreement does not imply sovereignty sharing, does not endorse territorial claims or the sale of mineral resources, and grants no amnesty for crimes committed.

The President further highlighted that the security crisis in eastern DRC stems from a proxy war and resource plundering, while expressing solidarity with displaced populations and victims of armed conflict, affirming the state’s commitment to their protection.

title: Washington Agreement Threatened: Tshisekedi Alerts Luanda
excerpt: Kinshasa - Faced with the deteriorating security situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), President Félix Tshisekedi sent Minister of Regional Integration Floribert Anzuluni Isiloketshi as a special…
title_en: Washington Agreement Threatened: Tshisekedi Alerts Luanda
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - Faced with the deteriorating security situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), President Félix Tshisekedi sent Minister of Regional Integration Floribert Anzuluni Isiloketshi as a special…
body_en:
Kinshasa - Faced with the deteriorating security situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), President Félix Tshisekedi sent Minister of Regional Integration Floribert Anzuluni Isiloketshi as a special envoy to Angolan President João Lourenço in Luanda on December 12, 2025.

The envoy conveyed concerns over threats to the implementation of the peace agreement signed in Washington between the DRC and Rwanda. The message highlighted ongoing offensives by the AFC/M23, supported by Kigali, including the capture of Uvira, actions deemed incompatible with ceasefire commitments.

According to the Angolan presidency, this situation is worrying and could jeopardize diplomatic efforts. Luanda reaffirmed its willingness to continue its role as facilitator and its commitment to a peaceful and lasting solution, based on respect for agreements and the sovereignty of states, in pursuit of stability in the Great Lakes region.
body_fr:
Kinshasa - Faced with the deteriorating security situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), President Félix Tshisekedi sent Minister of Regional Integration Floribert Anzuluni Isiloketshi as a special envoy to Angolan President João Lourenço in Luanda on December 12, 2025.

The envoy conveyed concerns over threats to the implementation of the peace agreement signed in Washington between the DRC and Rwanda. The message highlighted ongoing offensives by the AFC/M23, supported by Kigali, including the capture of Uvira, actions deemed incompatible with ceasefire commitments.

According to the Angolan presidency, this situation is worrying and could jeopardize diplomatic efforts. Luanda reaffirmed its willingness to continue its role as facilitator and its commitment to a peaceful and lasting solution, based on respect for agreements and the sovereignty of states, in pursuit of stability in the Great Lakes region.

title: United States Accuses Paul Kagame of Orchestrating War in Eastern DRC
excerpt: New York - During a UN Security Council meeting on December 12, 2025, US Permanent Representative Michael Waltz accused Rwandan President Paul Kagame of having “planned and executed the war in eastern Democratic…
title_en: United States Accuses Paul Kagame of Orchestrating War in Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: New York - During a UN Security Council meeting on December 12, 2025, US Permanent Representative Michael Waltz accused Rwandan President Paul Kagame of having “planned and executed the war in eastern Democratic…
body_en:
New York - During a UN Security Council meeting on December 12, 2025, US Permanent Representative Michael Waltz accused Rwandan President Paul Kagame of having “planned and executed the war in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).”

The US representative claimed that Kigali has controlled the M23 rebel movement and its political wing, the AFC, since 2021, providing logistical support, equipment, training, and troops-estimated at 5,000 to 7,000 soldiers-to carry out armed operations in eastern Congo.

According to Washington, Rwanda has deployed surface-to-air missiles and sophisticated weaponry on multiple fronts, fueling the offensive that led to the AFC/M23 capture of the strategic city of Uvira. The US also reported increased use of suicide drones and ground artillery.

The United States called for the immediate withdrawal of Rwandan forces and accountability measures against those responsible for these acts, emphasizing the urgent need to restore peace and stability in the eastern DRC.

title: Martin Fayulu Calls Washington Agreement a “Trap” Set by Kagame
excerpt: Kinshasa - Congolese opposition leader Martin Fayulu described the peace agreement signed on December 4, 2025, in Washington between the DRC and Rwanda as a “trap” orchestrated by Rwandan President Paul Kagame, during…
title_en: Martin Fayulu Calls Washington Agreement a “Trap” Set by Kagame
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - Congolese opposition leader Martin Fayulu described the peace agreement signed on December 4, 2025, in Washington between the DRC and Rwanda as a “trap” orchestrated by Rwandan President Paul Kagame, during…
body_en:
Kinshasa - Congolese opposition leader Martin Fayulu described the peace agreement signed on December 4, 2025, in Washington between the DRC and Rwanda as a “trap” orchestrated by Rwandan President Paul Kagame, during an interview on France 24 on December 11.

Fayulu argued that the agreement, concluded following European and American sanctions as well as UN Resolution 2773, was designed to circumvent international pressure and prepare for war in eastern Congo, driven by economic and territorial interests.

He claimed that while US President Donald Trump was facilitating a strategic partnership agreement between the DRC and the United States, Kagame pursued his own objectives, disregarding the spirit of peace intended by the deal.

Fayulu also denounced the sub-regional nature of the ongoing crisis, involving the DRC, Rwanda, Uganda, Burundi, and Tanzania, noting that the resumption of fighting in South Kivu-particularly the capture of Uvira by AFC/M23 rebels supported by Kigali-demonstrates the persistent tensions despite the agreement.

Economy and Tech.

title: Over 1,100 Taxpayers Adopt Standardized Invoicing
excerpt: Kinshasa - The Ministry of Finance announced on Tuesday, December 2, 2025, that more than 1,100 taxpayers are now using standardized invoicing through the e-UF electronic invoicing system, provided free of charge by the…
title_en: Over 1,100 Taxpayers Adopt Standardized Invoicing
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - The Ministry of Finance announced on Tuesday, December 2, 2025, that more than 1,100 taxpayers are now using standardized invoicing through the e-UF electronic invoicing system, provided free of charge by the…
body_en:
Kinshasa - The Ministry of Finance announced on Tuesday, December 2, 2025, that more than 1,100 taxpayers are now using standardized invoicing through the e-UF electronic invoicing system, provided free of charge by the government.

In a press release, Minister Doudou Fwamba reaffirmed his support for economic operators following the implementation of the invoicing requirement. He specified that the e-UF system can be used temporarily or permanently, including by large companies with their own invoicing systems.

The Minister also emphasized that providing a tax identification number remains mandatory for sales to legal entities, but is optional for individuals. The DGI (General Directorate of Taxes) is increasing webinars, technical sessions, and targeted assistance to support the transition, while the Minister reiterated that the measure will not be postponed, encouraging businesses to continue their compliance efforts.

This reform, driven by the vision of President Félix Tshisekedi, represents a major step toward modernizing tax administration and improving the traceability of commercial transactions in the DRC.

title: AFC/M23 Announces Major Tax Reform in Kivu
excerpt: Goma - On December 3, 2025, the AFC/M23 coalition unveiled a historic tax reform in North and South Kivu, aimed at simplifying the taxation system and reducing administrative burdens.
title_en: AFC/M23 Announces Major Tax Reform in Kivu
excerpt_en: Goma - On December 3, 2025, the AFC/M23 coalition unveiled a historic tax reform in North and South Kivu, aimed at simplifying the taxation system and reducing administrative burdens.
body_en:
Goma - On December 3, 2025, the AFC/M23 coalition unveiled a historic tax reform in North and South Kivu, aimed at simplifying the taxation system and reducing administrative burdens.

The plan calls for the elimination of 225 taxes and duties, representing nearly 60% of the current system, according to Fanny Kaj, Deputy Head of the Finance Department. The reform seeks to end the fragmentation of the 536 existing taxes by merging levies, removing various operating licenses, and consolidating sector-specific taxes.

The reform also includes the complete digitization of tax collection, the creation of a permanent tax reform commission, the opening of local collection centers, and the establishment of a single-window system operational from January 2026.

Developed in consultation with the Federal Executive Council (CEF), civil society, and religious actors, this initiative is expected to improve transparency, reduce the burden on businesses, and strengthen the economic attractiveness of North and South Kivu.

title: Standardized Invoicing Adopted to Modernize Tax Management
excerpt: Kinshasa - As of December 1, 2025, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has made the use of standardized invoicing mandatory, marking a major reform in the country’s tax system.
title_en: Standardized Invoicing Adopted to Modernize Tax Management
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - As of December 1, 2025, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has made the use of standardized invoicing mandatory, marking a major reform in the country’s tax system.
body_en:
Kinshasa - As of December 1, 2025, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has made the use of standardized invoicing mandatory, marking a major reform in the country’s tax system.

Led by the General Directorate of Taxes (DGI), this reform aims to strengthen transparency and combat tax fraud. The secure electronic document standardizes the identification of the seller and buyer, the unique invoice number, the goods or services invoiced, and the applicable taxes.

The measure applies to public and private companies, NGOs, public institutions, traders, and various service providers, requiring an adaptation of invoicing systems while providing consumers with reliable and traceable proof of purchase.

Backed by a broad awareness campaign, the reform is designed to increase public revenue collection and improve the country’s economic governance, aligning with the government’s modernization agenda.

title: Central Bank of Congo Assumes Chairmanship in Central Africa for 2025-2026
excerpt: Kinshasa - The Central Bank of Congo (BCC) has been appointed chairman of the Central Africa sub-region within the Bureau of the Association of African Central Banks (AACB) for the 2025-2026 term, following the 47th…
title_en: Central Bank of Congo Assumes Chairmanship in Central Africa for 2025-2026
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - The Central Bank of Congo (BCC) has been appointed chairman of the Central Africa sub-region within the Bureau of the Association of African Central Banks (AACB) for the 2025-2026 term, following the 47th…
body_en:
Kinshasa - The Central Bank of Congo (BCC) has been appointed chairman of the Central Africa sub-region within the Bureau of the Association of African Central Banks (AACB) for the 2025-2026 term, following the 47th annual meeting held from November 23 to 28, 2025, in Yaoundé.

Represented by its Governor André Wameso, the BCC participated in discussions on the African single currency, the African Monetary Fund, and the integration of climate issues into monetary policies. The review of the African Monetary Cooperation Programme revealed that only 12 countries meet the five key macroeconomic convergence criteria, prompting the AACB to call for an acceleration of reforms.

This appointment positions the BCC as a strategic actor in harmonizing the regional monetary framework and preparing for the 48th AACB meeting, scheduled for 2026 in Kenya. On the sidelines, Wameso met with the Governor of the BEAC, Yvon Sana Bangui, concluding a cooperation agreement aimed at strengthening expertise exchange and pooling efforts to address common macroeconomic challenges.

title: U.S. Treasury Department Commends Congo's Efforts to Be Removed from the FATF Gray List
excerpt: Kinshasa - On December 8, 2025, a U.S. Treasury delegation, led by Acting Assistant Secretary of State Warren Ryan, met with the leadership of the Congolese National Financial Intelligence Unit (Cenaref) and experts…
title_en: U.S. Treasury Department Commends Congo's Efforts to Be Removed from the FATF Gray List
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - On December 8, 2025, a U.S. Treasury delegation, led by Acting Assistant Secretary of State Warren Ryan, met with the leadership of the Congolese National Financial Intelligence Unit (Cenaref) and experts…
body_en:
Kinshasa - On December 8, 2025, a U.S. Treasury delegation, led by Acting Assistant Secretary of State Warren Ryan, met with the leadership of the Congolese National Financial Intelligence Unit (Cenaref) and experts from the Congolese Ministry of Finance to commend the Democratic Republic of Congo's efforts to be removed from the FATF gray list.

Discussions focused on strengthening technical cooperation in the fight against money laundering, terrorist financing, and the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, as well as Cenaref's future integration into the Egmont Global Network.

This initiative is part of the International Cooperation Review Group (ICRG) process and the reforms undertaken by Kinshasa, including the modernization of its legal and institutional framework and its accession to the ESAAMLG, aimed at restoring international financial confidence and attracting foreign investment.

title: Rawbank Named Bank of the Year 2025 by The Banker
excerpt: Kinshasa - Rawbank has been named Bank of the Year 2025 in the Democratic Republic of Congo by The Banker, a Financial Times Group publication, announced on December 12, 2025.
title_en: Rawbank Named Bank of the Year 2025 by The Banker
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - Rawbank has been named Bank of the Year 2025 in the Democratic Republic of Congo by The Banker, a Financial Times Group publication, announced on December 12, 2025.
body_en:
Kinshasa - Rawbank has been named Bank of the Year 2025 in the Democratic Republic of Congo by The Banker, a Financial Times Group publication, announced on December 12, 2025.

This award recognizes the best-performing and strongest financial institutions in their market. Rawbank distinguished itself through improved results, progress on its transformation program, and its role in financing major projects, including a $400 million international consortium for the expansion of the Kamoa-Kakula oil pipeline.

Between 2022 and 2024, Rawbank strengthened its financial position and undertook a strategic rebranding in April 2025. CEO Mustafa Rawji hailed the award as recognition of the hard work of his teams and the trust of customers.

This new trophy adds to previous awards received this year, including Best Bank in the DRC (Euromoney Awards 2025) and World's Safest Bank 2025 (Global Finance). With $6.2 billion in assets and a network of over 100 branches across 19 provinces, Rawbank remains a major player in the Congolese banking sector.

title: DRC to Launch Chatbot to Strengthen Consumer Protection
excerpt: Kinshasa - On December 12, 2025, the Ministry of National Economy, through Minister Daniel Mukoko Samba, announced the upcoming launch of a chatbot.
title_en: DRC to Launch Chatbot to Strengthen Consumer Protection
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - On December 12, 2025, the Ministry of National Economy, through Minister Daniel Mukoko Samba, announced the upcoming launch of a chatbot.
body_en:
Kinshasa - On December 12, 2025, the Ministry of National Economy, through Minister Daniel Mukoko Samba, announced the upcoming launch of a chatbot. This virtual assistant is designed to inform consumers about their rights and facilitate the handling of complaints across several regulated sectors, including banking, insurance, telecommunications, air transport, pharmaceuticals, agri-food, and electricity.

The chatbot will allow users to submit reports, consult summaries of applicable laws, and check the processing times for complaints. Additionally, the data collected will be used to strengthen market surveillance and identify sectors requiring particular attention.

Scheduled for the first quarter of 2026, this initiative forms part of the Ministry's strategy to promote transparency, citizen participation, and effective consumer protection nationwide.

body_en:
Kinshasa - Addressing Parliament on December 8, 2025, President Félix Tshisekedi announced that the Democratic Republic of Congo's foreign exchange reserves had reached nearly $7.4 billion, equivalent to roughly three months of essential imports.

The President described this level as a sign of confidence and resilience in the Congolese economy, despite global market volatility. This increase in reserves is intended to strengthen the country's capacity to withstand external shocks and reassure economic partners, while also emphasizing the importance of economic diversification to reduce dependence on mining exports.

excerpt: Kinshasa - The National Assembly has adopted the 2026 budget, totaling 54,335.8 billion Congolese francs, underlining the emphasis on security and national defense amid ongoing conflict in eastern DRC.
title_en: DRC National Assembly Approves 2026 Budget with Focus on Security and Social Protection
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - The National Assembly has adopted the 2026 budget, totaling 54,335.8 billion Congolese francs, underlining the emphasis on security and national defense amid ongoing conflict in eastern DRC.
body_en:
Kinshasa - The National Assembly has adopted the 2026 budget, totaling 54,335.8 billion Congolese francs, underlining the emphasis on security and national defense amid ongoing conflict in eastern DRC.

Presented by Prime Minister Judith Suminwa, the draft budget now proceeds to the Senate for review. Nearly 30% of expenditures are allocated to security, while agriculture, education, health, and social protection remain key priorities.

Speaker of the National Assembly, Aimé Boji, expressed Parliament’s solidarity with the population and armed forces facing Rwandan aggression, while ECOFIN Committee Chairman Guy Mafuta Kabongo described the budget as realistic and suited to the current economic and humanitarian context of the DRC.

excerpt_en: Kinshasa - On December 8, 2025, the Ministry of National Economy launched a pre-registration campaign for informal economy actors in Kinshasa, under the National Mass Formalization Program.

The initiative seeks to identify and integrate small traders, artisans, and service providers into the formal economy, providing access to economic opportunities, universal health coverage, social protection, vocational training, and bank credit.

title: DRC: MSF Warns of 15,000 New HIV Infections Among Youth in 2024
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - Doctors Without Borders (MSF) revealed on Wednesday, December 3, 2025, that nearly 15,000 young Congolese under the age of 25 contracted HIV in 2024, according to data from the National AIDS Control…
title_en: DRC: MSF Warns of 15,000 New HIV Infections Among Youth in 2024
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - Doctors Without Borders (MSF) revealed on Wednesday, December 3, 2025, that nearly 15,000 young Congolese under the age of 25 contracted HIV in 2024, according to data from the National AIDS Control…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - Doctors Without Borders (MSF) revealed on Wednesday, December 3, 2025, that nearly 15,000 young Congolese under the age of 25 contracted HIV in 2024, according to data from the National AIDS Control Program (PNMLS) presented during a press conference in Kinshasa on the sidelines of World AIDS Day.

Gisèle Mucinya, medical coordinator of MSF's HIV project, described the situation as alarming, citing insufficient prevention of mother-to-child transmission, limited access to information, testing, and treatment, and persistent stigma.

She highlighted key obstacles, including the limited availability of tests, the cost of voluntary testing, and restrictions on minors being tested without parental consent.

Since 2019, MSF has been running youth clubs providing medical and psychological support, and the organization is calling on the government to increase funding amid the disengagement of partners such as USAID and the World Bank. This support is aimed at intensifying awareness campaigns and expanding HIV prevention initiatives nationwide.

title: Validation of the National Child Policy Marks Major Step for Child Protection
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - Validated on December 4, 2025, the National Child Policy (NCP) represents a decisive step forward for the Democratic Republic of Congo, providing a guiding framework for all public actions in favor of…
title_en: Validation of the National Child Policy Marks Major Step for Child Protection
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - Validated on December 4, 2025, the National Child Policy (NCP) represents a decisive step forward for the Democratic Republic of Congo, providing a guiding framework for all public actions in favor of…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - Validated on December 4, 2025, the National Child Policy (NCP) represents a decisive step forward for the Democratic Republic of Congo, providing a guiding framework for all public actions in favor of children.

Jean Mulumba Kubayi, coordinator of the National Child Policy Committee (NCC), emphasized that the policy is an essential governance tool, particularly for guiding budgetary decisions. The NCP seeks to eradicate children separated from their families, eliminate all forms of violence, abuse, and exploitation, and strengthen the protection of minors in conflict with the law or associated with armed groups.

John Agbor, UNICEF representative, welcomed this milestone, stressing that a policy “is not just a document, but a lever for transformation” that must lead to concrete actions.

Congolese authorities described the moment as historic, reaffirming that the protection of children remains a national and international priority.

body_en:
Demba, Kasai-Central - Teachers in the Demba territory of Kasai-Central province began an indefinite strike on Thursday, December 4, 2025, suspending classes to protest delayed salary payments dating back to September, amounting to three months of arrears.

The situation, described as "miserable" by the union spokesperson, has left many teachers’ families struggling to make ends meet and paralyzed the local education system.

The teachers are demanding the immediate payment of their accumulated salaries and have threatened to continue the strike until their demands are met.

title_en: Ituri (DRC): 18 STAR-EST Projects to Be Handed Over to Local Communities Soon
excerpt_en: Bunia, Ituri - Eighteen community development projects implemented in the territories of Irumu and Djugu - including the construction of schools and health centers and the rehabilitation of agricultural roads - were…
body_en:
Bunia, Ituri - Eighteen community development projects implemented in the territories of Irumu and Djugu - including the construction of schools and health centers and the rehabilitation of agricultural roads - were presented on Monday, December 1, 2025, at an evaluation meeting in Bunia.

The meeting brought together provincial authorities, traditional leaders, civil society representatives, and experts from the provincial advisory committee.

These infrastructure projects, carried out under the government's STAR-EST program, which aims at stabilizing conflict zones, are set to be officially handed over to local authorities by January 2026 to directly benefit local communities.

According to coordinator Steve Singida, these achievements strengthen local resilience and promote peace. The governor commended their impact and encouraged the continuation of the program into its second phase, scheduled for 2026.

title: North Kivu: At Least 92 Newborns Die in Lubero in Three Months Amid Lack of Neonatal Care
excerpt: Lubero, North Kivu - Over the past three months, at least 92 newborns have died in the Kayna health zone of Lubero territory due to the absence of a neonatal unit at the main general referral hospital and surrounding…
title_en: North Kivu: At Least 92 Newborns Die in Lubero in Three Months Amid Lack of Neonatal Care
excerpt_en: Lubero, North Kivu - Over the past three months, at least 92 newborns have died in the Kayna health zone of Lubero territory due to the absence of a neonatal unit at the main general referral hospital and surrounding…
body_en:
Lubero, North Kivu - Over the past three months, at least 92 newborns have died in the Kayna health zone of Lubero territory due to the absence of a neonatal unit at the main general referral hospital and surrounding health centers.

The Lubero Territory Midwives Association raised the alarm on December 11, 2025, citing that premature infants and newborns with serious illnesses, including malaria and urogenital infections, are not receiving adequate care, resulting in a high mortality rate - approximately one infant dying every day between 0 and 28 days.

Gerlas Kasiko, president of the Order of Midwives of Lubero, called on the government and humanitarian partners to equip and strengthen neonatal services, aiming to significantly reduce infant mortality and save lives.

title: Government Bans Abuses Related to Escorts, Sirens, and Flashing Lights
excerpt: Kinshasa - On Monday, December 8, 2025, the Congolese government announced a ban on the use of military and police escorts, sirens, flashing lights, and multi-colored lights throughout the country.
title_en: Government Bans Abuses Related to Escorts, Sirens, and Flashing Lights
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - On Monday, December 8, 2025, the Congolese government announced a ban on the use of military and police escorts, sirens, flashing lights, and multi-colored lights throughout the country.
body_en:
Kinshasa - On Monday, December 8, 2025, the Congolese government announced a ban on the use of military and police escorts, sirens, flashing lights, and multi-colored lights throughout the country.

This measure, issued on the instructions of the President of the Republic, responds to observed abuses, particularly by unauthorized individuals. The decision aims to restore public order and strictly regulate security escorts, explicitly prohibiting their use by private vehicles.

The New Congolese Civil Society welcomed the initiative, calling it an important step toward fairness, respect for the highway code, and the end of undue privileges. The organization urged rigorous and uncompromising enforcement, under the close supervision of law enforcement authorities.

title: President Félix Tshisekedi Deplores Unsanitary Conditions and Traffic Gridlocks

title_en: President Félix Tshisekedi Deplores Unsanitary Conditions and Traffic Gridlocks

body_en:
Kinshasa - Addressing both houses of Parliament on December 8, 2025, President Félix Tshisekedi denounced poor waste management in Kinshasa, which he said caused clogged sewers, severe flooding, and traffic jams that paralyze traffic during the rainy season.

He stressed that this situation poses a challenge to national governance, endangers the health of residents, and degrades their quality of life. The Head of State also expressed concern about the resurgence of banditry in the capital and other cities, reaffirming the government’s commitment to strengthening security and implementing structural reforms.

Despite these challenges, he noted positive signs on the economic front, highlighting the recent stability of the Congolese franc.

title: Launch of 3rd Phase of Compensation for Ring Road Project
excerpt: Kinshasa - The third phase of the compensation operation for residents affected by the Ring Road Project began on Thursday, December 11, 2025, in Kinshasa.
title_en: Launch of 3rd Phase of Compensation for Ring Road Project
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - The third phase of the compensation operation for residents affected by the Ring Road Project began on Thursday, December 11, 2025, in Kinshasa.
body_en:
Kinshasa - The third phase of the compensation operation for residents affected by the Ring Road Project began on Thursday, December 11, 2025, in Kinshasa. Over 100 beneficiaries were expected at the meeting room of the General Secretariat for Infrastructure and Public Works in the Lingwala district.

Under the leadership of Secretary General for Infrastructure Georges Koshi, the inter-ministerial commission in charge of expropriations reaffirmed its commitment to transparency and fairness in payment of compensation.

This initiative is part of the over 70 km road project, financed by the Sino-Congolese program and executed by Chinese companies CREC 4 and CREC 8, under the coordination of the Congolese Agency for Major Works (ACGT). During the second phase, nearly 200 cases were processed out of 3,442 registered, and the commission is now working to optimize the payment process to ensure prompt compensation to beneficiaries.

title: Reopening of Komanda-Luna Section Brings Mixed Relief
excerpt: Ituri - After nearly three years of closure due to ADF rebel attacks and the poor condition of the road, the 75-kilometer Komanda-Luna section of National Route 4 was officially reopened to traffic on December 9, 2025…
title_en: Reopening of Komanda-Luna Section Brings Mixed Relief
excerpt_en: Ituri - After nearly three years of closure due to ADF rebel attacks and the poor condition of the road, the 75-kilometer Komanda-Luna section of National Route 4 was officially reopened to traffic on December 9, 2025…
body_en:
Ituri - After nearly three years of closure due to ADF rebel attacks and the poor condition of the road, the 75-kilometer Komanda-Luna section of National Route 4 was officially reopened to traffic on December 9, 2025, during a ceremony in Luna, on the border between Ituri and North Kivu.

Funded by the government and rehabilitated with support from Ugandan military engineers, this vital section now provides a shorter and safer route for the transport of people and goods, while also facilitating the intervention of security forces against the ADF.

However, the reopening was overshadowed by tragedy: on the same day, an ADF attack claimed the lives of four civilians, including a three-month-old baby, underscoring that the rebel threat persists and that security along this strategic route must be strengthened to ensure safe traffic and the protection of the population.

title: Fire in Mambasa Kills One, Destroys Over 50 Businesses
excerpt: Mambasa, Ituri - A devastating fire broke out on the night of December 12, 2025, ravaging the commercial center of Mambasa, located about 165 km southwest of Bunia.
title_en: Fire in Mambasa Kills One, Destroys Over 50 Businesses
excerpt_en: Mambasa, Ituri - A devastating fire broke out on the night of December 12, 2025, ravaging the commercial center of Mambasa, located about 165 km southwest of Bunia.
body_en:
Mambasa, Ituri - A devastating fire broke out on the night of December 12, 2025, ravaging the commercial center of Mambasa, located about 165 km southwest of Bunia. The incident left one dead and destroyed approximately fifty businesses, including restaurants, food warehouses, and homes.

According to local sources, the fire originated at the Pygmées Hotel around 1:00 a.m. and rapidly spread to neighboring buildings, fueled by wooden structures and a lack of effective firefighting equipment. Residents, who gathered in large numbers, were largely helpless as the flames consumed food and goods intended for festivities, effectively paralyzing local economic activity.

It was not until dawn that construction equipment was deployed to slow the fire's advance toward the "Zala na Mbango" market. Local authorities have launched an investigation to determine the exact cause of the blaze.

title: DRC: Training for Magistrates in Kinshasa to Strengthen International Judicial Cooperation
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - A workshop dedicated to strengthening international judicial cooperation concluded on Wednesday, December 3, 2025, in Kinshasa after three days of sessions involving civilian and military magistrates…
title_en: DRC: Training for Magistrates in Kinshasa to Strengthen International Judicial Cooperation
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - A workshop dedicated to strengthening international judicial cooperation concluded on Wednesday, December 3, 2025, in Kinshasa after three days of sessions involving civilian and military magistrates…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - A workshop dedicated to strengthening international judicial cooperation concluded on Wednesday, December 3, 2025, in Kinshasa after three days of sessions involving civilian and military magistrates from multiple provinces.

Under the theme "International Judicial Cooperation: Some Regional Experiences," the workshop aimed to enhance understanding of cooperation agreements signed by the DRC, the management of requests for mutual legal assistance, and the use of letters rogatory, with the goal of limiting impunity for criminals who have taken refuge abroad.

Speakers, including Magistrate Aurélien Kajangu and Attorney General Pierre Shindano, emphasized that the training is essential for enabling Congolese courts to effectively prosecute offenders, regardless of their location of refuge.

Participants recommended better coordination between law enforcement agencies and the creation of liaison networks to improve regional cooperation.

The workshop was organized by the Great Lakes Region Judicial Cooperation Network, in partnership with the MONUSCO Justice Support Section.

title: Brig Gen Byamungu Returns to Uvira Amid M23 Takeover
excerpt: Uvira, DRC - The remarkable story of Brig Gen Bernard Byamungu unfolded in the city where he once served as head of operations for the Congolese government army.
title_en: Brig Gen Byamungu Returns to Uvira Amid M23 Takeover
excerpt_en: Uvira, DRC - The remarkable story of Brig Gen Bernard Byamungu unfolded in the city where he once served as head of operations for the Congolese government army.
body_en:
Uvira, DRC - The remarkable story of Brig Gen Bernard Byamungu unfolded in the city where he once served as head of operations for the Congolese government army. Originally a CNDP soldier, Byamungu was integrated into government forces in 2009, but his journey would take a dramatic turn.

In May 2012, Brig Gen Byamungu returned to Uvira, his last place of residence, facing life imprisonment and the stripping of his military medals. Between 2009 and 2012, he had commanded operations for the government army across Uvira, earning notoriety in the region.

Later in 2012, Byamungu joined a new rebel group composed of former CNDP soldiers. Those who defected from the government army in Fizi and Uvira were few, and many were quickly arrested. Some attempted to flee to North Kivu, where they would later establish the M23 rebel group. Byamungu, however, opposed this move.

On May 30, 2012, a special military court was convened to try the rebels. Thousands of citizens gathered outside the military palace in Uvira as Byamungu and other senior leaders faced trial. Ultimately, eight leaders, including Byamungu, were sentenced to life imprisonment and stripped of their military ranks. They were then transferred to Bukavu and onward to Ndolo military prison in Kinshasa.

After eight years, an agreement between President Félix Tshisekedi and M23 resulted in Byamungu’s release. By December 9, 2025, the city of Uvira had fallen under the control of AFC/M23, the same group with which Byamungu aligned. Upon returning to the courthouse where he had been sentenced, he was arrested by small soldiers, who confiscated his rings and necklace following the verdict.

Meanwhile, the AFC/M23 solidified its presence in Uvira, as well as other key cities including Goma and Bukavu, asserting control over large parts of eastern DRC.

title: DRC Military Court Sentences Officers Who Fled During Goma Capture
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - December 5, 2025 - The High Military Court of the Democratic Republic of Congo has sentenced senior officers who fled when AFC/M23 rebels captured the city of Goma in late January 2025.
title_en: DRC Military Court Sentences Officers Who Fled During Goma Capture
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - December 5, 2025 - The High Military Court of the Democratic Republic of Congo has sentenced senior officers who fled when AFC/M23 rebels captured the city of Goma in late January 2025.
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - December 5, 2025 - The High Military Court of the Democratic Republic of Congo has sentenced senior officers who fled when AFC/M23 rebels captured the city of Goma in late January 2025.

The officers include Brig Gen Dany Yangba Tene, Brig Gen Papy Lupembe Mopenzo, Commissioner Eddy-Léonard Mukuna, and Jean-Lomuard Ekuka Lipopo, who briefly served as the interim Governor of North Kivu Province following the death of Gen Maj Peter Cirimwami.

Gen Maj Alengbia Nzambe, former commander of the 34th Military District, was also detained but his case was closed after his death in April 2025.

The trial began in March 2025, with the prosecution arguing that the officers had abandoned their posts and fled to areas including Bukavu, leaving junior soldiers behind during the AFC/M23 assault on Goma. The court heard that the officers’ actions contributed to the rebels’ seizure of weapons and military equipment.

The officers defended themselves, stating that their withdrawal to South Kivu Province was a tactical maneuver ordered by the military high command.

The military court convicted the officers of desertion, disobeying orders, and abandoning military equipment, handing down light sentences:

Brig Gen Tene and Brig Gen Lupembe: 1 year in prison each, plus a fine of 2.8 million Congolese francs

The DRC military prosecution had sought 20 years to life imprisonment for the accused.

title: Magloire Paluku, AFC/M23 Leader and Former Journalist, Assassinated
excerpt: Goma, North Kivu - Magloire Paluku Kavunga, a former journalist, writer, poet, and founder of Radio Kivu 1, was shot dead on Wednesday, December 10, 2025, in the streets of Goma while returning to his home in the Himbi…
title_en: Magloire Paluku, AFC/M23 Leader and Former Journalist, Assassinated
excerpt_en: Goma, North Kivu - Magloire Paluku Kavunga, a former journalist, writer, poet, and founder of Radio Kivu 1, was shot dead on Wednesday, December 10, 2025, in the streets of Goma while returning to his home in the Himbi…
body_en:
Goma, North Kivu - Magloire Paluku Kavunga, a former journalist, writer, poet, and founder of Radio Kivu 1, was shot dead on Wednesday, December 10, 2025, in the streets of Goma while returning to his home in the Himbi neighborhood.

Aged 58 and originally from Butembo, Paluku had served at the Ministry of Culture before joining the AFC/M23 rebellion from Bunagana, in Rutshuru territory. In July 2024, he was sentenced to death in absentia during the trial of Corneille Nangaa and 24 others, accused of war crimes, treason, and participating in an insurrection.

The exact circumstances of his death remain unclear, prompting his family to demand a thorough investigation to ensure that the perpetrators are brought to justice. His assassination has sparked strong emotions in eastern DRC, where he was widely recognized as a cultural and media figure.
body_fr:
Goma, North Kivu - Magloire Paluku Kavunga, a former journalist, writer, poet, and founder of Radio Kivu 1, was shot dead on Wednesday, December 10, 2025, in the streets of Goma while returning to his home in the Himbi neighborhood.

Aged 58 and originally from Butembo, Paluku had served at the Ministry of Culture before joining the AFC/M23 rebellion from Bunagana, in Rutshuru territory. title: AFC/M23 Leader Corneille Nangaa Considers DRC Presidency, Advocates Federalism
excerpt: Goma, November 27, 2025 - Corneille Nangaa, leader of the AFC/M23 coalition fighting the government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), has indicated that he sees himself as a potential future president of the country.
title_en: AFC/M23 Leader Corneille Nangaa Considers DRC Presidency, Advocates Federalism
excerpt_en: Goma, November 27, 2025 - Corneille Nangaa, leader of the AFC/M23 coalition fighting the government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), has indicated that he sees himself as a potential future president of the country.
body_en:
Goma, November 27, 2025 - Corneille Nangaa, leader of the AFC/M23 coalition fighting the government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), has indicated that he sees himself as a potential future president of the country. Speaking to SBS News, Nangaa acknowledged, “I am a Congolese and I have the right to be president, it can happen and I accept it as a responsibility.”

During the interview, Nangaa addressed accusations that M23 is supported by Rwanda, firmly denying them. “We don’t receive any support from Rwanda. We are Congolese and we are fighting for our cause,” he said, calling claims by the Kinshasa government “lies and smearing.”

Nangaa also dismissed allegations of war crimes and crimes against humanity, stating, “I deny it, I denounce it, I say it’s a lie.” He claimed that in areas currently under M23 control, particularly Goma, “Life has returned, people are living, children have returned to school, there are no more insecurity issues, Goma is safe.”

At a seminar in Goma on November 27, Nangaa outlined AFC/M23’s vision for governance reform, advocating for federalism. Under this system, provinces would have independent administrations, manage their own resources, and share powers with the national government.

Nangaa proposed renaming the country to Republique Fédérale du Congo (RFC), emphasizing that “our vision as a coalition is that what is called DRC today should become the Republique Fédérale du Congo. That is the choice, that is the vision.”

He added that the coalition seeks equitable distribution of regional resources and aims to end what he describes as oppression from Kinshasa.

Nangaa has repeatedly criticized the current DRC governance under President Félix Tshisekedi, asserting that if AFC/M23 achieves its objectives, it will replace the president with a leader capable of restoring the country’s stability and international standing.

The statements signal Nangaa’s political ambitions, as well as AFC/M23’s broader strategy to transform the DRC’s governance structure through regional autonomy and federalism.

body_en:
Oicha, North Kivu - More than 1,000 officers from the Congolese National Police (PNC) were deployed on Monday, December 1, 2025, to Oicha, in the Beni territory, to bolster security in the rural commune and surrounding agricultural areas, which are regularly threatened by armed groups, ahead of the holiday season.

During a parade led by Provincial Commissioner General Dieudonné Makambo, the officers were tasked with protecting the population, securing property, and maintaining order.

The general urged residents to cooperate closely with law enforcement, emphasizing the need for collective action to ensure a peaceful atmosphere during the holidays. He also reaffirmed his commitment to strengthening security measures and promoting the National Fund for the Security of Civil Servants.

title_en: South Kivu: Violent Clashes Between FARDC and AFC/M23 Trigger Humanitarian Crisis in the Ruzizi Plain
excerpt_en: South Kivu, DRC - Violent clashes erupted at dawn on Tuesday, December 2, 2025, in the Kaziba chiefdom, Walungu territory, pitting the FARDC against AFC/M23 rebels following a strategic repositioning of both sides in…
body_en:
South Kivu, DRC - Violent clashes erupted at dawn on Tuesday, December 2, 2025, in the Kaziba chiefdom, Walungu territory, pitting the FARDC against AFC/M23 rebels following a strategic repositioning of both sides in the highlands.

The fighting, marked by heavy gunfire and the use of heavy weapons, is concentrated around Nguka Hill, plunging the towns of Katogota, Luvungi, Lubarika, and Kamanyola into panic. A shell struck a house in Kamanyola, further escalating fears among residents.

The population, sheltering in their homes, faces a critical humanitarian situation: roads are cut off, supplies are blocked, and access for NGOs is difficult in an area already ravaged by years of insecurity.

Local stakeholders are urgently calling on authorities to restore security to prevent a further deterioration of the situation.

title: South Kivu: DRC Forces Launch Multiple Attacks Against AFC/M23
excerpt: South Kivu, December 2, 2025 - In the early hours of December 2, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) armed forces launched major attacks in several areas of South Kivu province, targeting regions under the control of…
title_en: South Kivu: DRC Forces Launch Multiple Attacks Against AFC/M23
excerpt_en: South Kivu, December 2, 2025 - In the early hours of December 2, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) armed forces launched major attacks in several areas of South Kivu province, targeting regions under the control of…
body_en:
South Kivu, December 2, 2025 - In the early hours of December 2, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) armed forces launched major attacks in several areas of South Kivu province, targeting regions under the control of the AFC/M23 coalition.

The coalition in South Kivu comprises the DRC army (FARDC), Wazalendo groups, Burundian troops, and the FDLR terrorist group, which opposes the Rwandan government.

AFC/M23 spokesman Lawrence Kanyuka warned that the attacks affected densely populated areas, exacerbating the humanitarian situation for civilians.

The areas targeted included the Katogota-Luvungi road in Uvira territory, connecting Kaziba in Walungu with the highlands, Tchivanga-Hombo in Kabare and Kalehe, and Kasika in Mwenga territory.

These offensives follow previous clashes, highlighting the difficulty of enforcing ceasefire agreements despite the creation of a Qatari-backed monitoring body established under the October 14, 2025, agreement between AFC/M23 and the DRC government, which reinforced earlier accords signed in April.

The AFC/M23 maintains that it has the right to defend itself and protect civilians in danger, while the DRC government asserts that its forces are acting in self-defense.

title: DRC: AFC/M23 Accuses Burundi of Deadly Cross-Border Strikes in the East
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - In a statement released on December 5, 2025, the Congo River Alliance (AFC/M23) claimed that bombings launched from Burundian territory have been targeting several villages in North and South Kivu for…
title_en: DRC: AFC/M23 Accuses Burundi of Deadly Cross-Border Strikes in the East
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - In a statement released on December 5, 2025, the Congo River Alliance (AFC/M23) claimed that bombings launched from Burundian territory have been targeting several villages in North and South Kivu for…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - In a statement released on December 5, 2025, the Congo River Alliance (AFC/M23) claimed that bombings launched from Burundian territory have been targeting several villages in North and South Kivu for over three days, resulting in the deaths of at least 23 civilians, along with injuries and significant material damage.

The rebel movement accused Burundi of supporting strikes carried out by fighter jets, drones, and artillery against densely populated areas, describing the actions as a "methodically planned offensive."

According to AFC/M23, these attacks have caused new mass displacements of people toward Bukavu and Rwanda, and the group considers these acts to be war crimes.

While condemning what it describes as Burundi’s involvement alongside the Congolese government, the rebellion reaffirmed its commitment to "protecting civilians."

At this stage, no official reaction from Kinshasa or Bujumbura has been reported to confirm or deny these allegations.

title: Heavy Fighting Resumes in South Kivu Between AFC/M23 and DRC Government
excerpt: South Kivu, DRC - December 2-4, 2025 - Fighting between the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) government forces and the AFC/M23 rebel group has escalated across multiple areas of South Kivu, including Kaziba…
title_en: Heavy Fighting Resumes in South Kivu Between AFC/M23 and DRC Government
excerpt_en: South Kivu, DRC - December 2-4, 2025 - Fighting between the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) government forces and the AFC/M23 rebel group has escalated across multiple areas of South Kivu, including Kaziba…
body_en:
South Kivu, DRC - December 2-4, 2025 - Fighting between the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) government forces and the AFC/M23 rebel group has escalated across multiple areas of South Kivu, including Kaziba (Walungu), Luvungi (Uvira), Mudaka (Kabare), Katogota, and Lubarika.

December 2: Fighting erupted early in the day; AFC/M23 reportedly fired first, anticipating attacks from DRC, Burundian, and Rwandan forces.

Impact on civilians: Three civilians were killed in Kamanyola; in Kaziba, bombings destroyed homes, with reports of over 20 civilian deaths, including the head of the Muhumba Gurupoma and his four children. Infrastructure in several towns was severely damaged.

Territorial shifts: The DRC army lost control of Katogota, and some Burundian troops retreated to Uvira or Burundi. AFC/M23 forces approached Luvungi but avoided immediate entry to protect civilians.

December 3: Fighting continued; DRC forces shelled Kamanyola and Kaziba. AFC/M23 reported shells fired from Burundi killed 4 civilians and injured 6, including 3 children.

Government response: The provincial administration was destabilized; Governor Jean-Jacques Purusi fled to Bujumbura. Some Wazalendo fighters protested against the Commander of Military Operations, Brig Gen Amuli Chiviri.

Regional context: The clashes coincided with a Rwanda-DRC agreement signed in Washington, D.C., on December 4, committing both countries to support a ceasefire in North and South Kivu and pursue political dialogue as the path to peace.

title: Heavy Fighting in South Kivu: AFC/M23 Forces Push Back DRC and Wazalendo Troops
excerpt: South Kivu, DRC - December 4, 2025
title_en: Heavy Fighting in South Kivu: AFC/M23 Forces Push Back DRC and Wazalendo Troops
excerpt_en: South Kivu, DRC - December 4, 2025
body_en:
South Kivu, DRC - December 4, 2025

The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) government forces and allied Wazalendo troops suffered a setback in the battle for control in South Kivu province, withdrawing from several areas after days of intense fighting with AFC/M23 forces. Key flashpoints included Katogota, Luvungi, Lubarika in Uvira territory, and Kaziba in Walungu.

According to reports, DRC, Burundian, and Wazalendo forces launched heavy shelling on Kamanyola and Kaziba, while Wazalendo troops fired indiscriminately in Mudaka center from the Kajeje mountains, resulting in two civilian deaths and injuries to three students, disrupting local businesses and closing main roads.

AFC/M23 fighters quickly responded, reclaiming Mudaka center, reopening the roads, and counterattacking government positions in Kaziba, including Butuzi, Chemba, Nabumbu, and Mwera. Despite the use of BM-Grad rockets, Sukhoi-25 aircraft, and combat drones, DRC forces failed to retake Kamanyola, leaving civilians in panic. Hundreds reportedly fled to Rwanda and other parts of the DRC to escape the violence.

AFC/M23 spokesman Lawrence Kanyuka condemned attacks on civilians, reporting deaths and injuries, including students, during assaults on schools. The ongoing clashes underscore the fragile security situation in South Kivu and the challenges faced by local populations.

title: South Kivu: AFC/M23 Reports Heavy Shelling from Burundian Forces
excerpt: South Kivu, December 5, 2025 - The AFC/M23 coalition, engaged in fighting against DRC government forces, has confirmed that shells are falling in areas under its control in South Kivu Province, reportedly coming from…
title_en: South Kivu: AFC/M23 Reports Heavy Shelling from Burundian Forces
excerpt_en: South Kivu, December 5, 2025 - The AFC/M23 coalition, engaged in fighting against DRC government forces, has confirmed that shells are falling in areas under its control in South Kivu Province, reportedly coming from…
body_en:
South Kivu, December 5, 2025 - The AFC/M23 coalition, engaged in fighting against DRC government forces, has confirmed that shells are falling in areas under its control in South Kivu Province, reportedly coming from Burundian troops.

Since the morning of December 5, combined forces of the DRC, Burundi, and Wazalendo have launched attacks on several parts of Uvira District, including Katogota, Kamanyola, and Luvungi Gurupoma.

The shelling in Luvungi camp forced numerous residents to flee to safer areas such as Sange, Runingu, Ndolera, and the city of Uvira.

Bertrand Bisimwa, AFC/M23 deputy leader for politics, said:"This morning, Burundian troops are shelling densely populated areas in Kamanyola, Katogota, and Luvungi, killing innocent people, including children, and destroying houses, schools, churches, and markets."

Images posted on social media by Bisimwa showed extensive damage to homes, with a local resident reporting six deaths near Ngomo Hill in Kamanyola.

AFC/M23 spokesman Lawrence Kanyuka confirmed that Burundian forces have been shelling these populated areas for more than three days, asserting that their fighters remain committed to protecting civilians in the affected zones.

Keywords: AFC/M23, South Kivu, Burundi, DRC government, shelling, Kamanyola, Katogota, Luvungi, Bertrand Bisimwa, Lawrence Kanyuka, civilian displacement, conflict.

title: Nearly 900,000 New Displaced Persons Registered in the East Between July and October 2025, OCHA Warns
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - Nearly 886,000 new internally displaced persons (IDPs) were registered between July and October 2025 in the provinces of Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, and Tanganyika, according to the latest figures…
title_en: Nearly 900,000 New Displaced Persons Registered in the East Between July and October 2025, OCHA Warns
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - Nearly 886,000 new internally displaced persons (IDPs) were registered between July and October 2025 in the provinces of Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, and Tanganyika, according to the latest figures…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - Nearly 886,000 new internally displaced persons (IDPs) were registered between July and October 2025 in the provinces of Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, and Tanganyika, according to the latest figures published on December 2 by OCHA.

The UN humanitarian agency attributes these mass displacements to clashes between the FARDC (Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo) and armed groups, land disputes, and natural disasters.

Simultaneously, returns were recorded: 72,000 in Ituri, 67,400 in South Kivu, and 318,000 in North Kivu.

OCHA raised the alarm about the deteriorating humanitarian situation in the affected areas and called for the lifting of restrictions hindering assistance operations, amid violence perpetrated by the ADF, M23, CODECO, and other militias.

Despite the dismantling of several camps following the M23’s capture of Goma and Bukavu, many families continue to host displaced people, while the implementation of the humanitarian corridor announced at the Paris summit remains slow to materialize.

title: South Kivu Escalates: DRC Forces Retaliate Against AFC/M23
excerpt: South Kivu, December 5, 2025
title_en: South Kivu Escalates: DRC Forces Retaliate Against AFC/M23
excerpt_en: South Kivu, December 5, 2025
body_en:
South Kivu, December 5, 2025

title: Kinshasa Warns: FDLR Threatens Entire DRC, MP Okitundu Calls for Immediate Action
excerpt: Kinshasa, December 5, 2025 - MP Léonard She Okitundu, former Minister of Foreign Affairs (2016-2019) and current Vice President of the Foreign Affairs Committee in the National Assembly, has urged the DRC government to…
title_en: Kinshasa Warns: FDLR Threatens Entire DRC, MP Okitundu Calls for Immediate Action
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, December 5, 2025 - MP Léonard She Okitundu, former Minister of Foreign Affairs (2016-2019) and current Vice President of the Foreign Affairs Committee in the National Assembly, has urged the DRC government to…
body_en:
Kinshasa, December 5, 2025 - MP Léonard She Okitundu, former Minister of Foreign Affairs (2016-2019) and current Vice President of the Foreign Affairs Committee in the National Assembly, has urged the DRC government to take decisive action against the FDLR terrorist group, which he says has effectively taken over the country.

In an interview with RFI, Okitundu emphasized that the United Nations Security Council had called in February 2025 for the cessation of support to the FDLR and their dismantling, a directive he believes the DRC government must urgently enforce.

“The FDLR is taking the entire DRC hostage,” Okitundu stated. “Strong measures must be taken against this group. It is not optional, nor should the government appear to tolerate their presence.”

Responding to remarks from FDLR military spokesman Lt Col Octavien Mutimura, who declared that the group has no intention of disarming, Okitundu warned that such statements complicate the DRC government’s position and must not be ignored. He suggested that expelling all armed group members, including FDLR fighters, should be a priority.

Okitundu dismissed claims that obstacles prevent action against the FDLR. “There are no major obstacles. The government must act decisively and avoid any appearance of collaboration with the group,” he said.

The call for action comes shortly after the Rwanda-DRC Peace and Economic Cooperation Agreement was signed on December 4, 2025, in Washington, D.C., by President Paul Kagame and Félix Tshisekedi. The agreement includes provisions for the destruction of the FDLR, removal of security measures, and cooperation in trade, mining, and economic development activities.

title: Kinshasa Accuses Kigali of Violating the Washington Peace Agreement
excerpt: Kinshasa - The Congolese government denounced on Tuesday, December 9, 2025, Rwanda's “flagrant violation” of the peace agreement signed on December 4, 2025, in Washington between President Félix Tshisekedi and President…
title_en: Kinshasa Accuses Kigali of Violating the Washington Peace Agreement
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - The Congolese government denounced on Tuesday, December 9, 2025, Rwanda's “flagrant violation” of the peace agreement signed on December 4, 2025, in Washington between President Félix Tshisekedi and President…
body_en:
Kinshasa - The Congolese government denounced on Tuesday, December 9, 2025, Rwanda's “flagrant violation” of the peace agreement signed on December 4, 2025, in Washington between President Félix Tshisekedi and President Paul Kagame. The government expressed deep concern over new Rwandan incursions into South Kivu.

During a meeting with Prime Minister Judith Suminwa, the government delegation emphasized the urgency of implementing the commitments outlined in the agreement and responding to an escalation described as intolerable, given that it challenges the authority of the American mediator.

Following the meeting, government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya denounced a “regionalization of the conflict”, accusing Kigali of also targeting Burundi, and urged the mediator to act to restore peace.

The government reaffirmed its determination to defend territorial integrity, protect civilian populations affected by the rebel advance, and intensify diplomatic consultations to preserve the peace process initiated in Washington.
