title: AFC/M23: Dispute with DRC to Be Resolved in Qatar
excerpt: South Kivu, December 5, 2025 - The AFC/M23 coalition, engaged in conflict with the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), announced that its dispute with the DRC government will be addressed through talks in Doha, Qatar…
title_en: AFC/M23: Dispute with DRC to Be Resolved in Qatar
excerpt_en: South Kivu, December 5, 2025 - The AFC/M23 coalition, engaged in conflict with the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), announced that its dispute with the DRC government will be addressed through talks in Doha, Qatar…
body_en:
South Kivu, December 5, 2025 - The AFC/M23 coalition, engaged in conflict with the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), announced that its dispute with the DRC government will be addressed through talks in Doha, Qatar, rather than in the United States, according to Deputy Spokesperson Dr. Oscar Balinda.

Dr. Balinda emphasized that while the Rwanda-DRC peace agreement signed on December 4, 2025, in Washington includes provisions relevant to AFC/M23 demands-notably the destruction of the FDLR terrorist group and the repatriation of Congolese refugees-it does not halt fighting in eastern DRC. He clarified, “The ones fighting on the battlefield are the Kinshasa regime, the Tshisekedi government, and AFC/M23. Our problem is in Doha. There is no war between them.”

Despite the Washington agreement, DRC armed forces, including Congolese, Burundian, and Wazalendo troops, continued attacks on Kamanyola, Katogota, and Luvungi, resulting in 23 confirmed deaths and multiple injuries, according to AFC/M23 spokesman Lawrence Kanyuka.

The group stressed that the Qatar-mediated talks are intended to create a ceasefire environment conducive to lasting peace negotiations.

title: Over 74 Civilians Killed in One Week of Fighting Between FARDC and M23
excerpt: South Kivu - At least 74 civilians have been killed and 83 wounded since December 2, 2025, amid clashes between the FARDC and the M23, further deteriorating an already critical humanitarian situation.
title_en: Over 74 Civilians Killed in One Week of Fighting Between FARDC and M23
excerpt_en: South Kivu - At least 74 civilians have been killed and 83 wounded since December 2, 2025, amid clashes between the FARDC and the M23, further deteriorating an already critical humanitarian situation.
body_en:
South Kivu - At least 74 civilians have been killed and 83 wounded since December 2, 2025, amid clashes between the FARDC and the M23, further deteriorating an already critical humanitarian situation. The information was provided on Wednesday, December 10, by Bruno Lemarquis, Humanitarian Coordinator in the DRC and acting head of MONUSCO.

He warned of escalating violence, which is hindering medical evacuations, disrupting schools, and forcing over 200,000 people to flee within the province, while thousands more seek refuge in Burundi and Rwanda. The living conditions of displaced persons remain alarming, with overcrowding, health risks, and gender-based violence.

Mr. Lemarquis stressed that civilians and civilian infrastructure must be protected, calling for an immediate cessation of explosive weapons in populated areas. He also emphasized that the peace agreement signed on December 4 in Washington between the DRC and Rwanda can only take effect if hostilities cease.

title: FARDC Airstrikes Target AFC/M23 Positions in North and South Kivu
excerpt: NORTH KIVU - As fighting persists in South Kivu, the Congolese Armed Forces (FARDC) have intensified operations in North Kivu, carrying out airstrikes on AFC/M23 positions in Masisi Territory, according to local sources.
title_en: FARDC Airstrikes Target AFC/M23 Positions in North and South Kivu
excerpt_en: NORTH KIVU - As fighting persists in South Kivu, the Congolese Armed Forces (FARDC) have intensified operations in North Kivu, carrying out airstrikes on AFC/M23 positions in Masisi Territory, according to local sources.
body_en:
NORTH KIVU - As fighting persists in South Kivu, the Congolese Armed Forces (FARDC) have intensified operations in North Kivu, carrying out airstrikes on AFC/M23 positions in Masisi Territory, according to local sources.

On December 7, 2025, FARDC drones reportedly struck positions on Kahongole Hill and near the Masisi territorial administration, after reconnaissance flights over the area. Similar strikes were earlier reported in Nyabiondo, a strategic locality near Walikale, captured by AFC/M23 in March 2025.

Additional bombardments targeted Bukombo, between Masisi and Nyabiondo. Meanwhile, FARDC and allied forces have continued shelling Kamanyola and Kaziba in South Kivu since December 2, causing civilian casualties, displacement, and damage to property.

AFC/M23 retains control of the targeted areas and says it is maintaining security for civilians. The Congolese military operations are reportedly supported by Burundian forces, whose involvement has expanded despite ongoing losses.

The escalation comes as AFC/M23 continues rapid territorial advances, including the recent capture of Uvira, a key government stronghold held by FARDC for nearly ten months after its withdrawal from Bukavu.

title: 36 Killed in FARDC-Wazalendo Clashes in Uvira
excerpt: Uvira Territory, South Kivu - At least 36 people were killed and 19 others injured following violent clashes between the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and Wazalendo factions in Uvira…
title_en: 36 Killed in FARDC-Wazalendo Clashes in Uvira
excerpt_en: Uvira Territory, South Kivu - At least 36 people were killed and 19 others injured following violent clashes between the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and Wazalendo factions in Uvira…
body_en:
Uvira Territory, South Kivu - At least 36 people were killed and 19 others injured following violent clashes between the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and Wazalendo factions in Uvira territory, eastern DRC, according to local sources.

The fighting erupted in the Sange area, which has been under the control of Congolese, Burundian, and Wazalendo forces for several days. These forces are jointly engaged in operations against the AFC/M23 coalition, which has intensified military pressure across South Kivu province.

The province has witnessed heavy fighting in recent days, with government forces suffering setbacks and losing control of several strategic localities, including Katogota, Rurambo, Luvungi, Luberizi, and Bwegera, sources in South Kivu reported.

According to the same sources, on December 7, 2025, FARDC troops retreating from the frontlines arrived in Sange, seeking to regroup and move with their weapons and equipment toward the city of Uvira. However, the Wazalendo fighters reportedly opposed this move.

The Wazalendo demanded that the FARDC forces withdraw to Uvira without their arms and ammunition, arguing that the weapons should be used locally in the fight against the AFC/M23. The disagreement quickly escalated into armed confrontations between the two sides.

During the clashes, an explosive device was reportedly detonated, killing 36 people, including civilians and soldiers, and leaving 19 others wounded.

The Burundian news outlet SOS Médias reported that seven Burundian soldiers were among those killed in the fighting.

The incident underscores the growing fragmentation among allied forces in eastern DRC, further complicating efforts to stabilize the conflict-hit South Kivu region.

title: AFC/M23 Advances Toward Uvira as Fighting Intensifies in South Kivu
excerpt: South Kivu, DRC - The AFC/M23 coalition continues to expand its territorial control in South Kivu province, advancing steadily toward the strategic city of Uvira, a key administrative hub of the Democratic Republic of…
title_en: AFC/M23 Advances Toward Uvira as Fighting Intensifies in South Kivu
excerpt_en: South Kivu, DRC - The AFC/M23 coalition continues to expand its territorial control in South Kivu province, advancing steadily toward the strategic city of Uvira, a key administrative hub of the Democratic Republic of…
body_en:
South Kivu, DRC - The AFC/M23 coalition continues to expand its territorial control in South Kivu province, advancing steadily toward the strategic city of Uvira, a key administrative hub of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

On December 8, 2025, AFC/M23 fighters seized several positions in Uvira Territory, including the centers of Nyakabere and Sange, following clashes with DRC government forces. These gains come after earlier captures of Bwegera, Luberizi, Luvungi, Rurambo, and Katogota, which fell as the group advanced from Kamanyola, an area it has controlled for the past 10 months.

The coalition is moving southward along the RN5 national road, pushing toward Uvira town, the seat of the South Kivu provincial administration appointed by Kinshasa. Sange, now at the center of the fighting, lies approximately 30 kilometers from Uvira.

To reach the city, AFC/M23 must still secure other strategic localities, including Runingo and Kiliba, also located within Uvira Territory, marking another 30-kilometer stretch along the route.

Fighting earlier last week was marked by heavy shelling around Kamanyola, slowing the advance. However, the situation has since shifted, with AFC/M23 fighters moving at a rapid pace, dramatically altering the battlefield dynamics.

At the same time, the DRC army (FARDC) has become embroiled in clashes with Wazalendo militias, groups it has often fought alongside. The confrontations stem from growing mistrust and battlefield failures, making it increasingly difficult to determine command authority and coordination among pro-government forces.

On December 7, 2025, Sange was under the control of a pro-government coalition backed by the DRC, including Wazalendo fighters. As FARDC units attempted to withdraw toward Uvira, they were reportedly blocked by Wazalendo groups, who demanded that government troops surrender their weapons.

When FARDC refused, heavy fighting erupted, drawing in Burundian forces. The clashes left at least 36 people dead, including civilians and soldiers, and more than 20 others injured, according to local sources.

Wazalendo militias, known for defying orders from the DRC military command, have since accused government forces of colluding with AFC/M23, questioning how the group has been able to seize territory so quickly.

The accusations reflect deepening fractures within the pro-government camp, further complicating efforts to halt the AFC/M23 advance and raising concerns over security and civilian protection as fighting edges closer to Uvira city.

title: Twirwaneho Says It Shot Down Mercenary Helicopter After Attacks on Civilians
excerpt: South Kivu, DRC - The Twirwaneho armed group has claimed responsibility for the downing of a military helicopter allegedly operated by foreign mercenaries employed by the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)…
title_en: Twirwaneho Says It Shot Down Mercenary Helicopter After Attacks on Civilians
excerpt_en: South Kivu, DRC - The Twirwaneho armed group has claimed responsibility for the downing of a military helicopter allegedly operated by foreign mercenaries employed by the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)…
body_en:
South Kivu, DRC - The Twirwaneho armed group has claimed responsibility for the downing of a military helicopter allegedly operated by foreign mercenaries employed by the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) government, saying the action followed repeated attacks on civilians in South Kivu province.

According to local accounts, on December 6, 2025, fishermen on the shores of Lake Tanganyika recovered the body of a white man from the water in the Yumbi area of Fizi Territory, where a helicopter had crashed. Reports said the man and several companions were initially pulled from the lake alive, identified as mercenaries involved in the ongoing conflict in South Kivu.

In a statement released on December 7, 2025, Twirwaneho said the incident occurred amid a humanitarian blockade imposed by the Burundian army, which it claims had cut off civilians from markets and basic supplies. The group said that after the blockade eased briefly, around 100 civilians traveled to the Ndondo and Bijombo markets to buy food and medicine.

According to Twirwaneho spokesperson Colonel Kamasa Ndakize Welcome, those civilians were later ambushed while returning.

“Yesterday morning, as these civilians were coming back, they were ambushed by the Burundian army, killed, and taken hostage-mostly women,” he said, adding that the number of victims remains unknown.

Colonel Kamasa further alleged that women captured during the ambush were subjected to sexual violence and other abuses at the Mikalati military base and other undisclosed locations.

Twirwaneho said its fighters moved to rescue civilians, prompting the Burundian army to request air support. The group claims that three helicopters, piloted by white foreign operators, were then deployed and carried out bombing raids on several localities, including Mikalati, Mikenke, Gahwera, Gisoke, and Rugezi.

“After repeated attacks on these villages, our forces shot down one of the helicopters, which crashed into Lake Tanganyika in Fizi Territory, in the Yumbi area,” the statement said.

Twirwaneho also alleged that on December 6, two battalions of the Burundian army moved from Mwenga Center toward Mikalati via Kipupu, with the aim of reinforcing forces there. The group accused the troops of intending to carry out attacks against the Banyamulenge community.

The armed group called on the Burundian army to withdraw immediately from DRC territory, vowing to continue what it described as defensive measures to protect civilians and their property.

The allegations could not be independently verified. Burundian authorities and the DRC government have not publicly responded to the claims at the time of publication.

The armed group called on the Burundian army to withdraw immediately from DRC territory, vowing to continue what it described as defensive measures to protect civilians and their property.

title: Fall of Uvira: Burundi Closes Border to Prevent Incursions
excerpt: Uvira - Following the capture of Uvira by M23 rebels on Wednesday, December 10, 2025, Burundi announced the immediate closure of its border with the DRC, citing the need to protect itself from any attempted incursion.
title_en: Fall of Uvira: Burundi Closes Border to Prevent Incursions
excerpt_en: Uvira - Following the capture of Uvira by M23 rebels on Wednesday, December 10, 2025, Burundi announced the immediate closure of its border with the DRC, citing the need to protect itself from any attempted incursion.
body_en:
Uvira - Following the capture of Uvira by M23 rebels on Wednesday, December 10, 2025, Burundi announced the immediate closure of its border with the DRC, citing the need to protect itself from any attempted incursion. Thousands of displaced Congolese are already seeking refuge in Burundi, as the humanitarian crisis deepens.

The closure followed the withdrawal of the Congolese army the previous day to Swima, Makobola, and Baraka, leaving the town vulnerable. M23 elements, reportedly supported by Rwanda, appeared publicly in Uvira late in the morning after a sweep operation, a presence confirmed by residents and the rebels themselves.

The United States and the European Union called for an immediate halt to the offensive in eastern DRC, while Congolese authorities had not issued an official response by late Wednesday afternoon.

title: Washington and EU Demand Immediate Halt to M23 and Rwandan Forces’ Offensive in South Kivu
excerpt: Kinshasa - The United States and several European countries, convening within the Great Lakes Contact Group on Tuesday, December 9, 2025, called on the M23/AFC and Rwandan forces to immediately cease their offensives in…
title_en: Washington and EU Demand Immediate Halt to M23 and Rwandan Forces’ Offensive in South Kivu
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - The United States and several European countries, convening within the Great Lakes Contact Group on Tuesday, December 9, 2025, called on the M23/AFC and Rwandan forces to immediately cease their offensives in…
body_en:
Kinshasa - The United States and several European countries, convening within the Great Lakes Contact Group on Tuesday, December 9, 2025, called on the M23/AFC and Rwandan forces to immediately cease their offensives in eastern DRC.

The group expressed deep concern over the escalating violence around Uvira, a city seized the following day by the Kigali-backed rebellion. In a joint statement, Germany, Belgium, Denmark, the United States, France, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, Sweden, Switzerland, and the European Union condemned the increased use of attack drones, calling it a "significant escalation" posing a serious threat to civilians.

The statement demands the withdrawal of Rwandan troops in accordance with UN Resolution 2773, full compliance by M23 with the Doha Declaration of July 19, 2025, and the implementation of the Washington Agreements of December 4, 2025. Signatories also call for the protection of civilians, respect for the territorial integrity of the DRC, the unequivocal restoration of the ceasefire, and full and safe humanitarian access.

title: Four Dead in Irumu After Another ADF Attack
excerpt: Irumu, Ituri - Four people were killed on Tuesday in Idohu, about 100 kilometers from Bunia, during an attack by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) that paralyzed socio-economic activity in the Irumu territory, where…
title_en: Four Dead in Irumu After Another ADF Attack
excerpt_en: Irumu, Ituri - Four people were killed on Tuesday in Idohu, about 100 kilometers from Bunia, during an attack by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) that paralyzed socio-economic activity in the Irumu territory, where…
body_en:
Irumu, Ituri - Four people were killed on Tuesday in Idohu, about 100 kilometers from Bunia, during an attack by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) that paralyzed socio-economic activity in the Irumu territory, where violence has been escalating over the past week.

According to civil society sources, the assailants beheaded three villagers ambushed in Kimbaseke before advancing on Idohu, where they were repelled by the FARDC (Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo). A child was fatally struck by a stray bullet.

Several residents abducted in Monge remain hostage, while about ten houses were burned down, and an illegal administration imposed by the rebels is spreading to nearby villages, where the ADF are demanding “gifts” for access to fields.

Faced with this resurgence of attacks as the end-of-year holidays approach, civil society is calling on the army to strengthen security, while the FARDC have not yet responded.

title: North Kivu: Civil Society Raises Alarm Over Deteriorating Humanitarian Situation in M23-Occupied Areas
excerpt: North Kivu - Civil society is raising the alarm about the critical humanitarian situation in the territories of Masisi and Rutshuru, where people returning to areas controlled by the AFC-M23 are living in extremely…
title_en: North Kivu: Civil Society Raises Alarm Over Deteriorating Humanitarian Situation in M23-Occupied Areas
excerpt_en: North Kivu - Civil society is raising the alarm about the critical humanitarian situation in the territories of Masisi and Rutshuru, where people returning to areas controlled by the AFC-M23 are living in extremely…
body_en:
North Kivu - Civil society is raising the alarm about the critical humanitarian situation in the territories of Masisi and Rutshuru, where people returning to areas controlled by the AFC-M23 are living in extremely precarious conditions.

According to Léopold Mwisha, a local civil society activist, families, mainly composed of farmers and herders, are suffering from malnutrition, lack of medical care, and insufficient shelter, while their agricultural and pastoral activities are severely disrupted.

He is calling for urgent intervention from authorities and humanitarian partners to assist these vulnerable communities and mitigate the consequences of the rebel occupation.

The period from December 1 to 14, 2025, was marked by a stark and troubling contradiction between diplomatic ambition and security reality in the Great Lakes region.

The signing of the DRC-Rwanda Peace Agreement in Washington on December 4 raised hopes for a lasting de-escalation, outlining commitments to a ceasefire, the neutralization of the FDLR, and the launch of joint economic initiatives such as the Rusizi III hydroelectric project.

Yet this diplomatic breakthrough was almost immediately undermined by a sharp deterioration of security in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, particularly in South Kivu. The capture of Uvira by the AFC/M23, accompanied by renewed fighting and mass displacement, exposed the fragility of the agreement. Kinshasa and Washington openly accused Rwanda of violating the accord, alleging continued military support for the rebellion and an escalation of cross-border operations.

At the same time, both countries pressed ahead with internal reforms: Rwanda advanced key infrastructure projects, while the DRC emphasized economic stabilization and state resilience, citing nearly $7.4 billion in foreign exchange reserves and the adoption of a security-centered 2026 national budget.

Ultimately, this two-week period illustrates a central paradox: while political frameworks for peace and development are taking shape, their success remains hostage to realities on the ground. The rapid collapse of the ceasefire underscores that the implementation of agreements, the cessation of proxy warfare, and the protection of civilians remain the most urgent-and most fragile-tests for peace in the Great Lakes region.

title: Burundi Counts the Cost as AFC/M23 Seizes Uvira
excerpt: Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye believed his calculations were solid.
title_en: Burundi Counts the Cost as AFC/M23 Seizes Uvira
excerpt_en: Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye believed his calculations were solid.
body_en:
Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye believed his calculations were solid. After Burundian troops were pushed out of Masisi territory, Bujumbura had reinforced its military posture with long-range heavy weapons and combat drones, hoping to outmaneuver AFC/M23 fighters and restore national prestige shaken by months of fighting on Congolese soil.

When Burundian forces began shelling AFC/M23-held positions in South Kivu Province, including the Kamanyola Center, the objective was clear: retake lost ground, reassert control, and reclaim what officials described as the honor of Burundi.

Instead, the offensive backfired.

In rapid succession, AFC/M23, which had also strengthened its supply lines, pushed back a coalition of forces comprising the Burundian army, the DRC armed forces (FARDC), Wazalendo militias, and the FDLR as they moved on the strategic city of Uvira. As the situation deteriorated, statements from Burundian authorities began to reflect growing anxiety.

On December 10, 2025, Burundi’s Foreign Affairs Minister, Dr. Edouard Bizimana, warned in an interview with Radio France Internationale (RFI) that the fall of Uvira would pose a direct threat to Burundi’s security.

“If Uvira were to be captured, the economic capital would be threatened,” Bizimana said, referring to Bujumbura, located just minutes away. “The movement of goods and people between our two countries would be cut off. With the influx of refugees, our capacity would be strained. This is therefore a direct problem for Burundi.”

That same day, AFC/M23 announced the capture of Uvira.

Within hours, the Burundian government closed the Kavimvira and Vugizo border crossings with the Democratic Republic of Congo, suspending cross-border trade and movement for an indefinite period.

The city of Uvira, covering more than 200 square kilometers, lies along the northern shores of Lake Tanganyika and was home to an estimated 700,000 residents last year. Its proximity-about 30 kilometers-to Bujumbura makes it a vital economic and social hub for both countries.

Following the fighting, thousands of residents fled toward Burundi, mainly through the Kavimvira border, which leads into the Gatumba Zone.

Daily trade between Congolese and Burundians has long depended on Kavimvira. Commonly traded goods include maize, beans, yams, and fish from Lake Tanganyika.

According to Faustin Ndikumana, head of the Burundian civil society organization PARCEM, the economic impact is severe.

“More than 60% of Burundi’s exports go to the DRC,” Ndikumana said. “This activity generates significant foreign exchange. Its disruption will only worsen an already fragile foreign currency market.”

Data from the Central Bank of Burundi show that in 2024, Burundi exported 135,300 tons of goods, of which 69,400 tons-more than half-were destined for the DRC, largely via the Kavimvira border.

Burundi has long faced chronic shortages of petroleum products, which officials attribute to a lack of foreign exchange and illegal trading networks. Many Burundians previously relied on fuel purchased in South Kivu, where prices were lower, crossing through Kavimvira.

Since the border closure, that lifeline has vanished.

Ndikumana noted that Burundians are now unable to source gasoline and diesel from the DRC, worsening the crisis.

RFI journalist Esdras Ndikumana reported a sharp spike in prices: a 20-liter jerrycan of fuel that previously sold for 150,000 Rwandan francs now costs as much as 400,000 francs. At the same time, the US dollar has surged from 5,400 to 6,500 Rwandan francs, further straining the economy.

The Burundian government insists it will not tolerate AFC/M23’s control of Uvira, vowing to do everything necessary to safeguard Bujumbura’s security, including the possible use of military options.

For its part, AFC/M23 says it seeks peaceful coexistence with Burundi, not confrontation. The group maintains that it favors good-neighborly relations and claims that, if necessary, it can allow the reopening of borders and the resumption of movement and trade.

As diplomatic tensions rise, Uvira’s capture stands as both a military setback and a major economic shock for Burundi-one whose full consequences are still unfolding.

title: “Burundi Has a New Neighbor It Doesn’t Like” - Senator Evode Uwizeyimana Warns After Uvira Falls to AFC/M23
excerpt: Burundian Senator Evode Uwizeyimana has warned that Burundi must come to terms with AFC/M23 following the group’s capture of Uvira, cautioning that continued confrontation could plunge the country into intractable…
title_en: “Burundi Has a New Neighbor It Doesn’t Like” - Senator Evode Uwizeyimana Warns After Uvira Falls to AFC/M23
excerpt_en: Burundian Senator Evode Uwizeyimana has warned that Burundi must come to terms with AFC/M23 following the group’s capture of Uvira, cautioning that continued confrontation could plunge the country into intractable…
body_en:
Burundian Senator Evode Uwizeyimana has warned that Burundi must come to terms with AFC/M23 following the group’s capture of Uvira, cautioning that continued confrontation could plunge the country into intractable political, economic, and security problems.

Speaking in an interview aired on National Television, Uwizeyimana said the seizure of Uvira, a strategic city in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), has fundamentally altered Burundi’s regional environment, leaving the country with what he described as a new and unwelcome neighbor.

On December 15, 2025, the senator explained that Uvira’s importance lay in its dual role as both the center of military planning against AFC/M23 and the backbone of Burundi’s cross-border trade.

“All those who were defeated in Goma and Bukavu, including the Governor of Kivu and Wazalendo fighters, were there,” Uwizeyimana said.

According to the senator, the concentration of forces hostile to AFC/M23 in Uvira turned the city into a prime military target.

He said the arrival of the AFC/M23 coalition in Uvira, where it regrouped and prepared new operations, ultimately led to the capture of the city, the neutralization of armed opponents, and the creation of a strategic dilemma for Burundi-one that may force Bujumbura to negotiate directly with the fighters now controlling the area.

“If M23 continues to advance southwards, Burundi would be isolated, with only Tanzania left,” Uwizeyimana warned. “There is also the port of Mpurungu in Zambia, but it is far away. What is clear is that trade between Bujumbura and Uvira shows how much this city means to Burundi.”

Uwizeyimana also pointed to the plight of Burundian soldiers deployed in eastern DRC, describing the situation as increasingly untenable.

“Some Burundian soldiers have returned home, which is good, but others remain trapped in the mountains,” he said. “The question is: where will those who remain go? Burundi will have to reach an agreement with M23 to allow them a way out.”

He stressed that Burundi now faces a harsh reality.

“Burundi today has a new and unfriendly neighbor-one that came to us against our will, because we opposed it, failed to repel it, and could not drive it away,” Uwizeyimana said.

Addressing the timing of the offensive, the senator dismissed claims that the capture of Uvira was linked to the peace agreement signed in the United States between Rwanda and the DRC.

Instead, he said AFC/M23 acted after months of careful preparation, fully aware that large numbers of troops and heavy equipment had been deployed in Uvira following its victories in Goma and Bukavu.

Uwizeyimana added that while the DRC government had entered negotiations with the group and agreed to a cessation of hostilities, the failure to implement those agreements convinced AFC/M23 that the talks were yielding no results.

As a result, the group resumed fighting and succeeded in capturing additional territories, including Uvira.

Following the fall of Uvira in South Kivu Province, the Burundian government closed the Kavimvira and Vugizo border crossings with the DRC, halting trade and movement.

The decision came amid an already tense regional climate, after borders between Burundi and Rwanda had also been closed for a prolonged period.

Uwizeyimana’s remarks underscore growing concern within Burundi’s political class that the country is entering a new geopolitical reality, one in which dialogue with AFC/M23 may no longer be optional, but unavoidable.

title: AFC/M23 Announces Withdrawal from Uvira in Support of Peace Process
excerpt: The Alliance Fleuve Congo/March 23 Movement (AFC/M23) has announced a unilateral withdrawal of its forces from the city of Uvira, citing its commitment to ongoing peace efforts in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).
title_en: AFC/M23 Announces Withdrawal from Uvira in Support of Peace Process
excerpt_en: The Alliance Fleuve Congo/March 23 Movement (AFC/M23) has announced a unilateral withdrawal of its forces from the city of Uvira, citing its commitment to ongoing peace efforts in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).
body_en:
The Alliance Fleuve Congo/March 23 Movement (AFC/M23) has announced a unilateral withdrawal of its forces from the city of Uvira, citing its commitment to ongoing peace efforts in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

In a statement dated December 15, 2025, the movement said the decision follows progress made under the Doha Peace Process, including the signing of the Doha Framework Agreement on November 15, 2025. AFC/M23 said the withdrawal was carried out at the request of United States mediation, as a confidence-building measure aimed at giving peace negotiations the best chance of success.

Despite accusing the Congolese army (FARDC) and allied Wazalendo militias of continued provocations and abuses, the group said it chose to pursue de-escalation to help achieve a lasting solution to the conflict.

AFC/M23 called on guarantors of the peace process to put in place measures to secure Uvira, including demilitarization, protection of civilians and infrastructure, and neutral monitoring of the ceasefire.

title: DRC: Kinshasa Dismisses M23 Announcement as Rwandan “Diversion”
excerpt: Kinshasa, December 17, 2025 - The Congolese government has dismissed the recent announcement by the AFC/M23 rebel movement, which claimed it was ready to withdraw from the city of Uvira under unspecified “security…
title_en: DRC: Kinshasa Dismisses M23 Announcement as Rwandan “Diversion”
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, December 17, 2025 - The Congolese government has dismissed the recent announcement by the AFC/M23 rebel movement, which claimed it was ready to withdraw from the city of Uvira under unspecified “security…
body_en:
Kinshasa, December 17, 2025 - The Congolese government has dismissed the recent announcement by the AFC/M23 rebel movement, which claimed it was ready to withdraw from the city of Uvira under unspecified “security guarantees,” describing it as a “non-event” and a calculated diversion aimed at shielding Rwanda from responsibility.

Speaking in an interview with France 24, Patrick Muyaya, Minister of Communication and government spokesperson, rejected the statement outright, accusing Kigali of backing the armed group and using it as a proxy in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

“The son (M23) is sacrificing himself to protect the father (Rwanda),” Muyaya said, arguing that recent Rwandan military offensives demonstrate that President Paul Kagame does not genuinely believe in the peace agreement brokered by the United States under former President Donald Trump.

The minister also warned of a worsening humanitarian crisis in South Kivu, particularly in and around Uvira. According to government figures, hundreds of thousands of civilians have been internally displaced, while at least 85,000 refugees have fled across the border into Burundi.

Muyaya stressed that the only sustainable solution lies in the safe and peaceful return of displaced populations, a condition he said cannot be guaranteed by “those who govern through crimes.”

Reiterating Kinshasa’s position, the government spokesperson called for the immediate and unconditional withdrawal of Rwandan troops from Congolese territory. “Leave our territory,” he said, urging national mobilization in defense of the country’s sovereignty.

title: UK Imposes Visa Restrictions on DRC Over Migrant Repatriation
excerpt: LONDON / KINSHASA - December 28, 2025 - The United Kingdom has imposed visa restrictions on citizens of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) after the country failed to implement measures to repatriate illegal…
title_en: UK Imposes Visa Restrictions on DRC Over Migrant Repatriation
excerpt_en: LONDON / KINSHASA - December 28, 2025 - The United Kingdom has imposed visa restrictions on citizens of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) after the country failed to implement measures to repatriate illegal…
body_en:
LONDON / KINSHASA - December 28, 2025 - The United Kingdom has imposed visa restrictions on citizens of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) after the country failed to implement measures to repatriate illegal immigrants and other individuals wanted by UK authorities.

According to the UK government, the DRC did not comply with new asylum rules announced in November 2025. As a result, DRC citizens will no longer have access to fast-track visa services, and dignitaries and politicians from the DRC will no longer receive special entry privileges previously reserved for state leaders.

The UK also reported that Angola and Namibia have agreed to increase efforts to repatriate their citizens, following warnings that non-compliance could lead to similar sanctions. Countries that fail to adhere to the new rules risk denial of visas for their citizens.

Under the new UK measures, asylum seekers will be granted temporary rather than long-term residence, and support for accommodation will be removed. A new entry system limits the number of people who can enter the UK through this route. The UK government had previously warned that countries refusing to accept their nationals could face punitive actions.

title: At Least 40 Congolese Refugees Die from Cholera and Malnutrition in Gatumba

title_en: At Least 40 Congolese Refugees Die from Cholera and Malnutrition in Gatumba
excerpt_en: Gatumba, Burundi - December 18, 2025 - At least 40 Congolese refugees have died over ten days in the Gatumba transit camp due to cholera and malnutrition, amid severe shortages of drinking water, food, medicine, and…
body_en:
Gatumba, Burundi - December 18, 2025 - At least 40 Congolese refugees have died over ten days in the Gatumba transit camp due to cholera and malnutrition, amid severe shortages of drinking water, food, medicine, and survival supplies.

The deputy mayor of Uvira, Kifara Kapenda, himself a refugee in Bujumbura after the city fell to AFC/M23 forces, chaired a meeting with the Congolese diaspora to coordinate aid and urge urgent action from the Congolese government and humanitarian organizations.

Many of the refugees are women and children, living in overcrowded conditions that increase their vulnerability to disease. A crisis committee has been established to manage assistance and reduce mortality among the roughly 30,000 Congolese residents of Gatumba.

title_en: Over 1,000 Flood-Affected Families in Zongo Receive Humanitarian Aid
excerpt_en: Zongo, South Ubangi - December 15, 2025 - More than 1,000 families affected by recent floods in Zongo have received food, non-food items, and financial assistance from the National Solidarity and Humanitarian Disaster…
body_en:
Zongo, South Ubangi - December 15, 2025 - More than 1,000 families affected by recent floods in Zongo have received food, non-food items, and financial assistance from the National Solidarity and Humanitarian Disaster Management Fund (CSN-GHC).

Recipients were provided with essential items including rice, beans, sugar, salt, soybeans, semolina, and household goods such as mattresses, buckets, pots, cups, and soap. The aid distribution ceremony took place at the Zongo town hall, with the participation of the mayor, MP Coco Mbozi, representatives of Governor Michée Mobongo, civil society members, and local authorities.

This humanitarian effort complements existing government measures to support residents affected by the torrential rains of 2024, providing relief to the most vulnerable communities.

excerpt: Beni, North Kivu - December 15, 2025 - Over 2,000 Congolese passports arrived in Beni, the provisional capital of North Kivu, bringing relief to residents who had been waiting for months.
title_en: Beni Receives 2,000 Congolese Passports, Easing Wait for Applicants
excerpt_en: Beni, North Kivu - December 15, 2025 - Over 2,000 Congolese passports arrived in Beni, the provisional capital of North Kivu, bringing relief to residents who had been waiting for months.
body_en:
Beni, North Kivu - December 15, 2025 - Over 2,000 Congolese passports arrived in Beni, the provisional capital of North Kivu, bringing relief to residents who had been waiting for months.

This shipment is the fourth batch distributed to applicants since December 16, while photo registration continues in Butembo for more than 3,000 people. Residents welcomed the arrivals but criticized the slow pace of the issuance process.

To improve accessibility, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has established a photo-taking center in Beni, allowing residents from Beni, Butembo, and surrounding areas to obtain biometric passports without traveling to Kinshasa or Bunia.

title: Kwango River Tragedy: Over 30 Dead in Shipwreck
excerpt: Bagata, Kwango Province - December 13, 2025 - More than 30 people died when a small boat capsized on the Kwango River near the village of Bolo.
title_en: Kwango River Tragedy: Over 30 Dead in Shipwreck
excerpt_en: Bagata, Kwango Province - December 13, 2025 - More than 30 people died when a small boat capsized on the Kwango River near the village of Bolo.
body_en:
Bagata, Kwango Province - December 13, 2025 - More than 30 people died when a small boat capsized on the Kwango River near the village of Bolo.

According to MP Gary Sakata, most of the victims were teachers traveling to Bandundu to collect their salaries, while several other passengers remain missing. The vessel was also carrying around 700 sacks of corn and cassava, all of which were lost when the boat struck an obstacle.

This disaster echoes a similar incident in September 2024, which resulted in 12 deaths, multiple missing persons, and dozens of survivors.

Authorities have yet to provide further details on rescue operations or investigations into the cause of the accident.

excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - December 18, 2025 - Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka inaugurated a high-level private investment workshop organized by the American Chamber of Commerce in the DRC, in partnership with the U.S.

Kinshasa, DRC - December 18, 2025 - Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka inaugurated a high-level private investment workshop organized by the American Chamber of Commerce in the DRC, in partnership with the U.S. Embassy and under the patronage of the President of the Republic.

The workshop, themed “DRC-U.S. Partnership: Challenges, Opportunities, and New Investment Dynamics,” aimed to advance commitments made at the U.S.-DRC Economic and Investment Forum in Washington, D.C., in October 2025.

Prime Minister Suminwa highlighted that responsible private investment is key to economic growth, innovation, and sustainable job creation. U.S. Ambassador Lucy Tamlyn expressed American confidence in the DRC’s economic potential, while Yannick Sukamunu, from the American Chamber of Commerce, noted that the recent peace agreement with Rwanda created a favorable environment for investment and development.

title: Belgium Condemns Arrest of Ramazani Shadary, Calls for Political De-escalation in the DRC
excerpt: Brussels, December 18, 2025 - Belgium has expressed strong disapproval over the arrest of Emmanuel Ramazani Shadary, Permanent Secretary of the People’s Party for Reconstruction and Democracy (PPRD) and former Minister…
title_en: Belgium Condemns Arrest of Ramazani Shadary, Calls for Political De-escalation in the DRC
excerpt_en: Brussels, December 18, 2025 - Belgium has expressed strong disapproval over the arrest of Emmanuel Ramazani Shadary, Permanent Secretary of the People’s Party for Reconstruction and Democracy (PPRD) and former Minister…
body_en:
Brussels, December 18, 2025 - Belgium has expressed strong disapproval over the arrest of Emmanuel Ramazani Shadary, Permanent Secretary of the People’s Party for Reconstruction and Democracy (PPRD) and former Minister of the Interior of the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Shadary was arrested on Tuesday, December 16, 2025, an action that Belgium says does not contribute to easing political tensions or supporting peace efforts, particularly in the eastern part of the country.

In a statement released on Thursday, December 18, Belgian Minister of Foreign Affairs Maxime Prévot urged the Congolese authorities to take concrete steps to reduce political tensions and encourage dialogue, in line with the Constitution and republican principles.

Belgium emphasized that political de-escalation is essential to allow Congolese political actors to honor international commitments, engage in meaningful dialogue, and contribute to the reforms necessary for stability, governance, and lasting peace in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

title: Kinshasa: Sacred Union Holds Peaceful Rally Demanding Rwandan Withdrawal and Enforcement of Resolution 2773
excerpt: Kinshasa, December 19, 2025 - The Sacred Union for the Nation (USN), the political coalition backing President Félix Tshisekedi, organized a peaceful demonstration in the Congolese capital on Friday, calling for the…
title_en: Kinshasa: Sacred Union Holds Peaceful Rally Demanding Rwandan Withdrawal and Enforcement of Resolution 2773
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, December 19, 2025 - The Sacred Union for the Nation (USN), the political coalition backing President Félix Tshisekedi, organized a peaceful demonstration in the Congolese capital on Friday, calling for the…
body_en:
Kinshasa, December 19, 2025 - The Sacred Union for the Nation (USN), the political coalition backing President Félix Tshisekedi, organized a peaceful demonstration in the Congolese capital on Friday, calling for the strict implementation of Resolution 2773.

The resolution urges Rwanda to withdraw from Congolese territory and to end all support for the AFC/M23 armed group. The march began at the Cohydro fuel station in Limete and proceeded to the People’s Palace, where demonstrators gathered without incident.

Addressing the crowd at the final stop, André Mbata, Permanent Secretary of the USN, reiterated the coalition’s demand for respect for international resolutions and the preservation of the Democratic Republic of Congo’s sovereignty.

Several political leaders took part in the rally, including Sylvain Mutombo and Déo Bizibu, alongside representatives of member parties of the Sacred Union. Throughout the march, demonstrators displayed the flags of the United States, which mediated the December 4, 2025 agreement in Washington, as well as flags representing parties within the USN platform.

The rally concluded peacefully, with organizers reaffirming their commitment to non-violence and diplomatic efforts aimed at restoring stability in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

title: DRC: United States Says AFC/M23 Withdrawal from Uvira Is Insufficient
excerpt: New York, December 19, 2025 - The United States has stated that the withdrawal announced by the AFC/M23 armed group from the city of Uvira, in South Kivu province, is insufficient, calling for a broader pullback in line…
title_en: DRC: United States Says AFC/M23 Withdrawal from Uvira Is Insufficient
excerpt_en: New York, December 19, 2025 - The United States has stated that the withdrawal announced by the AFC/M23 armed group from the city of Uvira, in South Kivu province, is insufficient, calling for a broader pullback in line…
body_en:
New York, December 19, 2025 - The United States has stated that the withdrawal announced by the AFC/M23 armed group from the city of Uvira, in South Kivu province, is insufficient, calling for a broader pullback in line with existing agreements.

Speaking during a United Nations Security Council meeting on Friday, the U.S. representative urged the Rwandan-backed rebel movement to withdraw at least 75 kilometers from Uvira, as stipulated in the framework agreement signed with the Congolese government.

The statement comes amid continued territorial expansion by the AFC/M23 in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, where the group is accused of establishing a parallel administration, heightening concerns in Kinshasa and among international partners.

Uvira, considered a strategic hub for the Congolese government’s security apparatus, remains a focal point of tensions. The worsening security situation in eastern DRC coincides with the ratification on November 15, 2025, of the Washington agreements, which were intended to consolidate the ceasefire between Kinshasa and Kigali.

title: DRC: Prime Minister Suminwa Urges Government Unity Amid Security Crisis
excerpt: Kinshasa, December 19, 2025 - During the 71st session of the Council of Ministers, held on Friday at the African Union City complex, Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka called on members of the government to…
title_en: DRC: Prime Minister Suminwa Urges Government Unity Amid Security Crisis
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, December 19, 2025 - During the 71st session of the Council of Ministers, held on Friday at the African Union City complex, Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka called on members of the government to…
body_en:
Kinshasa, December 19, 2025 - During the 71st session of the Council of Ministers, held on Friday at the African Union City complex, Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka called on members of the government to demonstrate cohesion, discipline, and collective commitment in responding to the country’s ongoing security and socio-economic challenges.

The Prime Minister pointed to the continued expansion of the AFC/M23 rebellion, backed by Rwanda, as a major threat to national stability. While acknowledging progress made in governance and political stability, she stressed that significant efforts remain necessary to improve the daily living conditions of the Congolese population.

Government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya announced that a comprehensive evaluation of government performance will be conducted in January 2026, covering the period from August to December 2025. The assessment aims to draw lessons from the past months and enhance the effectiveness of the current administration.

The Suminwa II government comprises 53 members, including 6 Deputy Prime Ministers, 12 Ministers of State, 24 Ministers, 5 Deputy Ministers, and 6 Under-Ministers.
body_fr:
Kinshasa, December 19, 2025 - During the 71st session of the Council of Ministers, held on Friday at the African Union City complex, Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka called on members of the government to demonstrate cohesion, discipline, and collective commitment in responding to the country’s ongoing security and socio-economic challenges.

The Prime Minister pointed to the continued expansion of the AFC/M23 rebellion, backed by Rwanda, as a major threat to national stability. While acknowledging progress made in governance and political stability, she stressed that significant efforts remain necessary to improve the daily living conditions of the Congolese population.

Government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya announced that a comprehensive evaluation of government performance will be conducted in January 2026, covering the period from August to December 2025. The assessment aims to draw lessons from the past months and enhance the effectiveness of the current administration.

The Suminwa II government comprises 53 members, including 6 Deputy Prime Ministers, 12 Ministers of State, 24 Ministers, 5 Deputy Ministers, and 6 Under-Ministers.

body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - December 18, 2025 - The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Interior and Security, Jacquemain Shabani Lukoo, has called on residents of Kinshasa to remain vigilant during the end-of-year festivities to prevent crime and urban banditry.

The warning follows an expanded meeting of the Provincial Security Committee, which brought together municipal authorities, local administrative officials, and security services to anticipate potential risks linked to the holiday influx of people and festive activities.

Minister Shabani emphasized that the initiative aligns with directives from the recent Council of Ministers, which instructed all 26 provinces to implement appropriate measures to ensure peaceful celebrations. Similar exercises are expected to be carried out across the country under the coordination of provincial governors.

Meanwhile, the UN Secretary-General called for an immediate and unconditional ceasefire, warning that the escalation could undermine peace efforts and increase the risk of regional conflict.

excerpt_en: Kinshasa - December 17, 2025 - The Congolese government has adopted a pragmatic and measurable roadmap to guide actions in the mining sector until 2026, following a seminar held from December 15 to 17 in Kinshasa…
body_en:
Kinshasa - December 17, 2025 - The Congolese government has adopted a pragmatic and measurable roadmap to guide actions in the mining sector until 2026, following a seminar held from December 15 to 17 in Kinshasa focused on operational strategies for the National Plan of Voluntary Principles.

At the closing ceremony, Minister of Human Rights Samuel Mbemba highlighted that the recommendations are now a key benchmark for effective implementation, stressing that the roadmap should be an operational tool rather than a mere administrative document.

Minister of Mines Louis Watum pledged to implement the resolutions across all extractive companies, aiming to promote responsible mining that respects human rights, protects the environment, and benefits local communities.

title_en: DRC National Assembly Holds Hearings Amid Worsening Security
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - December 17, 2025 - In response to the deteriorating security situation across the Democratic Republic of Congo, the National Assembly has launched a series of closed-door hearings with government and…
body_en:
Kinshasa - December 17, 2025 - In response to the deteriorating security situation across the Democratic Republic of Congo, the National Assembly has launched a series of closed-door hearings with government and security officials, in line with Article 43 of its rules of procedure.

On December 17, Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister Jacquemain Shabani was heard by the Defense and Security Committee, chaired by MP Rubens Mikindo. Lawmakers expressed deep concern over widespread insecurity, particularly in the eastern provinces, and sought to identify the root causes to formulate actionable proposals to restore peace and state authority.

The committee had previously heard from Minister of Defence Guy Kabongo Mwadianvita and announced that hearings with other security officials will continue in the coming days.

title: Belgium Urges Inclusive Political Process to Support Peace in Eastern DRC
excerpt: Kinshasa - December 17, 2025 - Belgian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Maxime Prévot has called on the Democratic Republic of Congo to complement regional peace and de-escalation efforts with an inclusive…
title_en: Belgium Urges Inclusive Political Process to Support Peace in Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - December 17, 2025 - Belgian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Maxime Prévot has called on the Democratic Republic of Congo to complement regional peace and de-escalation efforts with an inclusive…
body_en:
Kinshasa - December 17, 2025 - Belgian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Maxime Prévot has called on the Democratic Republic of Congo to complement regional peace and de-escalation efforts with an inclusive internal political process.

Prévot emphasized that Congolese actors, representing the country’s diverse political landscape, must take ownership of international commitments, translate them into tangible actions, and agree on key reforms, particularly in governance.

Reacting to the recent arrest of Emmanuel Shadary, Permanent Secretary of the PPRD, Prévot described the situation as concerning. He urged Kinshasa authorities to prioritize dialogue and political détente, respecting the Constitution and republican principles, and highlighted inclusion as a critical tool to ease political tensions and strengthen national unity amid ongoing security challenges in the eastern provinces.

title: DRC National Assembly Questions Mines Minister on Military Deployment at Mining Sites
excerpt: Kinshasa - December 18, 2025 - The National Assembly’s Defense and Security Committee summoned Minister of Mines Louis Watum Kabamba to answer questions regarding the deployment of military personnel at mining sites in…
title_en: DRC National Assembly Questions Mines Minister on Military Deployment at Mining Sites
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - December 18, 2025 - The National Assembly’s Defense and Security Committee summoned Minister of Mines Louis Watum Kabamba to answer questions regarding the deployment of military personnel at mining sites in…
body_en:
Kinshasa - December 18, 2025 - The National Assembly’s Defense and Security Committee summoned Minister of Mines Louis Watum Kabamba to answer questions regarding the deployment of military personnel at mining sites in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Parliamentarians expressed concern over the alleged involvement of some FARDC members in illegal mining activities, which they say contributes to ongoing insecurity in the eastern provinces.

Minister Watum requested an additional 48 hours to prepare comprehensive responses, highlighting the sensitivity of the issue.

The Committee also questioned Finance Minister Doudou Fwamba Likunde on the regularity of special bonuses for military personnel, especially amid the recent surge of violence in North Kivu and South Kivu.

According to Carly Nzanzu, the Commission’s first vice-president, all answers were provided in a closed session, and the conclusions will be transmitted to the plenary assembly. Hearings with other government members are expected to continue in the coming days.

title: DRC Government Condemns Goma Demonstration, Accuses AFC/M23 of Coercion
excerpt: Kinshasa - December 22, 2025 - The Congolese government has strongly condemned the massive demonstration in Goma earlier on Monday, accusing the AFC/M23 rebel coalition of forcing civilians to march under coercion and…
title_en: DRC Government Condemns Goma Demonstration, Accuses AFC/M23 of Coercion
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - December 22, 2025 - The Congolese government has strongly condemned the massive demonstration in Goma earlier on Monday, accusing the AFC/M23 rebel coalition of forcing civilians to march under coercion and…
body_en:
Kinshasa - December 22, 2025 - The Congolese government has strongly condemned the massive demonstration in Goma earlier on Monday, accusing the AFC/M23 rebel coalition of forcing civilians to march under coercion and threats of violence.

In an official statement, Patrick Muyaya, government spokesperson and Minister of Communication and Media, described the protest as a staged mobilization designed to conceal abuses perpetrated in territories under rebel control.

Muyaya alleged that civilians who refused to participate were subjected to whippings, forced labor, and other forms of intimidation, emphasizing that such methods highlight the lack of genuine popular support for the armed group.

“Forcing victims to take part in a demonstration organized by their oppressors will not change the infamous and internationally recognized image of torture and crime associated with the father, Rwanda, and the son, the M23,” Muyaya said.

He added that attempts to gain compliance through coercion demonstrate the unpopularity of the armed group and the illegitimacy of its authority in occupied areas.

The statement reaffirmed the government’s commitment to protect civilians and hold perpetrators accountable:

“No support is ever gained through coercion. This persistence in evil clearly demonstrates the total unpopularity of those who govern through crime. Whips and intimidation will never extinguish the flame of resistance and patriotism burning in the hearts of our compatriots.”

The condemnation comes amid heightened security and humanitarian concerns in North and South Kivu, following mass demonstrations in Goma and renewed clashes around Uvira. Analysts warn that continued violence, forced mobilizations, and coercive practices risk further destabilizing the region and exacerbating civilian suffering.

title: DRC Government Condemns Forced Civilian Marches in Eastern Provinces
excerpt: Kinshasa, 23 December 2025 - The Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo has strongly condemned the forced marches imposed on civilians in several eastern areas currently described as under Rwandan occupation.
title_en: DRC Government Condemns Forced Civilian Marches in Eastern Provinces
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, 23 December 2025 - The Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo has strongly condemned the forced marches imposed on civilians in several eastern areas currently described as under Rwandan occupation.
body_en:
Kinshasa, 23 December 2025 - The Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo has strongly condemned the forced marches imposed on civilians in several eastern areas currently described as under Rwandan occupation. According to the statement, these actions were allegedly carried out by AFC/M23 elements operating alongside the Rwandan Defence Forces (RDF) in Uvira on 16 December, Kamanyola on 19 December, Goma on 22 December, and Bukavu and Sake on 23 December.

The government denounces the coercion of civilians, including women and youth, into staged demonstrations as a violation of human rights and international law, describing the acts as political and psychological manipulation of local communities. Officials emphasized that using civilians as human shields or instruments of propaganda constitutes a grave attack on national sovereignty and human dignity.

Authorities reaffirmed their determination to protect civilian populations, restore state authority across the national territory, and hold accountable the perpetrators and sponsors of these violations. The government also commended the courage of civilians resisting manipulation and called on all Congolese citizens to remain vigilant, united, and confident in the national institutions and the Armed Forces.

Finally, Kinshasa reiterated its unwavering support for ongoing peace processes aimed at achieving lasting peace, stability, and development in the eastern DRC and the Great Lakes region.

title: Tshopo Provincial Assembly Rejects Request to Lift President’s Immunity
excerpt: Kisangani, Tshopo Province, DRC - Saturday, December 27, 2025
title_en: Tshopo Provincial Assembly Rejects Request to Lift President’s Immunity
excerpt_en: Kisangani, Tshopo Province, DRC - Saturday, December 27, 2025
body_en:
Kisangani, Tshopo Province, DRC - Saturday, December 27, 2025

The Tshopo Provincial Assembly rejected the request to lift the immunity of its president, Mattheus Kanga. The request, submitted by the Attorney General to the Court of Cassation, sought authorization to investigate the case against him.

Two individuals had filed complaints, accusing the president of embezzling US$200 received from FRIVAO for the renovation or construction of the offices of the main provincial political institution.

The rejection followed a plenary session in which members voted on the conclusions of an ad hoc committee tasked with examining the Attorney General’s request. The Attorney General to the Court of Cassation was represented at the session by the Attorney General to the Kisangani Court of Appeal.

During the session, Albert Lussumbe explained the circumstances prompting the request, noting that the whistleblower alleged the funds were shared among members of parliament, which led to the Attorney General’s audit request.

In response, members of the commission and several members of parliament highlighted the lack of material evidence supporting the accusations against the President.

“Regarding the work we are doing here at the Provincial Assembly with FRIVAO funds, you are accusing us of embezzlement. That is false, completely false,” he insisted.

title: Tshisekedi Rejects Claims of AFC/M23 Withdrawal from Uvira
excerpt: Kampala/Kinshasa - December 19, 2025
title_en: Tshisekedi Rejects Claims of AFC/M23 Withdrawal from Uvira
excerpt_en: Kampala/Kinshasa - December 19, 2025
body_en:
Kampala/Kinshasa - December 19, 2025

President Félix Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has once again dismissed reports that AFC/M23 forces have withdrawn from the city of Uvira, insisting that armed elements remain present despite announcements to the contrary.

Speaking via video conference during a special regional meeting convened by Ugandan President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni to address insecurity in eastern DRC, Tshisekedi said available information contradicts claims of a completed withdrawal.

“Reports of the withdrawal of AFC/M23 from Uvira do not correspond to the truth or to what has been observed,” Tshisekedi stated. “The information we have indicates that armed forces are still present in the city and its surroundings, and the population continues to suffer the consequences of their actions.”

The Congolese leader argued that any declaration of withdrawal must be concrete, verifiable, and monitored, followed by the effective restoration of state authority.

“A withdrawal that is not implemented in practice, not monitored, and not followed by the establishment of government authority cannot be considered a real withdrawal,” he said.

Tshisekedi stressed that progress toward peace depends on tangible actions, not temporary or tactical moves.

“What we are waiting for is not a redeployment or a tactical withdrawal,” he added. “We want all troops on the territory of the Democratic Republic of the Congo to withdraw completely, in accordance with existing agreements and decisions.”

The President also reaffirmed the DRC’s support for the renewed mandate of MONUSCO, emphasizing that the protection of civilians remains the top priority. He said the government would continue to take strong and effective measures, including maintaining special forces and the capacity to conduct targeted operations against armed groups.

Tshisekedi’s remarks came despite an earlier announcement that AFC/M23 had withdrawn from Uvira on December 18, 2025. The group had captured the city on December 10, forcing out Burundian troops, the FARDC, and allied groups including Wazalendo.

The seizure of Uvira triggered heightened international pressure, with European countries, the United States, and international organizations condemning the offensive. AFC/M23, which says it is fighting for the rights of Mulenge and Tutsi communities in eastern DRC, stated on December 16 that it had agreed to vacate the city at the request of the United States, while calling for measures to ensure the protection of civilians.

He said the government would continue to take strong and effective measures, including maintaining special forces and the capacity to conduct targeted operations against armed groups.

Tshisekedi’s remarks came despite an earlier announcement that AFC/M23 had withdrawn from Uvira on December 18, 2025. The group had captured the city on December 10, forcing out Burundian troops, the FARDC, and allied groups including Wazalendo.

The seizure of Uvira triggered heightened international pressure, with European countries, the United States, and international organizations condemning the offensive. AFC/M23, which says it is fighting for the rights of Mulenge and Tutsi communities in eastern DRC, stated on December 16 that it had agreed to vacate the city at the request of the United States, while calling for measures to ensure the protection of civilians.

title: Bukavu-Uvira Road Reopens After Ten Months

title_en: Bukavu-Uvira Road Reopens After Ten Months
excerpt_en: South Kivu, DRC - December 17, 2025 - Road transport between Bukavu and Uvira resumed today after a ten-month suspension caused by clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and the FARDC in the Ruzizi Plain, including Luvungi…
body_en:
South Kivu, DRC - December 17, 2025 - Road transport between Bukavu and Uvira resumed today after a ten-month suspension caused by clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and the FARDC in the Ruzizi Plain, including Luvungi, Katogota, Bwegera, and Sange.

The reopening of National Route 5 now allows travelers to complete the journey in four hours, avoiding the long detour through Burundi, Tanzania, and Rwanda that was necessary during the conflict.

The first bus, operated by El Shadai, arrived in Bukavu, carrying passengers eager to return after months of displacement. Witnesses reported that the journey was largely smooth, with only voter card checks at a few checkpoints, and the fare set at 300,000 FCF per person via Ngomu.

title: Rawbank and Visa Extend Five-Year Strategic Partnership in the DRC
excerpt: Kinshasa, December 15, 2025 - Rawbank and Visa have renewed their strategic partnership for an additional five years, reinforcing their commitment to the modernization of payment systems and the digitization of…
title_en: Rawbank and Visa Extend Five-Year Strategic Partnership in the DRC
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, December 15, 2025 - Rawbank and Visa have renewed their strategic partnership for an additional five years, reinforcing their commitment to the modernization of payment systems and the digitization of…
body_en:
Kinshasa, December 15, 2025 - Rawbank and Visa have renewed their strategic partnership for an additional five years, reinforcing their commitment to the modernization of payment systems and the digitization of financial services in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Launched more than 15 years ago, the partnership has played a key role in expanding electronic payments, supporting e-commerce, widening the merchant network, and promoting digital payment awareness, including through campaigns linked to major international sporting events between 2022 and 2025.

Under the renewed agreement, Rawbank and Visa will prioritize payment tokenization, the development of tailored solutions for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), cross-border payment services, and the promotion of financial inclusion. Special emphasis will be placed on youth, women, and entrepreneurs, through initiatives such as the Visa Academia Card and virtual payment cards.

Rawbank Chief Executive Officer Mustafa Rawji and Sophie Kafuti, Chief Executive Officer of Visa in the DRC, said the renewed partnership strengthens their shared ambition to support the country’s transition toward a formal, inclusive, and fully digital economy.

title: IMF Releases $445 Million to Support the Congolese Economy
excerpt: Kinshasa, December 19, 2025 - The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has approved the immediate disbursement of $445 million to the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), following the successful completion of the second…
title_en: IMF Releases $445 Million to Support the Congolese Economy
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, December 19, 2025 - The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has approved the immediate disbursement of $445 million to the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), following the successful completion of the second…
body_en:
Kinshasa, December 19, 2025 - The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has approved the immediate disbursement of $445 million to the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), following the successful completion of the second review of the Extended Credit Facility (ECF) and the first review of the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF).

With this latest release, total IMF support to the DRC now stands at 570.9 million Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) under the ECF and 133.25 million SDRs under the resilience-focused financing mechanism.

Despite ongoing armed conflict in the eastern part of the country, the IMF notes that the Congolese economy remains resilient. Real GDP growth is projected to exceed 5 percent in both 2025 and 2026, while inflation has dropped sharply, from 11.7 percent at the end of 2024 to 2.2 percent in November 2025.

In early October 2025, the Central Bank of Congo reduced its key policy rate from 25 percent to 17.5 percent, reflecting improved macroeconomic stability.

The IMF confirmed that all performance criteria were met, with the exception of one related to multiple exchange rate practices, which has since been discontinued.

Going forward, the Fund has urged the Congolese authorities to maintain fiscal discipline, strengthen coordination between fiscal and monetary policy, continue structural reforms, and ensure adequate social spending to respond to the country’s ongoing humanitarian challenges.

title: DRC Strengthens Electricity Sector Governance with New Protocol
excerpt: Kinshasa - December 18, 2025 - The Congolese government signed a key memorandum of understanding aimed at improving transparency and regulation in the electricity sector.
title_en: DRC Strengthens Electricity Sector Governance with New Protocol
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - December 18, 2025 - The Congolese government signed a key memorandum of understanding aimed at improving transparency and regulation in the electricity sector.
body_en:
Kinshasa - December 18, 2025 - The Congolese government signed a key memorandum of understanding aimed at improving transparency and regulation in the electricity sector. The agreement focuses on the declaration, collection, and monitoring of electricity charges for medium- and high-voltage consumers.

The protocol was signed by the General Secretariat for Water Resources, the DGRAD (Directorate General of Administrative and Fiscal Revenue), the ANSER (National Agency of Electricity and Drinking Water), and SNEL (National Electricity Company).

According to Minister of Water Resources Aimé Molendo Sakombi, the collaboration ensures that electricity billing becomes more legal, predictable, and equitable, while supporting the financing of rural electrification projects.

The agreement is seen as a strategic step to improve governance and efficiency in the energy sector, with the government emphasizing its commitment to maximizing public resources and accelerating the country’s energy transition.

title: Congo Airways Receives New Aircraft, Marks Resumption of Operations
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - Wednesday, December 24, 2025
title_en: Congo Airways Receives New Aircraft, Marks Resumption of Operations
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - Wednesday, December 24, 2025
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - Wednesday, December 24, 2025

Congo Airways, the national airline, received a new Embraer E-190 aircraft with a capacity of 90 passengers at N’djili International Airport. The ceremony was presided over by Jean-Bertrand Ewanga, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the state-owned company.

The aircraft was acquired through a partnership between Congo Airways and the National Social Security Fund (CNSS). According to company officials, this acquisition marks the resumption of operations, which had been suspended since April 12, 2025.

Ewanga paid tribute to President Félix Tshisekedi, highlighting his support for the security situation in the country’s East and his role in ensuring Congo Airways contributes to national unity.

Operations had been halted due to the expiration of wet-lease contracts with KlasJet, along with technical issues, lack of engines, and insufficient maintenance. In September 2024, IATA and the DRC Civil Aviation Authority granted a 90-day moratorium to preserve the airline’s Air Operator Certificate (AOC) and IATA accreditation, allowing some aircraft to return to service.

The new CEO, Alexandre Tshikala Mukendi, appointed by presidential decree on January 16, 2025, is tasked with turning the company around. The recovery plan, presented in January 2025, includes acquiring three Airbus A320s over five years, reorganizing governance, securing government support, and mobilizing financial resources via the CNSS and the government.

title: Mining Traders Protest Suspension of Artisanal Copper and Cobalt Mining in Lualaba
excerpt: Kolwezi, Lualaba, DRC - December 19, 2025
title_en: Mining Traders Protest Suspension of Artisanal Copper and Cobalt Mining in Lualaba
excerpt_en: Kolwezi, Lualaba, DRC - December 19, 2025
body_en:
Kolwezi, Lualaba, DRC - December 19, 2025

Mining traders in Lualaba are protesting the suspension of artisanal copper and cobalt mining. The national Minister of Mines, Louis Watum Kabamba, issued a decree on December 19 suspending mining activities and the marketing of mineral substances from artisanal mining throughout the Democratic Republic of Congo.

The decision has sparked serious concerns among stakeholders in the artisanal mining sector, particularly in Kolwezi. Mutra Mutunda, provincial president of the Network of Mining Traders of Congo (RENEMICO), is advocating for the lifting of the suspension, warning that the abrupt halt affects thousands of families and could lead to social unrest.

“If the artisanal miners stop working, there will be social unrest. We are facing a complicated situation; we don't know what to do,” Mutunda said. On the day the ministerial decree was published, operations at the quarries ceased, all services stopped functioning, and even the traders halted activities.

To ease the situation, the Minister of Mines promised the creation of 64 Artisanal Mining Zones (AZEs) in Lualaba province, with the allocation process already underway. The suspension aims to end illegal transactions and prevent clandestine miners from encroaching on authorized mining areas.

title: Goma Residents Protest AFC/M23 Withdrawal from Uvira, Demand Lasting Peace
excerpt: Goma, DRC - December 22, 2025
title_en: Goma Residents Protest AFC/M23 Withdrawal from Uvira, Demand Lasting Peace
excerpt_en: Goma, DRC - December 22, 2025
body_en:
Goma, DRC - December 22, 2025

Residents of Goma and surrounding areas in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) staged protests on the morning of December 22, 2025, in response to the recent withdrawal of AFC/M23 fighters from Uvira. The demonstrators carried messages calling for lasting peace and expressing opposition to the return of government and allied forces to the city.

“Residents of Goma and neighboring areas, we refuse to withdraw from Uvira to AFC/M23. We refuse to allow FARDC, Wazalendo, Burundian troops and mercenaries to return to Uvira.”

The protesters voiced frustration over the ongoing conflict in eastern DRC and urged immediate dialogue to resolve the fighting.

The demonstrations followed the AFC/M23 withdrawal from Uvira on December 17-18, after the group had controlled the city for a week. The withdrawal was reportedly made at the request of the United States as a confidence-building measure ahead of continuing peace negotiations with the DRC government.

AFC/M23 has publicly stated that it does not want DRC, Burundian, Wazalendo, or FDLR forces to return to Uvira, urging the United States and other international partners to establish security guarantees for the civilian population. The group emphasized that neutral or non-military control of Uvira would allow residents to resume daily life safely, without fear of abuses experienced under previous government operations.

The US Special Representative for Political Affairs at the United Nations, Ambassador Jennifer Locetta, indicated that AFC/M23’s request could be feasible if the group relocates to areas within 75 kilometers of Uvira, enabling them to return later to areas previously held before the fighting in early December, including the Kamanyola center.
