title: DRC: 65 Schools Closed in Kwilu Province Amid Rising Insecurity
excerpt: KWILU, Democratic Republic of Congo - December 27, 2025 - At least 65 schools in Kwilu Province, in the southwest of the Democratic Republic of Congo, have been forced to close due to worsening insecurity, local…
title_en: DRC: 65 Schools Closed in Kwilu Province Amid Rising Insecurity
excerpt_en: KWILU, Democratic Republic of Congo - December 27, 2025 - At least 65 schools in Kwilu Province, in the southwest of the Democratic Republic of Congo, have been forced to close due to worsening insecurity, local…
body_en:
KWILU, Democratic Republic of Congo - December 27, 2025 - At least 65 schools in Kwilu Province, in the southwest of the Democratic Republic of Congo, have been forced to close due to worsening insecurity, local education authorities have confirmed.

The closures include 48 primary schools and 17 secondary schools, all located in Bagata Territory. Most of the affected schools were reportedly burned by the Mobondo armed group, which has been carrying out violent attacks against civilians in western DRC for the past three years.

The violence has displaced large numbers of residents, forcing families to flee to Bandundu, the provincial capital, as well as other safer areas. Displaced students from the closed schools are now being relocated to Bandundu and neighboring regions.

The Director of Education in Kwilu Province, Hervé Mungera, announced that students from Bagata Territory will be allowed to continue their studies and sit for examinations free of charge, as part of emergency measures to support them.

“Some of the students are also being assisted with food,” Mungera said. “Most of them come from Wamba Sector and are now in Bandundu. Thousands of children would normally be studying in the city.”

Despite efforts by provincial authorities, Mungera acknowledged that many displaced children continue to face serious challenges, including food shortages and lack of adequate shelter.

Meanwhile, the Congolese government has intensified security measures in and around Kinshasa, particularly in areas such as Maluku and Kingakati, following the spread of Mobondo attacks closer to the capital.

While authorities say progress has been made in containing the armed group near Kinshasa, the situation in Kwilu Province remains dire, with ongoing killings, displacement, and persistent insecurity forcing families to flee in search of safety.

title: South Kivu: Bukavu-Bunyakiri Road Closure Halts Vaccine Distribution
excerpt: South Kivu - December 2025 - Health zones in Kalonge, Bunyakiri, and Bulungu are experiencing a shortage of polio vaccines due to the closure of the Bukavu-Bunyakiri road, which has been blocked for nearly 30 days amid…
title_en: South Kivu: Bukavu-Bunyakiri Road Closure Halts Vaccine Distribution
excerpt_en: South Kivu - December 2025 - Health zones in Kalonge, Bunyakiri, and Bulungu are experiencing a shortage of polio vaccines due to the closure of the Bukavu-Bunyakiri road, which has been blocked for nearly 30 days amid…
body_en:
South Kivu - December 2025 - Health zones in Kalonge, Bunyakiri, and Bulungu are experiencing a shortage of polio vaccines due to the closure of the Bukavu-Bunyakiri road, which has been blocked for nearly 30 days amid ongoing clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and the FARDC.

The road closure has made it impossible for vehicles to deliver vaccine doses, leaving thousands of children without immunization. Local medical authorities warn that the disruption is also causing food shortages, further worsening the health and nutritional vulnerability of the population.

Health officials are calling on both armed parties to allow safe passage for civilians and humanitarian aid, emphasizing the urgent need to prevent a growing public health crisis.

title: Bukavu Erupts as March in Support of Uvira Turns Violent
excerpt: Bukavu, South Kivu - December 23, 2025 - A large-scale march that began early this morning in Bukavu to show solidarity with the population of Uvira and oppose the withdrawal of AFC/M23 forces quickly degenerated into…
title_en: Bukavu Erupts as March in Support of Uvira Turns Violent
excerpt_en: Bukavu, South Kivu - December 23, 2025 - A large-scale march that began early this morning in Bukavu to show solidarity with the population of Uvira and oppose the withdrawal of AFC/M23 forces quickly degenerated into…
body_en:
Bukavu, South Kivu - December 23, 2025 - A large-scale march that began early this morning in Bukavu to show solidarity with the population of Uvira and oppose the withdrawal of AFC/M23 forces quickly degenerated into chaos, leaving residents in panic.

According to eyewitnesses, the march initially proceeded in an organized manner along the city streets. However, tensions escalated as gunfire erupted, causing demonstrators to scatter in fear. Preliminary reports indicate that the shots may have come from Wazalendo elements, who reportedly entered the city firing live ammunition and explosive projectiles.

Heavy shooting reportedly spread to multiple neighborhoods, including Panzi, where an explosive projectile struck a residential home. While human casualties have been reported, authorities have not yet provided official figures.

The march revealed sharp divisions within the population. Some participants openly opposed the AFC/M23, chanting hostile slogans, while others expressed support, calling for the movement to continue advancing toward Kinshasa. This polarization reflected the complex and fragmented local sentiment over the ongoing conflict in eastern DRC.

By late morning, Bukavu was largely paralyzed, with residents fleeing the streets and uncertainty prevailing over the security response. Observers warn that the situation remains extremely volatile, with a significant risk of further violence and unrest.

Authorities and humanitarian organizations have yet to release statements or deploy interventions, leaving the city on edge as the situation develops.

Rutshuru, North Kivu - December 23, 2025 - Thousands of residents took to the streets of Kiwanja on Tuesday in a peaceful demonstration expressing support for the AFC/M23 coalition and rejecting the government of President Félix Tshisekedi.

Organized primarily by local women’s groups, the marchers called for peace and stability, emphasizing the need for careful coordination regarding any withdrawal of AFC/M23 forces from Uvira. Participants warned that an unplanned pullback could spark renewed insecurity and result in loss of life.

Demonstrators later submitted a memorandum to MONUSCO, urging inclusive dialogue and stressing that security should take precedence over political disputes.

The protest highlights deepening divisions in eastern DRC, where control of key territories continues to shift amid ongoing military, political, and humanitarian challenges.

title: Women Leaders Engage Authorities on Dialogue and Governance in Goma

title_en: Women Leaders Engage Authorities on Dialogue and Governance in Goma
excerpt_en: Goma, North Kivu, DRC - December 26, 2025
body_en:
Goma, North Kivu, DRC - December 26, 2025

Corneille Nangaa and Bertrand Bisimwa on Friday received a broad delegation of women leaders from across North Kivu in Goma, including entrepreneurs, traders, customs officers, and political actors, in a meeting focused on dialogue and governance.

The delegation praised improved security in Goma and surrounding areas, citing freer movement and a revival of economic activity. They also expressed satisfaction with socio-economic governance and submitted a memorandum of support for the AFC/M23.

Nangaa acknowledged the recommendations and pledged sector-by-sector solutions starting January 5, emphasizing that women’s stability and empowerment are central to their vision for the DR Congo.

title: The population of Kirumba, in the southern part of Lubero territory, held a demonstration to
excerpt: The population of Kirumba, in the southern part of Lubero territory, held a demonstration to protest atrocities committed by ADF rebels against civilians in the Bapere sector.
title_en: The population of Kirumba, in the southern part of Lubero territory, held a demonstration to
excerpt_en: The population of Kirumba, in the southern part of Lubero territory, held a demonstration to protest atrocities committed by ADF rebels against civilians in the Bapere sector.
body_en:
The population of Kirumba, in the southern part of Lubero territory, held a demonstration to protest atrocities committed by ADF rebels against civilians in the Bapere sector.

“For ten years, the population has been massacred by the ADF, but Kinshasa has never provided a solution,” lamented Samy Saa Kumi, president of the local civil society.

The demonstration aimed to urge the national and international community to take action to restore peace in areas threatened by the ADF. “We want the inhabitants of Beni and Bapere to regain security and live in peace,” Kumi said, emphasizing the need for liberation after years of loss.

This protest comes nine days after the publication of the Kivu Security Barometer, a project of the Ebuteli Research Institute, which recorded 226 security incidents in eastern DRC in November 2025. The report highlighted a sharp increase in civilian deaths, with 289 fatalities compared to 205 the previous month.

According to the Barometer, Lubero territory, particularly the Bapere sector and the Baswagha chiefdom, became the epicenter of violence in November, with 121 civilians, including 22 women, killed during the period under review.

Despite limited media coverage, the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) remain the deadliest armed group in eastern DRC. Also active in Ituri, in the territories of Mambasa and Irumu, the ADF target bases of Operation Shujaa, impose taxes on local populations, and promote conversion to Islam, notably during a meeting held on November 5 in the village of Elake in Mambasa territory.

title: DRC Military Court Tries 124 Soldiers and Police Officers for Alleged Desertion After Uvira’s Fall
excerpt: Kalemie, DRC - December 19, 2025
title_en: DRC Military Court Tries 124 Soldiers and Police Officers for Alleged Desertion After Uvira’s Fall
excerpt_en: Kalemie, DRC - December 19, 2025
body_en:
Kalemie, DRC - December 19, 2025

The Kalemie Military Court on Friday opened proceedings against 124 soldiers and police officers accused of desertion following the capture of Uvira by the AFC/M23 coalition.

According to court documents, the defendants are charged with abandoning their posts during fighting that led to the takeover of the city. The group comprises 68 members of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC) and 56 police officers, with 66 defendants already formally identified.

Military prosecutors allege that, as AFC/M23 forces advanced, elements of the FARDC, allied Wazalendo, the national police, and Burundian troops engaged in combat, after which some security personnel withdrew or fled. Several crossed into Burundi, while others moved toward areas not under AFC/M23 control, including Kalemie.

Those who arrived in Kalemie were arrested and brought before the military court to answer charges related to desertion and misconduct.

Presiding judge Lt. Col. Désiré Dionda Mukolee, President of the Kalemie Military Court, said the trial seeks to sanction failures within the security forces, citing weaknesses and disregard for command guidance that he said contributed to repeated AFC/M23 advances.

“This process is intended to restore discipline, order, and proper conduct within the military and security services,” Lt. Col. Mukolee stated, adding that accountability measures are necessary to “put things in order.”

The military prosecution further argued that the actions attributed to the accused violated military law and professional codes governing the conduct of soldiers and police officers.

The case unfolds amid heightened scrutiny of the DRC’s security response in eastern provinces, where renewed fighting has placed sustained pressure on government forces and civilian populations.

title: Roger Lumbala Sentenced to 30 Years in Prison: Key Milestones in the Trial
excerpt: Paris, December 15, 2025 - Former Congolese rebel leader and ex-minister Roger Lumbala has been sentenced to 30 years in prison by the Paris Assize Court for complicity in crimes against humanity.
title_en: Roger Lumbala Sentenced to 30 Years in Prison: Key Milestones in the Trial
excerpt_en: Paris, December 15, 2025 - Former Congolese rebel leader and ex-minister Roger Lumbala has been sentenced to 30 years in prison by the Paris Assize Court for complicity in crimes against humanity.
body_en:
Paris, December 15, 2025 - Former Congolese rebel leader and ex-minister Roger Lumbala has been sentenced to 30 years in prison by the Paris Assize Court for complicity in crimes against humanity.

The ruling brings to an end more than two decades of impunity for atrocities committed between 2002 and 2003 in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, particularly during the military operation known as “Erase the Board.”

The trial opened on November 12, 2025, in Paris, following Lumbala’s arrest in France, where he was detained in 2020 and formally charged in 2023 under the principle of universal jurisdiction, which allows national courts to prosecute the most serious international crimes regardless of where they were committed.

After five weeks of hearings, the verdict was delivered late in the afternoon. The accused was summoned to the courtroom before being escorted to the dock for the reading of the judgment.

Roger Lumbala has ten days to file an appeal. A separate civil hearing to determine damages for victims has been scheduled for June 30, 2026.

title: Constitutional Court Rejects Constant Mutamba’s Appeal
excerpt: Kinshasa, December 19, 2025 - The Constitutional Court on Friday rejected an appeal filed by Constant Mutamba, upholding a preliminary ruling issued by the Court of Cassation that found his objections admissible but…
title_en: Constitutional Court Rejects Constant Mutamba’s Appeal
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, December 19, 2025 - The Constitutional Court on Friday rejected an appeal filed by Constant Mutamba, upholding a preliminary ruling issued by the Court of Cassation that found his objections admissible but…
body_en:
Kinshasa, December 19, 2025 - The Constitutional Court on Friday rejected an appeal filed by Constant Mutamba, upholding a preliminary ruling issued by the Court of Cassation that found his objections admissible but unfounded.

Mutamba, who was prosecuted for the embezzlement of public funds earmarked for the construction of a prison in Kisangani, had challenged the legality of the parliamentary vote that authorized his indictment.

After examining the appeal, the Constitutional Court dismissed his arguments, thereby confirming the lower court’s decision. As a result, Constant Mutamba was sentenced to three years in prison.

The ruling brings legal clarity to a case that has drawn significant public attention due to its implications for public accountability and the management of state funds.

title: DRC Constitutional Court Rejects Former Justice Minister Constant Mutamba’s Petitions
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - December 19, 2025 - The Constitutional Court of the Democratic Republic of the Congo on Friday dismissed two petitions filed by former Justice Minister Constant Mutamba, ruling them admissible but…
title_en: DRC Constitutional Court Rejects Former Justice Minister Constant Mutamba’s Petitions
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - December 19, 2025 - The Constitutional Court of the Democratic Republic of the Congo on Friday dismissed two petitions filed by former Justice Minister Constant Mutamba, ruling them admissible but…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - December 19, 2025 - The Constitutional Court of the Democratic Republic of the Congo on Friday dismissed two petitions filed by former Justice Minister Constant Mutamba, ruling them admissible but unfounded.

The court rejected Mutamba’s challenges against National Assembly resolutions that authorized his judicial investigation and prosecution, as well as his appeal of a pretrial ruling by the Court of Cassation. Judges found no serious constitutional violations in either case.

Mutamba had argued that the parliamentary resolutions violated procedural guarantees and separation of powers, and that the Cassation Court infringed on constitutional provisions regarding rule of law, equality before the law, fair trial rights, and judicial independence. All claims were dismissed on their merits.

This ruling follows the September 2, 2025, decision of the Court of Cassation, which sentenced Mutamba to three years of forced labor for embezzlement of $19 million in public funds. He was also barred from holding public office or standing for election for five years.

title: Shelling reported in Mikenke, Uvira, after AFC/M23 announces withdrawal
excerpt: Heavy bombardments were reported early Friday morning in Mikenke, a locality in Uvira territory, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, despite the AFC/M23’s earlier announcement that it had withdrawn from Uvira.
title_en: Shelling reported in Mikenke, Uvira, after AFC/M23 announces withdrawal
excerpt_en: Heavy bombardments were reported early Friday morning in Mikenke, a locality in Uvira territory, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, despite the AFC/M23’s earlier announcement that it had withdrawn from Uvira.
body_en:
Heavy bombardments were reported early Friday morning in Mikenke, a locality in Uvira territory, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, despite the AFC/M23’s earlier announcement that it had withdrawn from Uvira.

According to Bertrand Bisimwa, President of the M23 and Deputy Coordinator of the AFC/M23, shelling began at 6:38 a.m. on December 19, 2025. He accused forces allied to the Kinshasa government-namely the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC), Wazalendo militias, and the Burundian army-of carrying out the attacks.

The reported bombardments come at a time when the AFC/M23 maintains that it no longer exercises military control over Uvira, raising questions about the current security dynamics in the area.

There was no immediate independent confirmation of the shelling, and no information was available on casualties or damage. Congolese and Burundian authorities had not commented at the time of publication.

title: AFC/M23 Declares Unilateral Ceasefire Amid Ongoing Attacks by Kinshasa Forces
excerpt: Kinshasa, DR Congo - December 19, 2025 - The Congo River Alliance (AFC/M23) announced a unilateral ceasefire on Friday, citing a spirit of responsibility and a desire to provide a genuine opportunity for the restoration…
title_en: AFC/M23 Declares Unilateral Ceasefire Amid Ongoing Attacks by Kinshasa Forces
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DR Congo - December 19, 2025 - The Congo River Alliance (AFC/M23) announced a unilateral ceasefire on Friday, citing a spirit of responsibility and a desire to provide a genuine opportunity for the restoration…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DR Congo - December 19, 2025 - The Congo River Alliance (AFC/M23) announced a unilateral ceasefire on Friday, citing a spirit of responsibility and a desire to provide a genuine opportunity for the restoration of peace in eastern DR Congo.

However, the coalition accused the Kinshasa regime of continuing what it described as a campaign of systematic attacks against civilians and AFC/M23 positions, in clear violation of prior commitments.

According to AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, coalition forces from the Kinshasa government targeted populated areas with kamikaze drones, naval artillery, and heavy weapons, escalating violence despite the ceasefire.

“Starting at 5:00 a.m., coalition forces launched attacks using kamikaze drones and naval forces, striking densely populated areas and our positions in Makobola, near Baraka. At 5:30 a.m., the same forces targeted Minembwe with drones and heavy artillery, spreading terror among civilians,” Kanyuka said.

The spokesperson called on Congolese citizens and international partners to bear witness to what AFC/M23 characterized as repeated and deliberate violations of the ceasefire, highlighting the continued massacres of civilians.

“These acts unequivocally demonstrate that the Kinshasa regime seeks neither peace nor the protection of civilians, but persists in maintaining violence and impunity,” Kanyuka added.

The statement underscores the fragile security situation in eastern DR Congo, where attempts at ceasefire and diplomacy remain under severe strain due to ongoing clashes between government forces and rebel groups.

title: Cholera and Hunger Claim Lives of Dozens of Congolese Refugees in Burundi
excerpt: More than 40 Congolese refugees who fled renewed fighting in South Kivu province, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), have died in the Gatumba makeshift camp in Burundi, according to local Congolese officials.
title_en: Cholera and Hunger Claim Lives of Dozens of Congolese Refugees in Burundi
excerpt_en: More than 40 Congolese refugees who fled renewed fighting in South Kivu province, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), have died in the Gatumba makeshift camp in Burundi, according to local Congolese officials.
body_en:
More than 40 Congolese refugees who fled renewed fighting in South Kivu province, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), have died in the Gatumba makeshift camp in Burundi, according to local Congolese officials.

On December 18, 2025, Kifara Kapenda, the Vice Mayor of Uvira and himself among the refugees in Burundi, told Congolese nationals living in the country that the deaths were caused by cholera, exacerbated by pollution and hunger.

Speaking to Radio Okapi, Kapenda said that eight people died on December 18 alone, while five others died the previous day. “In total, in just 10 days, more than 40 people have died due to cholera and hunger,” he stated.

Kapenda explained that the Gatumba temporary camp alone is hosting approximately 30,000 Congolese refugees, a situation he described as critical. He appealed to the DRC government and humanitarian organizations to urgently intervene to prevent further loss of life.

The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) reported that between December 5 and 16, more than 82,000 Congolese refugees crossed into Burundi, fleeing violence in areas including Kamanyola, Luvungi, Katogota, and the city of Uvira.

According to UNHCR, the refugees are currently sheltering in temporary camps near the border, notably Kansega, Gatumba, Cishemere, Makombe, Vugizo, Rumonge, and Magara. The Burundian government has acknowledged that the number of refugees hosted in these camps has far exceeded their capacity, raising concerns over worsening humanitarian and health conditions.

title: Burundi: Congolese Refugees Seeking to Return Home Allegedly Beaten and Killed
excerpt: Gatumba/Bujumbura - December 21, 2025
title_en: Burundi: Congolese Refugees Seeking to Return Home Allegedly Beaten and Killed
excerpt_en: Gatumba/Bujumbura - December 21, 2025
body_en:
Gatumba/Bujumbura - December 21, 2025

The AFC/M23 coalition, which is fighting the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) government, has accused Burundian security forces of beating and killing Congolese refugees attempting to return home from Burundi, as a severe humanitarian crisis continues to unfold along the border.

The allegations come as the Burundian government says it can no longer adequately care for the growing influx of refugees fleeing violence in eastern DRC, particularly from Uvira, Katogota, Sange, Kiliba, Luvungi, and Kamanyola. Authorities have appealed to international partners for urgent assistance, estimating a funding shortfall of 33 million US dollars.

Refugees describe extremely harsh living conditions in Burundi, marked by acute food shortages, high prices, and poor sanitation.

One refugee, Ajax Ramadhani, described the situation as increasingly unbearable, citing the sharp rise in food prices and the lack of income opportunities for displaced people.

“We did not come here because we were happy, but because we had no choice. Life here is very difficult, and people assume refugees have money, which is not true,” he said.

At the Gatumba makeshift camp, near the DRC border, refugees are reportedly dying from hunger and cholera, a disease linked to unsafe water and inadequate sanitation.

title: AFC/M23 Fighters Deploy Warships in South Kivu Combat
excerpt: South Kivu, DRC - December 21-22, 2025
title_en: AFC/M23 Fighters Deploy Warships in South Kivu Combat
excerpt_en: South Kivu, DRC - December 21-22, 2025
body_en:
South Kivu, DRC - December 21-22, 2025

AFC/M23 fighters operating in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo have begun using warships in combat, marking a new escalation in the ongoing conflict in South Kivu Province.

On December 21, government and allied forces launched a major attack on AFC/M23 positions in Bangwi, Fizi territory, aiming to recapture territory. The offensive was repelled, prompting residents to flee to safer areas such as Swima and Mboko.

The following day, DRC and Wazalendo forces attacked the Makabola center, held by AFC/M23 for nearly two weeks. In response, AFC/M23 deployed a warship on Lake Tanganyika, firing on attacking forces and forcing them to retreat.

“After these shells, we saw FARDC soldiers leaving the battlefield and heading towards Mboko. This situation caused panic among the population, forcing many to flee again,” an eyewitness said.

This year’s fighting has demonstrated the AFC/M23’s access to advanced military equipment, including aircraft, combat drones, and long-range heavy weapons, much of which was captured from the DRC army during earlier operations, including the takeover of Goma.

The rebel group has used these heavy weapons extensively in the Rusizi Valley and now extends its control to parts of Lake Tanganyika, challenging the dominance of DRC and Burundian forces in the region.

title: Burundi Plans Covert Operations in Eastern DRC Despite Recent Troop Withdrawals
excerpt: BUJUMBURA / SOUTH KIVU, DRC - Burundi is reportedly preparing to resume covert operations in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), following a defeat of its forces in the Rusizi Valley of South Kivu province.
title_en: Burundi Plans Covert Operations in Eastern DRC Despite Recent Troop Withdrawals
excerpt_en: BUJUMBURA / SOUTH KIVU, DRC - Burundi is reportedly preparing to resume covert operations in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), following a defeat of its forces in the Rusizi Valley of South Kivu province.
body_en:
BUJUMBURA / SOUTH KIVU, DRC - Burundi is reportedly preparing to resume covert operations in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), following a defeat of its forces in the Rusizi Valley of South Kivu province. After the losses, a large number of Burundian soldiers returned home, particularly between the nights of 15 and 16 December 2025.

Africa Intelligence reported that the withdrawal was influenced by a request from Rwanda on 15 December, following a border meeting between the two countries’ security officials. The move coincided with the AFC/M23’s withdrawal from Uvira, part of the rebels’ effort to build confidence in peace talks with the DRC government.

Despite the troop pullback, sources indicate that Burundi intends to resume hostilities alongside DRC and Wazalendo forces, launching attacks in areas bordering Lake Tanganyika, including Makobola.

In Baraka, Fizi territory, Burundian army brigades are reportedly stationed, including the 11th Battalion in Gatanga, and the 29th and 16th Battalions in Tujenge. These units have been instructed to prepare for combat if clashes with AFC/M23 continue, and may wear DRC military uniforms starting next week-a tactic previously used in North Kivu in 2023 to obscure their origin.

Many Burundian soldiers captured by AFC/M23 were reported wearing DRC military uniforms, though President Evariste Ndayishimiye denied direct involvement, labeling them as fighters of the RED Tabara armed group, citing their shared Kirundi language.

Observers suggest that President Ndayishimiye has a strategic interest in the ongoing conflict in South Kivu, explaining the continued presence of Burundian forces. The AFC/M23 has reiterated that it will defend itself professionally and protect civilians whenever attacked.

title: Walikale: Residents Appeal to AFC/M23 Amid FDLR and Wazalendo Attacks
excerpt: WALIKALE, North Kivu - December 26, 2025 - Community representatives in Walikale Territory, an area currently under the control of the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, have issued an appeal to the…
title_en: Walikale: Residents Appeal to AFC/M23 Amid FDLR and Wazalendo Attacks
excerpt_en: WALIKALE, North Kivu - December 26, 2025 - Community representatives in Walikale Territory, an area currently under the control of the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, have issued an appeal to the…
body_en:
WALIKALE, North Kivu - December 26, 2025 - Community representatives in Walikale Territory, an area currently under the control of the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, have issued an appeal to the AFC/M23 coalition, urging the group to take control of the area to protect civilians from ongoing violence.

In a statement released on December 26, the residents’ representatives said the population is exhausted by repeated attacks attributed to the FDLR, Wazalendo militias, and, in some cases, elements of the FARDC.

According to the statement, civilians are facing persistent insecurity, including killings, arson, and human rights abuses, prompting the unusual call for intervention by AFC/M23.

The residents urged the coalition to continue expanding into areas controlled by the Congolese government, saying the objective is to liberate civilians who are being abused and terrorized.

For its part, AFC/M23 claimed that Walikale has become a stronghold for FDLR and Wazalendo fighters, who it accuses of harassing the local population with the support and collaboration of certain FARDC members.

“This situation has left the population without security, exposed to violence, destruction of property, and serious human rights violations,” the group said.

The appeal highlights the deepening security crisis in Walikale, where civilians remain caught between multiple armed actors amid the continuing conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.

title: Uvira: Uncertainty Persists Over AFC/M23 Withdrawal
excerpt: Uvira, South Kivu - December 18, 2025 - Uncertainty continues to surround the announced withdrawal of AFC/M23 fighters from the city of Uvira, despite claims by the armed group that its troops have begun leaving the…
title_en: Uvira: Uncertainty Persists Over AFC/M23 Withdrawal
excerpt_en: Uvira, South Kivu - December 18, 2025 - Uncertainty continues to surround the announced withdrawal of AFC/M23 fighters from the city of Uvira, despite claims by the armed group that its troops have begun leaving the…
body_en:
Uvira, South Kivu - December 18, 2025 - Uncertainty continues to surround the announced withdrawal of AFC/M23 fighters from the city of Uvira, despite claims by the armed group that its troops have begun leaving the area.

On Thursday, the security situation in Uvira remained calm, with no major incidents reported. Several witnesses indicated that AFC/M23 fighters were gradually withdrawing toward Kamanyola, their former positions, and vacating some houses they had occupied, particularly in the Nyamianda neighborhood.

However, doubts persist among residents, as some fighters were still observed inside the city and along roads leading toward the Burundi border, raising questions about whether the withdrawal is complete or partial.

Meanwhile, clashes between the AFC/M23 and the FARDC were reported on Wednesday in Fizi territory, notably around the villages of Kazimia, Some, and Sebele. The fighting triggered a mass displacement of civilians, mainly women and children, who fled the affected areas in search of safety.

Local authorities confirmed that the humanitarian situation in these areas remains fragile, as population movements continue amid ongoing insecurity.

title: Eastern DRC: Violence Against Civilians Surges in November
excerpt: Eastern DRC - December 18, 2025 - Violence against civilians in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo saw a sharp increase in November 2025, despite a slight decline in overall security incidents.
title_en: Eastern DRC: Violence Against Civilians Surges in November
excerpt_en: Eastern DRC - December 18, 2025 - Violence against civilians in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo saw a sharp increase in November 2025, despite a slight decline in overall security incidents.
body_en:
Eastern DRC - December 18, 2025 - Violence against civilians in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo saw a sharp increase in November 2025, despite a slight decline in overall security incidents.

According to a recent assessment, 289 civilians were killed in November, up from 205 in October, even though reported security incidents fell by 5 percent to 226 cases. Lubero territory in North Kivu, particularly the Bapere sector and Baswagha chiefdom, remains the epicenter of violence, with 121 civilians killed, including 22 women.

The Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) were identified as the deadliest armed group, active in North Kivu and Ituri, while the AFC/M23 coalition continues its expansion to the west and south of the country, despite the recent Doha agreement signed on November 15.

These developments have prompted intensified operations by the FARDC, notably in the Mwenga highlands of South Kivu, as the government seeks to curb the growing threats to civilians and regional stability.

title: North Kivu: Thousands Displaced by M23 Live in Precarious Conditions in Rutshuru
excerpt: Rutshuru, North Kivu - December 2025 - Nearly 4,700 families, or 23,580 people, have been forcibly displaced from the Walikale territory by M23 rebels and are now living in extremely precarious conditions along the…
title_en: North Kivu: Thousands Displaced by M23 Live in Precarious Conditions in Rutshuru
excerpt_en: Rutshuru, North Kivu - December 2025 - Nearly 4,700 families, or 23,580 people, have been forcibly displaced from the Walikale territory by M23 rebels and are now living in extremely precarious conditions along the…
body_en:
Rutshuru, North Kivu - December 2025 - Nearly 4,700 families, or 23,580 people, have been forcibly displaced from the Walikale territory by M23 rebels and are now living in extremely precarious conditions along the Birundule-Iyobora-Bulindi axis in the Kibirizi health zone of Rutshuru.

The displaced families originate from villages including Ikobo, Kateku, Mukigi, Lubwe, and Kasungu. They are scattered across Bulindi, Buheri, Birundule, and Iyobora, joining thousands of other families already present, putting additional strain on host communities that are already weakened by insecurity and deprived of access to their land.

Reports indicate that the M23 justified the evictions citing “security reasons” before conducting sweep operations, which triggered a mass exodus toward southern Lubero and northern Bwito. Local committees have highlighted the urgent need for food aid, household essentials, and humanitarian support, even as interventions in health, water, hygiene, and sanitation sectors are underway.

Humanitarian agencies are calling for accelerated assistance to prevent further deterioration of living conditions among the displaced population.

title_en: Kwamouth: FARDC Neutralizes Mobondo Insurgents in Epumbulu
excerpt_en: Kwamouth, Maï-Ndombe Province - December 19, 2025 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) engaged a group of Mobondo insurgents in the village of Epumbulu, Kwamouth territory, during operations on…
body_en:
Kwamouth, Maï-Ndombe Province - December 19, 2025 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) engaged a group of Mobondo insurgents in the village of Epumbulu, Kwamouth territory, during operations on the night of Thursday, December 19.

A preliminary report indicates that four insurgents were killed and one captured alive. According to Captain Antony Mualushayi, spokesperson for Operation Ngemba (Peace), sweep and security operations are ongoing to fully restore order and prevent any resurgence of these armed groups.

The FARDC also reassured civilians that all necessary measures are being taken to ensure their protection, particularly during the end-of-year period, amid ongoing threats from armed groups opposing peace efforts in the region.

title: Walikale: Violent Clashes Leave Four Dead and Homes Burned
excerpt: Walikale, North Kivu - December 15, 2025 - Violent clashes erupted on Monday, December 15, in the village of Tuonane, Waloa Loanda group, between suspected FDLR fighters and Mai-Mai Kifuafua militiamen.
title_en: Walikale: Violent Clashes Leave Four Dead and Homes Burned
excerpt_en: Walikale, North Kivu - December 15, 2025 - Violent clashes erupted on Monday, December 15, in the village of Tuonane, Waloa Loanda group, between suspected FDLR fighters and Mai-Mai Kifuafua militiamen.
body_en:
Walikale, North Kivu - December 15, 2025 - Violent clashes erupted on Monday, December 15, in the village of Tuonane, Waloa Loanda group, between suspected FDLR fighters and Mai-Mai Kifuafua militiamen.

The fighting, reportedly linked to a land dispute involving an FDLR leader, began around 4:00 a.m. and lasted most of the day. The clashes left at least four dead, including two leaders of the Kifuafua group, and caused significant destruction: six houses and two traditional huts (barza) were burned.

One civilian remains missing, while most villagers fled to the nearby town of Hombo for safety. Authorities report that a fragile calm has since returned to the area.

title: Heavy Shelling in Mikenke Despite AFC/M23 Withdrawal Announcement
excerpt: Uvira, DRC - December 19, 2025 - Residents of Mikenke, a locality in Uvira territory, reported heavy shelling early Friday morning, despite the AFC/M23’s earlier claims of having withdrawn from the city.
title_en: Heavy Shelling in Mikenke Despite AFC/M23 Withdrawal Announcement
excerpt_en: Uvira, DRC - December 19, 2025 - Residents of Mikenke, a locality in Uvira territory, reported heavy shelling early Friday morning, despite the AFC/M23’s earlier claims of having withdrawn from the city.
body_en:
Uvira, DRC - December 19, 2025 - Residents of Mikenke, a locality in Uvira territory, reported heavy shelling early Friday morning, despite the AFC/M23’s earlier claims of having withdrawn from the city.

Bertrand Bisimwa, President of the M23 and Deputy Coordinator of the AFC/M23, stated that bombardments began at 6:38 a.m., attributing the attacks to forces allied with the Kinshasa government, including the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC), Wazalendo militias, and the Burundian army.

The shelling underscores ongoing uncertainty over the security situation, as the AFC/M23 insists it no longer maintains military control over Uvira.

No independent confirmation of the attacks was available at the time, and information on casualties or damage remains unknown. Authorities from both the DRC and Burundi had not commented publicly.

excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - December 19, 2025 - The Congo River Alliance (AFC/M23) declared a unilateral ceasefire on Friday, citing a commitment to peace and a desire to provide a genuine opportunity for the restoration of…
title_en: AFC/M23 Announces Unilateral Ceasefire Amid Kinshasa Attacks
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - December 19, 2025 - The Congo River Alliance (AFC/M23) declared a unilateral ceasefire on Friday, citing a commitment to peace and a desire to provide a genuine opportunity for the restoration of…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - December 19, 2025 - The Congo River Alliance (AFC/M23) declared a unilateral ceasefire on Friday, citing a commitment to peace and a desire to provide a genuine opportunity for the restoration of stability in eastern DR Congo.

Despite the ceasefire, the coalition accused government forces of continuing systematic attacks against civilians and AFC/M23 positions, in violation of previous agreements.

Lawrence Kanyuka, spokesperson for AFC/M23, reported that government forces targeted populated areas using kamikaze drones, naval artillery, and heavy weapons, escalating violence even after the ceasefire was announced.

body_en:
Uvira, South Kivu - December 19, 2025 - Following the recent withdrawal of AFC/M23 rebels, Wazalendo forces are now confirmed to be present in the city of Uvira, according to National Deputy Willy Mishiki, a prominent pro-government leader.

In an interview broadcast on Télé 50, Mishiki stated that his forces are awaiting the arrival of the FARDC, Congolese National Police (PNC), and civilian administrators to fully secure the city.

“I can assure you that the Wazalendo are already in Uvira. We are now awaiting the arrival of the FARDC, the PNC, and the restoration of civilian administration. I can also confirm that these groups have left the city,” Mishiki said.

The announcement has sparked controversy, with the Congolese government cautioning that the statement could be manipulated by M23. Meanwhile, NGOs, including Doctors Without Borders, report abuses against civilians by Wazalendo fighters allied with the FARDC, highlighting ongoing security and humanitarian concerns despite the rebel withdrawal.

title: FARDC Denounces “Fictitious Withdrawal” of Rwandan Forces and M23 from Uvira
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - December 20, 2025 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) on Saturday accused the coalition formed by the Congo River Alliance (AFC), the March 23 Movement (M23), and the Rwandan…
title_en: FARDC Denounces “Fictitious Withdrawal” of Rwandan Forces and M23 from Uvira
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - December 20, 2025 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) on Saturday accused the coalition formed by the Congo River Alliance (AFC), the March 23 Movement (M23), and the Rwandan…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - December 20, 2025 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) on Saturday accused the coalition formed by the Congo River Alliance (AFC), the March 23 Movement (M23), and the Rwandan Defence Forces (RDF) of staging a sham withdrawal from Uvira city and surrounding areas in South Kivu province.

In an official statement, the FARDC described the reported withdrawal as a “media diversion” intended to mislead both national and international audiences amid increasing pressure on Rwanda to respect peace agreements.

Major General Sylvain Ekenge Bomusa Efomi, FARDC spokesperson, stated:

“This so-called withdrawal is in no way related to the reality on the ground and demonstrates Rwanda's blatant bad faith regarding its commitments under the Washington Peace Agreement.”

According to the Congolese army, the operation aims to manipulate the confidence of international mediators, including representatives from the United States and Qatar, who are facilitating talks to resolve the conflict in eastern DRC.

Continued Presence and Activities of Rebel Forces

Local reports, corroborated by NGOs, civil society, and residents, indicate no genuine withdrawal. FARDC claims that M23/AFC/RDF fighters continue to occupy strategic neighborhoods of Uvira, controlling key roads, checkpoints, and access points.

Rwandan soldiers, allegedly disguised as police or civilians, have been spotted in the city center and at the port of Kalundu, near the Burundi border.

Roadblocks and checkpoints remain active, severely restricting civilian movement and trade.

Reports of abuses-including intimidation, extortion, and arbitrary arrests-persist, alongside nighttime military patrols.

A small contingent of rebels was filmed leaving the city only to redeploy to the surrounding hills and highlands of Uvira and Fizi, attempting to bypass FARDC positions.

Clashes were also reported recently in Kasekezi, approximately 30 kilometers south of Uvira, involving Rwandan forces.

The FARDC cited a viral statement from M23 spokesperson Willy Ngoma, declaring:

“The AFC/M23 will never, ever leave the city of Uvira,” as evidence of the coalition’s duplicity.

The Congolese army accused Rwanda of subterfuges, stratagems, and deceptions, asserting that these actions violate UN Security Council Resolution 2773 and the Washington Agreements.

FARDC emphasized that the coalition’s maneuvers are not only a breach of peace commitments but also a direct threat to civilians. The army reassured residents of Uvira that it is committed to restoring state authority and protecting the population, urging vigilance and encouraging the public to report suspicious activities to intelligence services.

This statement comes amid ongoing tensions in eastern DRC, where M23, supported by Kigali according to Kinshasa, has controlled several territories since 2022. Despite ongoing negotiations, repeated ceasefire violations continue to undermine regional peace efforts.

title: Heavy Fighting Erupts in Uvira as Wazalendo Launch Offensive Against AFC/M23
excerpt: Uvira, South Kivu - December 22, 2025 - Intense clashes involving heavy and light weapons erupted early Monday across multiple neighborhoods in Uvira, raising fears of a new escalation in South Kivu province.
title_en: Heavy Fighting Erupts in Uvira as Wazalendo Launch Offensive Against AFC/M23
excerpt_en: Uvira, South Kivu - December 22, 2025 - Intense clashes involving heavy and light weapons erupted early Monday across multiple neighborhoods in Uvira, raising fears of a new escalation in South Kivu province.
body_en:
Uvira, South Kivu - December 22, 2025 - Intense clashes involving heavy and light weapons erupted early Monday across multiple neighborhoods in Uvira, raising fears of a new escalation in South Kivu province.

Local sources reported that gunfire began around 8:20 a.m., affecting areas from Kalundu to Mulongwe, and reaching as far as Kasenga. The Wazalendo militia reportedly launched an offensive targeting positions held by AFC/M23 rebels, signaling a sharp deterioration in security following recent troop movements and protests.

The clashes are not limited to the city. In Fizi territory, additional fighting has been reported in Katuta, the heart of the Makobola area, where armed confrontations continue.

As of midday, official casualty figures remain unavailable, and authorities had yet to issue a formal statement. Residents described widespread panic, with many seeking shelter amid the sustained sound of gunfire. The local population continues to face heightened insecurity, building on the chaos caused by prior clashes, rebel withdrawals, and contested control of urban zones.

The renewed fighting comes amid heightened political and military tensions in eastern DRC, following demonstrations in Goma and Uvira, disputes over AFC/M23 withdrawals, and ongoing humanitarian concerns. Analysts warn that repeated clashes risk destabilizing the region further, undermining both ceasefire efforts and civilian safety.

This situation is ongoing, with further updates expected as additional information emerges.

excerpt: Uvira, DRC - December 25, 2025 - Columns of M23 fighters, accompanied by elements of the Rwandan army, have retreated from Bangwe toward Luanga Hill, and further toward Kigongo, a strategic hill overlooking the first…
title_en: FARDC Forces Push Back M23 Near Uvira After Intense Clashes
excerpt_en: Uvira, DRC - December 25, 2025 - Columns of M23 fighters, accompanied by elements of the Rwandan army, have retreated from Bangwe toward Luanga Hill, and further toward Kigongo, a strategic hill overlooking the first…
body_en:
Uvira, DRC - December 25, 2025 - Columns of M23 fighters, accompanied by elements of the Rwandan army, have retreated from Bangwe toward Luanga Hill, and further toward Kigongo, a strategic hill overlooking the first village past Uvira, following intense clashes with the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC) and allied Wazalendo forces.

The withdrawal comes after Wednesday’s fighting in and around Makobola 1, where rebels reportedly came under heavy fire from FARDC and Wazalendo units.

On Thursday morning, at around 8:00 a.m., FARDC conducted a strike on Lwangwa Hill, where several M23 elements were regrouping. Security sources indicate that several fighters were neutralized, and others captured during the joint FARDC-Wazalendo operations.

Currently, Makobola 1 and surrounding villages are under FARDC and Wazalendo control. The security situation remains fluid, and authorities continue to monitor developments closely.

title: Gunfire and Military Escalation Shake Uvira
excerpt: Uvira, DRC - December 26, 2025
title_en: Gunfire and Military Escalation Shake Uvira
excerpt_en: Uvira, DRC - December 26, 2025
body_en:
Uvira, DRC - December 26, 2025

Tensions have sharply escalated in Uvira after the Congolese Armed Forces (FARDC) reportedly destroyed two Rwandan fast patrol boats at Kalundu Port early Friday morning.

The boats-described as rapid gunboats allegedly linked to Rwandan forces-were neutralized near the shores of Lake Tanganyika. Only one vessel is said to remain in the attackers’ possession.

This development follows the recent AFC/M23 setback in Makobola and comes as FARDC units advance to within 8 kilometers of Uvira, with only two strategic hills separating government forces from full control of the city.

Early this morning, gunshots were also heard in several neighborhoods, including Kalimabengi and Kanvinvira, sparking panic among residents.

Local sources report increased military mobilization, while residents fear a further escalation as the situation on the ground continues to evolve rapidly.

No official statement has yet been released by Congolese authorities.

title: Heavy Gunfire Rocks Djugu as Fighting Resumes
excerpt: Djugu, Ituri - Friday, December 26, 2025
title_en: Heavy Gunfire Rocks Djugu as Fighting Resumes
excerpt_en: Djugu, Ituri - Friday, December 26, 2025
body_en:
Djugu, Ituri - Friday, December 26, 2025

Powerful explosions from heavy and light weapons have been echoing since 7:00 a.m. across the territory of Djugu, in Ituri Province, as clashes resumed between the FARDC and fighters of the CRP - The “CRP armed group” the Convention for the People’s Revolution (CRP), a political-military movement led by Thomas Lubanga in Ituri, Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), which regularly clashes with the FARDC (Armed Forces of the DRC).

The rebel group claims to have seized control of the locality of Bule, a statement firmly denied by the Congolese army. The FARDC report ongoing sweep operations and allege the suspected involvement of certain displaced persons in the violence.

On Thursday, persistent insecurity had already disrupted socio-economic and religious activities throughout the area.

The situation remains tense and rapidly evolving.

title: FARDC Airstrikes Intensify in Uvira Amid Sukhoi Su-25 Downing
excerpt: Uvira, DRC - Friday, December 26, 2025
title_en: FARDC Airstrikes Intensify in Uvira Amid Sukhoi Su-25 Downing
excerpt_en: Uvira, DRC - Friday, December 26, 2025
body_en:
Uvira, DRC - Friday, December 26, 2025

According to local sources, a third airstrike was carried out over the Kalundu area by a Sukhoi Su-25 fighter jet of the Congolese Air Force (FARDC), intensifying aerial operations over the city.

In a major escalation, the Sukhoi Su-25 aircraft, which reportedly conducted three bombing runs over Uvira, was later shot down, marking a significant setback for the Congolese air operation. Details surrounding the circumstances of the aircraft’s downing remain unclear.

At the same time, FARDC airstrikes targeted the alleged headquarters of AFC/M23 rebels, located at the former MONUSCO camp in Kala, on the outskirts of Uvira. The extent of damage and possible casualties has not yet been officially confirmed.

title: FARDC Recaptures Katoyi After Fierce Clashes with AFC/M23
excerpt: Masisi, North Kivu, DRC - Monday, December 29, 2025
title_en: FARDC Recaptures Katoyi After Fierce Clashes with AFC/M23
excerpt_en: Masisi, North Kivu, DRC - Monday, December 29, 2025
body_en:
Masisi, North Kivu, DRC - Monday, December 29, 2025

The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) recaptured Katoyi, the main town in the sector of the same name in Masisi territory, on Monday after fierce fighting on Sunday against AFC/M23 rebels.

The rebels had controlled the center of Katoyi since mid-November 2025, allowing them to increase pressure on neighboring areas, notably Oufamandu, Matanda, and Nyamaboko, in the south of the territory.

According to local security sources, the FARDC and Wazalendo fighters from the PARECO movement were expected to reoccupy Katoyi around noon on Sunday. These sources also indicated that, in addition to the town center, at least four strategic positions had been retaken: Mitimingi, Kahundu, Kasheke, and Kakoka.

The fighting, which began very early in the morning around 4:00 a.m., gradually subsided in the evening, according to the same sources.

Local civil society reports that the situation remains unstable in and around Katoyi. In addition to losses suffered by both sides, military sources indicate that at least 28 AFC/M23 fighters have been captured and 12 weapons have been recovered from the rebel side.

This violence has caused further population displacement: several hundred residents have reportedly sought refuge in neighboring villages, while others remain hidden in the bush, according to civil society actors.

title: FARDC Condemns Discriminatory Remarks, Suspends Spokesperson
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - Monday, December 29, 2025
title_en: FARDC Condemns Discriminatory Remarks, Suspends Spokesperson
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - Monday, December 29, 2025
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - Monday, December 29, 2025

The General Staff of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) clarified that discriminatory remarks targeting the Tutsi community, made last weekend by army spokesperson Major General Sylvain Epenge, “in no way reflect the official position of the country, nor that of the Supreme Commander of the FARDC, nor that of the government.”

In a statement consulted on Monday by Radio Okapi, the Chief of Staff of the FARDC condemned the remarks and reaffirmed the FARDC’s determination to defend and protect, with discipline and professionalism, the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the country, as well as the security of all Congolese, without discrimination, even unto death.

The statement also called on the entire population to unite, stand together, and reject all hate speech in order to support the FARDC in carrying out their mission.

Major General Sylvain Epenge has been suspended from his duties following the controversial remarks, which have sparked numerous comments and strong reactions across the DRC.

title: At Least 20 Killed in Clashes Between Mobondo Militia and FARDC in Kikwit
excerpt: Kikwit, Kwilu Province, DRC - Sunday, December 29, 2025
title_en: At Least 20 Killed in Clashes Between Mobondo Militia and FARDC in Kikwit
excerpt_en: Kikwit, Kwilu Province, DRC - Sunday, December 29, 2025
body_en:
Kikwit, Kwilu Province, DRC - Sunday, December 29, 2025

At least 20 people were killed in recent clashes between the Mobondo militia and the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) in Kikwit, Kwilu province, including 15 Mobondo militiamen and five FARDC soldiers, according to the army.

On Sunday, the FARDC presented weapons and documents seized from the Mobondo fighters to the press. The items included 29 12‑gauge shotguns, six AK‑47 rifles, and several identity documents, recovered during military operations in the villages of Bolingo and Nkana, in Kikwit.

The regional FARDC spokesperson, Captain Antony Mualushay, reaffirmed the army’s determination to definitively neutralize the Mobondo movement, which he described as a direct threat on the outskirts of Kinshasa.

He expressed regret over the deaths of five soldiers, stressing that they were killed with weapons of war, not knives, an indication, he said, that the group is not merely an isolated militia but a structured rebellion.

Captain Mualushay warned that any belief by the Mobondo that they could act with impunity near the capital was mistaken. He emphasized that the army has no political affiliation and would act against anyone supporting the movement, directly or indirectly, to prevent further bloodshed among Congolese civilians.

title: Approximately 423 candidates, including 29 women, took the entrance exam for military academies
excerpt: Approximately 423 candidates, including 29 women, took the entrance exam for military academies across the Democratic Republic of Congo in Kisangani.
title_en: Approximately 423 candidates, including 29 women, took the entrance exam for military academies
excerpt_en: Approximately 423 candidates, including 29 women, took the entrance exam for military academies across the Democratic Republic of Congo in Kisangani.
body_en:
Approximately 423 candidates, including 29 women, took the entrance exam for military academies across the Democratic Republic of Congo in Kisangani.

Over two days, candidates were tested in French, English, general knowledge, mathematics, and specialized subjects.

According to Deputy Senior Military Auditor Major Magistrate Feinto Kabuya Mwadiamvita, successful candidates will have the choice between the Special Academy and the Ordinary Academy, with training lasting 9 months for the former and 3 years for the latter.

Training will be conducted in Kinshasa, Kitona (Kongo-Central Province), or Kananga (Kasai-Central Province). The exams are overseen by Brigadier General Bertin Mfutela, commander of the training centers.

More than 372 young people took the national entrance exam on Saturday, December 27, for military academy admission and military studies. Tests were held at Saint Pierre Dibua dia Buakane Episcopal College in the Kanshi district, following an opening ceremony by the provincial governor, who commended the courage of the candidates in light of aggression from neighboring Rwanda.

The recruitment officer for the 21st Military Region stated that the top candidates will be shortlisted to study in Kananga, the capital of Kasai Central province.

The latter half of December 2025 finds the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) in a state of profound complexity, where significant economic progress and humanitarian efforts are overshadowed by a volatile security landscape and shifting regional geopolitics.

Security and Geopolitics: The fall and subsequent disputed withdrawal of AFC/M23 from the strategic city of Uvira has fundamentally altered the regional power balance. While the rebel group claims a tactical withdrawal in support of peace processes, the Congolese government remains skeptical, viewing these moves as calculated diversions backed by Rwanda. The resulting closure of borders with Burundi has triggered a severe economic shock for the neighbor and left thousands of Congolese refugees in dire humanitarian conditions.

Internal Political Tensions: Domestically, the arrest of senior opposition figure Emmanuel Ramazani Shadary has drawn international criticism, notably from Belgium, and risks further polarizing the political environment at a time when national unity is critical for addressing eastern aggression.

Economic Resilience vs. Human Cost: Paradoxically, while the IMF reports resilient GDP growth exceeding 5% and stabilized inflation, the everyday reality for many Congolese is defined by tragedy and displacement. Deadly shipwrecks, chronic cholera outbreaks in refugee camps, and forced civilian marches in occupied territories highlight the severe human cost of ongoing instability.

Governance and Reform Efforts: Amidst these crises, the government continues to push for structural reforms. Initiatives like the roadmap for human rights in the mining sector, the modernization of public services, and strategic partnerships for digital finance (e.g., Rawbank and Visa) signal a long-term commitment to state efficiency and economic formalization.

Ultimately, the report underscores that while the DRC is making strides in macro-economic stability and governance reform, its future stability hinges on the effective implementation of peace agreements and the restoration of state authority in the East. Without a verifiable cessation of hostilities and a reduction in political friction, the human and social development of the Congolese people remains precarious

title: Burundi Signals Openness to Renewed Dialogue With Rwanda
excerpt: Bujumbura, November 28, 2025 - Burundi’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Regional Cooperation, Edouard Bizimana, has indicated that talks with Rwanda remain possible despite what he described as a “less than satisfactory” pace.
title_en: Burundi Signals Openness to Renewed Dialogue With Rwanda
excerpt_en: Bujumbura, November 28, 2025 - Burundi’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Regional Cooperation, Edouard Bizimana, has indicated that talks with Rwanda remain possible despite what he described as a “less than satisfactory” pace.
body_en:
Bujumbura, November 28, 2025 - Burundi’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Regional Cooperation, Edouard Bizimana, has indicated that talks with Rwanda remain possible despite what he described as a “less than satisfactory” pace. He made the remarks during a press conference held on Friday.

Minister Bizimana emphasized the natural ties between the two nations, insisting that the relationship should not remain strained indefinitely.

“Burundians and Rwandans are like brothers. We share borders and a common culture,” he said. “I do not think there is a problem so big that it should lead families to remain closed. There are issues, but all will be resolved through dialogue - and that dialogue is ongoing.”

Bizimana acknowledged that meetings between the two countries are infrequent, but maintained that communication channels remain open.“Even countries in conflict always keep the path of dialogue open,” he noted. “Not all doors are closed. We continue to talk because we share a past, a region, and a future. Both sides are obliged to make efforts.”

The minister added that Burundi has made steps to improve bilateral relations, though some issues remain unresolved.

Burundi closed its border with Rwanda in January 2024, accusing Kigali of supporting the RED Tabara armed group - an allegation Rwanda has repeatedly rejected as baseless. Rwanda has argued that the accusations serve as a way for Burundi to deflect attention from its internal security challenges.

Since the closure, several attempts at reviving diplomatic ties have taken place, but without concrete results.

The decision to impose the border closure followed President Évariste Ndayishimiye’s 2023 state-of-the-nation address, during which he hinted at the move while accusing Rwanda of backing RED Tabara. Despite this, subsequent statements from Burundian officials have often contradicted one another, with accusations made one day and denied the next.

Speaking to journalists on November 27, 2025, Rwandan President Paul Kagame was asked about the current state of relations, days after a group of Burundian refugees voluntarily returned home and Burundian military officers participated in a meeting of regional land-forces commanders in Kigali.

Kagame reiterated that Rwanda has never closed its border with Burundi.

“The borders are still the same as they were,” he said. “But for us, even before the closure, Rwanda had no hand in it. It was the Burundians who chose to close the borders. Wherever they wish to open them, we have never closed them.”

title: Rwanda and DRC to Sign Final Peace Agreement in Washington on December 4
excerpt: Washington, December 1, 2025 - The White House has confirmed that Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will sign a final peace agreement on December 4, 2025.
title_en: Rwanda and DRC to Sign Final Peace Agreement in Washington on December 4
excerpt_en: Washington, December 1, 2025 - The White House has confirmed that Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will sign a final peace agreement on December 4, 2025.
body_en:
Washington, December 1, 2025 - The White House has confirmed that Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will sign a final peace agreement on December 4, 2025. The announcement was made by White House Spokesperson Caroline Leavitt during a press conference.

Leavitt stated, “On Thursday, President Trump will host the Presidents of Rwanda and the DRC, who signed historic peace and economic agreements.”

Last week, Presidents Paul Kagame of Rwanda and Félix Tshisekedi of the DRC confirmed their readiness to travel to the United States for the ceremony, expressing confidence in the prospects for lasting peace.

The United States has also invited regional leaders to witness the signing, including the Presidents of Kenya and Burundi. Burundian President Evariste Ndayishimiye is scheduled to travel to Washington today to attend the event.

Additionally, the DRC government has dispatched a high-level delegation, including the President of the National Assembly and several ministers, to participate in the ceremony.

title: DRC-Rwanda Peace and Cooperation Agreement
excerpt: Washington, D.C. - December 4, 2025
title_en: DRC-Rwanda Peace and Cooperation Agreement
excerpt_en: Washington, D.C. - December 4, 2025
body_en:
Washington, D.C. - December 4, 2025

President Félix Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) confirmed that the DRC is committed to implementing all provisions of the peace and economic cooperation agreement with Rwanda, including the dismantling of armed groups.

The agreement was signed during a ceremony in the United States, with both countries pledging mutual respect, non-interference, and cooperation.

The DRC will dismantle armed groups, including the FDLR terrorist organization and affiliates.

Rwanda will remove its security measures currently in place.

Both countries will collaborate to combat and prevent support to armed groups.

Joint development projects, including the Rusizi III hydroelectric dam.

Shared management of Lake Kivu resources.

Cooperation in trade, mining, and environmental protection.

Promote lasting peace, security, and development in the region.

Foster a new era of partnership and collaboration benefiting citizens of both countries.

President Tshisekedi emphasized vigilance, continuity in peace efforts, and the importance of mutual respect.

The United States indicated that full implementation of this agreement would support regional stability and development.

This agreement represents a major step toward resolving long-standing conflicts in the Great Lakes region and enhancing bilateral cooperation between the DRC and Rwanda.

title: Macron Urges Commitment to DRC-Rwanda Peace Agreement
excerpt: Washington, D.C., December 4, 2025
title_en: Macron Urges Commitment to DRC-Rwanda Peace Agreement
excerpt_en: Washington, D.C., December 4, 2025
body_en:
Washington, D.C., December 4, 2025

French President Emmanuel Macron has welcomed the peace agreement signed by Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), emphasizing that both sides must honor their commitments to achieve lasting peace in the Great Lakes Region.

The agreement, signed by President Paul Kagame of Rwanda and President Félix Tshisekedi of the DRC, includes provisions for preserving national sovereignty, dismantling armed groups, establishing joint security structures, repatriating refugees, and promoting regional economic cooperation. It also outlines the roles of MONUSCO and other institutions in supporting humanitarian operations.

The signing ceremony was attended by several heads of state and dignitaries, including Angola’s João Lourenço, Kenya’s William Ruto, Burundi’s Evariste Ndayishimiye, African Union Commission Chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, former Kenyan President Uhuru Kenyatta, Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo, and Ugandan Vice President Jessica Alupo.

President Macron praised the diplomatic efforts of the United States, Qatar, Togo, and the African Union in facilitating the agreement. He called on all parties to respect their obligations so that the people of the DRC and the region can enjoy peace and stability.

During the ceremony, President Kagame expressed gratitude to the attending leaders, highlighting the support of President Donald Trump in advancing peace, and reaffirmed Rwanda’s commitment to stability and compliance with the agreement.

President Tshisekedi assured that the DRC is prepared to implement all provisions, including the dismantling of armed groups, and emphasized a partnership based on mutual respect, non-interference, and cooperation to fight armed groups.

Both countries agreed to resolve disagreements peacefully, avoid provocative actions, and refrain from supporting or engaging in military aggression, either directly or indirectly.

title: President Kagame Holds High-Level Talks in Washington Following DRC-Rwanda Peace Agreement
excerpt: Washington, D.C., December 5, 2025
title_en: President Kagame Holds High-Level Talks in Washington Following DRC-Rwanda Peace Agreement
excerpt_en: Washington, D.C., December 5, 2025
body_en:
Washington, D.C., December 5, 2025

President Paul Kagame of Rwanda held bilateral talks with several heads of state and government, including President William Ruto of Kenya, President Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé of Togo, and Prime Minister Mia Amor Mottley of Barbados, during his visit to Washington, D.C.

These discussions followed the signing of the historic peace agreement between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) on December 4, 2025, which Kagame attended alongside other leaders, including Ruto and Gnassingbé.

During the meeting with Prime Minister Mottley, the leaders focused on strengthening cooperation in security, health, and trade, building on recent exchanges that included Kagame’s visit to Barbados and Mottley’s trip to Kigali.

The talks with President Gnassingbé of Togo centered on enhancing bilateral relations and cooperation between Rwanda and Togo, emphasizing continued partnership in political and economic matters.

These meetings underscore Rwanda’s commitment to regional stability, international collaboration, and expanding diplomatic ties following its role in the DRC-Rwanda peace process.

title: Minister Nduhungirehe Highlights Challenges of Regional Integration Amid Burundi’s Role in DRC Conflict
excerpt: Washington D.C., December 5, 2025 - Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Ambassador Olivier Nduhungirehe, has stated that regional integration remains challenging as Burundi continues to wage war in the…
title_en: Minister Nduhungirehe Highlights Challenges of Regional Integration Amid Burundi’s Role in DRC Conflict
excerpt_en: Washington D.C., December 5, 2025 - Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Ambassador Olivier Nduhungirehe, has stated that regional integration remains challenging as Burundi continues to wage war in the…
body_en:
Washington D.C., December 5, 2025 - Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Ambassador Olivier Nduhungirehe, has stated that regional integration remains challenging as Burundi continues to wage war in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

Speaking to the Agasaro Kaburaga YouTube channel, Minister Nduhungirehe commented on the recent signing of a regional economic cooperation agreement between Rwanda and the DRC on December 4, 2025, facilitated by the United States. The agreement includes projects such as the Rusizi III hydroelectric dam, designed to generate 206 megawatts of energy for Rwanda, the DRC, and Burundi.

The signing ceremony was attended by Burundian President Evariste Ndayishimiye, who emphasized continued joint projects under the framework of agreements governing the Great Lakes Region.

Minister Nduhungirehe, however, criticized Burundi for destabilizing South Kivu, stating that its military presence is undermining regional peace. He said:

"What we see in eastern Congo, especially in South Kivu, is that the Burundian government is adding fuel to the fire, having sent 20,000 troops in recent days. They are besieging areas inhabited by the Banyamulenge, restricting market access, and attacking civilians."

He stressed that regional cooperation cannot succeed while Burundian forces continue operations alongside DRC and Wazalendo troops, preventing the ceasefire agreements from being implemented in Doha.

From December 2 to 5, 2025, these forces conducted heavy attacks on AFC/M23-controlled areas including Kamanyola, Katogota, and Kaziba, resulting in the destruction of houses, civilian deaths, injuries, and mass displacement.

The Rusizi District administration confirmed that over 750 Congolese refugees have fled to Rwanda as of December 5, with most accommodated at the Nyarushishi temporary camp.

title: President Kagame Meets U.S. Lawmakers to Strengthen Development and Peace Partnerships
excerpt: Washington, D.C. - Rwandan President Paul Kagame has held high-level meetings with members of the United States Congress to discuss partnerships for development, regional stability, and sustainable peace, as part of his…
title_en: President Kagame Meets U.S. Lawmakers to Strengthen Development and Peace Partnerships
excerpt_en: Washington, D.C. - Rwandan President Paul Kagame has held high-level meetings with members of the United States Congress to discuss partnerships for development, regional stability, and sustainable peace, as part of his…
body_en:
Washington, D.C. - Rwandan President Paul Kagame has held high-level meetings with members of the United States Congress to discuss partnerships for development, regional stability, and sustainable peace, as part of his official visit to the United States.

President Kagame met with several members of Congress, including Representative Brian Mast, Chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, alongside Representative Ronny Jackson, Representative Trent Kelly, Senator Mike Rounds, Senator Kevin Cramer, and Senator Pete Ricketts. Discussions focused on continued cooperation through key initiatives aimed at promoting peace, security, and long-term development.

Later on the evening of December 3, 2025, President Kagame also held talks with Senator Lindsey Graham, a long-serving lawmaker representing South Carolina. The meeting centered on strengthening the Rwanda-U.S. partnership in strategic areas, including environmental protection, security, and the economy.

The Rwandan Head of State is in Washington, D.C. to attend the signing ceremony of the final peace agreement between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), scheduled for December 4, 2025. The agreement is expected to serve as a framework for bilateral cooperation in sectors such as mining, trade, infrastructure development, health, and park and environmental protection.

Several regional leaders have also arrived in the U.S. capital for the ceremony, including President Félix Tshisekedi of the DRC, President Évariste Ndayishimiye of Burundi, President William Ruto of Kenya, as well as representatives of the East African Community (EAC).

In a statement released on December 3, 2025, the Office of the President at Village Urugwiro announced that President Kagame is also scheduled to meet with his U.S. counterpart, President Donald Trump, during his visit.

The diplomatic engagements highlight renewed efforts to reinforce regional cooperation and deepen Rwanda-U.S. relations amid evolving security and development challenges in the Great Lakes region.
