title: Nduhungirehe Challenges Claims That FDLR Is “Dead,” Questions DRC Commitment
excerpt: Kigali / Washington - Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Ambassador Olivier Nduhungirehe, has pushed back against claims that the FDLR terrorist group no longer exists, arguing that such…
title_en: Nduhungirehe Challenges Claims That FDLR Is “Dead,” Questions DRC Commitment
excerpt_en: Kigali / Washington - Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Ambassador Olivier Nduhungirehe, has pushed back against claims that the FDLR terrorist group no longer exists, arguing that such…
body_en:
Kigali / Washington - Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Ambassador Olivier Nduhungirehe, has pushed back against claims that the FDLR terrorist group no longer exists, arguing that such assertions contradict the Democratic Republic of Congo’s own commitments under a recently signed Rwanda-DRC peace agreement.

Nduhungirehe was responding to remarks by Gérard Araud, a former French Ambassador to the United Nations and the United States, who suggested that the FDLR had effectively ceased to exist. Araud, who previously served in France’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on security matters during the presidency of François Mitterrand, made the comments amid renewed debate over security in eastern DRC.

On November 7, 2025, Araud posted on X accusing Rwanda of using the M23 movement as a proxy to plunder natural resources in eastern Congo. In response, Nduhungirehe rejected the claim, insisting that the AFC/M23 is not a Rwandan tool, but rather a Congolese movement defending Kinyarwanda-speaking Congolese, whom he said have faced marginalization and persecution since independence.

The minister recalled that the persecution of Kinyarwanda-speaking communities, particularly the Tutsi, intensified in July 1994, when members of the defeated Ex-FAR and Interahamwe militias fled into eastern Congo following the genocide against the Tutsi. He noted that these forces were evacuated under France’s Operation Turquoise and were not disarmed, laying the foundation for continued insecurity in the region.

Addressing allegations of resource plunder, Nduhungirehe said Rwanda has long accused the DRC of exploiting its own natural resources, including the so-called “3T” minerals - tin, tantalum, and tungsten. He argued that the two countries sit on the same geological formations, a reality documented in colonial-era maps, and stressed that the extraction sector in the DRC is largely dominated by Western and Asian companies.“You will not find a Rwandan company among the top 100 firms extracting precious minerals from the DRC, even during periods of war,” he said.

Araud has also alleged that Rwandan troops entered DRC territory, a claim Nduhungirehe denied, stating that Rwanda instead implemented border security measures to prevent attacks by the FDLR.“These measures are not intended to support the AFC/M23, which does not need them,” he said, “but to protect Rwanda from repeated attacks by FDLR genocidal groups, which are supported by Kinshasa.”

Despite these explanations, Araud maintained that the FDLR was no longer active, describing its members as either dead or retired. Nduhungirehe dismissed the argument, pointing to the June 27, 2025 Washington peace agreement, signed by Rwanda and the DRC with U.S. support.

Under the agreement, the DRC government committed to dismantling the FDLR, while Rwanda agreed to lift its security measures once the threat is neutralized. The accord also provides for cooperation on refugee repatriation between the two countries.

“If the ‘FDLR genocidaires are dead or retired,’” Nduhungirehe asked, “why did the DRC government agree to destroy them?” He further referenced CONOPS and OPORDs-operational plans overseen by the United States-which outline step-by-step stages for dismantling the group, from identifying bases to disarmament, capture, and reintegration.

The foreign minister concluded that the FDLR remains an active organization, rooted in genocidal ideology, and warned that 31 years after its fighters fled into the DRC, the group continues to recruit new members, posing an ongoing threat to regional stability.

title: Kagame Accuses Burundi of Concealing Military Role in Eastern DRC Conflict
excerpt: Kigali - President Paul Kagame has accused Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye of attempting to conceal Burundi’s military involvement in the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), revealing that…
title_en: Kagame Accuses Burundi of Concealing Military Role in Eastern DRC Conflict
excerpt_en: Kigali - President Paul Kagame has accused Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye of attempting to conceal Burundi’s military involvement in the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), revealing that…
body_en:
Kigali - President Paul Kagame has accused Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye of attempting to conceal Burundi’s military involvement in the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), revealing that Burundian soldiers were captured during fighting in North Kivu despite official denials from Bujumbura.

Burundi initially deployed troops to eastern DRC as part of the East African Community Regional Force (EACRF) in North Kivu province, where their mandate was to separate warring parties and facilitate peace negotiations.

In late 2023, however, President Félix Tshisekedi ordered the expulsion of the EACRF from Masisi territory in North Kivu. While the regional force was withdrawn, Burundian troops remained, but with a new mandate to fight the M23 movement, according to President Kagame.

Following the EACRF’s departure, the Burundian government increased its military presence in North Kivu under a bilateral agreement with the DRC, coinciding with the deployment of troops from the Southern African Development Community (SADC).

Speaking after the swearing-in of leaders on December 11, 2025, President Kagame said he personally telephoned President Ndayishimiye to question why Burundian forces were still operating in the DRC after the EACRF had been expelled.

According to Kagame, Ndayishimiye initially justified the deployment by citing security threats emanating from Congo, particularly in southern areas such as Uvira and Minembwe. Kagame said he then questioned why Burundian troops were operating in North Kivu, far from those locations.

“He said to me, ‘Who told you that we have troops there?’” Kagame recounted. “I told him that I had been shown evidence, but that I wanted to hear it from him directly. He replied, ‘Whoever told you lied. There are no troops in your north.’ I said, ‘That’s good. Since you say so, I believe you.’”

Kagame said that shortly after the conversation, numerous Burundian soldiers were captured during fighting in North Kivu. He added that during subsequent regional heads-of-state meetings, the Burundian president continued to deny that his troops had been captured.

“Many were captured in the fighting,” Kagame said. “When this was raised in meetings, some leaders denied it, while others confronted them, asking, ‘If you deny your soldiers, do you no longer want them?’”

By January 2025, Kagame said, M23 fighters had seized areas previously held by Burundian forces in North Kivu, and had also pushed them out of parts of South Kivu, including Minova, Kavumu, and Bukavu.

President Kagame further claimed that Burundi deployed more than 20,000 troops across eastern and central DRC, including South Kivu, Kalemie in Tanganyika province, Kindu in Maniema, Kisangani in Tshopo, and Walikale in North Kivu.

He alleged that Burundian forces have killed numerous Congolese civilians, particularly in the Minembwe area, which links the territories of Uvira, Fizi, and Mwenga, accusing them of using heavy long-range weapons and combat drones.

President Kagame criticized the international community for what he described as silence and inaction in the face of Burundi’s alleged military operations in the eastern DRC, warning that the situation continues to fuel instability and civilian suffering in the region.

title: Rwanda Criticizes International Community Over Security Concerns and Killings of Banyamulenge
excerpt: United Nations, New York - Rwanda has accused the international community of ignoring its security concerns and the ongoing killings of Banyamulenge civilians in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), warning that…
title_en: Rwanda Criticizes International Community Over Security Concerns and Killings of Banyamulenge
excerpt_en: United Nations, New York - Rwanda has accused the international community of ignoring its security concerns and the ongoing killings of Banyamulenge civilians in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), warning that…
body_en:
United Nations, New York - Rwanda has accused the international community of ignoring its security concerns and the ongoing killings of Banyamulenge civilians in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), warning that inaction is exacerbating instability in the Great Lakes region.

Speaking on December 12, 2025, during a meeting of the UN Security Council, Rwanda’s Ambassador to the United Nations, Martin Ngoga, addressed discussions on the recent clashes between the AFC/M23 and the Congolese Armed Forces in the Rusizi Valley, South Kivu province.

Ambassador Ngoga said the renewed fighting was triggered by the violation of a ceasefire by the DRC government, Burundian forces, Wazalendo militias, the FDLR terrorist group, and foreign mercenaries. He added that Kinshasa had openly signaled its intention to breach the ceasefire, despite commitments made during peace talks in Doha, Qatar.

Ngoga stated that since 2017, Congolese forces and Mai Mai armed groups have carried out sustained attacks against the Banyamulenge community in the Minembwe region, destroying approximately 85% of their villages.

He further accused DRC, Burundian, and Mai Mai forces of blocking trade routes used by the Banyamulenge to access markets, a tactic he described as a deliberate attempt to starve the population.

According to the ambassador, airstrikes and drone attacks on Banyamulenge villages and refugee camps, including in Mikenke, have intensified in 2025, yet have drawn little international response.

“Between March and December this year, there were 15 airstrikes in this area, and no one is talking about it,” Ngoga said. “I and other members of this Council have raised this issue here repeatedly, but nothing has been done.”

He questioned whether the UN Security Council had been unaware of the situation or had chosen to ignore it, urging members to examine conditions in South Kivu prior to the latest fighting.

Ambassador Ngoga reaffirmed Rwanda’s support for sovereignty and territorial integrity, but warned that the FDLR, which he said is backed by the DRC government, poses a direct threat to Rwanda’s security.

He said the alleged support for the FDLR by Kinshasa is backed by irrefutable evidence, including multiple UN Security Council resolutions calling for the group’s dismantling.

“The existence of the FDLR undermines all of this,” he said. “The evidence is irrefutable, the resolutions are irrefutable, and the truth is that the DRC government has supported the FDLR for 30 years. The FDLR does not only threaten Rwanda’s sovereignty, it threatens its existence and its people.”

Ngoga warned that while the international community may appear indifferent to the security of Rwanda or the Congolese Tutsi communities facing violence, it should not go so far as to accuse victims of violence when they act in self-defense.

He welcomed the peace and economic development cooperation agreement signed by Rwanda and the DRC on December 4, 2025, noting that both sides committed to continue supporting political dialogue between the DRC government and the AFC/M23.

Ambassador Ngoga concluded that dialogue remains the only viable path to resolving regional conflicts, but stressed that genuine political will from all parties is essential to achieve lasting peace.

title: Rwanda Accredits Ambassador to Eritrea
excerpt: Asmara, Eritrea - December 9, 2025 - Ambassador Ernest Rwamucyo officially presented his credentials to President Isaias Afwerki to represent Rwanda in Eritrea.
title_en: Rwanda Accredits Ambassador to Eritrea
excerpt_en: Asmara, Eritrea - December 9, 2025 - Ambassador Ernest Rwamucyo officially presented his credentials to President Isaias Afwerki to represent Rwanda in Eritrea.
body_en:
Asmara, Eritrea - December 9, 2025 - Ambassador Ernest Rwamucyo officially presented his credentials to President Isaias Afwerki to represent Rwanda in Eritrea. The ceremony took place at the Eritrean Presidential Palace in Asmara.

During the meeting, Ambassador Rwamucyo assured President Afwerki of Rwanda’s commitment to maintaining and strengthening bilateral relations between the two countries and their peoples.

In response, President Afwerki reaffirmed Eritrea’s support for Ambassador Rwamucyo in his new role.

Currently, Ambassador Rwamucyo also represents Rwanda in Kenya and Somalia, with his base in Nairobi, Kenya.

title: Prime Minister Nsengiyumva Delivers Message from President Kagame to President Ouattara
excerpt: Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, December 7, 2025 - Prime Minister Dr. Justin Nsengiyumva arrived in Côte d’Ivoire to attend the inauguration of President Alassane Ouattara, delivering a special message from Rwandan President Paul Kagame.
title_en: Prime Minister Nsengiyumva Delivers Message from President Kagame to President Ouattara
excerpt_en: Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, December 7, 2025 - Prime Minister Dr. Justin Nsengiyumva arrived in Côte d’Ivoire to attend the inauguration of President Alassane Ouattara, delivering a special message from Rwandan President Paul Kagame.
body_en:
Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, December 7, 2025 - Prime Minister Dr. Justin Nsengiyumva arrived in Côte d’Ivoire to attend the inauguration of President Alassane Ouattara, delivering a special message from Rwandan President Paul Kagame. He was welcomed by the Ivorian Prime Minister, Robert Beugré Mambé, before the ceremony.

President Alassane Ouattara won a fourth term in the October 25, 2025 elections, securing 89.7% of the vote. His challengers, Jean-Louis Billon, former Minister of Commerce, and Simone Gbagbo, wife of former President Laurent Gbagbo, received 3% and 2.4%, respectively. All parties acknowledged Ouattara’s victory.

Dr. Nsengiyumva’s visit underscores the strong diplomatic ties between Rwanda and Côte d’Ivoire, particularly in trade and investment. President Kagame previously met with Ouattara in May 2025 during the Africa CEO Forum in Abidjan, a gathering of African and global business leaders, investors, and politicians.

The visit reflects Rwanda’s commitment to maintaining and strengthening bilateral relations with Côte d’Ivoire under Ouattara’s leadership.

title: Rwanda Raises Concerns Over DRC’s Compliance with Washington Agreement
excerpt: Kigali December 9, 2025 - Rwanda has expressed concern over the Democratic Republic of Congo’s (DRC) apparent unwillingness to comply with the Washington peace agreement.
title_en: Rwanda Raises Concerns Over DRC’s Compliance with Washington Agreement
excerpt_en: Kigali December 9, 2025 - Rwanda has expressed concern over the Democratic Republic of Congo’s (DRC) apparent unwillingness to comply with the Washington peace agreement.
body_en:
Kigali December 9, 2025 - Rwanda has expressed concern over the Democratic Republic of Congo’s (DRC) apparent unwillingness to comply with the Washington peace agreement. Government Spokesperson Yolande Makolo stated that the DRC continues to violate the ceasefire agreed with the M23 coalition and shows no willingness to honor the terms of the agreement signed in Washington, United States, on December 4, 2025.

The Washington agreement follows earlier principles signed in Doha on November 15, 2025, between the DRC and AFC/M23, which included:

Restoration of government institutions and services in the eastern DRC, implemented in phases in collaboration with both parties.

Interim security measures to maintain public order and protect civilians.

Despite these agreements, the coalition of FARDC, Burundian forces, and allied groups including Wazalendo and FDLR continued attacks against AFC/M23 positions.

On December 9, 2025, DRC Government Spokesperson Patrick Muyaya claimed on X that Rwanda violated the Washington agreement by supporting attacks in Kamanyola and other areas leading to Uvira.

In response, Yolande Makolo rejected these claims, stating that the DRC itself has failed to respect the truce:

“Enough of your lies. The DRC cannot control the truce while you are violating the truce and are unwilling to abide by the Washington agreement that the DRC signed.”

Rwanda emphasized that the AFC/M23 continued to capture key areas in South Kivu from FARDC and Burundian forces, highlighting ongoing tensions and non-compliance with the peace framework.

This situation underscores the fragility of the ceasefire in eastern DRC and Rwanda’s insistence on honoring the agreements signed in Washington.

title: Gen (Rtd) Kabarebe Hands Over Power to Dr. Usta Kayitesi at MINAFFET
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda - Gen (Rtd) James Kabarebe, former Secretary of State in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation (MINAFFET), officially handed over power to Dr.
title_en: Gen (Rtd) Kabarebe Hands Over Power to Dr. Usta Kayitesi at MINAFFET
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - Gen (Rtd) James Kabarebe, former Secretary of State in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation (MINAFFET), officially handed over power to Dr.
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - Gen (Rtd) James Kabarebe, former Secretary of State in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation (MINAFFET), officially handed over power to Dr. Usta Kayitesi, his successor, on the evening of Thursday, December 11, 2025. The handover coincided with the swearing-in ceremony of Dr. Kayitesi and other newly appointed officials before the Head of State at the National Assembly.

Following the transition, Gen (Rtd) Kabarebe was appointed Senior Security Advisor in the Office of the President, while Dr. Kayitesi, previously a Senator, assumed the role of Secretary of State at MINAFFET. Dr. Kayitesi had been replaced in the Senate by Dr. Muligande Charles.

At the ceremony, the newly appointed Permanent Secretary of MINAFFET, Fidelis Mironko, also handed over his powers to his successor, Mukeka Clementine. The event was presided over by the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Amb. Olivier Jean Patrick Nduhungirehe.

During the oath-taking, President Kagame urged the new leaders, including Dr. Kayitesi, to fulfill their responsibilities diligently, emphasizing that the country’s challenges require extraordinary effort.

Dr. Usta Kayitesi has an extensive background in governance and education. He served as Director General of the Rwanda Governance Board (RGB) from July 2019 to August 2024, following a tenure as Deputy Director General. He holds a Master of Laws, was a lecturer at the National University of Rwanda (NUR), and served as Chancellor of the University of Rwanda, College of Arts and Social Sciences (CASS).

Notably, Dr. Kayitesi was among seven commissioners tasked with assisting Parliament in revising the Constitution in 2015, serving as Vice-Chairman of the committee.

Gen (Rtd) James Kabarebe, born in 1959 in Uganda, rose to prominence as Chief of Staff of the Rwandan Armed Forces from 2002 to 2010, becoming the first to hold the post for an extended period. Educated at St. Henry’s College Kitovu and Makerere University, he earned a Bachelor of Arts in Economics and Political Science. He retired as one of the few Four-Star Generals in Rwanda’s military and has held numerous high-level positions in both the military and government.

title: Minister Nduhungirehe Condemns DRC Violations of Ceasefire
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda - Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation Amb. Olivier Nduhungirehe declared that it is impossible for a truce to be respected by one side while the other openly violates it, and the international…
title_en: Minister Nduhungirehe Condemns DRC Violations of Ceasefire
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation Amb. Olivier Nduhungirehe declared that it is impossible for a truce to be respected by one side while the other openly violates it, and the international…
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation Amb. Olivier Nduhungirehe declared that it is impossible for a truce to be respected by one side while the other openly violates it, and the international community fails to act. Speaking to ambassadors on December 12, 2025, Minister Nduhungirehe said that the DRC government has officially announced plans to attack AFC/M23 positions to reclaim lost territory, despite an existing ceasefire agreement mediated by the Government of Qatar.

He explained that during a joint security meeting in Washington D.C. on November 7, Rwanda and the DRC agreed that attacks should stop, but hostilities resumed afterwards, with Burundian troops participating. The attacks also targeted civilians, including Banyamulenge communities in Minembwe.

Minister Nduhungirehe criticized the deployment of 20,000 Burundian troops in South Kivu, noting that in addition to engaging AFC/M23, they have blocked roads used by Banyamulenge residents to access markets, effectively attempting to starve civilians. He stressed that their presence at the DRC’s request does not give them the right to attack civilians.

Rwanda has reportedly informed diplomatic missions of these violations, with most promising to convey the message to Kinshasa and Bujumbura, though the minister claimed the warnings were either not delivered or not strong enough to alter the situation.

“A ceasefire is an agreement between warring parties to stop fighting while waiting for a resolution. It cannot be respected by one side while the other avoids responsibility,” he said.

Minister Nduhungirehe expressed surprise that the international community only raised concerns when AFC/M23 defended itself, despite ongoing attacks by DRC forces, including warplanes and drones targeting civilians and AFC/M23 positions.

He also criticized recent statements by the United States, the United Kingdom, France, and Germany, which condemned AFC/M23’s occupation of South Kivu and accused Rwanda of aiding the group, while ignoring the DRC government’s attacks.

Economy and Tech.

title: Rwanda - Government Launches Major Overhaul of Kigali Public Transport System
excerpt: Kigali, November 28, 2025 - Rwanda is set to introduce a new public transport system in Kigali City, following Cabinet approval of a major reform designed to improve efficiency, safety, and passenger experience.
title_en: Rwanda - Government Launches Major Overhaul of Kigali Public Transport System
excerpt_en: Kigali, November 28, 2025 - Rwanda is set to introduce a new public transport system in Kigali City, following Cabinet approval of a major reform designed to improve efficiency, safety, and passenger experience.
body_en:
Kigali, November 28, 2025 - Rwanda is set to introduce a new public transport system in Kigali City, following Cabinet approval of a major reform designed to improve efficiency, safety, and passenger experience. The reform will be implemented through a newly created government agency, Ecofleet Solutions, announced Eng. Uwihanganye Jean de Dieu, the State Secretary for Infrastructure.

Under the new model, buses will not stay longer than 10 minutes at terminals and will not exceed three minutes at bus stops, ensuring faster turnaround and reducing congestion. Ecofleet Solutions will manage and coordinate nearly all aspects of public transport in the capital.

According to officials, Ecofleet Solutions will supervise the daily operation of public transport vehicles, while private companies will continue supplying buses, employing drivers, and monitoring day-to-day service delivery.

Ensuring enough buses are available and well distributed across routes.

Monitoring vehicle conditions and mechanical readiness.

Planning routes and tracking bus movements in real time.

Guaranteeing that buses are clean, safe, and properly maintained.

Managing infrastructure such as bus stops, terminals, and repair centers.

Overseeing all transport company contracts.

Importantly, companies will be paid based on service quality, not on the number of passengers transported - a shift intended to end the overcrowding that has long characterized Kigali’s buses.

All passengers will pay electronically, with funds going directly to Ecofleet before being redistributed to operators. The current Tap & Go system will remain in use during the trial phase, but authorities are considering bank cards and Mobile Money as additional payment options.

Those caught paying cash will face strict penalties, as inspections are being intensified.

Drivers will receive new contracts linking their pay to performance indicators, including:

Respecting the three-minute and 10-minute station limits.

Keeping buses clean.

Respectful treatment of passengers.

Safe and responsible driving.

“Ecofleet will buy, lease, operate, and manage the buses. Drivers will be paid based on meeting targets - profits are no longer their concern,” Eng. Uwihanganye explained.

Technology at the Heart of the System

The reform places heavy emphasis on technology, including:

Real-time tracking of buses.

Electronic passenger information boards at bus stops.

Mobile tools showing bus arrival times, routes, and nearby stops.

A modern system for detecting breakdowns and ensuring rapid repair.

The digital platform is expected to be fully operational within one month.

The government aims for all public transport vehicles in Kigali to be electric by the end of 2026. Ecofleet Solutions will roll out:

190 electric buses owned by the agency,

110 leased electric buses from private operators.

The program will launch on December 2, 2025, starting with the Downtown-Sonatubes-Remera corridor. Additional priority lanes will follow on Sonatubes-Gahanga and Nyabugogo-Gishushu routes.

During rainy seasons, buses will receive priority passage to reduce congestion and maximize movement of large passenger volumes.

This reform builds on previous government commitments. A pilot project on the Kabuga-Nyabugogo route in May 2025 tested technological and operational strategies now being scaled citywide.

During the 18th National Dialogue Council in February 2023, the government pledged to introduce over 300 new buses into Kigali’s fleet. Around 200 buses have already arrived, purchased with public funding and delivered in phases.

Eng. Uwihanganye urged residents to trust the new system, promising buses that are safer, on time, less crowded, and more comfortable.

“We want people to leave their cars, avoid relying on motorbikes, and choose these buses,” he said. “Our goal is punctual, reliable, and modern public transport for everyone.”

title: RwandAir Launches Flights to Zanzibar and Mombasa
excerpt: Kigali, December 1, 2025 - Rwandan national carrier RwandAir has officially launched flights to Zanzibar Island in Tanzania and Mombasa in Kenya.
title_en: RwandAir Launches Flights to Zanzibar and Mombasa
excerpt_en: Kigali, December 1, 2025 - Rwandan national carrier RwandAir has officially launched flights to Zanzibar Island in Tanzania and Mombasa in Kenya.
body_en:
Kigali, December 1, 2025 - Rwandan national carrier RwandAir has officially launched flights to Zanzibar Island in Tanzania and Mombasa in Kenya. The inaugural flight departed Kigali International Airport in Kanombe on Monday, December 1, 2025, aboard a Boeing B737-800NG bound for Zanzibar.

Upon arrival at Abeid Amani Karume International Airport, the aircraft was greeted with a ceremonial water salute, a traditional gesture to welcome a new aircraft or a new destination.

The Zanzibar route marks a new destination for RwandAir, while flights to Mombasa have resumed after last operating in 2019. With these additions, RwandAir now serves three routes in Tanzania and two in Kenya.

RwandAir CEO Yvonne Makolo emphasized the strategic importance of the expansion:“Returning to Mombasa and launching flights to Zanzibar is another step in our expansion journey. By expanding our reach in East Africa, it helps position Kigali as a key destination, provides our customers with more opportunities to explore the region, and opens doors for trade, tourism, and continued cooperation in East Africa.”

Flights between Zanzibar and Mombasa will operate four times a week - on Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays, and Sundays - enhancing connectivity within East Africa.

title: Rwanda’s Central Bank Reports Reduced Pressure on Rwandan Franc
excerpt: Kigali, December 1, 2025 - The Central Bank of Rwanda (BNR) has reported a decrease in depreciation pressure on the Rwandan Franc (FRw) against the US Dollar from January to September 2025, signaling improved currency…
title_en: Rwanda’s Central Bank Reports Reduced Pressure on Rwandan Franc
excerpt_en: Kigali, December 1, 2025 - The Central Bank of Rwanda (BNR) has reported a decrease in depreciation pressure on the Rwandan Franc (FRw) against the US Dollar from January to September 2025, signaling improved currency…
body_en:
Kigali, December 1, 2025 - The Central Bank of Rwanda (BNR) has reported a decrease in depreciation pressure on the Rwandan Franc (FRw) against the US Dollar from January to September 2025, signaling improved currency stability compared to the 2024/2025 fiscal year.

The announcement was made when BNR Governor Soraya Hakuziyaremye presented the annual report for 2024/2025 and outlined plans for 2025/2026 to both houses of Parliament.

Governor Hakuziyaremye noted that in 2024/25, the Rwandan franc depreciated by 9.6% against the US dollar, compared to 12.5% by June 2024. In 2025, the depreciation had slowed to 4.2% as of September, with hopes of remaining under 5% by year-end.

“The pressure on the Rwandan franc has decreased due to regulations limiting foreign currency payments and reforms implemented this year,” she said. The governor also cited the weakening of the US dollar internationally and a lower US central bank interest rate as contributing factors.

BNR indicated the current exchange rates as 1446 FRw for buyers of US dollars and 1456 FRw for sellers.

Hakuziyaremye highlighted other measures supporting currency stability, including increased exports of coffee, tea, and precious metals, foreign investment, and tourism, which generate additional foreign exchange.

The National Institute of Statistics (NISR) reported that market prices in September 2025 rose by 7.3% compared to September 2024, slightly up from 7.1% in August. Key contributors to the increase included:

Housing, water, electricity, gas, and other fuels: +4.1%

Governor Hakuziyaremye said that while inflation continues, the measures taken over the past three years have mitigated extreme depreciation and strengthened confidence in the Rwandan Franc.

title: RwandAir Kigali-Mombasa Route to Boost Trade and Tourism, Says Kenyan Ambassador
excerpt: Mombasa, December 1, 2025 - The Kenyan Ambassador to Rwanda, Janet Mwawasi Oben, has highlighted the potential of the new RwandAir Kigali-Mombasa route to strengthen trade and tourism between the two countries.
title_en: RwandAir Kigali-Mombasa Route to Boost Trade and Tourism, Says Kenyan Ambassador
excerpt_en: Mombasa, December 1, 2025 - The Kenyan Ambassador to Rwanda, Janet Mwawasi Oben, has highlighted the potential of the new RwandAir Kigali-Mombasa route to strengthen trade and tourism between the two countries.
body_en:
Mombasa, December 1, 2025 - The Kenyan Ambassador to Rwanda, Janet Mwawasi Oben, has highlighted the potential of the new RwandAir Kigali-Mombasa route to strengthen trade and tourism between the two countries. She spoke during the launch ceremony at Moi International Airport in Mombasa, where she was among the executives on board the inaugural flight.

Ambassador Mwawasi described the route as “very important for Kenya,” noting that a direct connection to Mombasa, a major tourist destination, has long been awaited. “It will boost tourism and trade,” she said.

RwandAir’s Chief Commercial Officer, Fouad Caunhye, emphasized that resuming flights to Mombasa is essential for reconnecting countries, markets, and communities.

On Monday, December 1, 2025, RwandAir also launched flights to Zanzibar Island in Tanzania, expanding its regional network. The Zanzibar-Mombasa route will operate four times a week - on Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays, and Sundays.

The airline resumes Mombasa flights after a pause since 2019, while Zanzibar represents a new destination, enhancing East African connectivity and trade opportunities.

title: Rwanda to Boost Tungsten Production with $60 Million Processing Plant
excerpt: Rulindo, December 2025 - Trinity Nyakabingo Mine, Rwanda’s leading tungsten producer, is set to construct a mineral processing plant in Shyorongi Sector, Rulindo District, expected to be operational by October 2027.
title_en: Rwanda to Boost Tungsten Production with $60 Million Processing Plant
excerpt_en: Rulindo, December 2025 - Trinity Nyakabingo Mine, Rwanda’s leading tungsten producer, is set to construct a mineral processing plant in Shyorongi Sector, Rulindo District, expected to be operational by October 2027.
body_en:
Rulindo, December 2025 - Trinity Nyakabingo Mine, Rwanda’s leading tungsten producer, is set to construct a mineral processing plant in Shyorongi Sector, Rulindo District, expected to be operational by October 2027. The plant, designed to process 60 tons of mined materials per hour, is projected to cost between $44 million (63 billion Frw) and $60 million (87 billion Frw).

Currently, Trinity Nyakabingo Mine produces over 1,000 tons of tungsten annually and employs 1,763 workers. With the new facility, production is expected to triple to 3,000 tons per year. Justin Uwiringiyimana, director of the mine, explained the significance:"This factory will help process ore that was previously discarded because it is not visible to the naked eye. Using improved methods, we expect to increase yields from 40% to 75% of mined sand, potentially producing 250 to 300 tons per month."

Rwanda’s Trinity Metals, one of the country’s largest mining companies, exported 2,226 tons of tungsten, gas, and coltan in 2024, earning $15 million in the first 11 months of 2025. By 2029, the company plans to export 5,201 tons of ore from its Musha, Rutongo, and Nyakabingo mines.

Additional processing plants are underway: a 12.5-ton per hour plant in Musha and a 30-ton per hour plant in Rutongo, with 12-ton per hour plants being installed at other sites. These expansions are part of Trinity Metals’ $100 million investment plan in Rwanda’s mining sector over the coming years.

title: Rwanda Showcases Development Model at Economic Forum in Brazzaville
excerpt: BRAZZAVILLE - Rwanda participated as guest of honor at the 30th “Vendredis de Carrefour” forum, held in Brazzaville from December 4-5, 2025, bringing together more than 700 economic and development experts from Central…
title_en: Rwanda Showcases Development Model at Economic Forum in Brazzaville
excerpt_en: BRAZZAVILLE - Rwanda participated as guest of honor at the 30th “Vendredis de Carrefour” forum, held in Brazzaville from December 4-5, 2025, bringing together more than 700 economic and development experts from Central…
body_en:
BRAZZAVILLE - Rwanda participated as guest of honor at the 30th “Vendredis de Carrefour” forum, held in Brazzaville from December 4-5, 2025, bringing together more than 700 economic and development experts from Central Africa.

Speaking at the forum, NAEB Director General Claude Bizimana highlighted Rwanda’s development strategy, citing growth in agricultural exports, industrialization, and job creation driven by the “Made in Rwanda” policy and food self-sufficiency programs launched in 2017.

Bizimana also underscored the impact of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), noting that Rwanda’s exports have doubled since early implementation. Rwandan coffee and tea were showcased at the event, allowing participants to sample products now gaining international markets.

The annual forum, organized by Think-Tank Carrefour, focuses on policy-driven strategies to boost domestic production, economic growth, and regional development across Africa.

title: Mysterious Insect Threatens Corn Harvest in Rusizi District
excerpt: RUSIZI, Rwanda - December 7, 2025 - Corn farmers in the Bugarama Valley, Rusizi District, are raising alarm over a strange insect infestation attacking maize crops ahead of harvest, raising fears of major losses this…
title_en: Mysterious Insect Threatens Corn Harvest in Rusizi District
excerpt_en: RUSIZI, Rwanda - December 7, 2025 - Corn farmers in the Bugarama Valley, Rusizi District, are raising alarm over a strange insect infestation attacking maize crops ahead of harvest, raising fears of major losses this…
body_en:
RUSIZI, Rwanda - December 7, 2025 - Corn farmers in the Bugarama Valley, Rusizi District, are raising alarm over a strange insect infestation attacking maize crops ahead of harvest, raising fears of major losses this season.

Farmers report that the insect penetrates the corn cob, causing the grain to rot before harvest. “It cuts the cob in half and the maize rots immediately,” said Marie Rose Mukabera, a farmer with 40 years of experience, who noted the pest has appeared in the area over the past two years.

Another farmer, Julienne Kabagwira, said delayed rains worsen the infestation, calling for government support to provide pesticides and spraying equipment, as manual control has proven ineffective.

Bugarama Sector Executive Secretary Daniel Ndamyimana confirmed that local authorities are working with agricultural officers to urgently secure pesticides from RAB and organize a community spraying exercise to protect the crops.

title: Rwanda Showcases Coffee and Tea at Marrakech Festival, Expands International Market
excerpt: Marrakech, Morocco - Rwanda has made a strong debut at the first-ever Marrakech Coffee & Tea Festival, highlighting its coffee and tea industries to an international audience.
title_en: Rwanda Showcases Coffee and Tea at Marrakech Festival, Expands International Market
excerpt_en: Marrakech, Morocco - Rwanda has made a strong debut at the first-ever Marrakech Coffee & Tea Festival, highlighting its coffee and tea industries to an international audience.
body_en:
Marrakech, Morocco - Rwanda has made a strong debut at the first-ever Marrakech Coffee & Tea Festival, highlighting its coffee and tea industries to an international audience. The festival, launched on December 6, 2025, was chaired by Moroccan Minister of Infrastructure and Water, Nizar Baraka, alongside Rwandan Ambassador to Morocco, Umutoni Shakilla.

A total of 16 Rwandan businessmen presented high-quality coffee and tea, renowned globally for their unique taste and originality, providing an opportunity for Rwandan investors to forge partnerships and explore international markets.

Robinah Uwera, Head of Public Relations at the National Development Bank (RDB), said, “The first round of talks went well, with Rwandan businessmen engaging investors in discussions that promise new steps in cooperation.”

Coffee and tea exports have been a significant contributor to Rwanda’s growing export earnings.

Tea earned $114.88 million in 2023/2024, a 7.1% increase from the previous year.

Coffee earned $116.1 million in 2024/2025, up 47.4%, with projections of $192 million this year from 32,000 tons of exports.

NAEB CEO Claude Bizimana emphasized Rwanda’s global recognition:“Rwanda is known worldwide for its high-altitude Arabica Bourbon coffee, which is famous for its unique taste and quality. We also continue to lead in international markets with CTC, orthodox, and green tea.”

Rwanda has over 400,000 coffee farmers, each managing around 300 trees, and has prioritized diverse coffee processing methods to cater to specialized consumer markets.

The festival provided a platform for trade and collaboration.

PSF COO Faustin Karasira said, “The Moroccan market has welcomed our products. We see great opportunities to partner with CCISM in Marrakech, increase trade, and build sustainable development.”

Discussions will continue, including trade visits and talks on market expansion, allowing Rwandan traders to expand networks, attract buyers, and explore investment opportunities.

“We did not come just to display products; we came to build relationships. Morocco welcomed us, and we are confident that the discussions will generate tangible business,” Karasira added.

The festival highlighted Rwanda’s ambition to strengthen cooperation, attract buyers, and sign export and processing agreements, positioning the country as a key player in the global coffee and tea market.

title: Rutsiro: Closed Mine Collapses, Killing Three, One Dead
excerpt: Rutsiro, Rwanda - A mine that had been inactive for 17 years collapsed on three people engaged in illegal mining in Nyabirasi Sector, Terimbere Cell, Gihinga Village, resulting in the death of Dushimimana Jean Bosco…
title_en: Rutsiro: Closed Mine Collapses, Killing Three, One Dead
excerpt_en: Rutsiro, Rwanda - A mine that had been inactive for 17 years collapsed on three people engaged in illegal mining in Nyabirasi Sector, Terimbere Cell, Gihinga Village, resulting in the death of Dushimimana Jean Bosco…
body_en:
Rutsiro, Rwanda - A mine that had been inactive for 17 years collapsed on three people engaged in illegal mining in Nyabirasi Sector, Terimbere Cell, Gihinga Village, resulting in the death of Dushimimana Jean Bosco, 36, on the morning of Monday, December 8, 2025.

Family sources said that Dushimimana, an experienced miner of precious metals, previously ran a licensed cooperative but was found engaging in illegal mining at the time of the accident.

Mpirwa Migabomu, Executive Secretary of Nyabirasi Sector, confirmed the incident, explaining that two of the miners escaped after witnessing their colleague collapse.

“The news is true. They went to dig in a mine that was closed in 2008. Two of them saw their colleague fall and ran to alert others, but due to the danger, he died when rocks fell on him during rescue efforts,” said Mpirwa.

He added that the area where the miners were working had soft and unstable ground, making it highly dangerous for illegal mining activities.

Mpirwa urged residents to avoid illegal mining, warning that it carries a high risk of death and potential legal consequences.

The collapsed mine had formerly been operated by KODUBU Company, which ceased activities in 2008.

title: Arsenal Signs Long-Term Sponsorship Deal with Deel, Replacing Visit Rwanda
excerpt: London, UK - English Premier League club Arsenal has announced a long-term partnership with Payroll and HR services provider Deel, replacing Visit Rwanda after eight years.
title_en: Arsenal Signs Long-Term Sponsorship Deal with Deel, Replacing Visit Rwanda
excerpt_en: London, UK - English Premier League club Arsenal has announced a long-term partnership with Payroll and HR services provider Deel, replacing Visit Rwanda after eight years.
body_en:
London, UK - English Premier League club Arsenal has announced a long-term partnership with Payroll and HR services provider Deel, replacing Visit Rwanda after eight years. The announcement was made on Friday, December 12, 2025, and the new sponsor will appear on the club’s left shirt sleeve starting from the 2026/27 season.

The deal was brokered by Darren Dein, son of former Arsenal shareholder and vice-chairman David Dein, and signed by Arsenal Chief Commercial Officer Juliet Slot, with approval from CEO Stan Kroenke.

Slot stated, “We are delighted to welcome Deel to the Arsenal family. They are a talented and innovative team. Their investment will help us achieve our goals and grow as a club.”

Arsenal’s contract with Visit Rwanda, which began in 2018 and was valued at $13.4 million annually, came to an end last month. Rwanda earned $647 million from tourism in 2024, with a goal of reaching $1 billion by 2029.

Rwanda has also pursued partnerships in the United States, including with the LA Clippers (NBA) and LA Rams (NFL). President Paul Kagame emphasized that if the Arsenal partnership is rejected, the funds could be redirected to other investments, noting that more sports collaborations are expected.

title: Rwanda - “Brush Your Teeth, I Beg You”: Health Minister Urges Stronger Hygiene Culture
excerpt: Nyamagabe, November 29, 2025 - Rwanda’s Minister of Health, Dr. Sabin Nsanzimana, has once again called on Rwandans to strengthen their culture of physical hygiene, emphasizing the crucial role of oral hygiene in overall health.
title_en: Rwanda - “Brush Your Teeth, I Beg You”: Health Minister Urges Stronger Hygiene Culture
excerpt_en: Nyamagabe, November 29, 2025 - Rwanda’s Minister of Health, Dr. Sabin Nsanzimana, has once again called on Rwandans to strengthen their culture of physical hygiene, emphasizing the crucial role of oral hygiene in overall health.
body_en:
Nyamagabe, November 29, 2025 - Rwanda’s Minister of Health, Dr. Sabin Nsanzimana, has once again called on Rwandans to strengthen their culture of physical hygiene, emphasizing the crucial role of oral hygiene in overall health. The Minister delivered this message on Saturday while participating in Umuganda, the monthly community service activity, in the district of Nyamagabe.

Speaking to residents, Dr. Nsanzimana stressed that cleanliness begins with the body, reminding citizens that maintaining hygiene is part of Rwanda’s national identity.

“Cleanliness has many levels. The first starts with the body. No one should leave home without washing, because it goes against our culture that must be rooted in hygiene,” he said.

The Minister placed particular emphasis on oral hygiene, warning that neglecting it can lead to tooth decay, tooth loss, and other long-term complications when treatment is delayed or ineffective.

“Please brush your teeth,” he urged. “You should not leave the house without brushing, because you end up giving the people you meet the smell of what you ate - sometimes from days before.”

Dr. Nsanzimana stressed that even households with limited means should prioritize buying a toothbrush and toothpaste, noting that these items remain affordable and essential.

Health experts explain that failing to clean one’s teeth regularly exposes the mouth to infections such as cavities, gum disease, and other oral health complications. The National Oral Health Survey 2021 ranked dental caries among the ten most common health problems in the country.

title: Rwanda: Challenges and Support for People with Disabilities
excerpt: Nyabihu District - December 3, 2025 - During the International Day of Persons with Disabilities, themed “Support a society that does not discriminate against people with disabilities - Let’s promote a better life”…
title_en: Rwanda: Challenges and Support for People with Disabilities
excerpt_en: Nyabihu District - December 3, 2025 - During the International Day of Persons with Disabilities, themed “Support a society that does not discriminate against people with disabilities - Let’s promote a better life”…
body_en:
Nyabihu District - December 3, 2025 - During the International Day of Persons with Disabilities, themed “Support a society that does not discriminate against people with disabilities - Let’s promote a better life”, participants highlighted ongoing challenges faced by persons with disabilities (PWDs) in Rwanda.

Social stigma and perceived incompetence: Many PWDs report that societal attitudes, including from family members, undermine their ability to work and participate fully in community life.

Insufficient capital: Lack of financial resources continues to limit the capacity of PWDs to start or expand businesses.

Mujawimana Sifa, a blind artisan from Jenda Sector, Nyabihu, has been sewing balls and crafts to support herself. She noted that while her work provides a livelihood, many people still consider her incompetent and are unwilling to buy her products.

Serugendo Bazira, from Musanze District, learned soap-making to support his household. While he can meet basic needs, he faces obstacles expanding his business and gaining recognition for his skills.

Emmanuel Ndayisaba, Executive Secretary of the National Council for Persons with Disabilities (NCPD), pledged assistance for PWDs who want to expand their businesses, emphasizing outreach to those still facing barriers.

Governor Ntibitura Jean Bosco highlighted the role of PWDs in national development and the government’s commitment to providing support as resources allow.

Rwanda has 544,100 people with disabilities across various categories.

Summary: Despite strong legal frameworks and government efforts, PWDs in Rwanda still face social, economic, and cultural barriers. Initiatives are underway to provide financial, technical, and social support to enhance their economic participation and social inclusion.

title: Rwanda Reports Breakthrough in HIV Treatment and Prevention
excerpt: Kigali, December 9, 2025 - The Minister of Health, Dr. Sabin Nsanzimana, has highlighted remarkable progress in the fight against HIV/AIDS, citing the news of a 10th person remaining asymptomatic for over six years…
title_en: Rwanda Reports Breakthrough in HIV Treatment and Prevention
excerpt_en: Kigali, December 9, 2025 - The Minister of Health, Dr. Sabin Nsanzimana, has highlighted remarkable progress in the fight against HIV/AIDS, citing the news of a 10th person remaining asymptomatic for over six years…
body_en:
Kigali, December 9, 2025 - The Minister of Health, Dr. Sabin Nsanzimana, has highlighted remarkable progress in the fight against HIV/AIDS, citing the news of a 10th person remaining asymptomatic for over six years without taking antiretroviral drugs (ARVs). This milestone follows advances with the lenacapavir Yeztugo drug, which prevents HIV infection.

Dr. Nsanzimana said, “While lenacapavir is a major step in the treatment of HIV, another 10th person has been asymptomatic for a long time and is not taking ARVs. After undergoing a stem cell transplant, this person has been asymptomatic for more than six years.” He noted that removing the virus from its reservoirs in the body may be key to achieving a real cure.

A stem cell transplant involves replacing a patient’s damaged blood cells with healthy ones from a donor. This procedure helps strengthen the immune system and replace the cells in which the HIV virus hides, allowing patients to remain symptom-free without medication. However, it requires careful medical supervision due to risks such as infections, organ failure, or death.

The lenacapavir Yeztugo drug, developed by Gilead Sciences, is administered twice a year and has undergone multiple trials. The third phase trial, conducted in South Africa and Uganda with 5,300 participants aged 16-24, demonstrated no detectable HIV in recipients. Additional trials in Argentina, Brazil, Mexico, Peru, South Africa, and the United States confirmed high protection among gay men, transgender people, and other high-risk groups, showing 99.9% effectiveness in preventing HIV infection.

According to MINISANTE statistics, Rwanda sees about 3,200 new HIV infections and 2,600 AIDS-related deaths annually. Thanks to recent interventions, new infections have decreased by 82% and AIDS-related deaths have dropped by 86%, signaling major progress in the fight against HIV/AIDS in the country.

title: Gisagara: Three Arrested for Alleged Murder of 21-Year-Old Man
excerpt: Gisagara, November 30, 2025 - The Rwanda National Police in Gisagara District have arrested three men suspected of killing and slitting the throat of a 21-year-old man, Abijuru Athanase.
title_en: Gisagara: Three Arrested for Alleged Murder of 21-Year-Old Man
excerpt_en: Gisagara, November 30, 2025 - The Rwanda National Police in Gisagara District have arrested three men suspected of killing and slitting the throat of a 21-year-old man, Abijuru Athanase.
body_en:
Gisagara, November 30, 2025 - The Rwanda National Police in Gisagara District have arrested three men suspected of killing and slitting the throat of a 21-year-old man, Abijuru Athanase. The incident occurred between the night of November 29 and 30 in Shyombo Village, Nyabikenke Cell, Kigembe Sector, as the victim was leaving his shop to go to Nyaruteja Health Centre.

Abijuru, who worked as a butcher and ran a canteen at Umurangara Health Centre, was reportedly ambushed and attacked in a secluded area of a coffee plantation, far from residential homes. The assailants allegedly robbed him before cutting his neck.

Nyabikenke Cell Leader, Antoinette Nyirakamana, stated that the attack occurred in a dark, isolated spot, highlighting the brutality of the crime.

According to Southern Province Police Spokesperson, CIP Kamanzi Hassan, the killing was likely motivated by revenge. Authorities noted that the suspects had been tracking the victim for some time and were reportedly upset because Abijuru had recently imprisoned their child.

“Those suspected of involvement in his death have been arrested, including a man who had threatened him previously, vowing to take revenge,” CIP Kamanzi said.

The victim’s body was taken to Kibirizi Hospital for a post-mortem examination, while the suspects are detained at Nyanza Police Station as investigations continue.

Abijuru leaves behind a wife and one child, marking a tragic loss for his family.

title: RIB Returns Over 431 Stolen Phones Worth 94.5 Million FRw
excerpt: Kigali, December 1, 2025 - The Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) has returned 431 phones valued at 94.5 million FRw to their owners.
title_en: RIB Returns Over 431 Stolen Phones Worth 94.5 Million FRw
excerpt_en: Kigali, December 1, 2025 - The Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) has returned 431 phones valued at 94.5 million FRw to their owners.
body_en:
Kigali, December 1, 2025 - The Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) has returned 431 phones valued at 94.5 million FRw to their owners. The devices, seized since May 2025, included both medium-range and high-end models, some of which had been stolen from traders who unknowingly purchased them.

The returned phones were taken from various locations, including provinces and Kigali, notably Nyabugogo Railway Station. The thefts occurred in diverse circumstances, including:

127 phones stolen from bicycles and buses

80 phones stolen directly from owners

63 phones stolen through fraud

59 phones taken from homes

Others stolen in public spaces, such as weddings, bars, and by motorcyclists tricking passengers

In the process of recovering the devices, 23 suspects were arrested, while 12 traders who had purchased stolen phones agreed to return them and were not prosecuted.

RIB spokesperson Dr. Murangira Thierry urged the public to remain vigilant and protect their devices.“Negligence makes it easy for thieves. At one wedding, for example, 10 phones were stolen,” he said. He advised people paying motorcyclists with phones to maintain distance to reduce the risk of theft.

Dr. Murangira also warned against buying stolen phones, highlighting the financial losses and legal risks involved. “Those who buy stolen phones not only lose money, but also encourage theft,” he said, explaining that stolen devices often circulate through buyers who cannot trace the original thief.

Regarding used phone dealers, RIB clarified that they are not a problem if they document ownership, ensuring transparency and preventing the circulation of stolen devices.

Finally, Dr. Murangira asked victims of theft to exercise patience, emphasizing that recovering stolen phones is complex, but protecting devices remains crucial.

title: Tragic Domestic Dispute in Rulindo Leaves Six Children Orphaned
excerpt: Rulindo, Rwanda - December 4, 2025
title_en: Tragic Domestic Dispute in Rulindo Leaves Six Children Orphaned
excerpt_en: Rulindo, Rwanda - December 4, 2025
body_en:
Rulindo, Rwanda - December 4, 2025

A domestic dispute in Kisaro Sector, Murama Cell ended in tragedy when a 52-year-old man killed his 40-year-old wife, who then ingested lethal drugs, authorities report. The incident stemmed from a disagreement over a plot of land the husband wanted to sell, which his wife had refused.

The couple’s six children were left orphaned. Local officials confirmed that the couple had a history of conflicts over property and finances.

The bodies were discovered early Thursday morning by a worker, and transported to Byumba Hospital for autopsy before burial. Authorities called on residents to resolve family disputes peacefully and reminded couples about equal property rights.

title: Capt Peninah Mutoni Sentenced to Five Years in APR Funds Misuse Case
excerpt: Nyamirambo, December 5, 2025 - The Nyamirambo Military Court has sentenced Capt Peninah Mutoni to five years in prison and a fine of 3 million Rwf for misappropriation of state funds, fraud, and forging official…
title_en: Capt Peninah Mutoni Sentenced to Five Years in APR Funds Misuse Case
excerpt_en: Nyamirambo, December 5, 2025 - The Nyamirambo Military Court has sentenced Capt Peninah Mutoni to five years in prison and a fine of 3 million Rwf for misappropriation of state funds, fraud, and forging official…
body_en:
Nyamirambo, December 5, 2025 - The Nyamirambo Military Court has sentenced Capt Peninah Mutoni to five years in prison and a fine of 3 million Rwf for misappropriation of state funds, fraud, and forging official documents.

The ruling comes as part of the trial involving Maj Vincent Murigande, Capt Peninah Mutoni, and Capt Peninah Umurungi, who faced charges of criminal conspiracy and misuse of state funds linked to various APR FC trips, including the September 2024 visit to Egypt for a CAF Champions League match against Pyramids FC.

The court acquitted Maj Vincent Murigande of misappropriation of state funds, but found him guilty of failing to report a serious or felony crime, resulting in a one-year prison sentence and a fine of 300,000 Rwf.

Capt Peninah Umurungi was not charged with complicity in any crimes related to the misappropriation of government funds or the forgery of documents.

The Ministry of Defense confirmed the court's decision, highlighting that the ruling upheld justice while differentiating the levels of responsibility among the accused.

title: IGP Namuhoranye Warns Foreigners Against Violence in Rwanda
excerpt: Kigali, December 5, 2025 - The Inspector General of Police (IGP), CG Felix Namuhoranye, warned that foreigners who attack Rwandans or other foreigners in the country will face severe measures, including deportation or…
title_en: IGP Namuhoranye Warns Foreigners Against Violence in Rwanda
excerpt_en: Kigali, December 5, 2025 - The Inspector General of Police (IGP), CG Felix Namuhoranye, warned that foreigners who attack Rwandans or other foreigners in the country will face severe measures, including deportation or…
body_en:
Kigali, December 5, 2025 - The Inspector General of Police (IGP), CG Felix Namuhoranye, warned that foreigners who attack Rwandans or other foreigners in the country will face severe measures, including deportation or prosecution and imprisonment.

The statement was made during a press conference held by the Rwanda Police and RIB, which reviewed the security situation in 2025. Police statistics indicate that crimes decreased by 15.7% compared to 2024, with a particular focus on combating violent crimes and theft.

IGP Namuhoranye emphasized that foreigners committing acts of abuse or violence in Kigali are immediately sent back to their countries, while others considered culpable are prosecuted and imprisoned.

He explained, “If you look at the decisions taken to send these people back home… many have already been sent home. Those who we arrest, they go to prison.”

According to the Rwandan Police, in the 12 months leading to August 2025, 64 foreigners were deported for assault and battery, and over 240 were prosecuted for various crimes.

title: Rwanda’s Judiciary Reports Over 20,000 Cases Resolved Through Mediation
excerpt: Kigali - Rwanda’s Chief Justice and President of the Supreme Council of the Judiciary, Domitilla Mukantaganzwa, has revealed that more than 20,000 cases have been resolved through mediation, underscoring its growing…
title_en: Rwanda’s Judiciary Reports Over 20,000 Cases Resolved Through Mediation
excerpt_en: Kigali - Rwanda’s Chief Justice and President of the Supreme Council of the Judiciary, Domitilla Mukantaganzwa, has revealed that more than 20,000 cases have been resolved through mediation, underscoring its growing…
body_en:
Kigali - Rwanda’s Chief Justice and President of the Supreme Council of the Judiciary, Domitilla Mukantaganzwa, has revealed that more than 20,000 cases have been resolved through mediation, underscoring its growing role in the country’s justice system.

Speaking at a press conference on December 8, 2025, Mukantaganzwa urged Rwandans not to view mediation as a new or foreign concept, emphasizing that it is deeply rooted in Rwandan tradition and culture.

“Mediation existed long before colonial rule,” she said. “Rwandans had their own ways of establishing the truth, punishing wrongdoing, reconciling families, and resolving disputes. This is not something new; it is who we are and how we live.”

According to the Chief Justice, mediation and plea bargaining have significantly eased the burden on courts, allowing disputes to be settled more quickly, at lower cost, and with less social tension.

Despite the progress, Mukantaganzwa acknowledged that public perception remains a challenge, noting that some citizens still believe mediation allows offenders to escape punishment.

“Changing mindsets takes time,” she said. “Many people are used to a system of winners and losers, or to pursuing personal victory even in cases that are not truly theirs.”

She added that successful mediation requires a willingness to embrace alternative approaches that promote efficiency, cost savings, and social harmony, rather than prolonged and expensive litigation.

Mukantaganzwa stressed that effective mediation requires the active involvement of all sectors, including judicial institutions, law enforcement, and communities. However, she acknowledged that mediation has been less effective in family separation cases, where deep-rooted disputes can lead to further complications.

She also criticized traditional litigation as costly and time-consuming, encouraging Rwandans to feel empowered to resolve disputes outside formal courtrooms where appropriate.

The President of the High Council of Commerce, Clotilde Mukamurera, said mediation has also delivered results in commercial disputes, with 320 business cases resolved through mediation in the past year alone.

The 2024/2025 Judiciary Annual Report shows that disputes worth 7.8 billion Rwandan francs (Rwf) were settled through mediation, highlighting its role as a tool for speedy and effective justice. The report notes that mediation allows disputing parties to play a central role in finding durable solutions, restoring working relationships, and continuing economic activities without prolonged court proceedings.

Support for mediation has also come from law enforcement agencies. Colonel Pacifique Kayigamba Kabanda, Secretary General of the Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB), said the Public Prosecution Service fully backs the mediation process.

He revealed that since 2025, the RIB has resolved 2,800 cases through mediation, further reinforcing its importance as an alternative dispute resolution mechanism within Rwanda’s justice system.

title: Rusizi: National Human Rights Commission Opens Channels for Citizens’ Complaints
excerpt: Rusizi District, Rwanda - The National Human Rights Commission (NCHR) has announced that it will receive citizens’ complaints directly in Rusizi and Nyamasheke districts, offering a streamlined way to address grievances…
title_en: Rusizi: National Human Rights Commission Opens Channels for Citizens’ Complaints
excerpt_en: Rusizi District, Rwanda - The National Human Rights Commission (NCHR) has announced that it will receive citizens’ complaints directly in Rusizi and Nyamasheke districts, offering a streamlined way to address grievances…
body_en:
Rusizi District, Rwanda - The National Human Rights Commission (NCHR) has announced that it will receive citizens’ complaints directly in Rusizi and Nyamasheke districts, offering a streamlined way to address grievances without going through other channels. The announcement was made on December 7, 2025, during the closing of a public walk in Kamembe Sector, attended by local authorities, NCHR staff, and citizens.

Umurungi Providence, President of NCHR, said the initiative aims to promote human rights and provide a direct platform for complaints.

“Our responsibilities include promoting human rights through education and receiving problems that institutions have not been able to resolve. We have staff here, you can call on them while we still have this space here. We are here until Wednesday,” Umurungi said, emphasizing that citizens will now be able to submit complaints immediately and begin follow-up processes without relying on electronic correspondence, phone calls, or visits to the Kigali office.

The NCHR’s outreach activities in the districts include speaking with youth in schools and groups, visiting farms, and other community engagement programs. Umurungi highlighted the link between sports and human rights, noting that playing sports teaches respect for oneself and others.

“When you play, there is respect and you know your rights and those of your neighbor. This means that the way you respect your neighbor, the same way he respects yours,” he said.

Sindayiheba Phanuel, Mayor of Rusizi District, added that sports should be a responsibility, emphasizing its role in preventing gender-based violence and combating human trafficking, where young men and women are often lured with false promises of jobs or scholarships abroad.

The NCHR will receive complaints at People’s Assemblies in Gihundwe, Giheke, Bweyeye, and Nkombo sectors on October 9, 2025. The commission’s presence in Rusizi and Nyamasheke will last from December 2-10, 2025, providing additional engagement through school and community visits.

The 2024/2025 NCHR activity report shows that of 654 complaints followed up, 575 (87.9%) were resolved, 27 (4.1%) are still under investigation, and 52 (8%) remain unresolved. The initiative underscores the NCHR’s commitment to promoting human rights, resolving grievances efficiently, and ensuring that citizens have direct access to justice and support.

title: Rutsiro: Police Officer Shoots Two People Before Taking His Own Life
excerpt: Rutsiro District - The National Police and the Criminal Investigation Department have opened an investigation after a police officer on duty in Rutsiro District shot two people before taking his own life.
title_en: Rutsiro: Police Officer Shoots Two People Before Taking His Own Life
excerpt_en: Rutsiro District - The National Police and the Criminal Investigation Department have opened an investigation after a police officer on duty in Rutsiro District shot two people before taking his own life.
body_en:
Rutsiro District - The National Police and the Criminal Investigation Department have opened an investigation after a police officer on duty in Rutsiro District shot two people before taking his own life. The incident occurred on the night of December 10, 2025, in Boneza Sector, Bushaka Cell, Bikono Village.

According to reports, the officer shot an employee of the District Security Support Unit (Dasso) and a local resident. Eyewitnesses indicated that the victims appeared to have been involved in an argument prior to the shooting.

Western Province Police Spokesperson, SP Sylvestre Twajamahoro, confirmed the incident:

“It is true that the police officer shot two people, injuring them (one resident and a Dasso employee) and then shot himself to death. An investigation into the cause of the shooting has been launched.”

The injured individuals were transported to CHUK University Hospital for treatment, while the body of the officer was taken to the National Forensic Science and Technology Institute (RFI) for examination.

Authorities continue to investigate the circumstances leading to this tragic incident.

title: Young Rwandans Escape FDLR Violence, Return Home After Decades in DRC
excerpt: Rwanda - Residents who returned to Rwanda after years in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have recounted harrowing experiences under the FDLR, a group responsible for the Genocide against the Tutsi.
title_en: Young Rwandans Escape FDLR Violence, Return Home After Decades in DRC
excerpt_en: Rwanda - Residents who returned to Rwanda after years in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have recounted harrowing experiences under the FDLR, a group responsible for the Genocide against the Tutsi.
body_en:
Rwanda - Residents who returned to Rwanda after years in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have recounted harrowing experiences under the FDLR, a group responsible for the Genocide against the Tutsi. On December 11, 2025, 337 Rwandans crossed the main border at ‘La Corniche’, sharing stories of abuse and survival.

Those who refused to join the FDLR were reportedly killed instantly, according to testimonies. Munyambanza Lazaro, 74, who fled Rwanda in 1994, described leaving behind his adult children and wife in the southern Ngungu area.

He said, “We thought we would only go home if God willed it. We didn’t raise animals, we didn’t farm, because of the FDLR and Wazalendo. Young men were chased and killed if they refused to work with them. As old men, we were spared, but when they encouraged us that peace had returned to Rwanda, we came home.”

Nzabirinda Reuben, 60, who left Mukingo Commune, Ruhengeri Prefecture, in 1994, fled to Kitchanga after facing insecurity from FDLR and FARDC collaborators, who would destroy crops and kill those unwilling to cooperate. “That’s when we decided to return home, though I regret the time spent in the forests of DRC,” he said. Reuben explained that young men were indoctrinated, fearing they would be labeled FDLR members upon return, while some joined the genocidal group.

Elie Ntakirutimana, 19, born in eastern Congo, could not complete school due to FDLR violence, but hopes to resume education in a safer environment.

Ishimwe Pacifique, Deputy Mayor of Rubavu District for social affairs, welcomed the returnees, calling them “the strength the country had lost.” He emphasized that they would receive assistance to rebuild their lives, including registration, basic necessities, and financial support.

The returnees were sent to Kijote Transitional Camp in Nyabihu District, where they will receive services before reintegration. Financial support includes $188 for returnees over 18, $113 for those under 18, and basic food supplies worth 45,000 Rwf per person.

Reuben explained that young men were indoctrinated, fearing they would be labeled FDLR members upon return, while some joined the genocidal group.

Elie Ntakirutimana, 19, born in eastern Congo, could not complete school due to FDLR violence, but hopes to resume education in a safer environment.

Ishimwe Pacifique, Deputy Mayor of Rubavu District for social affairs, welcomed the returnees, calling them “the strength the country had lost.” He emphasized that they would receive assistance to rebuild their lives, including registration, basic necessities, and financial support.

The returnees were sent to Kijote Transitional Camp in Nyabihu District, where they will receive services before reintegration. Financial support includes $188 for returnees over 18, $113 for those under 18, and basic food supplies worth 45,000 Rwf per person.

title: Rwanda Urged to Strengthen Human Rights Efforts, Focus on Prison Overcrowding
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda - Dr. Andrews Kananga, Director General of the Legal Aid Forum (LAF), has called on Rwanda to strengthen efforts to respect human rights, particularly by addressing prison overcrowding.
title_en: Rwanda Urged to Strengthen Human Rights Efforts, Focus on Prison Overcrowding
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - Dr. Andrews Kananga, Director General of the Legal Aid Forum (LAF), has called on Rwanda to strengthen efforts to respect human rights, particularly by addressing prison overcrowding.
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - Dr. Andrews Kananga, Director General of the Legal Aid Forum (LAF), has called on Rwanda to strengthen efforts to respect human rights, particularly by addressing prison overcrowding. He made the remarks on December 12, 2025, during the International Human Rights Day celebration in Kigali.

Dr. Kananga highlighted that in January 2026, Rwanda will participate in the Universal Periodic Review (UPR) at the UN Human Rights Council. The LAF, together with civil society partners, submitted a report detailing areas for improvement, including the need to align prison populations with facility capacity.

“In the report we prepared, we emphasized that although prison overcrowding has decreased, efforts must continue to ensure detention conditions respect international and national standards,” said Dr. Kananga.

According to the National Human Rights Commission, the prison population in Rwanda fell by 24.3% in 2024/2025, decreasing from 134.3% to 110% of capacity compared to the previous year. Commission President Umurungi Providence stressed that human rights are a continuous effort: “No country can claim to have fully achieved human rights. We have made progress, but the journey continues.”

Wibabara Charity, Head of the Department of International Justice and International Cooperation at the Ministry of Justice, reminded citizens that all people are equal before the law and that human rights are inviolable, emphasizing Rwanda’s ongoing legal reforms to strengthen protections.

The LAF also highlighted other areas requiring attention, including:

Improving the lives of rural women and increasing their visibility in local and national governance.

Combating human trafficking through youth-targeted awareness campaigns, particularly addressing risks on social media.

Continued protection of children’s rights and vulnerable populations.

Dr. Kananga concluded that respecting human rights is a continuous journey, requiring sustained efforts across multiple sectors to ensure all citizens are treated with dignity and fairness.

title: AFC/M23 Accuses Burundi of Planning Airstrikes on Civilians in DRC
excerpt: North and South Kivu, November 30, 2025 - The AFC/M23 coalition, engaged in fighting in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), has accused Burundi of planning airstrikes on civilians in the provinces of South Kivu and…
title_en: AFC/M23 Accuses Burundi of Planning Airstrikes on Civilians in DRC
excerpt_en: North and South Kivu, November 30, 2025 - The AFC/M23 coalition, engaged in fighting in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), has accused Burundi of planning airstrikes on civilians in the provinces of South Kivu and…
body_en:
North and South Kivu, November 30, 2025 - The AFC/M23 coalition, engaged in fighting in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), has accused Burundi of planning airstrikes on civilians in the provinces of South Kivu and North Kivu.

According to AFC/M23 spokesman Lawrence Kanyuka, the attacks carried out by Sukhoi-25 fighter jets and drones are coordinated from Burundi, which he described as a secret base for DRC government forces.

“All the attacks on densely populated areas and conflict zones are planned in Burundi,” Kanyuka said. “This country has become a base for the Kinshasa government forces.”

Kanyuka further alleged that Burundi is directly involved, with its army and the Imbonerakure militia participating in attacks on Congolese civilians.

Bertrand Bisimwa, deputy leader of AFC/M23 in charge of political affairs, condemned these operations as crimes against humanity and war crimes.

Since October 2025, the Burundian army has reportedly closed roads connecting residents of the Minembwe area in the territories of Fizi, Uvira, and Mwenga, limiting access to markets and medical care. A Burundian army spokesman, Brig Gen Gaspard Baratuza, confirmed the closures but accused local Banyamulenge communities of collaborating with enemies - a claim denied by human rights groups.

Since November 26, Burundian troops have engaged AFC/M23 forces in Mwenga territory, attempting to target positions held by DRC government forces. On November 30, AFC/M23 reported significant Burundian casualties, with many soldiers buried in mass graves and the wounded transported to Kisangani in Tshopo province for treatment.

title: 199 Congolese Refugees Flee to Rwanda Amid South Kivu Clashes
excerpt: Rusizi District, Rwanda - December 3, 2025 - 199 Congolese refugees, mainly women and children, crossed into Rwanda’s Kamanyola border fleeing armed clashes in South Kivu, DRC.
title_en: 199 Congolese Refugees Flee to Rwanda Amid South Kivu Clashes
excerpt_en: Rusizi District, Rwanda - December 3, 2025 - 199 Congolese refugees, mainly women and children, crossed into Rwanda’s Kamanyola border fleeing armed clashes in South Kivu, DRC.
body_en:
Rusizi District, Rwanda - December 3, 2025 - 199 Congolese refugees, mainly women and children, crossed into Rwanda’s Kamanyola border fleeing armed clashes in South Kivu, DRC.

Residents reported hearing gunfire and heavy machine-gun fire from the DRC from the morning of December 2 until the evening of December 3. The refugees were received by Rusizi District authorities and are currently housed at the Nyarushishi Temporary Camp, where basic necessities are being provided.

The mayor, Sindayiheba Phanuel, confirmed the refugees will remain in the camp until their homes are safe to return to. By the evening of December 3, the gunfire reportedly ceased. Local Rwandans working across the border noted that while no casualties were observed, fear disrupted normal work activities.
