title: Rwanda and Tanzania Hold 14th Border Military Commanders’ Meeting to Strengthen Security
excerpt: Ngoma District, Rwanda - December 4, 2025 ; The Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF) and Tanzanian Defence Forces (TPDF) concluded the 14th Border Military Commanders’ Meeting, held from December 2 to 4, 2025 in Ngoma District…
title_en: Rwanda and Tanzania Hold 14th Border Military Commanders’ Meeting to Strengthen Security
excerpt_en: Ngoma District, Rwanda - December 4, 2025 ; The Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF) and Tanzanian Defence Forces (TPDF) concluded the 14th Border Military Commanders’ Meeting, held from December 2 to 4, 2025 in Ngoma District…
body_en:
Ngoma District, Rwanda - December 4, 2025 ; The Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF) and Tanzanian Defence Forces (TPDF) concluded the 14th Border Military Commanders’ Meeting, held from December 2 to 4, 2025 in Ngoma District, Eastern Province, reaffirming their commitment to security and stability along the Rwanda-Tanzania border.

These quarterly meetings provide a platform for military commanders to review security developments, discuss illegal cross-border activities, and implement measures to protect border communities. Delegates also assessed progress since the 13th meeting in Ngara, Tanzania, in September 2025.

Maj Gen Ruki Karusisi, Commander of the RDF 5th Division, emphasized that military cooperation is a “strong pillar” that reinforces the good relations between the two countries. “Our cooperation is based on mutual respect, professionalism, and a shared vision to maintain peace in the region,” he said.

Brig Gen Gabriel Elias Kwiligwa, Commander of the TPDF 202nd Brigade, highlighted the constructive and professional engagement, noting that the meeting strengthens trust and joint security cooperation between the two armed forces.

The meeting concluded with a renewed commitment to information sharing, conducting joint patrols, and maintaining close coordination between neighboring forces. Both sides stressed that this collaboration is essential for regional peace and the well-being of border communities.

The 14th meeting underscores the long-standing partnership between Rwanda and Tanzania in promoting peace, security, and shared stability in the region.

title: Maj Gen Alex Kagame Applauds Inkeragutabara for Contribution to Community Development
excerpt: Southern Province, Rwanda - December 4, 2025
title_en: Maj Gen Alex Kagame Applauds Inkeragutabara for Contribution to Community Development
excerpt_en: Southern Province, Rwanda - December 4, 2025
body_en:
Southern Province, Rwanda - December 4, 2025

The Commander-in-Chief of the Inkeragutabara, Major General Alex Kagame, met with members from five districts of the Southern Province-Huye, Gisagara, Nyamagabe, Nyanza, and Nyaruguru-to commend their role in community development. The meeting aimed to exchange ideas, address challenges, and provide updates on RDF initiatives supporting local development.

This session follows a previous meeting held in Muhanga District on November 28, 2025, designed to strengthen collaboration between Inkeragutabara leaders and veterans in their communities, enabling better identification of local issues and solutions.

Maj Gen Kagame praised the rescuers for their conduct and dedication to the population’s welfare. He emphasized the importance of self-reliance, encouraging them to actively combat poverty rather than rely solely on government assistance.

He also urged the Inkeragutabara to continue serving as role models, uphold ethics, and avoid criminal activities that would draw RDF investigations. Despite their retired status, he reminded them of their responsibility to maintain local security, reaffirming Rwanda’s safe environment.

title: Rwanda Records 130 Deaths and 1,800 Houses Destroyed in 2025 Disasters
excerpt: Kigali, December 5, 2025 - The Rwandan Police announced that while the overall security situation in Rwanda remained stable in 2025, the country faced several disasters that claimed 130 lives and destroyed 1,800 houses.
title_en: Rwanda Records 130 Deaths and 1,800 Houses Destroyed in 2025 Disasters
excerpt_en: Kigali, December 5, 2025 - The Rwandan Police announced that while the overall security situation in Rwanda remained stable in 2025, the country faced several disasters that claimed 130 lives and destroyed 1,800 houses.
body_en:
Kigali, December 5, 2025 - The Rwandan Police announced that while the overall security situation in Rwanda remained stable in 2025, the country faced several disasters that claimed 130 lives and destroyed 1,800 houses. The announcement was made during a press conference with the Rwandan Investigation Bureau (RIB).

The Director General of Public Security and Public Order, CP G. Rumanzi, revealed that over 230 fires occurred across the country this year, with police actively intervening to extinguish them.

"Disasters killed 130 people nationwide, including those struck by lightning, victims of landmines, landslides, and floods," said CP Rumanzi. He added that 1,100 hectares of crops were damaged and over 100 livestock perished due to these incidents.

On a positive note, traffic accidents decreased by 2.4% compared to the previous year. CP Rumanzi attributed accidents to unsafe driving behaviors, including speeding, using mobile phones while driving, and driving under the influence of alcohol.

The Rwanda National Police continues to implement the “Turindane Tugereyo Amashoro” campaign, aiming to further reduce road accidents and enhance public safety.

title: Over 750 Congolese Flee to Rwanda Amid M23-DRC Fighting
excerpt: Rusizi District, December 5, 2025 - More than 750 Congolese refugees have crossed into Rwanda to escape ongoing clashes between the M23 rebels and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) Army, according to the Rusizi…
title_en: Over 750 Congolese Flee to Rwanda Amid M23-DRC Fighting
excerpt_en: Rusizi District, December 5, 2025 - More than 750 Congolese refugees have crossed into Rwanda to escape ongoing clashes between the M23 rebels and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) Army, according to the Rusizi…
body_en:
Rusizi District, December 5, 2025 - More than 750 Congolese refugees have crossed into Rwanda to escape ongoing clashes between the M23 rebels and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) Army, according to the Rusizi District Administration.

The refugees arrived at the Bugarama border and were largely sent to the Nyarushishi Temporary Camp, with a few opting to travel to Bukavu. Mayor Sindayiheba Phanuel reported that 60% of the refugees are children, 35% are women, and 5% are men. None of the arrivals were reported injured.

The refugees fall into three categories: those seeking transit back to the DRC via Bukavu, asylum seekers staying in the Nyarushishi camp, and individuals who had traveled to the DRC for business but returned due to the conflict. Medical assistance is being provided by the National Institute of Health where needed.

Mayor Sindayiheba reassured the public that Rwanda remains secure, despite the sound of distant gunfire near the border. “Security is being maintained, and development work continues. Rwanda is a peaceful country and welcomes refugees,” he said.

Refugees shared harrowing experiences of the conflict. Riziki Alphonsine, fleeing from Katogota, described houses collapsing from bombs, while Rachel Maombi, from Kamanyola, fled with her husband and five children after bullets struck their home. Maombi, who has a leg disability, stressed the urgent need for peace so they could safely return home.

title: Burundian Lt Col Athanase Minani Killed in DRC Fighting
excerpt: South Kivu, DRC, December 5, 2025 - Lieutenant Colonel Athanase Minani, commander of the 8th Battalion of the Burundian Army deployed in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), was reportedly killed during…
title_en: Burundian Lt Col Athanase Minani Killed in DRC Fighting
excerpt_en: South Kivu, DRC, December 5, 2025 - Lieutenant Colonel Athanase Minani, commander of the 8th Battalion of the Burundian Army deployed in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), was reportedly killed during…
body_en:
South Kivu, DRC, December 5, 2025 - Lieutenant Colonel Athanase Minani, commander of the 8th Battalion of the Burundian Army deployed in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), was reportedly killed during clashes with the AFC/M23 rebel group in the Luvungi area. The fighting also claimed the lives of several of his bodyguards.

Lt Col Minani, a former member of the Ex FAB, had been promoted to Lieutenant Colonel in July 2025. His death was confirmed by the Burundian Human Rights Commission and Pacifique Nininahazwe, leader of the FOCODE organization, who described him as the highest-ranking Burundian soldier killed in this conflict. Neither the Burundian Army nor AFC/M23 has officially confirmed the report.

The AFC/M23 resumed heavy attacks after learning of planned offensives by DRC, Burundian, and Wazalendo forces in Kamanyola. On December 2, AFC/M23 fighters opened fire, disrupting the DRC coalition. Subsequent shelling by DRC and Burundian forces targeted Kamanyola, destroying homes and infrastructure and killing three civilians.

Since the morning of December 5, joint forces have been attacking areas in Uvira Territory, including Katogota, Kamanyola, and Luvungi Gurupoma, prompting many residents to flee to Sange, Runingu, Ndolera, and Uvira city.

The Deputy Leader of AFC/M23, Bertrand Bisimwa, stated that Burundian forces are shelling densely populated areas, including schools, churches, and markets, resulting in civilian casualties, including children. Social media footage posted by Bisimwa shows extensive destruction near Ngomo Mountain in Kamanyola.

The fighting continues despite the Rwanda-DRC peace agreement signed on December 4, 2025, which AFC/M23 claims does not apply to them.

title: Over 1,000 Congolese Refugees Flee to Rwanda Amid Escalating South Kivu Conflict
excerpt: Rusizi District, December 6, 2025 - Rusizi District authorities report that in just three days, more than 1,000 Congolese refugees have crossed into Rwanda via the Bugarama border due to intensified fighting in South…
title_en: Over 1,000 Congolese Refugees Flee to Rwanda Amid Escalating South Kivu Conflict
excerpt_en: Rusizi District, December 6, 2025 - Rusizi District authorities report that in just three days, more than 1,000 Congolese refugees have crossed into Rwanda via the Bugarama border due to intensified fighting in South…
body_en:
Rusizi District, December 6, 2025 - Rusizi District authorities report that in just three days, more than 1,000 Congolese refugees have crossed into Rwanda via the Bugarama border due to intensified fighting in South Kivu Province.

From December 3 to 5, a total of 1,122 refugees arrived, with the first group of 199 people arriving on December 3. The majority of the refugees come from conflict-affected areas such as Kamanyola in Walungu Territory, where civilians have been killed and homes destroyed by ongoing clashes between the Democratic Republic of Congo Army (FARDC) and the M23 movement.

Mayor of Rusizi District, Sindayiheba Phanuel, provided a breakdown of the refugee arrivals on December 5: 923 Congolese crossed the border, including 643 children, 90 men, and 190 women. Among them, 263 refugees returned to the DRC via the Rusizi I border to Bukavu, while 755 were taken to the Nyarushishi Temporary Camp for shelter and assistance.

The district authorities ensured that children received vaccinations, including for measles, and that all refugees were tested and provided with medical support for any health concerns.

Local residents report hearing gunfire from the border areas, though no attacks have occurred within Rwanda. Mukankakaka Noëlla, a local accommodation worker, said:

"There was a break of about 10 to 15 minutes, and a single distant explosion could be heard. Some refugees from remote mountains arrived yesterday but were quickly accommodated. Daily activities on the road continued as usual."

The flow of refugees decreased on December 6 as minibuses transported newcomers to the Nyarushishi camp, compared to previous days when multiple large buses and minibuses were used.

Rusizi District, December 6, 2025 - Rusizi District authorities report that in just three days, more than 1,000 Congolese refugees have crossed into Rwanda via the Bugarama border due to intensified fighting in South Kivu Province.

From December 3 to 5, a total of 1,122 refugees arrived, with the first group of 199 people arriving on December 3. The majority of the refugees come from conflict-affected areas such as Kamanyola in Walungu Territory, where civilians have been killed and homes destroyed by ongoing clashes between the Democratic Republic of Congo Army (FARDC) and the M23 movement.

Mayor of Rusizi District, Sindayiheba Phanuel, provided a breakdown of the refugee arrivals on December 5: 923 Congolese crossed the border, including 643 children, 90 men, and 190 women. Among them, 263 refugees returned to the DRC via the Rusizi I border to Bukavu, while 755 were taken to the Nyarushishi Temporary Camp for shelter and assistance.

The district authorities ensured that children received vaccinations, including for measles, and that all refugees were tested and provided with medical support for any health concerns.

Local residents report hearing gunfire from the border areas, though no attacks have occurred within Rwanda. Mukankakaka Noëlla, a local accommodation worker, said:

"There was a break of about 10 to 15 minutes, and a single distant explosion could be heard. Some refugees from remote mountains arrived yesterday but were quickly accommodated. Daily activities on the road continued as usual."

The flow of refugees decreased on December 6 as minibuses transported newcomers to the Nyarushishi camp, compared to previous days when multiple large buses and minibuses were used.

title: AFC/M23 Says Burundian Forces “Learned a Lesson” in South Kivu Fighting
excerpt: SOUTH KIVU - AFC/M23 spokesperson Lt Col Willy Ngoma has warned Burundian forces involved in fighting in eastern DR Congo that they have “learned a lesson,” following clashes in Kamanyola, Katogota, and Kiziba.
title_en: AFC/M23 Says Burundian Forces “Learned a Lesson” in South Kivu Fighting
excerpt_en: SOUTH KIVU - AFC/M23 spokesperson Lt Col Willy Ngoma has warned Burundian forces involved in fighting in eastern DR Congo that they have “learned a lesson,” following clashes in Kamanyola, Katogota, and Kiziba.
body_en:
SOUTH KIVU - AFC/M23 spokesperson Lt Col Willy Ngoma has warned Burundian forces involved in fighting in eastern DR Congo that they have “learned a lesson,” following clashes in Kamanyola, Katogota, and Kiziba.

Ngoma accused Burundian troops of fighting alongside Congolese forces, Wazalendo militias, and the FDLR, and of firing artillery from Burundian territory. The AFC/M23 claims the shelling killed civilians and triggered mass displacement toward Rwanda and Bukavu.

On the night of December 4, AFC/M23 fighters launched counterattacks on Burundian army positions, killing and capturing several soldiers, including Lt Col Athanase Minani, a battalion commander.

Speaking to Mama Urwagasabo TV, Ngoma said Burundian reinforcements had crossed the border in recent days, warning that AFC/M23 would not tolerate what it called foreign aggression. He issued strong threats against Burundian troops entering Congolese territory.

Meanwhile, AFC/M23 continues to expand its control, having captured Rurambo, Lubarika, and, on December 6, the Luvungi center in Uvira territory.

title: Mocímboa da Praia Residents Thank Rwandan Forces for Restoring Security
excerpt: MOCÍMBOA DA PRAIA, Mozambique - Residents of Mocímboa da Praia in Cabo Delgado Province have publicly thanked the Rwandan Armed Forces (RDF) for restoring peace and security after years of terrorist violence.
title_en: Mocímboa da Praia Residents Thank Rwandan Forces for Restoring Security
excerpt_en: MOCÍMBOA DA PRAIA, Mozambique - Residents of Mocímboa da Praia in Cabo Delgado Province have publicly thanked the Rwandan Armed Forces (RDF) for restoring peace and security after years of terrorist violence.
body_en:
MOCÍMBOA DA PRAIA, Mozambique - Residents of Mocímboa da Praia in Cabo Delgado Province have publicly thanked the Rwandan Armed Forces (RDF) for restoring peace and security after years of terrorist violence. The tribute came during a public concert organized by local authorities and youth groups to celebrate the return of stability.

The RDF, deployed to Mozambique in 2021 under a bilateral security cooperation agreement, played a key role in combating terrorist groups that had displaced civilians and disrupted daily life. Following military operations, residents gradually returned home, economic activities resumed, and a second phase focused on training Mozambican security forces.

In a message shared on the Rwanda Defence Forces’ X account on December 6, 2025, the RDF confirmed that more than 300 residents and local leaders attended the event. Speaking on behalf of the Rwandan forces, ACP Bertin Mutezintare reaffirmed Rwanda’s commitment to continued cooperation and urged youth involvement in supporting security and development efforts.

Since their deployment, the Rwanda Defence Forces and the Rwanda National Police have significantly weakened terrorist networks across several districts. On November 29, 2025, the RDF also donated sports equipment to local youth to strengthen ties between security forces and communities.

Mozambican President Daniel Francisco Chapo, who recently inaugurated Rwandan security units in Ancuabe District, praised their collaboration with Mozambican forces, calling it essential to defeating terrorism. He stressed that terrorism is a global threat requiring unity, cooperation, and sustained joint action to ensure lasting peace and development.

GABIRO, Rwanda - December 6, 2025 - A brigade of the Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF) has completed a five-month Advanced Infantry Course at the Gabiro Military Training Centre, with the closing ceremony led by RDF Chief of Staff Gen Mubarakh Muganga.

title: Heavy Losses Reported Among Burundian Forces in South Kivu Fighting
excerpt: SOUTH KIVU-DRC - Burundian troops deployed alongside Congolese government forces, Wazalendo militias, and the FDLR have suffered significant losses in ongoing fighting against AFC/M23 in eastern DR Congo, particularly…
title_en: Heavy Losses Reported Among Burundian Forces in South Kivu Fighting
excerpt_en: SOUTH KIVU-DRC - Burundian troops deployed alongside Congolese government forces, Wazalendo militias, and the FDLR have suffered significant losses in ongoing fighting against AFC/M23 in eastern DR Congo, particularly…
body_en:
SOUTH KIVU-DRC - Burundian troops deployed alongside Congolese government forces, Wazalendo militias, and the FDLR have suffered significant losses in ongoing fighting against AFC/M23 in eastern DR Congo, particularly in South Kivu, according to multiple sources.

Burundi’s involvement follows an agreement with President Félix Tshisekedi to support operations against AFC/M23. Since late November, clashes have intensified around Kamanyola, Kaziba, Katogota, Uvira, and surrounding areas. AFC/M23 has repelled several coordinated offensives and retained control of key positions.

On the night of December 4, AFC/M23 launched a major assault on Burundian army positions, killing and capturing dozens of soldiers. Among the dead was Lt Col Athanase Minani, a Burundian battalion commander - the highest-ranking Burundian officer reported killed in the conflict so far. Human rights activist Pacifique Nininahazwe said Minani was killed by a drone strike.

Between December 5 and 6, AFC/M23 seized Rurambo, Lubarika, and the Luvungi center, about 60 km from Uvira. Burundian and allied forces reportedly withdrew southward or crossed back into Burundi.

AFC/M23 spokesperson Lt Col Willy Ngoma said Burundian forces had suffered heavy setbacks, warning against continued foreign involvement in the conflict.

The fighting has triggered civilian casualties, displacement, and widespread destruction. Despite repeated international calls for a political solution, military operations continue, further worsening the humanitarian situation in eastern DR Congo.

title: Reports Allege Burundi Has Hosted FDLR Fighters as Fighting Intensifies in South Kivu
excerpt: Bujumbura / South Kivu - Burundi is facing renewed scrutiny amid reports that it has hosted fighters from the FDLR, a group designated as terrorist, following recent advances by the AFC/M23 coalition in the Rusizi…
title_en: Reports Allege Burundi Has Hosted FDLR Fighters as Fighting Intensifies in South Kivu
excerpt_en: Bujumbura / South Kivu - Burundi is facing renewed scrutiny amid reports that it has hosted fighters from the FDLR, a group designated as terrorist, following recent advances by the AFC/M23 coalition in the Rusizi…
body_en:
Bujumbura / South Kivu - Burundi is facing renewed scrutiny amid reports that it has hosted fighters from the FDLR, a group designated as terrorist, following recent advances by the AFC/M23 coalition in the Rusizi Valley, South Kivu province, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

According to multiple sources, FDLR fighters crossed into Burundi between December 7 and 10, 2025, alongside approximately 2,000 DRC army (FARDC) and Wazalendo fighters, after M23 seized large areas of the Rusizi Valley.

Most of the fighters reportedly entered Burundi via the Rusizi River bridge, which separates the two countries. Upon arrival, Burundian troops gathered them at the Buganda football stadium, as well as at temporary camps in Cishemere and Kansega.

Sources say that at the Buganda airfield, Burundian forces provided food assistance to about 1,600 FDLR and FARDC fighters, while more than 400 Wazalendo fighters were reportedly excluded, a move observers say highlights the long-standing ties between Burundi and the FDLR.

The Burundian outlet SOS Médias reported that authorities in Bujumbura are preparing a camp located far from the border to host FDLR, Wazalendo, and FARDC fighters, while awaiting support from the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC).

The ICRC has previously played a central role in the region, particularly in the transfer of prisoners of war, including the evacuation of Congolese troops from M23-controlled areas to Kinshasa. Analysts note that the ICRC could similarly facilitate the transfer of FARDC and Wazalendo fighters from Burundi to DRC-controlled territory.

However, uncertainty remains over the fate of the FDLR fighters, many of whom are Rwandan nationals. Observers question whether Burundi will retain them or agree to repatriate them to Rwanda.

Meanwhile, there are reports of ongoing coordination meetings between the Burundian and DRC governments to plan a large-scale military campaign aimed at retaking areas of the Rusizi Valley, including the strategic city of Uvira, recently captured by M23.

Sources suggest the plan could involve FDLR and Wazalendo fighters, both those who retreated to the South Kivu highlands and those currently inside Burundi, raising concerns about a broader regional escalation.

Allegations of cooperation between Burundi and the FDLR are not new. A UN Group of Experts report published on November 23, 2009, documented weapons transfers allegedly involving the FDLR through Burundi, Uvira, and Fizi.

In 2008, Burundi reportedly purchased 40,000 Steyr AUG rifles from Malaysia, officially claiming they were intended for the police force, which then numbered fewer than 20,000 officers. UN experts later questioned the purchase, alleging that the weapons were instead supplied to the FDLR, which reportedly paid in precious stones.

The report further stated that since 2005, when the CNDD-FDD party came to power, Burundi had become a rear base for the FDLR, with hundreds of fighters trained in Bujumbura before being sent to fight in eastern DRC.

During Kimia II operations against the FDLR between July and August 2009, many FDLR fighters fled to Burundi, where they were arrested. Some reportedly confirmed having direct links with General Adolphe Nshimirimana, then head of Burundian intelligence, and senior police officials-ties later acknowledged by the Burundian government.

UN experts found that between June and August 2009, Agricole Ntirampeba, head of Nshimirimana’s office at the time, held 13 meetings with an FDLR officer known as Major Mazuru, during which Burundian officials allegedly assisted the group with equipment and medical supplies.

Ntirampeba, later promoted to Major General, has served as Burundi’s Ambassador to the DRC since 2022, an appointment made by President Évariste Ndayishimiye. Gen. Nshimirimana was assassinated in August 2015.

During the 2015 political crisis in Burundi, which followed an attempted coup against President Pierre Nkurunziza, sources say the Burundian government again called on FDLR fighters for support.

More recently, as relations between Rwanda and Burundi deteriorated following the 2022 truce, Burundi is reported to have strengthened ties with the FDLR and FLN, bringing the groups together in a coordinated effort against Rwanda.

Meetings reportedly took place in August and September 2024 at hotels in Bukinanyana and Kabarore, involving senior leaders of these armed groups, including Gen Omega, Hamada, Jeva, and Theophile, alongside Burundian military officers.

When Burundi deployed troops to eastern DRC beginning in 2022, they were repeatedly accused of operating alongside FDLR fighters, particularly in Masisi territory, allegedly bound by shared ideology and economic interests.

Although M23 fighters have since pushed Burundian forces out of North Kivu and much of South Kivu, advancing into Uvira territory, reports suggest continued coordination between Burundi, FARDC, Wazalendo, and the FDLR.

Analysts warn that under these conditions, FDLR fighters who have fled to Burundi may not be treated as refugees, but rather as strategic partners, potentially playing a key role in preparations for a counter-offensive against M23.

title: Maj Gen Joseph Adinkra, Recipient of President Kagame’s Medal for Protecting Civilians, Dies
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda - Maj Gen Joseph Narh Adinkra, one of two Ghanaian soldiers awarded the medal of valor by President Paul Kagame in 2022 for their courage in protecting civilians during difficult circumstances, has died of illness.
title_en: Maj Gen Joseph Adinkra, Recipient of President Kagame’s Medal for Protecting Civilians, Dies
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - Maj Gen Joseph Narh Adinkra, one of two Ghanaian soldiers awarded the medal of valor by President Paul Kagame in 2022 for their courage in protecting civilians during difficult circumstances, has died of illness.
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - Maj Gen Joseph Narh Adinkra, one of two Ghanaian soldiers awarded the medal of valor by President Paul Kagame in 2022 for their courage in protecting civilians during difficult circumstances, has died of illness. He passed away on December 4, 2025, at the 37 Military Hospital.

Gen. Adinkra served as a Battalion Commander in the Ghanaian Army and was part of the UN peacekeeping force (UNAMIR) in Rwanda during the Genocide against the Tutsi. He was widely respected for his dedication and determination in ensuring the safety of thousands of civilians who had sought refuge under the protection of his troops.

During the genocide, Ghana contributed approximately 850 soldiers to the UNAMIR force. Another notable Ghanaian, Gen Henry Kwami Anyidoho, who served as deputy commander to Gen Romeo Dallaire, was also awarded the medal of valor.

The Indengabaganti, or medal of valor, is a circular medal featuring a five-pointed star at its center, surrounded by a circle with a bow and two arrows. Each element symbolizes critical values:

The bow represents courage to sacrifice and protect others and the country.

The arrows signify the power to sacrifice from afar.

The five-pointed star reflects the sacrifice made in all directions to protect others.

This prestigious award is presented to individuals or groups who have demonstrated supreme self-sacrifice, risking their lives to save others, even at the cost of their own life.

Gen. Adinkra’s passing marks the loss of a hero whose bravery and humanity left a lasting legacy in Rwanda and the history of UN peacekeeping.

title: Why RPA Soldiers Carried Ibitenge During the Struggle for National Liberation
excerpt: Rwamagana, Rwanda - During the RPF-Inkotanyi’s liberation struggle in 1990, RPA soldiers were often seen carrying ibitenge-around their waists, stomachs, or shoulders-a symbol of determination and resilience.
title_en: Why RPA Soldiers Carried Ibitenge During the Struggle for National Liberation
excerpt_en: Rwamagana, Rwanda - During the RPF-Inkotanyi’s liberation struggle in 1990, RPA soldiers were often seen carrying ibitenge-around their waists, stomachs, or shoulders-a symbol of determination and resilience.
body_en:
Rwamagana, Rwanda - During the RPF-Inkotanyi’s liberation struggle in 1990, RPA soldiers were often seen carrying ibitenge-around their waists, stomachs, or shoulders-a symbol of determination and resilience. On December 7, 2025, leaders and residents of Rwamagana District visiting the historic Rugano site were reminded of the significance of this practice.

Bashana Medard, Director of the Museum of the History of the Struggle to Stop the Genocide, explained that on October 28, 1990, President Paul Kagame, leading the RPA forces, withdrew troops from Mutara to Rugano, a forested area between the Muhabura and Gahinga volcanoes in the Musanze and Burera districts, where the Inkotanyi camped in late December 1990.

Bashana outlined three reasons for choosing Rugano:

The dense forest made it difficult for government troops to attack with heavy weapons.

A thick fog above the forest hindered aerial attacks.

It provided space to gather troops, re-energize them, and build morale.

The ibitenge belts served practical and symbolic purposes:

Practical: They helped soldiers tighten their belts when hungry and stay warm in cold conditions.

Symbolic: They represented discipline, resilience, and focus on the mission, reminding soldiers to persevere despite hardships.

“Most photos of the Inkotanyi in the 1990s show them with belts,” Bashana said. “If you are tired or facing challenges, think about what lies ahead and how to build a better future.”

Rugano became a place where the RPA forces regained strength, planned strategic attacks, and began to see the possibility of national liberation.

Rushimisha Marc, Executive Secretary of Kigabiro Sector, emphasized that visits to Rugano are about studying history to inspire development, not just military training:

“We have a population that needs leadership for development. Today, we follow the foundation laid by the Inkotanyi to move our citizens forward.”

The story of the ibitenge serves as a reminder of the courage, discipline, and vision that fueled the struggle for Rwanda’s liberation.

Rwamagana, Rwanda - During the RPF-Inkotanyi’s liberation struggle in 1990, RPA soldiers were often seen carrying ibitenge-around their waists, stomachs, or shoulders-a symbol of determination and resilience. On December 7, 2025, leaders and residents of Rwamagana District visiting the historic Rugano site were reminded of the significance of this practice.

Bashana Medard, Director of the Museum of the History of the Struggle to Stop the Genocide, explained that on October 28, 1990, President Paul Kagame, leading the RPA forces, withdrew troops from Mutara to Rugano, a forested area between the Muhabura and Gahinga volcanoes in the Musanze and Burera districts, where the Inkotanyi camped in late December 1990.

Bashana outlined three reasons for choosing Rugano:

The dense forest made it difficult for government troops to attack with heavy weapons.

A thick fog above the forest hindered aerial attacks.

It provided space to gather troops, re-energize them, and build morale.

The ibitenge belts served practical and symbolic purposes:

Practical: They helped soldiers tighten their belts when hungry and stay warm in cold conditions.

Symbolic: They represented discipline, resilience, and focus on the mission, reminding soldiers to persevere despite hardships.

“Most photos of the Inkotanyi in the 1990s show them with belts,” Bashana said. “If you are tired or facing challenges, think about what lies ahead and how to build a better future.”

Rugano became a place where the RPA forces regained strength, planned strategic attacks, and began to see the possibility of national liberation.

Rushimisha Marc, Executive Secretary of Kigabiro Sector, emphasized that visits to Rugano are about studying history to inspire development, not just military training:

“We have a population that needs leadership for development. Today, we follow the foundation laid by the Inkotanyi to move our citizens forward.”

The story of the ibitenge serves as a reminder of the courage, discipline, and vision that fueled the struggle for Rwanda’s liberation.

title: Burundi Calls for Calm After Soldiers’ Deaths in Uvira
excerpt: Uvira, DRC - Burundian Foreign Minister Dr. Edouard Bizimana has urged calm following the deaths of several Burundian soldiers in the Uvira area of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
title_en: Burundi Calls for Calm After Soldiers’ Deaths in Uvira
excerpt_en: Uvira, DRC - Burundian Foreign Minister Dr. Edouard Bizimana has urged calm following the deaths of several Burundian soldiers in the Uvira area of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
body_en:
Uvira, DRC - Burundian Foreign Minister Dr. Edouard Bizimana has urged calm following the deaths of several Burundian soldiers in the Uvira area of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. Speaking to diplomats on December 8, 2025, Minister Bizimana highlighted that the AFC/M23 coalition had sought to capture Uvira prior to the Washington peace agreement signed on December 4, but Burundian troops intervened.

“They wanted the agreement to be signed after capturing Luvungi and Uvira, but our troops stood firm. I congratulate the Burundian soldiers fighting for peace in Congo so that the enemy does not invade our country,” said Bizimana.

The minister stressed that Burundian troops are in the DRC to protect their borders, citizens, and property, and will remain until the mission’s objectives are resolved.

Since early December, Burundian forces have faced intense fighting against AFC/M23 in South Kivu Province, especially in heavily populated areas like Kamanyola.

AFC/M23 spokesman Lt Col Willy Ngoma warned on December 6:

“Those who crossed over have learned their lesson. Congo is not Cibitoke, it is not Ngozi or Bujumbura. They find us here, we are fighting for the truth.”

In coordination with DRC, Wazalendo, and FDLR groups, Burundian troops have helped liberate several towns including Katogota, Rurambo, Luberizi, Luvungi, Mutalule, Bwegera, Nyakabere, and Sange. However, many Burundian soldiers were killed, including Lt Col Athanase Minani, and over 100 were taken prisoner on December 4.

Kamenge Military Hospital received 87 wounded soldiers, with others transported to facilities like Tanganyika Care Polyclinic in Bujumbura.

After the capture of Sange hospital on December 8, Burundian troops were reportedly ordered to leave Uvira, though it remains unclear whether this was for strategic withdrawal or self-protection. They were accompanied by DRC and Wazalendo forces, Imbonerakure, and civilians, with most remaining soldiers concentrated around Minembwe, covering Uvira, Fizi, and Mwenga territories.

As of December 8, 2025, AFC/M23 fighters were within 30 kilometers of Uvira, and Minister Bizimana confirmed their objective of capturing the city before Christmas remains on track.

title: AFC/M23 Captures Kiliba Center Near Uvira
excerpt: Uvira, South Kivu - December 9, 2025 - The AFC/M23 coalition fighting the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has seized control of Kiliba center, located approximately 20 kilometers from Uvira city in Uvira Territory.
title_en: AFC/M23 Captures Kiliba Center Near Uvira
excerpt_en: Uvira, South Kivu - December 9, 2025 - The AFC/M23 coalition fighting the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has seized control of Kiliba center, located approximately 20 kilometers from Uvira city in Uvira Territory.
body_en:
Uvira, South Kivu - December 9, 2025 - The AFC/M23 coalition fighting the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has seized control of Kiliba center, located approximately 20 kilometers from Uvira city in Uvira Territory.

Since the start of last week’s fighting in the Rusizi Valley, AFC/M23 fighters have steadily pushed back DRC government forces, capturing several key areas, including Katogota, Rurambo, Luberizi, Luvungi, Mutalule, Bwegera, Nyakabere, Sange, and Runingo before advancing to Kiliba.

The advance has caused turmoil in Uvira, with reports of gunfire, reportedly from Wazalendo fighters, prompting the closure of businesses and schools due to security concerns.

Observers also noted that many Burundian troops withdrew from the captured areas, including Runingo, returning home after being overpowered by AFC/M23 forces. The withdrawal followed similar movements on December 8, after the capture of Sange center.

title: AFC/M23 Pledges Humane Treatment for Captured Burundian Soldiers
excerpt: Goma, December 9, 2025 - The AFC/M23 coalition fighting the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has announced that Burundian soldiers captured on the battlefield in South Kivu province will be treated well until they are…
title_en: AFC/M23 Pledges Humane Treatment for Captured Burundian Soldiers
excerpt_en: Goma, December 9, 2025 - The AFC/M23 coalition fighting the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has announced that Burundian soldiers captured on the battlefield in South Kivu province will be treated well until they are…
body_en:
Goma, December 9, 2025 - The AFC/M23 coalition fighting the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has announced that Burundian soldiers captured on the battlefield in South Kivu province will be treated well until they are safely returned home.

Bertrand Bisimwa, AFC/M23 Deputy Director for Political Affairs, Democracy and Governance, stated at a press conference in Goma:

“Even Burundian soldiers captured on the battlefield will be treated in a way that teaches them that this conflict is a Congolese issue that they should not interfere in. We will work to ensure that they return to their country peacefully.”

Bisimwa criticized Burundi’s involvement, claiming that President Félix Tshisekedi brought Burundian forces into the conflict to target AFC/M23 fighters, and warned that the war could spread throughout the region. He called for an immediate withdrawal of Burundian troops from DRC territory, stressing that AFC/M23 has no plans to attack Burundi, despite provocations.

The coalition has been gaining control over large parts of South Kivu, seizing areas from Burundian troops, DRC forces, Wazalendo, and FDLR groups. On December 9, AFC/M23 captured the Kiliba center, located approximately 20 kilometers from the city of Uvira.

This announcement highlights the coalition’s commitment to humane treatment of prisoners, while emphasizing that the conflict remains a domestic Congolese issue.

title: Uvira Falls to AFC/M23 After Intense Fighting
excerpt: Uvira, South Kivu, - The city of Uvira has fallen to the AFC/M23 coalition, following heavy clashes with combined forces of the DRC, Burundi, Wazalendo, and FDLR.
title_en: Uvira Falls to AFC/M23 After Intense Fighting
excerpt_en: Uvira, South Kivu, - The city of Uvira has fallen to the AFC/M23 coalition, following heavy clashes with combined forces of the DRC, Burundi, Wazalendo, and FDLR.
body_en:
Uvira, South Kivu, - The city of Uvira has fallen to the AFC/M23 coalition, following heavy clashes with combined forces of the DRC, Burundi, Wazalendo, and FDLR. On the evening of December 9, 2025, AFC/M23 fighters entered the city, marking a significant shift in control.

Uvira lies 22 kilometers by air from Bujumbura and is near Merchior Ndadaye Airport, a strategic route previously used by Burundian troops to enter South and North Kivu in support of FARDC operations.

Witnesses reported that Burundian soldiers fled to their homeland, while others were killed in the fighting. Many local leaders went into hiding, reflecting the scale of the displacement and fear among the city’s authorities.

The fall followed AFC/M23’s capture of surrounding areas, including Katogota, Rurambo, Luberizi, Luvungi, Mutalule, Bwegera, Nyakabere, Sange, Runingo, and Kiliba. By 9:15 PM, FARDC and Burundian troops began fleeing en masse as the fighters approached within a few kilometers of Uvira.

In a press briefing on December 9, AFC/M23 Coordinator Corneille Nangaa assured residents that the coalition aims to restore security, stating:

“The population has been abandoned, so what can we do? We are protecting the population and we cannot allow this chaos and fear to continue. We must unite to bring security.”

Politician Moïse Nyarugabo, a former DRC parliamentarian, urged citizens not to flee, emphasizing that the incoming forces are there to provide safety, not to harm civilians.

This development highlights the rapid territorial gains of AFC/M23 since the Rusizi Valley battle began last week, significantly altering the security dynamics in South Kivu province.

title: Rwanda Welcomes Congolese Refugees Amid South Kivu Fighting
excerpt: Rusizi District, 14 December 2025 - Mayor Sindayiheba Phanuel of Rusizi District emphasized that Rwanda is a peaceful country and continues to welcome Congolese refugees fleeing conflict in eastern Democratic Republic…
title_en: Rwanda Welcomes Congolese Refugees Amid South Kivu Fighting
excerpt_en: Rusizi District, 14 December 2025 - Mayor Sindayiheba Phanuel of Rusizi District emphasized that Rwanda is a peaceful country and continues to welcome Congolese refugees fleeing conflict in eastern Democratic Republic…
body_en:
Rusizi District, 14 December 2025 - Mayor Sindayiheba Phanuel of Rusizi District emphasized that Rwanda is a peaceful country and continues to welcome Congolese refugees fleeing conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

The mayor explained that some refugees requested to live with family and friends rather than in temporary camps. 207 individuals were relocated from the Nyarushishi camp to stay with relatives and friends in areas including Bugarama Sector.

“207 requested to live with families of friends, especially in Bugarama. Those we helped to leave the camp where they were temporarily hosted went to live with friends and relatives. As we have said, Rwanda is a peaceful country, a country that welcomes and treats well anyone who comes to us,” Mayor Sindayiheba said.

The first batch of 199 Congolese refugees arrived in Rwanda on December 3, 2025, following intensified clashes between the DRC Army and its allies against the AFC/M23 coalition in South Kivu Province. Some refugees have since returned to the DRC through the Rusizi border crossing to Bukavu, while the majority remain with host families in Rwanda.

Since the Rusizi Valley battle began last week, AFC/M23 fighters have captured several strategic areas, including Katogota, Rurambo, Luberizi, Luvungi, Mutalule, Bwegera, Nyakabere, Sange, Runingo, and Kiliba. Reports indicate that even Uvira town experienced gunfire prior to the capture of Kiliba, reportedly from Wazalendo fighters, heightening the urgency for civilians to seek safety.

Rwanda’s response underscores its role as a safe haven for those fleeing conflict in neighboring regions.

title: Burundi Deploys Military Veterans to South Kivu Amid AFC/M23 Advance
excerpt: Uvira, 14 December 2025 - The Burundian government has deployed military veterans to the ongoing conflict in South Kivu Province, eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.
title_en: Burundi Deploys Military Veterans to South Kivu Amid AFC/M23 Advance
excerpt_en: Uvira, 14 December 2025 - The Burundian government has deployed military veterans to the ongoing conflict in South Kivu Province, eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.
body_en:
Uvira, 14 December 2025 - The Burundian government has deployed military veterans to the ongoing conflict in South Kivu Province, eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. On December 6, 2025, veterans were transported in four trucks across the Nyamoma Bridge toward the Sange center in Uvira territory to support operations alongside Burundian, DRC, Wazalendo, and FDLR forces.

The veterans were reportedly well-equipped with weapons and ammunition, tasked with preventing the AFC/M23 coalition from advancing toward Uvira city. Additional Burundian troops had entered the DRC on December 3, establishing positions in Lubarika and Luvungi.

Observers note that the South Kivu conflict has depleted internal Burundian military camps, leaving only units of the Security Forces of the President (BSPI) and the Military Police to guard the Chief of Staff of the Army, Gen Prime Niyongabo.

Despite these efforts, AFC/M23 fighters have captured key areas, including Sange, Lubarika, Luvungi, Kiliba, and eventually Uvira city, forcing a mass withdrawal of Burundian forces after heavy losses, numerous injuries, and significant equipment seizures.

The Burundian high command has since ordered a strategic retreat, as the coalition continues to reorganize following the setbacks in South Kivu.

title: DRC: AFC/M23 Facilitates Return of Burundian Troops from South Kivu
excerpt: Uvira, DRC - Burundian troops defeated in South Kivu were allowed to return home on the evening of December 10, 2025, crossing the Kavimvira border, now controlled by AFC/M23.
title_en: DRC: AFC/M23 Facilitates Return of Burundian Troops from South Kivu
excerpt_en: Uvira, DRC - Burundian troops defeated in South Kivu were allowed to return home on the evening of December 10, 2025, crossing the Kavimvira border, now controlled by AFC/M23.
body_en:
Uvira, DRC - Burundian troops defeated in South Kivu were allowed to return home on the evening of December 10, 2025, crossing the Kavimvira border, now controlled by AFC/M23. Observers on both the Uvira and Bujumbura sides reported long lines of Burundian soldiers returning through the border, which has since been closed.

Since December 9, the Kavimvira border on the DRC side has been under the control of AFC/M23, which reportedly facilitated the soldiers’ repatriation.

These troops had been engaged in battles in the Ruzizi Valley and surrounding mountains, fighting alongside FARDC, Wazalendo, and FDLR forces against AFC/M23. Despite witnesses confirming their return, the Burundian Ambassador to the DRC denied the reports. Burundi had stationed more than 20,000 troops in South Kivu, and the conflict to capture Uvira resulted in heavy casualties and others fleeing to nearby mountains or back home. During these operations, Burundian forces were reportedly defeated in North and South Kivu.

In response to the ongoing conflict, Burundi has closed its border with the DRC on the South Kivu side to prevent infiltration by enemies.

title: AFC/M23 Investigates Death of Communications Advisor in Goma
excerpt: Goma, DRC - The AFC/M23 coalition, active in the Democratic Republic of Congo, announced the tragic death of its communications advisor, Magloire Paluku, on December 10, 2025.
title_en: AFC/M23 Investigates Death of Communications Advisor in Goma
excerpt_en: Goma, DRC - The AFC/M23 coalition, active in the Democratic Republic of Congo, announced the tragic death of its communications advisor, Magloire Paluku, on December 10, 2025.
body_en:
Goma, DRC - The AFC/M23 coalition, active in the Democratic Republic of Congo, announced the tragic death of its communications advisor, Magloire Paluku, on December 10, 2025. Paluku, a longtime journalist, was shot dead in the city of Goma, and the assailants remain unidentified.

The head of the AFC/M23 office, Corneille Nangaa, along with Alumba Lukamba Omokoko Jean Pierre, confirmed that Paluku died at Goma General Hospital.

“Following this criminal act, investigations are ongoing to identify those responsible,” said Alumba.

Born in Butembo, North Kivu Province, Paluku was the operator of Radio Kivu One. He joined AFC/M23 in July 2024, and since then has been a close advisor and friend to the group’s leader, Corneille Nangaa.

title: AFC/M23 Delegates Return to Doha Peace Talks Following Uvira Capture
excerpt: Doha, Qatar - The AFC/M23 coalition, active in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), announced that its delegates have returned to peace talks in Doha, Qatar. The announcement was made by AFC/M23 Deputy Spokesperson Dr.
title_en: AFC/M23 Delegates Return to Doha Peace Talks Following Uvira Capture
excerpt_en: Doha, Qatar - The AFC/M23 coalition, active in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), announced that its delegates have returned to peace talks in Doha, Qatar. The announcement was made by AFC/M23 Deputy Spokesperson Dr.
body_en:
Doha, Qatar - The AFC/M23 coalition, active in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), announced that its delegates have returned to peace talks in Doha, Qatar. The announcement was made by AFC/M23 Deputy Spokesperson Dr. Oscar Balinda on December 11, 2025, following the coalition’s capture of Uvira in South Kivu province.

Dr. Balinda stated: “The invitation reached us, our people have taken the plane, and we are moving forward to complete the remaining six fundamental principles. We must also show a strong will to implement each principle to achieve lasting peace in the DRC and the region.”

The AFC/M23 delegation arrived in Doha on the morning of December 12, where they are scheduled to meet with the DRC government in talks facilitated by the Government of Qatar.

title: South Kivu: DRC Forces Clash with Wazalendo Amid AFC/M23 Advance
excerpt: Baraka, South Kivu, DRC - Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) forces taking refuge in Baraka, Fizi territory, clashed with Wazalendo armed groups on the morning of December 12, 2025.
title_en: South Kivu: DRC Forces Clash with Wazalendo Amid AFC/M23 Advance
excerpt_en: Baraka, South Kivu, DRC - Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) forces taking refuge in Baraka, Fizi territory, clashed with Wazalendo armed groups on the morning of December 12, 2025.
body_en:
Baraka, South Kivu, DRC - Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) forces taking refuge in Baraka, Fizi territory, clashed with Wazalendo armed groups on the morning of December 12, 2025. The Wazalendo attempted to disarm DRC forces after they fled Uvira, now controlled by the AFC/M23 coalition.

A local resident in the Mongemonge area described the chaos: “The bullets were above us. It was the Wazalendo who wanted to disarm the FARDC, but they failed.”

The fighting lasted about an hour, prompting authorities to suspend business and educational activities in Baraka while awaiting calm.

The DRC and Wazalendo forces had left Uvira on December 9, prior to the AFC/M23 entry. The DRC forces reached Baraka the following day, while others fled to Burundi. Sources confirm that DRC forces, previously in disarray, are still arriving in Baraka, joined by some Burundian troops who also fled.

Earlier, on December 7, AFC/M23 fighters attacked Sange, near Uvira, where Wazalendo clashed with DRC forces, leaving 36 dead, including civilians. Wazalendo reportedly attempted to recruit fleeing DRC forces to counter the AFC/M23 advance, but the DRC troops refused.

title: DRC Forces Launch Airstrike in Minembwe Amid South Kivu Conflict
excerpt: Minembwe, South Kivu, DRC - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) launched an airstrike in the Minembwe region, which connects the territories of Uvira, Fizi, and Mwenga, on the morning of…
title_en: DRC Forces Launch Airstrike in Minembwe Amid South Kivu Conflict
excerpt_en: Minembwe, South Kivu, DRC - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) launched an airstrike in the Minembwe region, which connects the territories of Uvira, Fizi, and Mwenga, on the morning of…
body_en:
Minembwe, South Kivu, DRC - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) launched an airstrike in the Minembwe region, which connects the territories of Uvira, Fizi, and Mwenga, on the morning of December 12, 2025. The attack targeted a camp in the Mikenke area as DRC and Burundian forces continue to clash in the region, according to politician Moïse Nyarugabo.

Nyarugabo condemned the strike, stating: “No army of this criminal alliance expects to gain military advantage from this attack. These are bombs being fired to kill and destroy. The planes and drones targeting civilian areas, villages, and people will not go unchallenged.”

He criticized the DRC government for accusing AFC/M23 of violating the ceasefire while conducting airstrikes and drone attacks on civilian populations.

DRC and Burundian forces are currently stationed in the highlands around Minembwe, where they have reportedly blocked access to markets and clinics, accusing local residents of collaboration with the enemy. The MRDP-Twirwaneho group, representing Minembwe residents, claimed these restrictions target civilians based on their Banyamulenge ethnicity.

In recent weeks, AFC/M23 has captured large parts of South Kivu in the Rusizi Valley, prompting many Burundian, DRC, Wazalendo, and FDLR forces to flee to areas including Bujumbura and Fizi. Nyarugabo noted that troops in the South Kivu highlands are the main source of security problems for civilians, but nearby, AFC/M23 and Twirwaneho fighters have pledged to end the threat.

title: Rwandan Senior Prison Guards Graduate in Zimbabwe
excerpt: Harare, Zimbabwe - A total of 42 prison guards, including five Rwandans, successfully completed the Senior Management Development Course in Corrections (SMDCC), which began in January 2025.
title_en: Rwandan Senior Prison Guards Graduate in Zimbabwe
excerpt_en: Harare, Zimbabwe - A total of 42 prison guards, including five Rwandans, successfully completed the Senior Management Development Course in Corrections (SMDCC), which began in January 2025.
body_en:
Harare, Zimbabwe - A total of 42 prison guards, including five Rwandans, successfully completed the Senior Management Development Course in Corrections (SMDCC), which began in January 2025. The graduation ceremony was held on December 12, 2025, and attended by the First Secretary at the Rwandan Embassy in Zimbabwe, Nikuze Nkusi Euphrasie, Zimbabwe’s Minister of Justice, Ziyambi Ziyambi, and other senior officials.

This marks the third batch of graduates, and the second batch for the Rwandan Prison Service at this level.

All 42 participants were awarded the Senior Correctional Officers’ Ring, a Diploma in Entrepreneurship and Management from Zimbabwe Open University, and a Certificate in Farm Management from the Zimbabwe Prisons and Correctional Service Staff College.

The programme is part of the Rwandan Correctional Service’s (RCS) initiative to enhance performance, knowledge sharing, and training through international collaboration.

Subjects covered included correctional policy and management, effective planning, emergency management, human rights and ethical management, and employee welfare. Participants also gained skills in productive activities, innovation, and job creation.

Minister Ziyambi Ziyambi emphasized that effective correctional management focuses on maintaining security, promoting morale, and treating prisoners as human beings. He highlighted the importance of temporary release programmes to allow prisoners to serve sentences in society and the use of technology to accelerate reform.

title: Capture of Uvira Seen as Key Opportunity for Regional Peace
excerpt: Uvira, South Kivu, DRC - The capture of Uvira by AFC/M23 fighters has dominated headlines across Africa and globally.
title_en: Capture of Uvira Seen as Key Opportunity for Regional Peace
excerpt_en: Uvira, South Kivu, DRC - The capture of Uvira by AFC/M23 fighters has dominated headlines across Africa and globally.
body_en:
Uvira, South Kivu, DRC - The capture of Uvira by AFC/M23 fighters has dominated headlines across Africa and globally. While some view it as a normal military operation against over 20,000 Burundian soldiers allied with FARDC, FDLR, Wazalendo, and mercenaries targeting Banyamulenge communities, others see a deeper political significance.

A delegate from the Great Lakes region likened the capture of Uvira to Moses striking the rock to bring forth water, signaling hope for the region. He noted that following the Washington Agreement signed on December 4, 2025, the takeover does not threaten regional security, calling it “one of the best developments in regional politics in recent years.”

The diplomat explained that the operation is the culmination of previous talks in Washington, Doha, Nairobi, and Luanda, some of which have yet to reach a conclusion. He emphasized that the capture of Uvira diminishes the will to fight among opposing forces, particularly affecting Burundi, Kinshasa’s main ally. With Uvira under M23 control, Burundian ground troops can no longer easily move in or out of the DRC, limiting military options.

Located just over 20 kilometers from Bujumbura, Uvira is strategically significant. The Burundian government has warned that threats to Uvira could extend to Bujumbura. Meanwhile, for President Tshisekedi, the loss of Uvira disrupts the flow of war materials, reducing Kinshasa’s logistical advantages.

M23 believes it can defend Uvira effectively, arguing that its control protects Congolese Tutsis and other victims of violence in the two Kivus. The group stresses that for lasting peace, all parties-Kinshasa, M23, Rwanda, and Burundi-must respect the Washington and Doha agreements.

While Rwanda has shown willingness to honor its commitments, the diplomat underscored that Burundi must also uphold its obligations. Meanwhile, M23 and the DRC government have resumed talks in Doha, as Burundian troops who had entered the DRC fled Uvira, some returning home while others sought refuge in forests.

title: Burundian Warplanes and Drones Target Banyamulenge in South Kivu
excerpt: South Kivu, DRC - The AFC/M23 coalition fighting in the Democratic Republic of Congo reported that Burundian warplanes and drones launched new attacks on Banyamulenge communities in South Kivu province.
title_en: Burundian Warplanes and Drones Target Banyamulenge in South Kivu
excerpt_en: South Kivu, DRC - The AFC/M23 coalition fighting in the Democratic Republic of Congo reported that Burundian warplanes and drones launched new attacks on Banyamulenge communities in South Kivu province.
body_en:
South Kivu, DRC - The AFC/M23 coalition fighting in the Democratic Republic of Congo reported that Burundian warplanes and drones launched new attacks on Banyamulenge communities in South Kivu province. According to AFC/M23 spokesman Lawrence Kanyuka, the strikes occurred in the early hours of December 13, 2025, with Burundian troops directly involved.

Kanyuka said: “Sukhoi-25 warplanes, combat helicopters, and military drones operating from Burundian territory indiscriminately attacked the Banyamulenge villages of Mikenke and Rwitsankuku, in blatant violation of international humanitarian law.”

The AFC/M23 coalition condemned the attacks, stating they targeted civilians, killed women and children, and amounted to war crimes and crimes against humanity.

On the morning of December 12, 2025, a Sukhoi-25 fighter jet also attacked a Banyamulenge refugee camp in the Mikenke area.

Politician Moïse Nyarugabo attributed the attacks on civilians to the continued battlefield defeats of DRC and Burundian forces, following their loss of large parts of the Rusizi Valley in the past two weeks.

title: AFC/M23 Warns International Community Against Labeling Its Fighters as Rwandan Agents
excerpt: South Kivu, DRC - The AFC/M23 coalition, active in the Democratic Republic of Congo, stated that its fighters should not be portrayed as foreigners or Rwandan agents, warning that such narratives could justify stripping…
title_en: AFC/M23 Warns International Community Against Labeling Its Fighters as Rwandan Agents
excerpt_en: South Kivu, DRC - The AFC/M23 coalition, active in the Democratic Republic of Congo, stated that its fighters should not be portrayed as foreigners or Rwandan agents, warning that such narratives could justify stripping…
body_en:
South Kivu, DRC - The AFC/M23 coalition, active in the Democratic Republic of Congo, stated that its fighters should not be portrayed as foreigners or Rwandan agents, warning that such narratives could justify stripping Congolese of their citizenship. Spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka made the statement on December 13, 2025, in response to accusations from members of the United Nations Security Council alleging ceasefire violations and support from Rwanda.

Kanyuka explained that recent heavy fighting in the Rusizi Valley, South Kivu province, was caused by DRC army forces, Burundian troops, FDLR militants, Wazalendo, and foreign mercenaries violating the ceasefire and attacking civilians.

He emphasized that AFC/M23 is a coalition of Congolese fighters addressing the root causes of insecurity, including poor leadership that backs armed groups such as the genocidal FDLR and targets Congolese Tutsi communities.

“The notion that AFC/M23 are ‘foreigners’ or agents of Rwanda distorts the truth dangerously, lending legitimacy to Kinshasa’s agenda to expel or marginalize Congolese citizens,” Kanyuka said.

While AFC/M23 and Rwanda share concerns over the FDLR threat, Kanyuka stressed that this does not indicate collaboration. The coalition is focused on protecting Congolese refugees, advocating for repatriation, and ensuring security for populations at risk from FDLR attacks, often in coordination with DRC and Burundian forces.

Kanyuka added: “We were forced to take up arms to defend ourselves, as the DRC government continues to target Congolese Tutsi and ignore signed agreements. Since the Doha talks began, DRC warplanes and drones have repeatedly attacked our positions and liberated areas, causing many innocent deaths.”

He also highlighted that DRC forces have blocked roads used by Banyamulenge residents in Minembwe, aiming to starve civilians, while attacks by drones continue, leaving them with no means of defense.

“The letters and announcements we have sent to the international community have not changed anything. If the DRC government can wage war on its own citizens, we have the right to defend our lives and those of our comrades under threat of extermination,” Kanyuka said.

AFC/M23 called for genuine dialogue and compliance by the DRC government with signed agreements to address the root causes of the conflict, urging the international community to press Kinshasa to honor its commitments.

title: DRC Government Accused of Maintaining Ties with FDLR Despite Promises to Dismantle It
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - Despite statements since October 10, 2025 claiming that the FDLR would be dismantled, evidence suggests the DRC government continues to support the group, raising concerns about ongoing regional…
title_en: DRC Government Accused of Maintaining Ties with FDLR Despite Promises to Dismantle It
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - Despite statements since October 10, 2025 claiming that the FDLR would be dismantled, evidence suggests the DRC government continues to support the group, raising concerns about ongoing regional…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - Despite statements since October 10, 2025 claiming that the FDLR would be dismantled, evidence suggests the DRC government continues to support the group, raising concerns about ongoing regional insecurity.

The FDLR, accused of participating in the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, was formed in 2000 by remnants of the Ex-FAR army, Interahamwe, politicians, and Rwandan refugees remaining in the DRC. Since May 2022, the FDLR has been directly involved in operations against M23, in coalition with the DRC army and groups such as Wazalendo.

The Rwandan government has repeatedly warned the international community that the FDLR receives support from the DRC government, including equipment, military training, and food, enabling the group to strengthen its operations.

On June 27, 2025, Rwanda and the DRC, with U.S. assistance, signed a peace agreement, which included the destruction of the FDLR, while Rwanda agreed to lift certain security measures. The DRC military statement of October 10 called on FDLR fighters to disarm and instructed Congolese military and civilians to stop collaborating with the group, in line with the Washington agreement.

However, a UN experts’ report released on December 8, 2025, revealed that the announcement strained relations between the DRC army and FDLR fighters, angering allied Wazalendo groups. The report stated that some DRC army officers and government representatives assured the FDLR that cooperation would continue due to the group’s significant role in ongoing operations, noting that the FARDC lacks the capacity to dismantle it.

Reliable sources indicate that on November 29, 2025, the DRC army delivered ammunition and food to the FDLR and allied groups, including NDC-R and Nyatura, in areas such as Bibwe and Hembe, following orders from Colonel Salomon Tokolonga, commander of the 3402nd Regiment of the DRC Army.

Col. Tokolonga, already on the U.S. sanctions list, has a history of supporting the FDLR and other armed groups responsible for atrocities against civilians.

The period from December 1 to 14, 2025, was marked by a striking paradox between major diplomatic progress and a rapid, violent escalation of regional conflict.

The central diplomatic development was the signing of the DRC-Rwanda Peace and Economic Cooperation Agreement in Washington, D.C., on December 4, 2025. The accord established a broad framework for regional stability, committing both parties to the dismantling of armed groups, notably the FDLR, and to joint economic initiatives such as the Rusizi III hydroelectric project.

Yet this newly established framework was immediately tested-and weakened-by a sharp resurgence of fighting in North and South Kivu, including the capture of strategic areas by the AFC/M23 coalition. The escalation triggered mutual accusations of ceasefire violations, undermining both the Washington agreement and the earlier Qatar-mediated truce. Kigali accused Burundi of deploying more than 20,000 troops and contributing to instability in South Kivu, while the renewed violence drove over 750 Congolese refugees into Rwanda. At the same time, reports alleging continued coordination between certain FARDC elements and the FDLR stood in direct contradiction to the commitments undertaken in Washington.

Ultimately, while a critical legal and political foundation for regional cooperation has been laid, the swift return to hostilities, persistent non-compliance, and continued proxy dynamics highlight how fragile the peace process remains. Lasting stability in the Great Lakes region will depend not on signed agreements alone, but on verifiable actions, sustained political will, and strict adherence to commitments by all parties involved.

The central diplomatic development was the signing of the DRC-Rwanda Peace and Economic Cooperation Agreement in Washington, D.C., on December 4, 2025. The accord established a broad framework for regional stability, committing both parties to the dismantling of armed groups, notably the FDLR, and to joint economic initiatives such as the Rusizi III hydroelectric project.

Yet this newly established framework was immediately tested-and weakened-by a sharp resurgence of fighting in North and South Kivu, including the capture of strategic areas by the AFC/M23 coalition. The escalation triggered mutual accusations of ceasefire violations, undermining both the Washington agreement and the earlier Qatar-mediated truce. Kigali accused Burundi of deploying more than 20,000 troops and contributing to instability in South Kivu, while the renewed violence drove over 750 Congolese refugees into Rwanda. At the same time, reports alleging continued coordination between certain FARDC elements and the FDLR stood in direct contradiction to the commitments undertaken in Washington.

Ultimately, while a critical legal and political foundation for regional cooperation has been laid, the swift return to hostilities, persistent non-compliance, and continued proxy dynamics highlight how fragile the peace process remains. Lasting stability in the Great Lakes region will depend not on signed agreements alone, but on verifiable actions, sustained political will, and strict adherence to commitments by all parties involved.

title: Rwandan Senator Dismisses Burundi’s Military Claims
excerpt: Rwandan Senator Evode Uwizeyimana has sharply criticized what he described as provocations by Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye against the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF), comparing them to a “rat posturing on a…
title_en: Rwandan Senator Dismisses Burundi’s Military Claims
excerpt_en: Rwandan Senator Evode Uwizeyimana has sharply criticized what he described as provocations by Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye against the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF), comparing them to a “rat posturing on a…
body_en:
Rwandan Senator Evode Uwizeyimana has sharply criticized what he described as provocations by Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye against the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF), comparing them to a “rat posturing on a lawn.”

Speaking in an interview aired on Rwanda National Television on December 14, 2025, Uwizeyimana said that despite Burundi’s repeated claims of military strength, its leadership knows it cannot prevail in a confrontation with Rwanda. He referred to earlier remarks by President Ndayishimiye suggesting that any Rwandan attack via Uvira could be resolved in less than two hours, dismissing them as mere rhetoric.

Uwizeyimana argued that the recent defeat of Burundian forces in Uvira, which later fell under AFC/M23 control, exposed what he called war propaganda by Bujumbura, insisting that Burundi lacks the capacity to back up such threats.

title: Rwanda, Burundi Hold Security Talks to Ease Rising Tensions
excerpt: Kigali, December 18, 2025 - Rwanda and Burundi have taken a tentative step toward de-escalating mounting bilateral tensions, with security officials from both countries holding a meeting over the weekend, according to…
title_en: Rwanda, Burundi Hold Security Talks to Ease Rising Tensions
excerpt_en: Kigali, December 18, 2025 - Rwanda and Burundi have taken a tentative step toward de-escalating mounting bilateral tensions, with security officials from both countries holding a meeting over the weekend, according to…
body_en:
Kigali, December 18, 2025 - Rwanda and Burundi have taken a tentative step toward de-escalating mounting bilateral tensions, with security officials from both countries holding a meeting over the weekend, according to Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Olivier Nduhungirehe.

The talks come against the backdrop of years of strained relations between the two neighbors. Since 2015, Burundi has repeatedly accused Rwanda of sheltering individuals involved in a failed coup attempt and of supporting the RED-Tabara rebel group-allegations Kigali has consistently denied.

Tensions have intensified since early 2024, when Burundi closed all its land borders with Rwanda. Burundian authorities, including President Évariste Ndayishimiye, have on several occasions claimed in international media that Rwanda was planning an attack on Burundi, assertions Rwanda firmly rejects.

Kigali, for its part, has accused Burundi of aligning itself with the armed forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC), which Rwanda says maintains links with the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR), a group Kigali designates as terrorist.

Relations have further deteriorated amid the ongoing conflict in eastern DRC, particularly as the city of Uvira remains under the control of the AFC/M23 movement. Burundi has accused Rwanda of shelling its territory during the fighting, claims Rwanda denies.

In an interview with France 24 on December 18, Minister Nduhungirehe dismissed the allegations as unfounded, asserting that it was Burundi that carried out shelling in eastern Congo.

“That’s false. It was actually shells from Burundi that hit the city of Kamanyola in Congo, causing refugees, which triggered movements of refugees to Rwanda, in Bugarama,” he said.

Asked about diplomatic engagement between Kigali and Bujumbura, Nduhungirehe confirmed that security services from both countries met over the weekend to discuss ways to defuse tensions.

“Regarding Burundi, a meeting was held this weekend between the security services of both states to discuss de-escalation. And we believe that if these meetings continue, we will reach an agreement on a way forward for regional de-escalation and the reactivation of peace agreements,” he stated.

On relations with the DRC, Nduhungirehe said discussions are being conducted within the framework of the Washington agreements, which established a joint security coordination mechanism tasked with dismantling the FDLR and addressing Rwanda’s security concerns.

Although a peace agreement was signed on December 4, 2025, Kigali argues that continued military operations by the DRC have hampered its implementation. According to Rwandan officials, the FDLR-estimated to comprise between 7,000 and 10,000 fighters-has fought alongside FARDC and more than 20,000 Burundian soldiers against the M23.

Minister Nduhungirehe added that upcoming joint security meetings will focus on dismantling the FDLR and paving the way for the lifting of Rwanda’s security measures, signaling cautious optimism for a broader regional de-escalation.

title: Rwanda Condemns FARDC Airstrikes, Urges International Action Against AFC/M23
excerpt: Kigali, December 15, 2025 - Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Ambassador Olivier Nduhungirehe, has criticized the international community for what he describes as its selective…
title_en: Rwanda Condemns FARDC Airstrikes, Urges International Action Against AFC/M23
excerpt_en: Kigali, December 15, 2025 - Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Ambassador Olivier Nduhungirehe, has criticized the international community for what he describes as its selective…
body_en:
Kigali, December 15, 2025 - Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Ambassador Olivier Nduhungirehe, has criticized the international community for what he describes as its selective attention to violence in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

Speaking on his X account, Amb. Nduhungirehe condemned airstrikes and drone attacks carried out by the DRC’s Armed Forces (FARDC) in the Rwitsankuku area on the morning of December 15, which reportedly killed multiple civilians. He emphasized that Western nations largely ignore these attacks on Banyamulenge villages, yet respond swiftly when the AFC/M23 rebel group retaliates.

“You will never hear Westerners condemn these despicable acts of violence by the FARDC. These airstrikes targeting densely populated areas, including Banyamulenge villages, have occurred repeatedly, with the DRC government itself advocating for them. But Western countries only take notice when AFC/M23 responds,” he said.

Amb. Nduhungirehe’s comments come amid an escalation of air and drone strikes in South Kivu Province following AFC/M23’s recent victories over Burundian, DRC, Wazalendo, and FDLR forces in the Rusizi Valley. The minister called for decisive international action against the rebel group while highlighting what he described as the double standard of the international community.

title: “The Army I Have Always Wanted” - Kagame Praises Rwanda’s Security Forces and National Unity
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda - December 19, 2025
title_en: “The Army I Have Always Wanted” - Kagame Praises Rwanda’s Security Forces and National Unity
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - December 19, 2025
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - December 19, 2025

President Paul Kagame on Friday strongly praised Rwanda’s security services and the unity of its citizens, describing the national army as “the army I have always wanted,” during the opening of the 17th General Assembly of the RPF-Inkotanyi Association held in Rusororo.

Addressing delegates, President Kagame expressed deep gratitude to Rwandans from various sectors who have contributed to the country’s development, singling out members of the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF), the National Police, and other security institutions for their service to the nation.

“Among the institutions I want to thank are the security services in general - the RDF, Police, and others,” Kagame said. “They serve our country as a whole. What I ask of them, they have fulfilled. Our army is the army I have always wanted to have.”

Beyond the security sector, the Head of State paid special tribute to the Rwandan population, commending citizens for resisting division despite Rwanda’s painful history.

“Looking at where we came from - from division politics and genocide - and where we are today, united as a people, is remarkable,” he said. “There is no country with citizens as good as ours.”

President Kagame emphasized that attempts by external actors to sow discord among Rwandans have failed, noting that those efforts were rejected by a population committed to national cohesion.

He further stated that some individuals who fled the country later became instruments for those seeking to divide Rwanda, citing influences from abroad, including Europe, the United States, and South Africa. Kagame warned against ambitions fueled by foreign backing rather than lawful political processes.

“Wanting leadership is not a crime,” he said, “but there is a way to pursue it. Believing that outsiders will impose it for you has failed many before.”

The President also criticized attempts to exploit NGOs or other platforms as vehicles for division, stressing that Rwandans have consistently refused to be manipulated against their own country.

“When you have such citizens and fail to give them what they deserve, that is a serious crime,” Kagame said, urging leaders to regret, change, and do what is right.

He concluded by acknowledging the role of other political parties in preserving unity and rejecting divisive politics.

These remarks align with findings from the Rwanda Governance Scorecard (RGS) released by the Rwanda Governance Board (RGB), which ranks security and population stability among the country’s strongest pillars, scoring 90.02%, one of the highest indicators of national performance.
