title: Rwanda Faces Continued Diplomatic Pressure from DRC-Linked Consultant
excerpt: Kigali - December 23, 2025
title_en: Rwanda Faces Continued Diplomatic Pressure from DRC-Linked Consultant
excerpt_en: Kigali - December 23, 2025
body_en:
Kigali - December 23, 2025

Dr. Karl Von Batten, a Nigerian-born political and legal consultant working closely with the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) government, continues to push for international sanctions against Rwanda, alleging the country is the source of insecurity in eastern DRC. Born Karl-Marx Edward Ikemefuna William George Okeke, he adopted the name Dr. Karl Von Batten after marrying an American, Elizabeth Von Batten.

Von Batten is the founder of Von Batten-Montague-York, L.C, a U.S.-based firm providing legal and political advice, which has reportedly collaborated with the DRC in efforts to destabilize Rwanda and seek sanctions.

In February 2025, the firm claimed that President Paul Kagame had been uninvited from a prayer service in Washington, D.C., citing his alleged activities in the DRC. The Rwandan Embassy in the United States immediately refuted this claim, calling it false.

According to President Kagame, these attempts, coordinated with DRC President Félix Tshisekedi, were intended to convince the United States that Rwanda was responsible for instability in eastern DRC and to influence international pressure in favor of DRC’s interests.

“Whether in Doha or Washington, Tshisekedi tried to manipulate these talks for his own benefit, believing the DRC’s size and resources would allow him to dictate outcomes,” President Kagame said in a recent interview.

Despite these ongoing efforts, U.S. authorities ignored demands for sanctions, instead advocating for peace talks, leading to negotiations between Rwanda and the DRC in Washington, and between the DRC and AFC/M23 in Doha.

On December 19, 2025, Von Batten’s firm posted statements on social media from Judi River, criticizing Rwanda and its leadership. The posts coincided with U.S. Senator Lindsey Graham praising the AFC/M23 withdrawal from Uvira, and urging renewed negotiations for lasting peace.

Von Batten reportedly sought to involve Senator Graham in visiting eastern DRC and requested the removal of Rwanda from the US-Africa Trade Program (AGOA). None of these efforts have succeeded in achieving sanctions or isolating Rwanda internationally.

title: DRC Government Refuses to Resume Peace Talks with AFC/M23
excerpt: KINSHASA, DRC - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) government has refused to resume peace talks with the AFC/M23 rebel group, rejecting both face-to-face and video-conference negotiations.
title_en: DRC Government Refuses to Resume Peace Talks with AFC/M23
excerpt_en: KINSHASA, DRC - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) government has refused to resume peace talks with the AFC/M23 rebel group, rejecting both face-to-face and video-conference negotiations.
body_en:
KINSHASA, DRC - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) government has refused to resume peace talks with the AFC/M23 rebel group, rejecting both face-to-face and video-conference negotiations. The government continues to allege that the group has taken control of Uvira and other areas in the Rusizi Valley, despite AFC/M23 claims to the contrary.

The AFC/M23 said it withdrew its fighters from Uvira on 17 and 18 December 2025 to foster trust and facilitate peace talks, but the government has not acknowledged this withdrawal.

Instead, the DRC is focusing on seeking sanctions against the rebel fighters, accusing them of violating the ceasefire. The AFC/M23 denied these allegations, arguing that the government had fired in several areas, including Kamanyola, breaching its obligations.

The two parties were expected to discuss six core principles aimed at achieving a lasting peace agreement:

Creating a commission for truth, reconciliation, and justice

Additionally, the parties had previously agreed on principles concerning the ceasefire, its monitoring, and the transfer of prisoners.

On 22 December 2025, Togo’s Prime Minister, Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, currently the African Union (AU) mediator, made a short visit to Kinshasa. While his visit’s details remain undisclosed, the Presidential Office of the DRC said he discussed the security situation in South and North Kivu and areas under AFC/M23 control with President Félix Tshisekedi.

title: Mozambique Parliamentary Speaker Visits Rwandan Security Forces in Cabo Delgado
excerpt: CABO DELGADO, Mozambique - The Speaker of the Mozambique Chamber of Deputies, Margarida Adamugi Talapa, visited Rwandan Security Forces (RSF) deployed in Cabo Delgado Province on 23 December 2025, commending their role…
title_en: Mozambique Parliamentary Speaker Visits Rwandan Security Forces in Cabo Delgado
excerpt_en: CABO DELGADO, Mozambique - The Speaker of the Mozambique Chamber of Deputies, Margarida Adamugi Talapa, visited Rwandan Security Forces (RSF) deployed in Cabo Delgado Province on 23 December 2025, commending their role…
body_en:
CABO DELGADO, Mozambique - The Speaker of the Mozambique Chamber of Deputies, Margarida Adamugi Talapa, visited Rwandan Security Forces (RSF) deployed in Cabo Delgado Province on 23 December 2025, commending their role in combating terrorism.

Talapa was accompanied by several high-ranking officials, including Cabo Delgado Governor Valige Tauabo and Mozambique Chief of Army Staff Maj. Gen. André Rafael Mahunguane. The delegation was received by the Head of Mozambique Security Forces, Maj. Gen. Vincent Gatama, who briefed them on operations in the region.

During the visit, Talapa praised the cooperation between Rwandan and Mozambican security agencies in restoring peace and security in Mocímboa da Praia, an area previously devastated by the Ansar al Sunnah terrorist group. She emphasized that peace and security are essential for the development of Mozambique, urging Rwandan forces to continue their mission.

Talapa also highlighted that the partnership between Rwanda and Mozambique reflects their unity and shared goal of promoting stability in Cabo Delgado.

Since July 2021, Rwandan and Mozambican forces have jointly worked to combat terrorist activities, successfully driving terrorists from their strongholds, neutralizing them in forests, and enabling residents to return home and rebuild.

In August 2025, the governments of Rwanda and Mozambique renewed cooperation agreements focusing on investment and counter-terrorism, further strengthening bilateral ties and regional security efforts.

KINSHASA - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) government has refused to engage in dialogue with the AFC/M23, rejecting both face-to-face and video-conference talks, while continuing to accuse the group of taking control of Uvira and other parts of the Rusizi Valley.

Political analyst Tubijye Imuzi Tite Gatabazi said President Félix Tshisekedi was following a familiar political strategy often used when he believes a security crisis may be resolved through other means.

“I am not surprised,” Gatabazi said. “Like many observers, I see this as a common tactic of President Tshisekedi. If we look back at recent events in Luanda and Washington, a clear pattern emerges.” He recalled that during talks in Washington, the two foreign ministers were present to sign an agreement, but Congolese Foreign Minister Christophe Lutundula Kaikwamba later claimed he had been ordered by his superior not to sign.

According to Gatabazi, statements made after those events provide evidence of deliberate obstruction. “The way Uvira was presented is completely different from what actually happened on the ground,” he said, arguing that the city was used as a pretext to undermine negotiations that could have produced results.

He added that when it comes to addressing the root causes of the conflict, the Congolese government consistently avoids the discussion. “Eight fundamental principles were signed, yet today the government is looking for ways to delay, postpone, or simply buy time,” Gatabazi noted.

Although the DRC government accuses the AFC/M23 of failing to withdraw from Uvira, the movement announced that it withdrew its fighters on December 17 and 18, 2025, in an effort to restore trust and allow the resumption of peace talks. The government, however, has not acknowledged this withdrawal.

Instead, Kinshasa is currently focused on seeking international sanctions against AFC/M23 fighters, accusing them of violating the ceasefire. The AFC/M23 has denied the accusations, claiming that it was the government forces that breached the ceasefire by opening fire in areas such as Kamanyola.

At this stage, both parties were expected to discuss key principles aimed at achieving a lasting peace, including:

facilitating humanitarian operations,

restoring state authority across the country,

establishing interim security measures,

repatriating refugees,

reviving the economy,

and creating a Truth, Reconciliation, and Justice Commission.

An additional principle concerns the ceasefire agreement and the monitoring of its implementation, including the transfer of prisoners, an accord previously signed by both sides.

On December 22, 2025, Togo’s Prime Minister, Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, the African Union (AU)-appointed mediator, paid a brief visit to Kinshasa, amid continued deadlock in the peace process.

title: Burundian Citizen Challenges President Ndayishimiye Over ‘Powerful Elites’
excerpt: GITEGA, Burundi - December 27, 2025 - A Burundian citizen has publicly questioned President Évariste Ndayishimiye, urging him to confront what he has repeatedly described as “powerful elites” undermining Burundi’s…
title_en: Burundian Citizen Challenges President Ndayishimiye Over ‘Powerful Elites’
excerpt_en: GITEGA, Burundi - December 27, 2025 - A Burundian citizen has publicly questioned President Évariste Ndayishimiye, urging him to confront what he has repeatedly described as “powerful elites” undermining Burundi’s…
body_en:
GITEGA, Burundi - December 27, 2025 - A Burundian citizen has publicly questioned President Évariste Ndayishimiye, urging him to confront what he has repeatedly described as “powerful elites” undermining Burundi’s economy, or to seek help from the population if he is unable to do so.

The citizen, Twagirayezu Désiré-Apollinaire, made the remarks on December 26, 2025, during a public interaction between the president, residents and journalists at Muramvya Stadium in Gitega Province.

President Ndayishimiye has, since 2022, frequently stated that he faces threats from influential individuals whom he accuses of sabotaging the country’s governance and economy. He previously claimed that certain figures sought to overthrow him, allegations that later appeared to refer to former Prime Minister Gen. Alain-Guillaume Bunyoni, who was arrested and subsequently sentenced to life imprisonment.

As Burundi’s economy has deteriorated in recent years-marked by fuel shortages, scarcity of foreign currency and rising prices-Ndayishimiye has accused unnamed powerful figures of hoarding fuel, hiding foreign exchange in private homes, illegally exporting coffee, tea and precious minerals, and selling them abroad for personal gain.

In October 2025, Gabriel Rufyiri, president of the anti-corruption watchdog OLUCOME, revealed that Burundi exported minerals worth 26 billion Burundian francs last year, yet no revenue was deposited into the state treasury.

“If you go to the international market, in Dubai or elsewhere, you find tons of gold, coltan, cassiterite and wolframite,” Rufyiri said. “The question is: where does the money go?”

Addressing the president directly, Twagirayezu cited several public statements in which Ndayishimiye complained about the influence of these elites, including remarks made during a city-cleanliness campaign, a visit to the Office of the Burundi Revenue Authority (OBR), and meetings with officials overseeing the precious stones sector.

“You said, ‘Those big men in Jeeps are what we are fighting against,’” Twagirayezu recalled. “At the OBR, you said, ‘All the people I appointed are looters.’ In Kayanza, you named traders and said, ‘These are thieves who export precious stones illegally.’”

Twagirayezu reminded the president that he was elected by the people and vested with the authority of Head of State, arguing that no individual should be more powerful than him.

“We elected one president-you,” he said. “If these people are too powerful for you, then tell us who they are and ask the people to help you.”

In response, President Ndayishimiye said that Burundi is a democracy, and that he cannot govern through arbitrary force as monarchs once did.

“We are not in a monarchy,” he said. “The country does not belong to the Head of State. The president must follow the law.”

On the issue of mineral theft, Ndayishimiye acknowledged that some individuals involved are known but said it remains difficult to determine the exact quantities being smuggled. He cited Rainbow Burundi, a company he said officially exports up to 2,000 tons of minerals.

The president urged citizens to expose other suspected offenders, saying this would allow authorities to take legal action against them.

title: Central African Republic Holds Presidential Elections with Rwandan Security Support
excerpt: BANGUI - December 28, 2025 - Citizens of the Central African Republic (CAR) went to the polls for the presidential election, with over 2.3 million registered voters participating.
title_en: Central African Republic Holds Presidential Elections with Rwandan Security Support
excerpt_en: BANGUI - December 28, 2025 - Citizens of the Central African Republic (CAR) went to the polls for the presidential election, with over 2.3 million registered voters participating.
body_en:
BANGUI - December 28, 2025 - Citizens of the Central African Republic (CAR) went to the polls for the presidential election, with over 2.3 million registered voters participating. The election also includes votes for members of the National Assembly as well as provincial and municipal leaders.

Incumbent President Faustin-Archange Touadéra is seeking a third term, facing seven candidates, including former Prime Ministers Anicet Georges Dologuélé and Henri-Marie Dondra. Dologuélé finished second in the 2015 and 2020 elections, while Dondra served as Prime Minister from June 2021 to February 2022.

Touadéra, a former mathematics teacher turned politician, is widely expected to secure re-election. He previously served as Prime Minister under then-President François Bozizé from 2008 until 2013, when his government was overthrown by a rebel coalition. After a turbulent transition, Touadéra won the presidency in 2016, largely due to his perceived neutrality and lack of ties to armed groups such as Séléka and Anti-Balaka.

The current election has been conducted successfully, thanks in part to the Rwandan Armed Forces, who maintained security across key voting areas, performing tasks that would typically challenge United Nations peacekeeping operations. Touadéra is credited with helping restore stability to CAR through agreements and cooperation with Rwandan security forces.

title: Burundi Finance Minister Says He Faces Intimidation Over Fertilizer Payments
excerpt: Bujumbura - December 27, 2025 - Burundi’s Finance Minister, Dr. Alain Ndikumana, told Parliament that the management of the fertilizer company FOMI is attempting to intimidate him into authorizing payments not…
title_en: Burundi Finance Minister Says He Faces Intimidation Over Fertilizer Payments
excerpt_en: Bujumbura - December 27, 2025 - Burundi’s Finance Minister, Dr. Alain Ndikumana, told Parliament that the management of the fertilizer company FOMI is attempting to intimidate him into authorizing payments not…
body_en:
Bujumbura - December 27, 2025 - Burundi’s Finance Minister, Dr. Alain Ndikumana, told Parliament that the management of the fertilizer company FOMI is attempting to intimidate him into authorizing payments not stipulated in the government contract.

Speaking during the presentation of the government’s draft 2025/2026 budget to the Senate, Minister Ndikumana said FOMI submitted two documents demanding additional payments for fertilizer supplied beyond the agreed contract terms. One request sought 50.78 billion Fbu for fertilizer provided in the B and C periods of 2025, while another demanded 6.83 billion Fbu for B 2024 and A 2025 periods. He rejected both demands.

“Tell me, can we do these things? I do not owe anyone anything. I will not be afraid,” Minister Ndikumana said. He emphasized that he remained committed to transparency and the country’s long-term development vision.

The President of the Senate, Lt Gen Gervais Ndirakobuca, expressed support for the minister, acknowledging the difficulties of confronting corruption. “For our society to change, it is necessary to expose the truth. Burundians do not like the truth, but it will come out. We encourage you, do not give up,” he said.

FOMI, founded in February 2019 by Adrien Ntigacika, also known as Ziranokse, was created to reduce Burundi’s reliance on imported fertilizer. The company has grown influential in the country’s agricultural sector.

Economy and Tech.

title: Rwanda Approves $48 Million Loan for Gisagara Irrigation Project
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda - December 2025
title_en: Rwanda Approves $48 Million Loan for Gisagara Irrigation Project
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - December 2025
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - December 2025

The Rwandan Parliament has approved a loan agreement between the Government of Rwanda and the Export-Import Bank of China (Exim Bank of China) to fund an irrigation project in Gisagara District. The loan, totaling 344.5 million Yuan (over $48 million), was initially signed in Kigali on August 21, 2025.

The repayment plan spans 13.5 years, with Rwanda starting repayments after six and a half years at an interest rate of 2% per annum.

According to Finance Minister Murangwa Yusuf, the project aims to strengthen the agricultural sector and improve resilience against climate change by irrigating 2,640 hectares of land and introducing water harvesting and efficient irrigation technology in Giseke, Gisagara District.

“This will enable farmers to farm year-round, achieve increased yields, and adopt productive farming methods,” Minister Murangwa said, emphasizing the project’s economic and sustainable development impact.

The project will involve infrastructure construction, including the building of an irrigation dam and associated pipelines, helping farmers transition from rain-fed to irrigated agriculture.

During parliamentary discussions, MPs raised questions about the terms of the agreement, particularly the requirement to purchase equipment and technology from China.

MP Mukabalisa Germaine cautioned that such provisions could delay the project or increase costs, noting that similar technologies might be available locally or in the region. MP Rubagumya Furaha added that aligning technical standards with China’s should not pose a problem, despite structural differences between the countries.

Minister Murangwa responded that the collaboration with Exim Bank is standard practice for international loans, offering favorable terms such as a six-year grace period before repayment, and reiterated that independent inspectors will ensure the quality of equipment and construction.

The irrigation project is slated to begin by 2028 and is expected to boost agricultural productivity, enhance food security, and support Rwanda’s economic development goals.

title: RRA Warns Taxpayers Against Last-Minute Tax Payments
excerpt: KIGALI - The Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) has urged taxpayers to avoid waiting until the last minute to declare and pay real estate tax, road tax, and the third installment of corporate income tax, warning that delays…
title_en: RRA Warns Taxpayers Against Last-Minute Tax Payments
excerpt_en: KIGALI - The Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) has urged taxpayers to avoid waiting until the last minute to declare and pay real estate tax, road tax, and the third installment of corporate income tax, warning that delays…
body_en:
KIGALI - The Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) has urged taxpayers to avoid waiting until the last minute to declare and pay real estate tax, road tax, and the third installment of corporate income tax, warning that delays could result in penalties. The deadline for declaration and payment is December 31, 2025.

The Commissioner for Inland Revenue, Batamuliza Hajara, cautioned that as the festive season approaches, taxpayers should complete their obligations early to avoid technical disruptions and late-payment sanctions.

“Waiting until the last minute exposes taxpayers to penalties, especially if technology fails,” she said. “Everyone should pay their taxes and duties in advance so they can enjoy the holidays without any problems.”

Commissioner Batamuliza noted that since the beginning of the year, the RRA has introduced a system allowing early declaration and gradual payment of real estate tax, making it easier for property owners to comply on time.

“With this system in place, there should be no reason for anyone to be late or penalized,” she explained.

Real estate tax in Rwanda is calculated based on a property’s location and use, in accordance with the law governing the financing of local authorities. When a property consists of land with buildings, tax is levied on the value of both the building and the land, even if the land is not developed.

The tax rate, set annually by the District Council or the City of Kigali, must not exceed Rwf 80 per square meter.

Residential properties are taxed at 0.5% of the combined market value of the building and land.

Commercial buildings are taxed at 0.3% of their market value.

Industrial properties and land for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are taxed at 0.1%.

Detached houses benefit from preferential rates to encourage efficient land use. A plot with a three-storey residential building is taxed at 0.25%, while buildings with more than three floors are taxed at 0.1% of their market value.

Properties exempt from real estate tax include a single residential building designated as the owner’s primary residence, as well as ancillary buildings intended for one household. Even if the owner temporarily does not live in the residence, the building remains exempt, although the land itself remains taxable.

Commissioner Batamuliza clarified that if a property has already been taxed within the same year, a new owner is not required to pay the tax again.

“As of today, more than 70% of taxpayers have already declared their taxes,” she said. “We understand that some have not yet paid, but our message is clear: those who have not declared must do so before December 31.”

title: Ndayishimiye Accused of Deploying Imbonerakure to Control Gold Mines in Eastern DRC
excerpt: SOUTH KIVU, DRC - Despite the withdrawal of Burundian troops from parts of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) following the capture of Uvira, Burundian activities in the region have not ceased, according to…
title_en: Ndayishimiye Accused of Deploying Imbonerakure to Control Gold Mines in Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: SOUTH KIVU, DRC - Despite the withdrawal of Burundian troops from parts of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) following the capture of Uvira, Burundian activities in the region have not ceased, according to…
body_en:
SOUTH KIVU, DRC - Despite the withdrawal of Burundian troops from parts of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) following the capture of Uvira, Burundian activities in the region have not ceased, according to local and regional sources.

Reports indicate that Burundian President Evariste Ndayishimiye ordered members of the Imbonerakure youth movement, initially deployed to fight the AFC/M23 alliance, to remain in the DRC and monitor gold mining sites in South Kivu Province.

The Imbonerakure are reportedly active in areas surrounding Uvira and Fizi Territory, where they are said to be involved in the management of gold mines following the withdrawal of Burundian troops from locations including Bijombo, Bibogobogo, Rugezi, Point-Zéro, Minembwe, and Bijabo between December 14 and 17, 2025.

The fall of Uvira reportedly triggered the large-scale withdrawal of Burundian forces, which had an estimated 20,000 troops deployed in South Kivu alone. The fighting around the city resulted in numerous casualties, while others fled toward surrounding hills and back into Burundi.

However, sources say the Imbonerakure remained behind, working alongside local armed groups, particularly Mai Mai fighters, in areas rich in precious minerals.

The Imbonerakure are alleged to be jointly managing mining sites in:

Kageregere, Gasozo, Mangwa, and Masango (Uvira area),

Kamituga, Nyamibungu, and Kitutu (Mwenga Territory).

These deployments reportedly trace back to 2018, when Burundian forces and Imbonerakure were sent to eastern DRC under the Burundi-DRC Joint Task Force (TAFOC), officially mandated to combat Burundian rebel groups operating across the border.

According to multiple sources, once in the DRC, these forces allegedly collaborated with Congolese armed groups, contributing to insecurity while focusing on control of mineral resources.

While President Ndayishimiye has consistently portrayed himself as a regional peacemaker, critics argue that the continued involvement of Burundian-linked forces in mining activities contradicts his stated objective of restoring peace and stability in eastern DRC.

Although Burundian authorities claim their deployment aimed at protecting civilians, sources allege that the forces failed to do so and instead became involved in violent operations, forced displacement, and the seizure of mining interests.

Some Imbonerakure members, speaking anonymously, reportedly expressed shock and disillusionment following the battle for Uvira, citing the deaths of comrades and serious injuries sustained during combat. Others said they fled the DRC rather than return to fighting, questioning the purpose of the war and their role in it.

Observers note that Ndayishimiye’s decision to deploy forces to the DRC has placed thousands of Burundian soldiers at risk, with many killed, wounded, or permanently disabled.

body_fr:
SOUTH KIVU, DRC - Despite the withdrawal of Burundian troops from parts of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) following the capture of Uvira, Burundian activities in the region have not ceased, according to local and regional sources.

Reports indicate that Burundian President Evariste Ndayishimiye ordered members of the Imbonerakure youth movement, initially deployed to fight the AFC/M23 alliance, to remain in the DRC and monitor gold mining sites in South Kivu Province.

The Imbonerakure are reportedly active in areas surrounding Uvira and Fizi Territory, where they are said to be involved in the management of gold mines following the withdrawal of Burundian troops from locations including Bijombo, Bibogobogo, Rugezi, Point-Zéro, Minembwe, and Bijabo between December 14 and 17, 2025.

The fall of Uvira reportedly triggered the large-scale withdrawal of Burundian forces, which had an estimated 20,000 troops deployed in South Kivu alone. The fighting around the city resulted in numerous casualties, while others fled toward surrounding hills and back into Burundi.

However, sources say the Imbonerakure remained behind, working alongside local armed groups, particularly Mai Mai fighters, in areas rich in precious minerals.

The Imbonerakure are alleged to be jointly managing mining sites in:

Kageregere, Gasozo, Mangwa, and Masango (Uvira area),

Kamituga, Nyamibungu, and Kitutu (Mwenga Territory).

These deployments reportedly trace back to 2018, when Burundian forces and Imbonerakure were sent to eastern DRC under the Burundi-DRC Joint Task Force (TAFOC), officially mandated to combat Burundian rebel groups operating across the border.

According to multiple sources, once in the DRC, these forces allegedly collaborated with Congolese armed groups, contributing to insecurity while focusing on control of mineral resources.

While President Ndayishimiye has consistently portrayed himself as a regional peacemaker, critics argue that the continued involvement of Burundian-linked forces in mining activities contradicts his stated objective of restoring peace and stability in eastern DRC.

Although Burundian authorities claim their deployment aimed at protecting civilians, sources allege that the forces failed to do so and instead became involved in violent operations, forced displacement, and the seizure of mining interests.

Some Imbonerakure members, speaking anonymously, reportedly expressed shock and disillusionment following the battle for Uvira, citing the deaths of comrades and serious injuries sustained during combat. Others said they fled the DRC rather than return to fighting, questioning the purpose of the war and their role in it.

Observers note that Ndayishimiye’s decision to deploy forces to the DRC has placed thousands of Burundian soldiers at risk, with many killed, wounded, or permanently disabled.

Meanwhile, activities linked to personal enrichment and mineral exploitation by armed actors are reported to be increasing, reinforcing concerns that economic interests, rather than security or peace, remain the driving force behind continued instability in eastern DRC.

title: Rwanda’s Agricultural and Livestock Exports Earn Over $13.7 Million in Five Days
excerpt: KIGALI - Rwanda’s agricultural and livestock exports generated more than $13.7 million in just five days, according to the National Agricultural and Livestock Export Board (NAEB).
title_en: Rwanda’s Agricultural and Livestock Exports Earn Over $13.7 Million in Five Days
excerpt_en: KIGALI - Rwanda’s agricultural and livestock exports generated more than $13.7 million in just five days, according to the National Agricultural and Livestock Export Board (NAEB).
body_en:
KIGALI - Rwanda’s agricultural and livestock exports generated more than $13.7 million in just five days, according to the National Agricultural and Livestock Export Board (NAEB).

NAEB reported that between December 15 and 19, 2025, exports totaling 9,538 tons earned $13,764,685 in foreign revenue.

The earnings were largely driven by coffee and tea exports. A total of 893 tons of coffee generated $6,264,518, while 931 tons of tea earned $2,758,516. Additionally, 500 tons of vegetables brought in $345,176.

Exports also included 313 tons of fruits, sold for $241,609, and 21 tons of flowers, which earned $113,958.

Rwandan agricultural products were exported to several international markets, including France, the United Kingdom, the United Arab Emirates, the Netherlands, Saudi Arabia, as well as neighboring and other African countries.

Other agricultural products, weighing 6,572 tons, generated $3,425,424, while animal products totaling 308 tons earned $615,484. These were mainly sold to regional markets, other African countries, and Oman.

NAEB noted that this performance follows another strong export window between December 8 and 12, 2025, during which Rwanda earned $12.5 million from agricultural and livestock exports weighing 9,650 tons.

Earlier, on December 18, 2025, the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock announced that Rwanda’s agricultural and livestock exports in 2025 had already generated more than $893.1 million, equivalent to approximately Rwf 1,301 billion.

According to a report by the National Institute of Statistics, agricultural and livestock exports reached over $893 million in the 2024/25 fiscal year, up from $839 million in 2023/24, marking an increase of 6.4%.

Under the Second National Strategy for Economic Acceleration (NST2), Rwanda aims to further boost foreign exchange earnings by increasing agricultural and livestock exports to Rwf 1,540 billion annually by 2029.

title: Rwanda Benefits from Double Taxation Agreements with 18 Countries
excerpt: KIGALI - December 22, 2025 - Rwanda has signed double taxation avoidance agreements with 18 countries, a move that has significantly contributed to attracting investors and strengthening the country’s position as a…
title_en: Rwanda Benefits from Double Taxation Agreements with 18 Countries
excerpt_en: KIGALI - December 22, 2025 - Rwanda has signed double taxation avoidance agreements with 18 countries, a move that has significantly contributed to attracting investors and strengthening the country’s position as a…
body_en:
KIGALI - December 22, 2025 - Rwanda has signed double taxation avoidance agreements with 18 countries, a move that has significantly contributed to attracting investors and strengthening the country’s position as a regional financial hub, the Minister of Finance and Economic Planning, Yusuf Murangwa, has said.

The minister made the remarks as the Chamber of Deputies approved a tax agreement between Rwanda and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People’s Republic of China. The agreement, signed in Hong Kong on October 9, 2025, aims to eliminate double taxation on income and prevent tax evasion.

According to Murangwa, the agreement will strengthen bilateral relations, promote trade and investment, enhance cooperation in tax matters, and facilitate the exchange of information related to tax evasion and avoidance, while ensuring respect for taxpayers’ rights.

“This agreement also helps us make Kigali a financial services hub,” Murangwa said.

He explained that Rwanda prioritizes signing such agreements with major trade and investment partners, as part of a broader strategy to attract foreign investors by creating a predictable and favorable tax environment.

“The Government of Rwanda is committed to increasing the number of countries with which it has agreements to eliminate double taxation on income and prevent tax evasion,” he added.

During the parliamentary session, MP Phoibe Kanyange questioned the tangible benefits Rwanda has gained from these agreements and asked how the country selects its partners.

In response, Murangwa said Rwanda has already approached 75 countries that could potentially sign similar agreements, while 18 agreements are currently in force and others are under negotiation.

“This requires a strong monitoring mechanism, because circumstances can change either in Rwanda or in partner countries,” he said. “These agreements are meant to facilitate financial investments, and monitoring them is part of the responsibilities of the Kigali International Financial Centre (KIFC).”

Murangwa noted that although Rwanda has only recently begun positioning itself as a financial hub in Africa through the KIFC, the results are already becoming visible.

“We are still at an early stage, but the benefits are starting to show. Some financial-sector investors have already established operations in Rwanda,” he said.

He added that Rwanda benefits not only through taxation but also through fees and service-related revenues, which in some cases generate more income than direct taxes, while remaining attractive to investors.

On the criteria for selecting partner countries, Murangwa emphasized that Rwanda focuses on strategic national interests and partners with countries that have strong financial influence and integrity.

“Hong Kong, for example, is a very strong international financial center. Working with such partners helps attract investment to the region and ensures that capital is spent in Rwanda,” he said.

Murangwa also stressed that investors themselves seek jurisdictions with double taxation agreements to avoid being taxed twice.

“We are careful and work only with countries that have integrity. We would not cooperate with countries that could create financial risks for Rwanda,” he said.

Earlier this month, on December 11, 2025, the Kigali International Financial Centre (KIFC) marked five years of operation, during which more than 200 investors established operations in Rwanda, with investments exceeding $1 billion.

title: RwandAir Assists Passengers After Dubai Flight Cancellations
excerpt: Kigali - December 28, 2025 - RwandAir, Rwanda’s national carrier, has announced support for passengers affected by the recent cancellation of flights to Dubai.
title_en: RwandAir Assists Passengers After Dubai Flight Cancellations
excerpt_en: Kigali - December 28, 2025 - RwandAir, Rwanda’s national carrier, has announced support for passengers affected by the recent cancellation of flights to Dubai.
body_en:
Kigali - December 28, 2025 - RwandAir, Rwanda’s national carrier, has announced support for passengers affected by the recent cancellation of flights to Dubai.

The airline confirmed it will help affected travelers secure alternative flights after reports emerged of passengers stranded at O.R. Tambo International Airport due to last-minute flight cancellations.

RwandAir expressed regret over the disruption, emphasizing that while the airline strives to inform passengers of schedule changes as early as possible, unexpected disruptions sometimes occur.

“We assure our passengers that our ticketing staff will assist them in boarding the next available flight,” the airline said in a statement.

RwandAir has recently expanded its network with new routes to Zanzibar and Mombasa, and continues to operate flights to multiple international destinations, both directly and through partnerships with global carriers.

title: Rwandan Security Forces Join Mozambican Communities in Sports Event to Promote Unity and Stability
excerpt: Mocímboa da Praia, Mozambique - December 21, 2023
title_en: Rwandan Security Forces Join Mozambican Communities in Sports Event to Promote Unity and Stability
excerpt_en: Mocímboa da Praia, Mozambique - December 21, 2023
body_en:
Mocímboa da Praia, Mozambique - December 21, 2023

Members of the Rwandan Security Forces (RSF) deployed in Cabo Delgado Province participated in a community sports event alongside residents and local authorities, highlighting growing civil-military cooperation in northern Mozambique.

The event, organized by the Mocímboa da Praia City Council, brought together security personnel, community members, and local leaders with the aim of strengthening unity, cooperation, and social cohesion between government institutions and the population. It also served as a celebration of the improved security situation in the area and underscored the role of sports in promoting public health and well-being.

Addressing participants after the activities, local leaders emphasized that such initiatives help build trust, encourage collaboration, and support the overall welfare of communities emerging from years of insecurity.

Speaking on behalf of the Rwandan Security Forces, ACP Bertin Mutezintare reaffirmed the RSF’s commitment to working closely with the local population on security matters and broader public initiatives.

“We believe in close cooperation with the population,” he said, expressing the RSF’s intention to expand community sports activities across the province as a means of strengthening relations with civilians.

The Mayor of Mocímboa da Praia, Helena Bandeila, praised both the Rwandan and Mozambican Security Forces for their decisive role in restoring peace and stability in Cabo Delgado. She also called on local leaders to encourage residents to take part in weekly public sports activities, stressing that regular physical exercise is vital for maintaining good health.

Since July 2021, Rwandan and Mozambican forces have jointly conducted operations against terrorist groups, particularly the Ansar al-Sunnah movement, which had severely destabilized Cabo Delgado. According to officials, these operations have successfully dislodged insurgents from key positions, pursued them into forested areas, and significantly reduced their capacity.

Following the restoration of security, displaced populations have gradually returned to their homes, resuming livelihoods and local development activities.

In a further sign of deepening bilateral ties, the governments of Rwanda and Mozambique renewed cooperation agreements in August 2025, covering investment and counter-terrorism, reinforcing their long-term partnership in regional security and development.

title: Bukavu Residents Protest AFC/M23 Withdrawal from Uvira
excerpt: BUKAVU, South Kivu - Thousands of residents of South Kivu Province in the city of Bukavu staged a peaceful demonstration on 23 December 2025, protesting the recent withdrawal of AFC/M23 forces from Uvira.
title_en: Bukavu Residents Protest AFC/M23 Withdrawal from Uvira
excerpt_en: BUKAVU, South Kivu - Thousands of residents of South Kivu Province in the city of Bukavu staged a peaceful demonstration on 23 December 2025, protesting the recent withdrawal of AFC/M23 forces from Uvira.
body_en:
BUKAVU, South Kivu - Thousands of residents of South Kivu Province in the city of Bukavu staged a peaceful demonstration on 23 December 2025, protesting the recent withdrawal of AFC/M23 forces from Uvira.

The AFC/M23 had taken control of Uvira on 9 December 2025 but committed to withdrawing on 15 December in support of the Doha peace process. Many residents expressed concern that the withdrawal could leave them vulnerable.

Miki Mutiki, a representative of SOCIVE, stated, “The people of South Kivu find the way to remove AFC/M23 from the city of Uvira inadequate.”

Governor of South Kivu, Patrick Busu Bwa Ng’wi, acknowledged the concerns of the population, thanking them for their peaceful march. He confirmed that the AFC/M23 will continue efforts to promote peace and engage with all stakeholders to ensure residents can live safely. He also urged Uvira residents to remain strong, promising a visit once the situation stabilizes.

The demonstrators called on both warring parties to respect the ceasefire agreed upon during the Doha talks, highlighting the community’s desire for peace and coexistence.

The march reflected a humanitarian plea from the people of Bukavu, emphasizing their commitment to stability and protection of civilian lives in the region.

title: Western Rwanda: 1,375 Families May Require Food Assistance After Poor Rains
excerpt: WESTERN PROVINCE, Rwanda - December 27, 2025 - Authorities in Rwanda’s Western Province have warned that 1,375 families may require food assistance following insufficient rainfall that severely affected crop production…
title_en: Western Rwanda: 1,375 Families May Require Food Assistance After Poor Rains
excerpt_en: WESTERN PROVINCE, Rwanda - December 27, 2025 - Authorities in Rwanda’s Western Province have warned that 1,375 families may require food assistance following insufficient rainfall that severely affected crop production…
body_en:
WESTERN PROVINCE, Rwanda - December 27, 2025 - Authorities in Rwanda’s Western Province have warned that 1,375 families may require food assistance following insufficient rainfall that severely affected crop production across several districts.

According to the Western Province Administration, prolonged dry spells and extreme heat caused crop failure in some areas, while previously planted fields recorded very low yields.

A province-wide assessment found that more than 1,375 households are at risk due to the poor agricultural season, particularly those whose crops withered under intense heat or failed to germinate due to lack of rain.

Speaking to Rwanda Broadcasting Agency (RBA), Western Province Governor Jean Bosco Ntibitura said the situation does not amount to famine, as vulnerable households have already been identified.

“We cannot say that there is a famine in the Western Province,” Ntibitura said. “The challenge is related to rainfall shortages in some fields. While some families will harvest normally, others will have low yields and may need food assistance.”

The crops most affected include beans, soybeans, sorghum, and parts of the maize crop.

“A total of 1,375 families across the province may face food shortages,” the governor explained. “While some households will be harvesting, others planted but will produce very little.”

In Rutsiro District, 57 families in Murunda and Mushubati sectors are likely to require assistance if current conditions persist.

In Rusizi District, authorities identified 837 families in Nkombo and Nkanka sectors who may need support due to overcrowding and reduced harvests.

Nyamasheke District remains among the hardest hit, with 481 families expected to need assistance. In Nyabitekeri Sector alone, 337 households were affected by scorching heat that destroyed crops, although areas that received sufficient rainfall recorded better yields.

In Karongi District, some crops initially showed signs of stunted growth but later improved after rainfall resumed.

The Western Province Administration emphasized that households that successfully planted earlier in the season are now entering the harvesting period, reducing the overall risk of widespread food insecurity.

title: Kicukiro: Domestic Worker Suspected of Killing Colleague and Hiding Body in Box
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda - December 21, 2025
title_en: Kicukiro: Domestic Worker Suspected of Killing Colleague and Hiding Body in Box
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - December 21, 2025
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - December 21, 2025

A 28-year-old male domestic worker is suspected of killing his female colleague, concealing her body in a clothes box, and fleeing the scene in a crime reported in Amahoro Village, Karembure Cell, Gahanga Sector, Kicukiro District, authorities said.

The City of Kigali Spokesperson, Ntirenganya Emma Claudine confirmed the incident, stating that local authorities immediately alerted security forces upon receiving the report.

“That is the case. A female domestic worker has died. As local authorities, the first thing we do when someone goes missing is to notify the security forces,” she said.

She added that the Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) and the National Police were informed and have launched a criminal investigation. Residents were urged to cooperate with authorities, avoid violence and crime, and report any suspicious activity without delay.

Samuel Ntakirutimana, identified the suspect as a 28-year-old man from Gasabo District, Rusororo Sector.According to Ntakirutimana, he and his wife left their home on the morning of December 21 to attend a wedding, leaving the household in the care of their domestic workers. One maid was assigned to childcare, while the other handled household chores.

At around 5:00 p.m., concern arose when repeated calls to the house went unanswered. Ntakirutimana then asked his younger brother, who lives nearby, to check on the situation.

“My brother knocked, but no one answered. The keys to our bedroom were kept at my grandmother’s house, so another brother went to get them. When they entered, they found the door open and went to check on the child. The door to our room was broken, but the child was found sleeping,” he said.

Ntakirutimana’s wife and his elder brother rushed to the house, discovering signs of a break-in. The bedroom was ransacked, clothes belonging to the couple were packed into bags, a mattress had been moved to the guest room, and the bags were grouped together-suggesting preparations to flee.

“My brother returned to the wedding venue and informed me by phone: ‘We found Mutoni in a box; she was killed,’” Ntakirutimana said. “I left immediately and went straight to the RIB.”

He noted that there had been no prior conflicts reported at the household. At the time of the incident, the children in the home were six months and three weeks old.

The suspect fled and is currently the subject of an active manhunt by security forces.

Under Rwandan law, anyone convicted by a court of manslaughter or homicide faces life imprisonment.

“That is the case. A female domestic worker has died. As local authorities, the first thing we do when someone goes missing is to notify the security forces,” she said.

She added that the Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) and the National Police were informed and have launched a criminal investigation. Residents were urged to cooperate with authorities, avoid violence and crime, and report any suspicious activity without delay.

Samuel Ntakirutimana, identified the suspect as a 28-year-old man from Gasabo District, Rusororo Sector.According to Ntakirutimana, he and his wife left their home on the morning of December 21 to attend a wedding, leaving the household in the care of their domestic workers. One maid was assigned to childcare, while the other handled household chores.

At around 5:00 p.m., concern arose when repeated calls to the house went unanswered. Ntakirutimana then asked his younger brother, who lives nearby, to check on the situation.

“My brother knocked, but no one answered. The keys to our bedroom were kept at my grandmother’s house, so another brother went to get them. When they entered, they found the door open and went to check on the child. The door to our room was broken, but the child was found sleeping,” he said.

Ntakirutimana’s wife and his elder brother rushed to the house, discovering signs of a break-in. The bedroom was ransacked, clothes belonging to the couple were packed into bags, a mattress had been moved to the guest room, and the bags were grouped together-suggesting preparations to flee.

“My brother returned to the wedding venue and informed me by phone: ‘We found Mutoni in a box; she was killed,’” Ntakirutimana said. “I left immediately and went straight to the RIB.”

He noted that there had been no prior conflicts reported at the household. At the time of the incident, the children in the home were six months and three weeks old.

The suspect fled and is currently the subject of an active manhunt by security forces.

Under Rwandan law, anyone convicted by a court of manslaughter or homicide faces life imprisonment.

title: Karongi: Four Arrested Over Killing of Man Accused of Witchcraft
excerpt: Karongi District, Rwanda - December 21, 2025
title_en: Karongi: Four Arrested Over Killing of Man Accused of Witchcraft
excerpt_en: Karongi District, Rwanda - December 21, 2025
body_en:
Karongi District, Rwanda - December 21, 2025

The Rwanda National Police (RNP), working in close collaboration with local authorities and residents, have arrested four suspects in connection with the killing of Ndiramiye Vianney, 55, who was accused by villagers of practicing witchcraft.

The attack occurred in Karambo Village, Gisovu Cell, Twumba Sector, where the suspects-part of a group of six-allegedly stormed the victim’s home armed with traditional weapons.

According to authorities, the incident followed the death of Mushimiye Ndimubanzi at Mugonero Hospital, who reportedly left a note claiming he had been poisoned by Ndiramiye.

Police say Ndiramiye was bathing when he noticed the assailants approaching. He ran inside his house and locked himself in, but the attackers forced the doors open, assaulted him, and inflicted serious injuries on both his wife and daughter. Some of the suspects reportedly guarded the entrance to prevent rescue attempts.

Alerted residents contacted the police, and the injured were rushed to hospital. However, Ndiramiye, who sustained a fatal head injury after being struck with an axe, succumbed to his wounds.

The Executive Secretary of Twumba Sector, Uwimana Phanuel, told IGIHE that the suspects initially fled the scene, but joint efforts by residents and security agencies led to the arrest of four individuals, while two remain at large.

“Four suspects have been arrested and are being held at the Twumba Criminal Investigation Department Station. Two others are still being sought,” Uwimana said.

He strongly condemned the killing, describing it as an inhumane act, and urged residents to refrain from mob justice.

Uwimana emphasized that Rwanda has legal institutions capable of scientifically investigating poisoning claims, calling on citizens to report suspicions to the Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) rather than resorting to violence.

“There are institutions in Rwanda with the capacity to test and confirm poisoning. Justice must be sought through the law, not through violence,” he said.

title: Kayonza: Police Officer Killed in Motorcycle Accident
excerpt: KAYONZA, Rwanda - August 26, 2025 - A 22-year-old police officer on duty in Kayonza District has died after being struck by a speeding motorcycle, prompting renewed calls from the Rwanda National Police (RNP) for…
title_en: Kayonza: Police Officer Killed in Motorcycle Accident
excerpt_en: KAYONZA, Rwanda - August 26, 2025 - A 22-year-old police officer on duty in Kayonza District has died after being struck by a speeding motorcycle, prompting renewed calls from the Rwanda National Police (RNP) for…
body_en:
KAYONZA, Rwanda - August 26, 2025 - A 22-year-old police officer on duty in Kayonza District has died after being struck by a speeding motorcycle, prompting renewed calls from the Rwanda National Police (RNP) for motorists to avoid reckless driving.

The accident occurred at around 7:00 a.m. in Karambi Cell, Murundi Sector, Kayonza District. According to police, the officer was on duty when he attempted to cross a dirt road and was hit by a motorcycle traveling at high speed.

The spokesperson for the Rwanda National Police Traffic Division, SP Emmanuel Kayigi, confirmed the incident, saying the officer sustained serious injuries and later died at Faisal Hospital on Friday evening.

“The motorcycle was speeding and struck the police officer, causing severe injuries. He did not die instantly but passed away upon arrival at the hospital,” SP Kayigi said.

Police confirmed that the motorcyclist, a young man, was also injured and has been admitted to Kanombe Hospital, while his passenger sustained minor injuries and returned home shortly after the incident.

SP Kayigi described the crash as an accident caused by excessive speed, emphasizing that most road accidents are preventable if traffic rules are respected.

“Drivers should avoid carelessness, whether on dirt roads or paved roads. Accidents can happen anywhere and at any time,” he said.“No one should assume that a road with little traffic allows for high speed. You must remember that you are not the only road user.”

The Rwanda National Police expressed its condolences to the family of the deceased officer and urged both drivers and passengers to play an active role in road safety, encouraging passengers to warn motorcyclists against speeding.

The incident comes just a week after another police officer was killed in a separate road accident in Kigali’s city center, highlighting ongoing concerns over road safety and reckless driving.

title: Burundi: Prisoners from 2015 Unrest Will Not Be Released After Serving Sentences
excerpt: BUJUMBURA, Burundi - December 26, 2025 - President Evariste Ndayishimiye has announced that individuals imprisoned for crimes committed during the 2015 political unrest will remain in prison even after completing their sentences.
title_en: Burundi: Prisoners from 2015 Unrest Will Not Be Released After Serving Sentences
excerpt_en: BUJUMBURA, Burundi - December 26, 2025 - President Evariste Ndayishimiye has announced that individuals imprisoned for crimes committed during the 2015 political unrest will remain in prison even after completing their sentences.
body_en:
BUJUMBURA, Burundi - December 26, 2025 - President Evariste Ndayishimiye has announced that individuals imprisoned for crimes committed during the 2015 political unrest will remain in prison even after completing their sentences. The announcement was made during a meeting with Bishop Martin Blaise Nyaboho, President of the National Commission for Human Rights (CNIDH), who raised concerns about the prolonged detention of some individuals, including those acquitted or who had served short terms.

President Ndayishimiye explained that a final decision on releases will be guided by a list from the Minister of Justice, but emphasized that individuals deemed criminals during the 2015 unrest will remain incarcerated. He stated, “Criminals because of the ongoing crime, if you release them, they will return to work with these criminals… People did evil here in 2015, then they were sentenced to a short term, today you release them and you find that they have returned to work with others.”

The 2015 unrest, sparked by Pierre Nkurunziza’s controversial third term, involved protests and attempts to overthrow the government. Those targeted for continued imprisonment include individuals prosecuted for their role in these events, with charges primarily related to threats against national security.

Under Burundian law, the Head of State has limited authority in cases of release, though the Supreme Court can grant pardons. President Ndayishimiye’s decision highlights the government’s continued caution in addressing security concerns tied to the events of 2015.

title: Burundi Masses Troops and Heavy Weapons Near Rwandan Border as Regional Tensions Escalate
excerpt: 15 December 2025 - Burundi has been deploying large numbers of troops and heavy weapons near its border with Rwanda for several days, amid rising tensions between the two neighboring countries.
title_en: Burundi Masses Troops and Heavy Weapons Near Rwandan Border as Regional Tensions Escalate
excerpt_en: 15 December 2025 - Burundi has been deploying large numbers of troops and heavy weapons near its border with Rwanda for several days, amid rising tensions between the two neighboring countries.
body_en:
15 December 2025 - Burundi has been deploying large numbers of troops and heavy weapons near its border with Rwanda for several days, amid rising tensions between the two neighboring countries.

The military buildup comes as the Burundian government faces mounting pressure following setbacks in South Kivu Province, where Burundian forces, alongside the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) army, Wazalendo militias, and the FDLR, lost control of significant parts of the Rusizi Valley to AFC/M23 fighters.

Speaking recently before the United Nations Security Council, Burundi’s Ambassador Zéphyrin Maniratanga accused Rwanda of supporting the AFC/M23, arguing that such backing justifies Burundi’s security posture and confrontation with the armed group.

A senior Burundian military official, speaking to SOS Médias, confirmed that substantial deployments have been made, particularly in Busoni commune, Butanyerera province, close to the Gasenyi-Nemba border with Rwanda.

“There are heavy weapons deployed to prevent anything from coming from Rwanda,” the officer said.

In Busoni, police trucks have reportedly been transporting additional troops to military camps, including the 411th battalion base in Mutwenzi, according to local media sources.

Security patrols have intensified across parts of northern Burundi near the Rwandan border. Police units and members of the Imbonerakure, the youth wing affiliated with the ruling CNDD-FDD party, have been seen conducting night patrols.

While no official announcements have been made instructing residents to limit their movements, locals say informal restrictions are being enforced. Civilians are reportedly expected to return home early, with roads effectively deserted after 8 p.m.

“They are ordered to return home early, before 8 p.m.,” said a resident of the Munzenze area. “It is not written anywhere, but we all know what it means.”

Residents living near the border say fear is growing as rumors of a possible war between Burundi and Rwanda circulate.

“We sleep in our clothes, ready to flee when they shoot,” another resident said.

In Bujumbura Province, formerly Cibitoke, security measures have also been reinforced. Heavy weapons stationed in the area have been used to shell the Kamanyola Center, near the Bugarama border with Rwanda.

The Burundian army’s shelling of Kamanyola reportedly triggered a swift response from AFC/M23 fighters, who then launched operations that enabled them to seize parts of the Rusizi Valley and advance as far as Uvira, on the shores of Lake Tanganyika.

According to reliable sources, Burundi has been acquiring significant quantities of heavy weapons and combat drones for some time, suggesting preparations for a large-scale conflict. Some of this equipment has already been used in the fighting in South Kivu.

In the past two weeks, at least 30 trucks loaded with weapons reportedly entered the Mukoni military base in Buhumuza Province, underscoring the scale of Burundi’s ongoing military buildup.

As regional tensions intensify, the concentration of forces along the Burundi-Rwanda border has heightened fears of a broader confrontation, with civilians increasingly caught in the shadow of a potential cross-border conflict.

title: Sukhoi-25 Jets and Drones Strike Banyamulenge Areas in South Kivu
excerpt: South Kivu Province, DR Congo - Congolese warplanes and combat drones have been deployed in a series of air strikes targeting areas inhabited by the Banyamulenge community in South Kivu Province, triggering civilian…
title_en: Sukhoi-25 Jets and Drones Strike Banyamulenge Areas in South Kivu
excerpt_en: South Kivu Province, DR Congo - Congolese warplanes and combat drones have been deployed in a series of air strikes targeting areas inhabited by the Banyamulenge community in South Kivu Province, triggering civilian…
body_en:
South Kivu Province, DR Congo - Congolese warplanes and combat drones have been deployed in a series of air strikes targeting areas inhabited by the Banyamulenge community in South Kivu Province, triggering civilian casualties and renewed condemnation from opposition figures.

Opposition politician Moïse Nyarugabo said the first drone strike occurred in the Rugezi area of Fizi territory at around 5:00 p.m. on December 15, 2025.

According to Nyarugabo, a Sukhoi-25 fighter jet later carried out attacks in the Rwitsankuku area, before continuing toward Gahwera and Mikenke, where it also opened fire.

“These attacks caused the deaths of many civilians and left others injured,” Nyarugabo said.

The strikes followed an earlier Sukhoi-25 attack in Rwitsankuku on the morning of December 14, indicating a sustained aerial campaign in the region. The aircraft and drones involved are believed to be Burundian.

Nyarugabo called for accountability, insisting that those responsible for ordering and executing the strikes must be held to account.

“Those who ordered these attacks, including the pilots and the airport authorities from which these aircraft operated, must be held responsible,” he said.

Escalating Air Campaign After Rusizi Valley Defeat

The intensification of air and drone attacks in Banyamulenge-inhabited areas comes amid shifting dynamics on the ground. Since last week, aerial operations in South Kivu have increased following the defeat of Burundian forces, the DRC army (FARDC), Wazalendo militias, and the FDLR by AFC/M23 fighters in the Rusizi Valley.

The latest strikes have heightened fears among civilians in Fizi territory and surrounding areas, as concerns grow over the use of heavy aerial firepower in populated zones and the rising toll on non-combatants.

As fighting continues to evolve in eastern DR Congo, calls for independent investigations and protection of civilians are mounting, amid warnings that the expanding use of warplanes and drones risks further destabilizing the region.

title: AFC/M23 Facilitates Return of More Than 500 Burundians Stranded in Uvira
excerpt: Uvira, DR Congo - December 14, 2025 - The AFC/M23 coalition has facilitated the return of more than 500 Burundian nationals from Uvira territory in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, after days during which they were…
title_en: AFC/M23 Facilitates Return of More Than 500 Burundians Stranded in Uvira
excerpt_en: Uvira, DR Congo - December 14, 2025 - The AFC/M23 coalition has facilitated the return of more than 500 Burundian nationals from Uvira territory in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, after days during which they were…
body_en:
Uvira, DR Congo - December 14, 2025 - The AFC/M23 coalition has facilitated the return of more than 500 Burundian nationals from Uvira territory in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, after days during which they were unable to go home due to border closures and ongoing fighting.

The Burundians, many of whom had traveled to South Kivu Province in search of livelihood opportunities, found themselves stranded when the Burundian government closed the Kavimvira and Vugizo border crossings following the entry of AFC/M23 into Uvira on December 9.

Several returnees described days of fear and uncertainty.

“I was stuck here because of the fighting. Sometimes we had to hide. Some of our brothers stayed behind in the city of Uvira. I am happy to return safely,” one Burundian man said as he crossed through the Kavimvira border.

Another returnee, identified as Mugenzi, said many Burundian traders faced the same predicament.

“I am not the only Burundian businessman in this city. There were many of us with the same problem. Our parents were worried about our lives,” he said. “But we are not fleeing. We are returning home while waiting to see if it will be possible to come back.”

AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the decision to facilitate the return was taken after discussions with the Burundian authorities, stressing that the group had not closed the border on its side.

“These are our fellow Africans,” Kanyuka said. “Burundians worked and lived in the DRC, but now they want to return to their country. Our border is always open, but Burundi’s is closed. We asked them to open it for humanitarian reasons so that their citizens could go home.”

The operation underscores the humanitarian impact of the border closures, which have disrupted the lives of civilians on both sides of the frontier.

Thousands of Congolese Still Stranded in Burundi

While Burundians have been assisted to return home, the situation remains unresolved for Congolese refugees in Burundi. More than 20,000 Congolese reportedly fled into Burundi when AFC/M23 entered Uvira.

According to sources on the ground, those Congolese who wish to return to the DRC are still unable to do so, as the Burundian government has not reopened the border.

As the security situation in South Kivu continues to evolve, civilians remain caught between military developments and political decisions, with border closures increasingly shaping the humanitarian landscape of the region.

title: FDLR Burns Village in Walikale, Killing Four
excerpt: The FDLR armed group has burned down an entire village in Walikale territory, North Kivu province, in eastern DRC, killing at least four people and forcing dozens to flee.
title_en: FDLR Burns Village in Walikale, Killing Four
excerpt_en: The FDLR armed group has burned down an entire village in Walikale territory, North Kivu province, in eastern DRC, killing at least four people and forcing dozens to flee.
body_en:
The FDLR armed group has burned down an entire village in Walikale territory, North Kivu province, in eastern DRC, killing at least four people and forcing dozens to flee.

The attack occurred on the morning of December 15, 2025, in the Tuonane area of Waloa Loanda, after an FDLR fighter identifying himself as “General Mudayongwa” ordered residents to leave the area. Locals rejected his claim that he had purchased the land from local authorities, prompting the assault and the destruction of all homes.

Clashes also erupted between the FDLR and Mai Mai Kifuafua fighters, leaving two Mai Mai combatants dead after exchanges involving light and heavy weapons.

title: AFC/M23 Accuses DRC Forces of Ceasefire Violation in South Kivu
excerpt: The AFC/M23 coalition has accused the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) armed forces of attacking its positions in the Makabola area, South Kivu province, on the morning of December 19, 2025, alleging a serious…
title_en: AFC/M23 Accuses DRC Forces of Ceasefire Violation in South Kivu
excerpt_en: The AFC/M23 coalition has accused the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) armed forces of attacking its positions in the Makabola area, South Kivu province, on the morning of December 19, 2025, alleging a serious…
body_en:
The AFC/M23 coalition has accused the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) armed forces of attacking its positions in the Makabola area, South Kivu province, on the morning of December 19, 2025, alleging a serious violation of the ceasefire.

According to Lawrence Kanyuka, spokesperson for AFC/M23, the operation involved combat drones and naval forces deployed from the town of Baraka, in Fizi Territory. He claimed that nearby civilian areas, including Makabola and the Minembwe region, were also hit with drones and heavy weapons, leaving local populations in a state of shock.

In a statement, Kanyuka called on Congolese authorities and international partners to bear witness to what he described as a breach of the ceasefire, warning that the attacks could lead to further casualties among AFC/M23 fighters and civilians.

The coalition said the incident highlights what it views as the DRC government’s lack of commitment to peace, accusing state forces of continued abuses against civilians without accountability.

The alleged attacks occurred shortly after AFC/M23 withdrew its fighters from the city of Uvira, which it said it had taken on December 9, describing the move as an effort to facilitate peace negotiations with the DRC government in Doha, Qatar.

Before its withdrawal, AFC/M23 appealed to mediators, including the United States, Qatar, and the African Union (AU), to establish a credible mechanism for civilian protection. The group also warned against the return of DRC, Burundian, Wazalendo, and FDLR forces to Uvira, accusing them of having committed abuses against the civilian population during their previous control of the city.

title: Tshisekedi Denies Defeat of DRC Army in Uvira Fighting
excerpt: Kampala/Kinshasa - December 21, 2025
title_en: Tshisekedi Denies Defeat of DRC Army in Uvira Fighting
excerpt_en: Kampala/Kinshasa - December 21, 2025
body_en:
Kampala/Kinshasa - December 21, 2025

President Félix Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has rejected claims that the Congolese army was defeated by the AFC/M23 coalition during recent fighting in the Uvira territory, South Kivu Province.

Speaking via video conference at a regional summit in Uganda on December 21, 2025, Tshisekedi said AFC/M23 forces employed combat drones and heavy weaponry during the clashes, challenging narratives that portray the developments as a military defeat for government forces.

According to the Congolese leader, the FARDC’s withdrawal from Uvira was a tactical decision aimed at limiting civilian casualties, rather than an admission of military failure.

“The DRC forces retreated for a reason - to avoid the loss of many civilian lives,” Tshisekedi said. “This choice is not a defeat or a sign of weakness. It reflects our commitment to protecting civilians under extremely difficult circumstances.”

The latest escalation began in early December 2025, when Congolese, Burundian, Wazalendo, and FDLR forces shelled areas held by AFC/M23 in Walungu territory, including Kamanyola and Kaziba, using heavy artillery.

The bombardment triggered mass displacement, with civilians fleeing toward Bukavu, while more than 1,000 people crossed into Rwanda through the Bugarama border.

In retaliation, AFC/M23 launched a counteroffensive, overrunning a key FARDC military base, seizing parts of the Rusizi Valley, including Katogota, Luvungi, Sange, and Kiliba, before entering Uvira on December 9.

Following the takeover, DRC soldiers dispersed in several directions: some crossed into Burundi, others retreated toward Baraka in Fizi territory, continuing into Tanganyika Province, while additional troops fled into the Itombwe forest. Others were reportedly captured by AFC/M23 forces.

Despite Tshisekedi’s explanation of a humanitarian-motivated withdrawal, several soldiers who abandoned positions in Uvira are accused of disobeying orders to continue fighting.

On December 19, the Kalemie Military Court in Tanganyika Province opened proceedings against 68 soldiers and 56 police officers accused of fleeing the battlefield during the Uvira clashes. Historically, such charges have carried the death penalty, highlighting the gravity of the accusations.

title: Rwandan and Burundian Security Officials Hold High-Level Talks After Uvira Takeover
excerpt: Uvira/Rwanda-Burundi Border - December 18, 2025
title_en: Rwandan and Burundian Security Officials Hold High-Level Talks After Uvira Takeover
excerpt_en: Uvira/Rwanda-Burundi Border - December 18, 2025
body_en:
Uvira/Rwanda-Burundi Border - December 18, 2025

In the wake of the AFC/M23 coalition capture of Uvira, senior Rwandan and Burundian security officials convened a high-level meeting at the border to discuss tension reduction and regional security. Details of the meeting were confirmed by Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Ambassador Olivier Nduhungirehe.

The meeting, held on December 15, 2025, included top Rwandan officials such as NISS Secretary General Havugiyaremye Aimable, his deputy Brig Gen Jean Paul Nyirubutama, Chief of Army Staff Maj Gen Vincent Nyakarundi, and Deputy Director of Military Intelligence Brig Gen François Regis Gatarayiha.

Burundi was represented by Director of Intelligence Maj Gen Ildephonse Habarurema, Deputy Director of Police Brig Gen Emmanuel Ndayiziga, and Director of Military Intelligence Jean d’Affaires Manirakiza.

The talks occurred amid heightened tensions after Burundi accused Rwanda of firing in Cibitoke, a claim Rwanda denied, stating instead that Burundian troops fired in Kamanyola, prompting many Congolese civilians to flee into Rwanda.

The capture of Uvira led Burundi to close its border with the DRC at Gatumba and Vugizo, citing security concerns as Burundian troops had been directly involved in fighting in the Rusizi Valley and other parts of South Kivu. At the height of the conflict, approximately 20,000 Burundian soldiers were reportedly deployed in South Kivu. Following the Uvira takeover, some troops returned home, others moved to areas including Baraka in Fizi territory, while some remained near Minembwe.

During the December 15 meeting, Rwandan officials assured Burundi that Rwanda would not attack, but emphasized that Burundian forces should withdraw from South Kivu and step back from the ongoing conflict.

According to information obtained by IGIHE, on the night of December 15-16, many Burundian troops left Baraka and the Mboko Center, crossing Lake Tanganyika. Six trucks reportedly transported the soldiers from Rumonge military port to Bujumbura, with soldiers appearing exhausted from long deployments. The repatriation operation was conducted in strict secrecy.

On December 18, a Burundian was arrested at Rumonge port while assisting with troop movements, suspected of espionage.

Despite the withdrawal of Burundian troops from the DRC, President Evariste Ndayishimiye expressed continued concern, stating on December 19, 2025, that “the enemy is at the gates” and warning of threats from the north.

Minister Nduhungirehe indicated that additional meetings between Rwanda and Burundi could take place in the future, aiming to restore stable relations between the two countries and the wider region.

title: RDF Soldiers Complete High-Level Training to Strengthen National Security
excerpt: Kirehe District, Rwanda - December 22, 2025
title_en: RDF Soldiers Complete High-Level Training to Strengthen National Security
excerpt_en: Kirehe District, Rwanda - December 22, 2025
body_en:
Kirehe District, Rwanda - December 22, 2025

The Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) has successfully concluded a four-month advanced training course aimed at enhancing the knowledge, skills, and combat capabilities of its officers and soldiers. The training was held at the Nasho Military Base in Kirehe District.

The closing ceremony, presided over by RDF Chief of Staff Gen. Mubarakh Muganga, was attended by senior military officers and showcased the soldiers’ newly acquired abilities.

During the event, participants demonstrated a range of competencies, including war tactics, combat training, and firearms proficiency, reflecting the Brigade’s readiness for operational duties and national security tasks.

Gen. Muganga praised the graduates for their dedication, discipline, and professionalism throughout the training, emphasizing the importance of applying these skills in protecting Rwanda’s sovereignty and addressing emerging security challenges.

“Ethics must come first. We are a military guided by good conduct and integrity, which form the foundation of all our values,” he said, stressing the need for soldiers to uphold RDF values in every aspect of their service.

The training program is part of RDF’s ongoing efforts to strengthen operational capacity and ensure that its personnel are well-prepared to maintain security and respond effectively to any threats.

title: 13 Rwandans Join MMA as New Athletes Following Training Course
excerpt: Rebero, Rwanda - December 20-21, 2025
title_en: 13 Rwandans Join MMA as New Athletes Following Training Course
excerpt_en: Rebero, Rwanda - December 20-21, 2025
body_en:
Rebero, Rwanda - December 20-21, 2025

The Rwanda Mixed Martial Arts Association (GAMMA Rwanda) has officially welcomed 13 new MMA athletes following a two-day technical training course, marking the second such program since the sport’s legalization in Rwanda. The course, held at The Great Warriors Sport Academy in Rebero, drew 28 participants, mostly young Rwandans, along with four foreigners.

The training aimed to enhance the skills and knowledge of players and coaches in this emerging combat sport. Sessions were led by international MMA trainer Lubega Ahmed Ali from Uganda.

“The majority of participants are young people who have shown a clear desire and capability to play MMA,” said Mwizerwa Dieudonné, President of GAMMA Rwanda.

Among the participants, three were from Uganda and one from Bukavu in the DRC, all already experienced in MMA, Boxing, Kickboxing, and Jiu-Jitsu.

During the course, GAMMA Rwanda officially inducted 13 new athletes who will now represent the country in national and international competitions.

Since its establishment, GAMMA Rwanda has rapidly gained recognition, becoming a member of both the International Mixed Martial Arts Association (GAMMA International) and the Federation for International Mixed Martial Arts (FIMMA), allowing Rwandan athletes to participate in global MMA events.
