excerpt_en: KIREHE, Rwanda - The Chief of Staff of the Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF), Gen. Mubarakh Muganga, has called on soldiers to uphold the country’s sovereignty and tackle security challenges, emphasizing that the foundation…
body_en:
KIREHE, Rwanda - The Chief of Staff of the Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF), Gen. Mubarakh Muganga, has called on soldiers to uphold the country’s sovereignty and tackle security challenges, emphasizing that the foundation of the RDF is integrity.

Speaking at the Nasho Military Base in Kirehe District during the closing ceremony of a high-level training course for officers and other ranks, Gen. Muganga urged troops to apply their knowledge and skills professionally. The training, which concluded on December 22, 2025, was designed to sharpen the military capabilities of RDF personnel.

The ceremony featured demonstrations of the soldiers’ newly acquired competencies, including combat tactics, shooting, and other military exercises.

Gen. Muganga highlighted the importance of ethical conduct, stating, “Ethics come first. We are a military that is guided by good ethics and values of integrity. Training such as this aims to enhance the knowledge and skills of soldiers so that they can carry out their duties as members of the Rwandan Armed Forces.”

He called on the soldiers to continue being professional in their duties, ensuring that they safeguard the integrity of the nation while addressing any emerging security challenges.

title: Rwanda Police Inducts 1,903 Graduates Trained in Unarmed Combat
excerpt: KIGALI, Rwanda - The Rwanda National Police (RNP) has inducted 1,903 new officers who completed an intensive eight-month training program in self-defense without weapons, demonstrating skills designed to defeat enemies…
title_en: Rwanda Police Inducts 1,903 Graduates Trained in Unarmed Combat
excerpt_en: KIGALI, Rwanda - The Rwanda National Police (RNP) has inducted 1,903 new officers who completed an intensive eight-month training program in self-defense without weapons, demonstrating skills designed to defeat enemies…
body_en:
KIGALI, Rwanda - The Rwanda National Police (RNP) has inducted 1,903 new officers who completed an intensive eight-month training program in self-defense without weapons, demonstrating skills designed to defeat enemies using only their physical strength.

The induction ceremony, held on 22 December 2025, celebrated 359 female and 1,544 male graduates. Among them, 40 trainees will be assigned to the Rwanda Correctional Service (RCS), while 178 officers trained at the Musanze Police College will continue studies across various departments.

The training equipped officers with the ability to fight swiftly in all directions, apply great force, and defend themselves even when opponents use truncheons or other weapons. Instructors emphasized using speed, precision, and body control as the primary tools of defense.

Addressing the new officers, Minister of Security Dr. Vincent Biruta urged them to uphold politeness, professionalism, and sincerity, while rejecting blame and striving for the pride of Rwanda. He emphasized collaboration with other institutions and placing citizens at the center of all police programs, noting that “the good of Rwandans is all we strive for.”

These young men and women now join the RNP ready to ensure the security of Rwandans and the protection of their property in every possible circumstance.

title: Burundi Loses Senior Officer in AFC/M23 Drone Attack in Eastern DRC
excerpt: BUJUMBURA / SOUTH KIVU - Burundi has lost another senior military officer following clashes in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Lt. Col.
title_en: Burundi Loses Senior Officer in AFC/M23 Drone Attack in Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: BUJUMBURA / SOUTH KIVU - Burundi has lost another senior military officer following clashes in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Lt. Col.
body_en:
BUJUMBURA / SOUTH KIVU - Burundi has lost another senior military officer following clashes in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Lt. Col. Patrice Manirakiza, a Burundian army officer, died on the morning of 24 December 2025 after nearly three weeks of medical treatment for injuries sustained in an AFC/M23 drone attack.

Lt. Col. Manirakiza was seriously wounded on 6 December 2025 in Luvungi, South Kivu Province, while stationed at the headquarters of the 18th Battalion of the Burundian army deployed in the DRC. He was immediately evacuated and admitted to Tanganyika Care Hospital, a facility that has treated many Burundian soldiers wounded in the ongoing conflict in eastern DRC.

Medical sources indicated that doctors were unable to stabilize his condition, as his wounds continued to deteriorate instead of healing. Physicians reportedly recommended his transfer to India for specialized treatment, but the Burundian military high command declined the request.

Sources in Bujumbura also confirmed that several other Burundian soldiers admitted to the same hospital have died in recent days, allegedly due to insufficient medical care.

Earlier this month, intense fighting in the Rusizi/Ruzizi Valley resulted in the deaths of numerous Burundian soldiers, with others captured by the AFC/M23, while surviving troops were forced to withdraw back to Burundi.

Lt. Col. Manirakiza’s death follows that of Lt. Col. Athanase Minani, who was killed on 4 December 2025 in a drone strike in the Lubarika area. Three soldiers guarding him were also killed in the same attack.

The incidents underscore the heavy toll the conflict continues to exact on foreign forces involved in the eastern DRC crisis.

title_en: AFC/M23 and DRC Forces Clash in Fizi Ahead of Christmas
excerpt_en: FIZI, South Kivu - Fierce fighting erupted between AFC/M23 fighters and the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), backed by Wazalendo militias, in the Makabola center of Fizi Territory on December…
body_en:
FIZI, South Kivu - Fierce fighting erupted between AFC/M23 fighters and the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), backed by Wazalendo militias, in the Makabola center of Fizi Territory on December 24, 2025, just days before Christmas.

The clashes lasted throughout the day and spread across several locations, including Makabola 1, Makabola 2, Kiringi, and Kirambi. Heavy weapons and drones were reportedly used during the confrontations, heightening fears among civilians.

As fighting intensified, large numbers of residents from Makabola and surrounding villages such as Bangwi, Kasenya, and Makabola 1 fled their homes on December 24, seeking safety in areas to the north, including the city of Uvira.

Local sources in Fizi reported that DRC forces are being reinforced, particularly in the Swima and Munene areas, with additional troops arriving by aircraft and boats.

At the same time, AFC/M23 fighters reportedly strengthened their presence in zones they have controlled for several days, notably in Makabola, as part of efforts to reinforce security.

On December 25, calm returned to Makabola. No fighting was reported, and residents were able to attend church services and celebrate Christmas, marking a brief pause in hostilities after a day of intense violence.

title: Uvira: AFC/M23 Shoots Down FARDC Sukhoi-25 Fighter Jet
excerpt: UVIRA, South Kivu - The AFC/M23 coalition has shot down a Sukhoi-25 fighter jet operated by the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) during military operations in South Kivu Province, according to…
title_en: Uvira: AFC/M23 Shoots Down FARDC Sukhoi-25 Fighter Jet
excerpt_en: UVIRA, South Kivu - The AFC/M23 coalition has shot down a Sukhoi-25 fighter jet operated by the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) during military operations in South Kivu Province, according to…
body_en:
UVIRA, South Kivu - The AFC/M23 coalition has shot down a Sukhoi-25 fighter jet operated by the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) during military operations in South Kivu Province, according to multiple local sources.

The aircraft was reportedly hit mid-air at around 7:00 a.m. on December 26, 2025, while flying over the port of Kalundu in Uvira Territory, before crashing into Lake Tanganyika.

Sources confirmed that since early morning, FARDC, supported by the Wazalendo coalition, had launched intense attacks on AFC/M23 positions, deploying combat drones and heavy weapons.

The clashes followed the withdrawal of AFC/M23 fighters from the Makabola camp on the afternoon of December 25, after which FARDC and Wazalendo forces moved in to inspect the area, according to local residents.

During the same operations, FARDC forces attacked the port of Kalundu, where two AFC/M23 boats on Lake Tanganyika were reportedly destroyed, killing fighters on board.

FARDC combat drones also targeted AFC/M23 facilities, including Kala, in Uvira Territory, a site that previously served as a base for the United Nations peacekeeping mission (MONUSCO).

Before being shot down, the Sukhoi-25 had reportedly conducted three airstrikes on areas under AFC/M23 control earlier that morning. Two crew members aboard the aircraft are reported to have fallen into Lake Tanganyika and died.

Additional reports indicate that the same aircraft had recently been used by the DRC army in attacks on Banyamulenge-inhabited areas in Minembwe Commune, as well as against positions held by the MRDP-Twirwaneho armed group.

This incident marks the second Sukhoi-25 lost by the DRC military. The first was captured by AFC/M23 fighters during the fall of Goma and its airport in late January 2025.

Earlier, on December 6, another helicopter operating over Lake Tanganyika crashed, killing one crew member. The MRDP-Twirwaneho group later claimed responsibility, stating the aircraft had continued firing on civilians.

The latest developments underscore the escalating intensity of air and ground combat in eastern DRC, particularly around Uvira and the Lake Tanganyika corridor.

title: Ngoma: Man Dies After Falling Into Abandoned Pit Latrine
excerpt: NGOMA, Rwanda - December 26, 2025 - A 50-year-old man died after falling into an abandoned pit latrine in Nkanga Cell, Sake Sector, Ngoma District, in an incident local authorities have described as an accident.
title_en: Ngoma: Man Dies After Falling Into Abandoned Pit Latrine
excerpt_en: NGOMA, Rwanda - December 26, 2025 - A 50-year-old man died after falling into an abandoned pit latrine in Nkanga Cell, Sake Sector, Ngoma District, in an incident local authorities have described as an accident.
body_en:
NGOMA, Rwanda - December 26, 2025 - A 50-year-old man died after falling into an abandoned pit latrine in Nkanga Cell, Sake Sector, Ngoma District, in an incident local authorities have described as an accident.

The deceased, who was known locally as a tax collector in Sake Sector, died on the night of December 26, 2025. A 29-year-old woman who was with him at the time survived and was later found lying on top of the man inside the pit.

According to residents who responded to the incident, the pair fell into a disused toilet pit located in a banana plantation, near a small footpath frequently used by locals. Witnesses believe the two may have been intoxicated after attending Christmas celebrations, which may have contributed to the fall.

A resident who witnessed the rescue efforts said the man and the woman had gone out to celebrate Christmas before the incident occurred.

“We pulled them out of the hole. One of them was already dead, while the other was alive,” the resident said.

The surviving woman was first taken to a local health center before being transferred to Kibungo Hospital for further medical care.

Confirming the incident, Ngoma District Mayor Nathalie Niyonagira said authorities are treating the case as an accidental death.

“We received the report in the early hours of the morning. The pit was located close to a path used by residents. It was an accident. One person died, and the other was taken to hospital for treatment,” she said.

Local authorities have urged residents to secure or properly cover abandoned pit latrines to prevent similar tragedies.

title: Kinshasa: Traditional Healers Gather at Cemetery to Pray for FARDC in Conflict With M23
excerpt: KINSHASA, DRC - December 21, 2025 - Traditional healers from across the Democratic Republic of Congo gathered early Sunday morning at the Gombe cemetery in Kinshasa to perform rituals and prayers seeking spiritual…
title_en: Kinshasa: Traditional Healers Gather at Cemetery to Pray for FARDC in Conflict With M23
excerpt_en: KINSHASA, DRC - December 21, 2025 - Traditional healers from across the Democratic Republic of Congo gathered early Sunday morning at the Gombe cemetery in Kinshasa to perform rituals and prayers seeking spiritual…
body_en:
KINSHASA, DRC - December 21, 2025 - Traditional healers from across the Democratic Republic of Congo gathered early Sunday morning at the Gombe cemetery in Kinshasa to perform rituals and prayers seeking spiritual support for the Congolese Armed Forces (FARDC) and allied Wazalendo fighters amid ongoing fighting against the AFC/M23 armed group.

The gathering took place at around 8:00 a.m., twelve days after M23 fighters captured the city of Uvira in South Kivu Province.

Arriving before dawn, the traditional leaders toured the cemetery, paid tribute to those buried there, poured water on graves, lit fires, and carried out ritual ceremonies intended to invoke ancestral protection and strength for the country during the conflict.

Participants said the prayers were aimed at calling upon ancestral spirits to intervene spiritually in the war and to support the nation during a period of insecurity.

Speaking on behalf of the group, Blanchard Ipipo Luzolo said the rituals also included prayers for the protection of national leaders, including President Félix Tshisekedi Tshilombo and Foreign Affairs Minister Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner.

The traditional healers also said they prayed for unity and blessings among Congolese communities, including the Bangala and Luba peoples, asking for strength, peace, and victory for the country.

The ceremony highlights the continued influence of traditional spiritual practices in Congolese society, particularly during moments of national crisis, as fighting persists in eastern regions of the country.

title: FARDC Launches Offensive to Retake Uvira Amid Ongoing Clashes with AFC/M23
excerpt: Uvira, South Kivu - December 27, 2025 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have launched a major campaign to retake strategic areas of South Kivu, including the city of Uvira, from the AFC/M23…
title_en: FARDC Launches Offensive to Retake Uvira Amid Ongoing Clashes with AFC/M23
excerpt_en: Uvira, South Kivu - December 27, 2025 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have launched a major campaign to retake strategic areas of South Kivu, including the city of Uvira, from the AFC/M23…
body_en:
Uvira, South Kivu - December 27, 2025 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have launched a major campaign to retake strategic areas of South Kivu, including the city of Uvira, from the AFC/M23 rebel coalition.

On December 24, FARDC, in coordination with Wazalendo forces, attacked AFC/M23 positions in the Makobola Center in Fizi territory, employing warplanes, drones, and heavy weaponry. By Christmas Eve, AFC/M23 fighters withdrew from Makobola after a two-week occupation, with Wazalendo forces making significant territorial gains.

On December 26, FARDC conducted air and drone strikes targeting AFC/M23 positions at the port of Kalundu, near Uvira on Lake Tanganyika.

As of December 27, FARDC has regained control of Makobola 1 and Makobola 2, while fighting continues in areas approximately seven kilometers from Uvira, including Katongo and Kabimba, according to military spokesman Gen. Maj. Sylvain Ekenge Bomusa.

The AFC/M23 entered Uvira on December 9 but withdrew on December 17-18 as part of efforts to build trust in ongoing peace talks with the DRC government. Despite leaving the city, rebel forces remain in surrounding areas, including southern Makobola, northern approaches, and western mountain regions, creating tension with the government, which insists the city has not truly been vacated.

FARDC and Wazalendo appear focused on pushing AFC/M23 fighters back into Uvira, signaling to mediators, including representatives from the United States and Qatar, that the city is not yet fully under civilian or neutral control. This approach mirrors FARDC’s earlier strategy in Makobola, where the city was retaken by force following a rebel withdrawal.

The period between December 14 and 28, 2025, reflects a complex interplay of regional security challenges, diplomatic maneuvers, and steady domestic progress for Rwanda. While tensions with neighboring Burundi and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) remain high-characterized by mutual allegations of shelling and support for rebel groups -Rwanda has maintained a proactive stance. This is evidenced by tentative security talks with Burundi and a commitment to dismantling the FDLR through international frameworks.

On the international stage, Rwanda continues to project stability and military competence. Its security forces have played a pivotal role in ensuring the success of presidential elections in the Central African Republic and maintaining security in Mozambique's Cabo Delgado province. These efforts have been bolstered by strong domestic messaging from President Paul Kagame, who emphasized national unity and the professionalism of the security services.

Economically, Rwanda shows significant resilience and strategic growth. The country successfully generated over $13.7 million in agricultural exports in a single five-day window and continues to expand its reach as a financial hub through new double taxation avoidance agreements. Coupled with major investments in infrastructure, such as the $48 million Gisagara irrigation project , Rwanda appears well-positioned to meet its long-term economic acceleration goals.

In summary, despite the persistent threat of regional instability and diplomatic pressure from external actors, Rwanda enters the final days of 2025 with a focus on internal cohesion, regional de-escalation, and sustained economic development.

title: Niger and Sahel States: Senior Officials Convene Ahead of CSA Foreign Ministers’ Meeting
excerpt: Meeting of Senior Officials Ahead of the Meeting of Foreign Ministers of the Confederation of Sahel States (CSA)
title_en: Niger and Sahel States: Senior Officials Convene Ahead of CSA Foreign Ministers’ Meeting
excerpt_en: Meeting of Senior Officials Ahead of the Meeting of Foreign Ministers of the Confederation of Sahel States (CSA)
body_en:
Meeting of Senior Officials Ahead of the Meeting of Foreign Ministers of the Confederation of Sahel States (CSA)

As a prelude to the CSA Foreign Ministers’ Meeting, scheduled for November 26, 2025, a preparatory meeting of experts opened on November 24, 2025, in Buenos Aires, Burkina Faso.

Experts from Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger, representing the Defense and Security, Diplomacy, and Development pillars, reviewed draft documents over the two days to be submitted to the CSA foreign ministers. These documents included draft legal instruments and draft activity and outlook reports for the CSA.

The opening was marked by speeches from the heads of delegation of Burkina Faso and Niger, and an opening address by Mali’s Ambassador Mahamane Amadou Maïga, Special Advisor to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, whose Head of State holds the Presidency of the ESA Confederation.

Strengthening fraternity, solidarity, and complementarity among the three countries.

Progress and future prospects in the three areas of action: defense/security, diplomacy, and development.

Military successes achieved through pooled military and security efforts.

Diplomatic coordination, particularly interventions representing the CSA in international forums.

Development initiatives, including mobilization of confederal resources and management through the Confederal Investment and Development Bank (CIDB-ASEAN), soon to be operational.

The meeting is part of the preparations for the second session of the ASEAN College of Heads of State, scheduled in Bamako, December 2025.

title: The meeting of Foreign Ministers of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) opened under the
excerpt: The meeting of Foreign Ministers of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) opened under the chairmanship of H.E.
title_en: The meeting of Foreign Ministers of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) opened under the
excerpt_en: The meeting of Foreign Ministers of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) opened under the chairmanship of H.E.
body_en:
The meeting of Foreign Ministers of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) opened under the chairmanship of H.E. Abdoulaye Diop, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali, whose Head of State holds the Presidency of the AES Confederation.

This session aimed to coordinate diplomatic action and serve as preparations for the Confederation's Council of Ministers session, itself a preparatory meeting for the 2nd session of the College of Heads of State of the AES Confederation.

Draft legal instruments and the draft activity and outlook report for the AES Confederation were examined.

These documents will also be submitted to the 2nd session of the College of Heads of State.

H.E. Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation, and Burkinabés Abroad, Burkina Faso.

H.E. Bakary Yaou Sangaré, Minister of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation, and Nigeriens Abroad, Niger.

H.E. Abdoulaye Diop, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Mali.

Significant progress in Defense and Security, Diplomacy, and Development was acknowledged.

Ministers commended the Defense and Security Forces for their courage, determination, and patriotism against armed terrorist groups.

The resilience of Sahelian populations in the face of multifaceted challenges was also praised.

Participants denounced destabilizing media campaigns targeting the Sahel countries and their institutions.

Mali, through Minister Diop, expressed gratitude to Burkina Faso and Niger for solidarity during the energy crisis, caused by obstacles from armed terrorist groups.

The foreign ministers issued a press release summarizing their conclusions.

H.E. Abdoulaye Diop met with Mr. Khosravi Nejad Akbar, Special Envoy of the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Iran.

Strengthening bilateral relations.

Prospects for partnerships between AES Confederation and Iran, particularly in diplomacy.

This initiative is part of Mali’s strategy to diversify partnerships.

title: Meeting at the Prime Minister’s Office: Strengthening ICRC Support in Mali
excerpt: On Thursday, November 27, 2025, Prime Minister and Head of Government Major General Abdoulaye Maïga received Mr.
title_en: Meeting at the Prime Minister’s Office: Strengthening ICRC Support in Mali
excerpt_en: On Thursday, November 27, 2025, Prime Minister and Head of Government Major General Abdoulaye Maïga received Mr.
body_en:
On Thursday, November 27, 2025, Prime Minister and Head of Government Major General Abdoulaye Maïga received Mr. Nicolas Lambert, Head of Delegation of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) in Mali, at the Prime Minister’s Office.

ICRC Commitment: Mr. Lambert and his delegation reaffirmed their dedication to strengthening humanitarian efforts in Mali, particularly for those affected by armed conflict and violence.

Humanitarian Focus: The ICRC aims to provide healthcare, access to drinking water, and other assistance to the most vulnerable populations.

Promotion of International Humanitarian Law: Mr. Lambert requested Mali’s expertise in this area to further enhance the ICRC’s mission.

Government Support: The Prime Minister thanked the delegation for their work, encouraged the continuation of their mission, and assured full facilitation of the ICRC’s activities, in line with Mali’s partnership priorities.

This meeting underscores the collaborative efforts between the Malian government and the ICRC to protect vulnerable populations and strengthen humanitarian responses across the country.
body_fr:

Bamako, December 4, 2025 - The Steering Committee of the ESA National Committee convened on Thursday under the chairmanship of Prime Minister Major General Abdoulaye Maïga to review preparations for the upcoming summit of the Confederation of Sahel States (ESA). The second session of the College of Heads of State of the Confederation is scheduled to take place in Bamako on December 22-23, 2025.

The meeting focused on assessing technical and organizational aspects of the main events in December, including the meeting of senior officials (December 15-18) and the first session of the Confederation's Council of Ministers (December 20-21). Highlighting the importance of the summit, the Prime Minister called for full mobilization to ensure flawless execution. He praised the efforts of the involved ministries and reaffirmed the government’s commitment to implementing the ESA’s first-year roadmap, under the chairmanship of General Assimi Goïta.

Concluding the meeting, the Prime Minister emphasized the strategic significance of this ESA session, describing it as a pivotal moment to consolidate shared ambitions, strengthen regional cooperation, and chart a path toward a more stable and prosperous future for member countries.

excerpt: Bamako, December 4, 2025 - Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Abdoulaye Diop received a delegation from the Regional Office of the Institute for Security Studies (ISS) for West Africa, the Sahel…
title_en: Mali Engages ISS Delegation on Regional Security and Strategic Priorities (December 4, 2025)
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 4, 2025 - Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Abdoulaye Diop received a delegation from the Regional Office of the Institute for Security Studies (ISS) for West Africa, the Sahel…
body_en:
Bamako, December 4, 2025 - Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Abdoulaye Diop received a delegation from the Regional Office of the Institute for Security Studies (ISS) for West Africa, the Sahel, and the Lake Chad Basin, led by Colonel (Retired) Hassane Koné, Senior Research Fellow and Consultant for the Sahel Program. Discussions focused on security challenges and current regional dynamics.

During the meeting, the Minister outlined Mali's new strategic direction, highlighting:

Renewed control of national affairs by the transitional authorities.

Integration into the East African Community (EAC).

Efforts to counter hybrid actors and protracted terrorism.

Implementation of the national peace and reconciliation approach, enshrined in the dedicated Charter.

The talks also addressed multilateral challenges, including the need for strengthened regional cooperation, African solidarity in global crises, and the mitigation of external interference disrupting state and organizational relations.

Minister Diop emphasized the importance of open and participatory dialogue to foster a shared understanding of current issues. Both parties reaffirmed their commitment to constructive exchanges, grounded in objective analysis, to support political decisions promoting peace, security, and development in Africa.

This dialogue framework aims to build trust and promote African solutions tailored to the continent's realities.

Baja, accompanied by Yacine Faye Sidibé, Honorary Consul of the Philippines in Mali. The meeting was part of a busy diplomatic agenda between the two countries.

Ambassador Baja presented a letter from Philippine President Ferdinand Romualdez Marcos Jr. addressed to President of the Transition, General Assimi Goïta, signaling the desire to strengthen political dialogue and expand bilateral cooperation.

The meeting also marked the opening of the Honorary Consulate of the Philippines in Bamako, an important step to facilitate exchanges and revitalize the Philippine presence in Mali. Both parties commended the quality of mutual support between Bamako and Manila in international forums.

Exploring economic cooperation, especially in the mining sector

Both officials reaffirmed their commitment to building a partnership based on solidarity, common interest, and mutually beneficial cooperation, paving the way for a structured and dynamic Mali-Philippines relationship.

title_en: Official Inauguration of the Honorary Consulate of the Philippines in Bamako (December 5, 2025)
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 5, 2025 - The Honorary Consulate of the Republic of the Philippines in Bamako was officially inaugurated on Friday during a ceremony presided over by Ambassador Seydou Coulibaly, Secretary General of…
body_en:
Bamako, December 5, 2025 - The Honorary Consulate of the Republic of the Philippines in Bamako was officially inaugurated on Friday during a ceremony presided over by Ambassador Seydou Coulibaly, Secretary General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation.

The event was attended by Philippine Ambassador to Mali Leslie J. Baja and several distinguished guests.

Speeches by Honorary Consul Yacine Faye Sidibé, Ambassador Baja, and the Secretary General

In his address, the Secretary General, on behalf of Minister Abdoulaye Diop, welcomed the initiative, emphasizing that the consulate gives new impetus to bilateral relations and strengthens diplomatic and consular ties. He also reminded the Honorary Consul of her mission to represent a friendly nation, protect its citizens, and promote exchanges between the two communities, assuring her of the Malian government's support.

Ambassador Baja noted that the opening of the consulate fulfills a commitment made to President Assimi Goïta, praising Mali as a welcoming country, a crossroads of civilizations, and a source of economic opportunities, and reaffirmed Manila's commitment to strengthening cooperation with Bamako.

The Honorary Consul expressed her gratitude to both governments and reaffirmed her dedication to promoting economic, trade, and people-to-people exchanges.

The Honorary Consulate is now operational, located in Hamdallaye ACI 2000, Street 250, near the Lafia Insurance headquarters.

title: Mali: IMF and WAEMU Commission Commend Country’s Economic Performance
excerpt: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the WAEMU Commission officially commended Mali’s resilience, fiscal discipline, and strong macroeconomic performance, despite ongoing security, climate, and economic challenges…
title_en: Mali: IMF and WAEMU Commission Commend Country’s Economic Performance
excerpt_en: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the WAEMU Commission officially commended Mali’s resilience, fiscal discipline, and strong macroeconomic performance, despite ongoing security, climate, and economic challenges…
body_en:
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the WAEMU Commission officially commended Mali’s resilience, fiscal discipline, and strong macroeconomic performance, despite ongoing security, climate, and economic challenges in recent years.

From November 10 to 21, 2025, an IMF mission led by Ms. Wenjie Chen conducted the first staff review of the program, which was completed in April 2025.

Objectives achieved and transparent management of funds.

Full commitment from the Malian authorities to economic reforms.

Macroeconomic indicators under control despite challenges such as:

Inflation: Below 3% in 2025

Economic Growth: Projected at 6.1% according to Malian authorities

Budget Deficit: Reduced to 2.7% (below WAEMU standard of 3%)

Public Debt: Controlled at 41.7%, well below the community ceiling of 70%

Unemployment: Managed since 2021

The WAEMU Commission also congratulated Mali, highlighting excellent economic performance in terms of growth, debt management, inflation control, and fiscal discipline.

Looking ahead, with the settlement of the dispute with Barrick Gold, 2026 promises to be particularly favorable, especially for the gold sector.

title_en: Managing the Hydrocarbon Crisis in Mali: 75 Individuals Honored (December 5, 2025)

body_en:
Bamako, December 5, 2025 - President of the Transition, Assimi Goïta, Head of State and Grand Master of the National Orders, presided over a solemn ceremony at the Koulouba Palace on Friday, December 5, 2025, to present awards to individuals who supported the Malian government in managing the recent hydrocarbon crisis.

A total of 75 people were honored through three decrees signed on November 26, 2025:

16 oil operators and union leaders were elevated to Knight of the National Order of Mali (Decree No. 2025818/PTRM)

31 injured drivers and 27 deceased drivers-including some foreign nationals-received the Silver Star Medal of National Merit with the emblem of the "Standing Lion" (Decrees No. 2025819 and 2025820/PTRM)

According to the Grand Chancellor of the National Orders, the decorations recognize the courage, sense of duty, and patriotism of the recipients, described as “unsung heroes” for risking-and in some cases losing-their lives to guarantee the country’s energy supply during a period when the crisis threatened national stability.

title_en: Reflections on Social Protection: CIPRES Expert Committee Meets in Bangui
excerpt_en: Bangui, Central African Republic, December 2-3, 2025 - In preparation for the 39th Ordinary Session of the Council of Ministers of member countries, the Committee of Experts on Social Protection, chaired by the…
body_en:
Bangui, Central African Republic, December 2-3, 2025 - In preparation for the 39th Ordinary Session of the Council of Ministers of member countries, the Committee of Experts on Social Protection, chaired by the Inter-African Conference on Social Prevention (CIPRES), convened in Bangui to assess the expansion of social security coverage and enhance the well-being of populations.

The Committee reviewed preparatory documents for the Council of Ministers meeting scheduled for December 5, 2025. Mali participated with a large delegation led by the Ministry’s Technical Advisor for Legal Affairs, Mr. Bakary Dembélé, along with:

National Director of Social Protection and Solidarity Economy, Mr. Mohamed Bassirou Traoré

Directors General of CANAM (Brigadier General Boubacar Dembélé), CMSS (Ichaka Koné), and ANAM (Hameth Ben Hamane Traoré)

Technical advisors from INPS, CMSS, and CANAM

CIPRES, with 18 member countries, coordinates and harmonizes social protection systems across Africa, develops common rules for the management of social security institutions, and monitors their operation.

Election of the President of the Council of Ministers

Review and adoption of minutes from the 38th Ordinary Session

Review and adoption of the draft 2026 action plan and budget

Adoption of the 2024 annual report

Adoption of codes of ethics and competency profiles for management and staff

Integration of Guinea’s CNPS into CIPRES agencies

Progress on statistical, financial, and accounting data communication

Review of arrears in contributions from Member States

Designation of the host country for the 41st session

Preparations for the High-Level Forum on Social Protection

At the opening, Cheick Tidiane Tounkara, Chairman of the CIPRES Oversight Committee, praised member states’ commitment and emphasized strengthening governance, transparency, and effectiveness of social protection systems.

On behalf of the Minister of Labor, Employment, Social Protection, and Vocational Training, Victor Mazamga highlighted the global challenges of economic instability and social inequalities, urging experts to share experiences and intensify collaboration to enhance social protection systems in the CIPRES region.

A high-level forum on social protection will also take place on the sidelines of the Council of Ministers meeting in Bangui.

excerpt_en: Bamako, November 29, 2025 - The 18th Scientific Day of the National Union of Private Sector Pharmacists (SYNAPPO) was held under the theme of professional commitment and solidarity, focusing on the creation of a mutual…
body_en:
Bamako, November 29, 2025 - The 18th Scientific Day of the National Union of Private Sector Pharmacists (SYNAPPO) was held under the theme of professional commitment and solidarity, focusing on the creation of a mutual insurance fund and the management of Mandatory Health Insurance (AMO).

The event was chaired by the Minister of Health and Social Development, Colonel-Major Assa Badiallo Touré, and brought together professionals from the healthcare and social services sector to discuss current challenges.

Creation of a mutual insurance fund for pharmacists to better cover social and health risks faced by professionals.

Addressing rejected reimbursement forms under AMO, a critical issue affecting the profitability of pharmacies, requiring coordinated solutions with CANAM and Regional Health Organizations (OGD).

In her address, Colonel-Major Assa Badiallo Touré praised community pharmacists as essential pillars of the healthcare system, emphasizing their commitment, professional rigor, and dedication to public health services, despite occasional delays in invoice payments.

She reaffirmed her ministry’s commitment to strengthen financing and regulatory mechanisms, aiming to consolidate a partnership based on trust, transparency, and mutual respect between the government and healthcare professionals.

The ceremony concluded with the presentation of certificates of recognition to individuals who have made a significant impact on the pharmaceutical sector, particularly in improving access to medicines for the population.

title: CIPRES Council of Ministers: Bangui Hosts the 39th Ordinary Session
excerpt: Bangui, December 5, 2025 - Eighteen ministers and social protection officials convened in Bangui, Central African Republic, for the 39th Ordinary Session of the Council of Ministers of the Inter-African Conference on…
title_en: CIPRES Council of Ministers: Bangui Hosts the 39th Ordinary Session
excerpt_en: Bangui, December 5, 2025 - Eighteen ministers and social protection officials convened in Bangui, Central African Republic, for the 39th Ordinary Session of the Council of Ministers of the Inter-African Conference on…
body_en:
Bangui, December 5, 2025 - Eighteen ministers and social protection officials convened in Bangui, Central African Republic, for the 39th Ordinary Session of the Council of Ministers of the Inter-African Conference on Social Security (CIPRES).

The meeting aimed to review sixteen items on the agenda, with Mali represented by Colonel-Major Assa Badiallo Touré, Minister of Health and Social Development, accompanied by his legal advisor, the Director General of the National Directorate of Social Protection (DNPSES), the Directors General of CMSS, INPS, CANAM, ANAM, and their technical advisors.

The outgoing CIPRES Chair, the Togolese Minister, praised the commitment of member states to guarantee the well-being of populations and emphasized social protection as a fundamental pillar of development.

The rotating presidency was officially handed over to the Central African Minister of Labor, Employment, Social Protection, and Vocational Training, Annie Michelle Mouanga, who highlighted solidarity, strengthening regional ties, and extending social and health coverage to vulnerable populations.

Mali’s delegation confirmed that all sixteen agenda items were reviewed and adopted, noting that Mali’s social security institutions are up-to-date with contributions.

The session concluded positively, with participants agreeing to:

Assess prospects for modernizing social protection systems;

Define priority actions to strengthen governance, efficiency, and transparency within CIPRES member organizations.

The next CIPRES Council meeting is scheduled for 2026 in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

title: Mali: Radio Stations Suspended and Journalists Arrested - Junta Tightens Press Freedom
excerpt: On November 23, 2025, the High Authority for Communication announced the three-month suspension of radio stations Aadar Koïma in Gao and Aadar Koukia in Ansongo.
title_en: Mali: Radio Stations Suspended and Journalists Arrested - Junta Tightens Press Freedom
excerpt_en: On November 23, 2025, the High Authority for Communication announced the three-month suspension of radio stations Aadar Koïma in Gao and Aadar Koukia in Ansongo.
body_en:
On November 23, 2025, the High Authority for Communication announced the three-month suspension of radio stations Aadar Koïma in Gao and Aadar Koukia in Ansongo. This decision followed their coverage of the creation of a movement demanding the departure of Assimi Goïta.

Journalist arrests: On November 5, 2025, journalists Malick Aliou Maïga and Youssoufa Moussa were arrested in Gao and Ansongo, respectively, for reporting on the same topic.

State control: These measures illustrate the total control exercised by the State over communication, where any critical speech or reporting can result in imprisonment.

Threat to journalists: Media professionals face constant risk of violent arrest or prolonged detention, even for a misinterpreted phrase or sensitive report.

Impact on independent media: Local radio stations, community television channels, and news platforms are regularly targeted, shut down, or intimidated, depriving communities in Gao and Ansongo of reliable sources of information.

Broader implications: This demonstrates the military dictatorship’s grip on freedom of expression, reinforcing a climate of fear and attempting to impose a single narrative, at the expense of debate, transparency, and public trust.

title: Mali: Kal-Akal Denounces New Ethnic Cleansing in Timbuktu Region (November 25-27, 2025)
excerpt: Following the violence between November 25 and 27, 2025, the Kidal-based human rights organization Kal-Akal issued a damning statement denouncing a new "ethnic cleansing" in the Timbuktu region.
title_en: Mali: Kal-Akal Denounces New Ethnic Cleansing in Timbuktu Region (November 25-27, 2025)
excerpt_en: Following the violence between November 25 and 27, 2025, the Kidal-based human rights organization Kal-Akal issued a damning statement denouncing a new "ethnic cleansing" in the Timbuktu region.
body_en:
Following the violence between November 25 and 27, 2025, the Kidal-based human rights organization Kal-Akal issued a damning statement denouncing a new "ethnic cleansing" in the Timbuktu region.

According to the organization, a joint patrol of the Malian army and Africa Corps conducted a series of deadly operations in localities including Goundam, Gargando, and Bintagoungou, resulting in numerous casualties, abductions, and significant material damage. Kal-Akal asserts that the victims are primarily civilians targeted because of their ethnicity.

Villages such as Amarnane, Nijhaltate, and Taroma saw mutilated bodies, wounded women and children, and people abducted to unknown locations

Destruction of water points, tents, and pastures, worsening the humanitarian situation in an already insecure region

Immediate protection of civilians and safe humanitarian access

Continued documentation of abuses to hold perpetrators accountable

For Kal-Akal, the stability of the region depends on justice, transparency, and protection of vulnerable communities.

title: Mali: Panel of Democrats Condemns Massacres by Malian Army and Afrika Korps in Timbuktu Region
excerpt: The Panel of Democrats, composed of members of the Malian opposition, expressed profound outrage at the massacres of November 25 and 26, 2025, committed by a joint patrol of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) and Russian…
title_en: Mali: Panel of Democrats Condemns Massacres by Malian Army and Afrika Korps in Timbuktu Region
excerpt_en: The Panel of Democrats, composed of members of the Malian opposition, expressed profound outrage at the massacres of November 25 and 26, 2025, committed by a joint patrol of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) and Russian…
body_en:
The Panel of Democrats, composed of members of the Malian opposition, expressed profound outrage at the massacres of November 25 and 26, 2025, committed by a joint patrol of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) and Russian elements of the Afrika Korps.

These attacks resulted in 14 civilian deaths and several disappearances in the Timbuktu region, notably in Razelma, Amaranane, Tissikoreye, Émimalane, Toroma, Takara, Zouéra, and Nijhaltate.

The Panel calls on the Attorney General of the Transition and the United Nations to open a formal investigation.

Unequivocal condemnation of summary executions and destruction of civilian property.

Independent international investigation and prosecution for war crimes.

Condemnation of the scorched-earth policy pursued by Africa Corps since 2024.

Immediate protection of civilians, particularly the nomads of Lake Faguibine.

Solidarity with the families of the victims.

title: Mali: CD-DPA and Experts Call for International Action Amid Escalating Atrocities in Azawad
excerpt: The Group of Experts calls on the United Nations, African Union, ECOWAS, European Union, and international human rights organizations to recognize the gravity of these crimes, document the violations, and take…
title_en: Mali: CD-DPA and Experts Call for International Action Amid Escalating Atrocities in Azawad
excerpt_en: The Group of Experts calls on the United Nations, African Union, ECOWAS, European Union, and international human rights organizations to recognize the gravity of these crimes, document the violations, and take…
body_en:
The Group of Experts calls on the United Nations, African Union, ECOWAS, European Union, and international human rights organizations to recognize the gravity of these crimes, document the violations, and take diplomatic, judicial, and law enforcement measures to end impunity.

According to the experts, these repeated massacres are no longer mere military operations-they constitute a campaign of ethnic cleansing targeting entire villages.

The Group of Experts reaffirms its commitment to truth, justice, human dignity, and the protection of all communities in Mali.

The Collective for the Defense of the Rights of the People of Azawad (CD-DPA) published a new summary report covering November 24 to 30, 2025, highlighting the gravity of violations committed in Azawad and certain regions of central Mali. Key findings include:

3 cases of arbitrary arrests, enforced disappearances, or abductions

4 cases of torture and other forms of violence

26 cases of destruction, looting, and property damage, illustrating a scorched-earth strategy

1 case of environmental damage

No sexual assaults recorded during this period

These figures confirm the continued deterioration of the security and humanitarian situation, marked by operations directly targeting civilians, leaving already vulnerable populations at great risk.

title: Bamako Military Court Hosts Training Workshop on Criminal Procedure Reform
excerpt: Bamako, December 3, 2025 - The Bamako Military Court organized a training workshop on the reform of the Penal Code and the Code of Criminal Procedure, bringing together both civilian and military magistrates.
title_en: Bamako Military Court Hosts Training Workshop on Criminal Procedure Reform
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 3, 2025 - The Bamako Military Court organized a training workshop on the reform of the Penal Code and the Code of Criminal Procedure, bringing together both civilian and military magistrates.
body_en:
Bamako, December 3, 2025 - The Bamako Military Court organized a training workshop on the reform of the Penal Code and the Code of Criminal Procedure, bringing together both civilian and military magistrates. The session was held with the support of the UNDP as part of the PROSMED project, contributing to Mali’s ongoing efforts to modernize its judicial system and strengthen the rule of law.

Unified Training Approach: Colonel-Major Boubacar Maïga, Director of Military Justice, emphasized the importance of cohesion within the judicial system and the consistent application of criminal procedures.

Adaptation to Contemporary Challenges: Mr. Olivier Tshibola, head of the PROSMED project, stressed the need for the judicial system to evolve alongside modern crimes and comply with international standards.

Strategic Reforms: Minister of Justice and Human Rights, Keeper of the Seals, Mr. Mamoudou Kassogue, highlighted that the reforms aim to provide a credible, coherent, and rights-respecting judicial system capable of addressing organized crime, cybercrime, terrorism, corruption, and offenses against public property.

Participants were encouraged to embrace the innovations, share best practices, and identify potential challenges to ensure harmonized and rigorous application of the laws.

The workshop reinforces Mali’s commitment to modernizing its judicial system through collaboration between the Ministry of Justice, Ministry of Defense, and technical and financial partners.

This initiative reflects Mali’s broader strategy to build an efficient, accessible, and internationally-aligned justice system, capable of meeting contemporary legal and security challenges.

title_en: Mali: Six Schoolchildren Die in Canoe Capsize in Bafoulabé (November 28, 2025)
excerpt_en: A tragic accident occurred on Friday morning, November 28, 2025, in Galoukoné, in the commune of Mahina (Bafoulabé circle).
body_en:
A tragic accident occurred on Friday morning, November 28, 2025, in Galoukoné, in the commune of Mahina (Bafoulabé circle). A canoe carrying 36 people capsized around 7:00 a.m., leading to the deaths of six schoolchildren-five girls and one boy-all attending primary and secondary school.
Thanks to rapid intervention, 30 passengers were rescued. All six bodies were recovered, and the victims were buried in the village at 11:00 a.m. the same day.

excerpt: Bamako, December 6, 2025 - Following a temporary lull in hostilities due to an agreement between JNIM and the Malian Military Council, attacks resumed between December 3 and 4, 2025, reigniting a fuel crisis in Bamako…
title_en: New Fuel Crisis Hits Mali as JNIM Attacks Resume

body_en:
Bamako, December 6, 2025 - Following a temporary lull in hostilities due to an agreement between JNIM and the Malian Military Council, attacks resumed between December 3 and 4, 2025, reigniting a fuel crisis in Bamako and Ségou.

In Ségou, fuel shortages were severe, with no gas stations reporting available supply on Thursday, December 4. On the black market, a liter of fuel was selling for 2,000 to 2,500 CFA francs.

In Bamako, residents faced long queues at the few operating gas stations. The resurgence of attacks and the breakdown of the temporary agreement have disrupted the energy supply, aggravating the economic and social strain on the population.

title: JNIM Ambush Devastates Fuel Convoy in Mali
excerpt: Bamako, December 6, 2025 - The Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (JNIM) announced that it ambushed a military convoy escorting fuel tankers between Bougouni and Bamako.
title_en: JNIM Ambush Devastates Fuel Convoy in Mali
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 6, 2025 - The Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (JNIM) announced that it ambushed a military convoy escorting fuel tankers between Bougouni and Bamako.
body_en:
Bamako, December 6, 2025 - The Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (JNIM) announced that it ambushed a military convoy escorting fuel tankers between Bougouni and Bamako.

The attack caused dozens of fuel tankers to be set ablaze and resulted in the deaths of numerous Malian soldiers and drivers. The convoy, consisting of approximately 200 tankers arriving from Ivory Coast, was largely destroyed. Only a handful of vehicles reached Bamako under air cover.

This ambush has worsened the ongoing fuel crisis, leaving the capital and surrounding regions struggling with severe fuel shortages.

excerpt_en: Bamako, December 6, 2025 - A temporary fuel agreement between the Malian Military Council and JNIM officially ended on Friday, December 5, 2025.
body_en:
Bamako, December 6, 2025 - A temporary fuel agreement between the Malian Military Council and JNIM officially ended on Friday, December 5, 2025. The accord, which had been overseen by Colonel Lasséni Diallo, head of counterterrorism at the National Intelligence Agency (ANR), during a meeting with Amadou Koufa, leader of Katiba Macina, did not hold.

The termination of the agreement was immediately followed by a JNIM ambush of tanker trucks on Saturday, December 6, marking the resumption of attacks. The last similar attack had occurred on November 6 near Kati, targeting a convoy from Senegal.

This development highlights the fragile nature of temporary security arrangements and the ongoing threat posed by armed groups to Mali’s supply lines.

title: JNIM Ambush on Pro-Government Militias in Djenné
excerpt: Djenné, Mopti Region, December 7, 2025 - On Sunday, December 7, JNIM announced via Al-Zalaqa that it had carried out an ambush against Malian pro-government militias near the village of Djini, on Friday, December 5.
title_en: JNIM Ambush on Pro-Government Militias in Djenné
excerpt_en: Djenné, Mopti Region, December 7, 2025 - On Sunday, December 7, JNIM announced via Al-Zalaqa that it had carried out an ambush against Malian pro-government militias near the village of Djini, on Friday, December 5.
body_en:
Djenné, Mopti Region, December 7, 2025 - On Sunday, December 7, JNIM announced via Al-Zalaqa that it had carried out an ambush against Malian pro-government militias near the village of Djini, on Friday, December 5.

The statement reported five militia members killed and the seizure of several automatic weapons and ammunition, highlighting the persistent threat posed by JNIM to local security forces in central Mali.

The period from November 24 to December 7, 2025, presents a stark duality in Mali’s trajectory, characterized by significant diplomatic and macroeconomic strides contrasted against a deteriorating security and human rights landscape.

1. Diplomatic and Economic Fortification The transitional government has successfully reinforced its international standing and regional integration. The Confederation of Sahel States (AES/CSA) is rapidly operationalizing, with intense preparations for the upcoming College of Heads of State session in Bamako. Simultaneously, Mali is diversifying its strategic partnerships, strengthening ties with Iran, Moldova, and the Philippines. Economically, the government received strong validation from the IMF and WAEMU for its fiscal discipline and a projected growth rate of 6.1%. The launch of the first National Export Day further signals a push toward economic autonomy and industrialization.

2. The Security Paradox and Energy Crisis Despite these institutional successes, the security situation remains precarious. While the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) continue to destroy terrorist bases and acquire new assets, insurgent groups like JNIM have intensified their blockade strategies. The encirclement of Bamako and the resumption of attacks on fuel convoys have triggered a severe hydrocarbon crisis, directly impacting the daily lives of citizens and threatening economic stability. The collapse of the temporary fuel agreement with JNIM highlights the fragility of the country's supply lines.

3. Human Rights and Social Strain The cost of the conflict on the civilian population is escalating. Human rights organizations and opposition panels have documented alarming allegations of "ethnic cleansing," summary executions, and scorched-earth tactics in the Timbuktu and Azawad regions attributed to FAMa and the Africa Corps. Concurrently, the civic space is shrinking, evidenced by the suspension of radio stations and the arrest of journalists, signaling a tightening grip on freedom of expression.

Final Outlook As Mali prepares to host the AES Heads of State summit in late December, the government faces the critical challenge of reconciling its diplomatic ambitions with urgent domestic realities. The coming weeks will be pivotal in determining whether the state can leverage its regional alliances to secure its territory and energy supply, or if the worsening humanitarian and security crises will undermine the macroeconomic and political gains achieved thus far.

title: Prime Minister Maïga Pays Working Visit to Guinea, Reaffirms Bilateral Cooperation
excerpt: Conakry, December 9, 2025 - Mali’s Prime Minister, Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, has paid a friendship and working visit to the Republic of Guinea, underscoring the strengthening of bilateral relations between the two…
title_en: Prime Minister Maïga Pays Working Visit to Guinea, Reaffirms Bilateral Cooperation
excerpt_en: Conakry, December 9, 2025 - Mali’s Prime Minister, Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, has paid a friendship and working visit to the Republic of Guinea, underscoring the strengthening of bilateral relations between the two…
body_en:
Conakry, December 9, 2025 - Mali’s Prime Minister, Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, has paid a friendship and working visit to the Republic of Guinea, underscoring the strengthening of bilateral relations between the two West African neighbors.

Upon arrival at Ahmed Sékou Touré International Airport in Conakry, Prime Minister Maïga was received by his Guinean counterpart, Amadou Oury Bah, alongside members of the Malian community. The visit featured a working session focused on economic and trade cooperation, including prospects for rail interconnection, transit corridors for goods, and the management of transhumance.

Both delegations reaffirmed their shared vision of a more integrated West Africa, with Guinea expressing its readiness to support Mali in advancing joint initiatives. The talks highlighted opportunities for future infrastructure and trade projects, which could contribute to economic stability and shared growth within the Alliance of Sahel States (AES).

Observers note, however, that translating these commitments into tangible outcomes will require addressing persistent security challenges along border areas, including jihadist threats that could disrupt trade and mobility. More broadly, the visit reflects the Malian transitional authorities’ strategy to diversify regional partnerships and recalibrate diplomatic relations, while navigating the balance between bilateral cooperation and wider regional integration within the AES framework.

title: AES Leaders Advance Plans for Sahel Confederation Bank in Bamako Talks
excerpt: Bamako, December 11, 2025 - Mali’s transitional president, General Assimi Goïta, on Wednesday received a high-level ministerial delegation from member states of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) at the Koulouba Palace…
title_en: AES Leaders Advance Plans for Sahel Confederation Bank in Bamako Talks
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 11, 2025 - Mali’s transitional president, General Assimi Goïta, on Wednesday received a high-level ministerial delegation from member states of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) at the Koulouba Palace…
body_en:
Bamako, December 11, 2025 - Mali’s transitional president, General Assimi Goïta, on Wednesday received a high-level ministerial delegation from member states of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) at the Koulouba Palace, as discussions moved forward on operationalizing the Confederation Bank for Investment and Development (BCID-AES).

The meeting focused on the bank’s mandate to finance priority infrastructure projects and support autonomous regional development, a core objective of the AES since its creation. According to officials, the BCID-AES is intended to mobilize regional resources for sectors such as transport, energy, and strategic connectivity, while reducing reliance on traditional international financial institutions.

Authorities described the talks as a decisive step toward consolidating the AES as a sovereign economic bloc, with Mali reaffirming its central role in driving the initiative. Supporters argue that the bank could inject much-needed capital into fragile economies, strengthen investor confidence, and accelerate regional integration among AES members.

Independent analysts have largely welcomed the momentum, noting that the project aligns with the alliance’s broader vision of economic self-reliance and integration. However, they caution that implementation risks remain significant, particularly in light of ongoing security challenges. Persistent jihadist activity and occasional blockades of key supply routes could slow project execution and undermine the bank’s operational viability if not adequately addressed.

Despite these concerns, Wednesday’s meeting signals renewed political commitment within the AES to translate regional cooperation into concrete financial instruments aimed at reshaping the Sahel’s economic landscape.

Bamako, December 11, 2025 - Mali’s transitional president, General Assimi Goïta, on Wednesday received a high-level ministerial delegation from member states of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) at the Koulouba Palace, as efforts intensify to make the Confederation Bank for Investment and Development (BCID-AES) fully operational.

The delegation, mandated by AES leaders, discussed the bank’s role in financing strategic infrastructure projects and promoting self-reliant regional growth, seen as a cornerstone of the alliance’s economic vision. Officials described the meeting as a decisive milestone in consolidating the AES as a sovereign economic bloc, while reaffirming Mali’s leadership within the alliance. Persistent security constraints, including jihadist attacks and periodic blockades of supply routes, could slow implementation and ultimately threaten the bank’s viability if not effectively managed.

Despite these risks, Wednesday’s discussions underscore a shared political will among AES members to translate regional cooperation into concrete financial mechanisms capable of reshaping the Sahel’s economic future.

title: Former Commander of Bamako Military Region Dismissed from Malian Armed Forces
excerpt: Bamako, December 12, 2025 - Colonel Alpha Yaya Sangaré, former commander of the Bamako military region, has been dismissed from the Malian Armed Forces (FAMA) following his arrest in connection with the publication of a…
title_en: Former Commander of Bamako Military Region Dismissed from Malian Armed Forces
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 12, 2025 - Colonel Alpha Yaya Sangaré, former commander of the Bamako military region, has been dismissed from the Malian Armed Forces (FAMA) following his arrest in connection with the publication of a…
body_en:
Bamako, December 12, 2025 - Colonel Alpha Yaya Sangaré, former commander of the Bamako military region, has been dismissed from the Malian Armed Forces (FAMA) following his arrest in connection with the publication of a book in which he denounced alleged “abuses by the army against civilian populations,” security sources confirmed on Thursday.

The decision underscores growing internal tensions within Mali’s military establishment, where discipline, loyalty, and adherence to the transition authorities’ line remain closely scrutinized amid an ongoing security crisis.

Supporters of the move argue that the dismissal could help reinforce cohesion within FAMA, by sanctioning voices seen as undermining unity at a time when the army is engaged on multiple fronts against jihadist groups. From this perspective, authorities view internal dissent as a potential threat to operational effectiveness and morale.

However, independent analysts and human rights observers have expressed concern over the implications of the decision. They warn that such measures could stifle internal debate, limit transparency on sensitive issues such as civilian protection, and fuel criticism from international partners and rights organizations.

The case also revives questions about the balance between national security and accountability, particularly in the context of Mali’s evolving security partnerships, including cooperation with the Africa Corps, which has faced allegations of controversial methods in counterterrorism operations.

Colonel Sangaré’s dismissal highlights the delicate line the transitional authorities are navigating between maintaining strict military discipline and addressing growing calls-both domestic and international-for openness and respect for human rights.

title: Mali: Community Leaders Commit to Dialogue as Transitional Authorities Step Up Peace Efforts
excerpt: Bamako, December 13, 2025 - Mali’s Minister of Reconciliation, Peace, and National Cohesion, Lieutenant General Ismaël Wagué, on Friday received two prominent community leaders from the country’s north, Abdoul Majid Ag…
title_en: Mali: Community Leaders Commit to Dialogue as Transitional Authorities Step Up Peace Efforts
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 13, 2025 - Mali’s Minister of Reconciliation, Peace, and National Cohesion, Lieutenant General Ismaël Wagué, on Friday received two prominent community leaders from the country’s north, Abdoul Majid Ag…
body_en:
Bamako, December 13, 2025 - Mali’s Minister of Reconciliation, Peace, and National Cohesion, Lieutenant General Ismaël Wagué, on Friday received two prominent community leaders from the country’s north, Abdoul Majid Ag Mohamed Ahmed, known as Nasser, and Mohamed Ousmane Ag Mohamedoun, in a renewed push to ease tensions and promote dialogue.

The meeting followed separate consultations held the previous day and concluded with a shared commitment by the two leaders to overcome their differences and work together in line with the National Charter for Peace and Reconciliation. Authorities say the initiative reflects the government’s determination to prioritize dialogue as a cornerstone of stability in fragile regions.

According to officials, such engagement could help facilitate social reintegration, reduce intercommunal tensions, and curb recruitment by jihadist groups, thereby strengthening national cohesion within the framework of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES). Observers caution, however, that dialogue alone will not be sufficient unless accompanied by concrete socio-economic reforms in vulnerable areas, where insecurity, poverty, and forced displacement remain widespread.

title: Mali’s CNT President Advocates Sovereignty at African Parliamentary Summit
excerpt: Rabat, December 12-14, 2025 - Meanwhile, Malick Diaw, President of Mali’s National Transitional Council (CNT), took part in the 3rd Conference of Presidents of African Legislative Assemblies in Rabat, Morocco.
title_en: Mali’s CNT President Advocates Sovereignty at African Parliamentary Summit
excerpt_en: Rabat, December 12-14, 2025 - Meanwhile, Malick Diaw, President of Mali’s National Transitional Council (CNT), took part in the 3rd Conference of Presidents of African Legislative Assemblies in Rabat, Morocco.
body_en:
Rabat, December 12-14, 2025 - Meanwhile, Malick Diaw, President of Mali’s National Transitional Council (CNT), took part in the 3rd Conference of Presidents of African Legislative Assemblies in Rabat, Morocco.

In his address, Diaw highlighted the long-standing historical ties between Mali and Morocco while denouncing what he described as a sustained media campaign against Mali. He called for accurate and responsible information to counter what he termed “economic and media terrorism.”

His participation underscores Mali’s intention to remain actively engaged in continental political dynamics and to strengthen pan-African cooperation, particularly in governance and institutional dialogue. Analysts note that while this sovereignist stance may reinforce alliances at the African level, it will need to be matched by greater transparency and internal reforms to address ongoing criticisms related to governance and accountability.

title: First Confederal Session of ESA Council of Ministers Opens in Bamako
excerpt: Bamako, December 20, 2025 - The Koulouba Palace hosted the first confederal session of the Council of Ministers of the Confederation of Sahel States (ESA), chaired by General Assimi Goïta.
title_en: First Confederal Session of ESA Council of Ministers Opens in Bamako
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 20, 2025 - The Koulouba Palace hosted the first confederal session of the Council of Ministers of the Confederation of Sahel States (ESA), chaired by General Assimi Goïta.
body_en:
Bamako, December 20, 2025 - The Koulouba Palace hosted the first confederal session of the Council of Ministers of the Confederation of Sahel States (ESA), chaired by General Assimi Goïta. The meeting reviewed the implementation report of the first-year roadmap and additional protocols on defense, diplomacy, and development, with participation from ministers of Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger.

In his address, Mr. Goïta condemned “economic and media terrorism” targeting the ESA, asserting that such pressures only strengthen the sovereign resolve of Sahelian peoples.

The session lays the groundwork for the second Heads of State meeting, scheduled for December 22-23, which is expected to accelerate regional integration, joint infrastructure, and security initiatives, thereby enhancing the Sahel’s autonomy from external influences.

Analysts note that ongoing tensions with ECOWAS could pose challenges to policy harmonization, requiring careful coordination to ensure sustainable progress.

excerpt: Bamako, December 21, 2025 - The High Council of Malians Abroad (CSDM) has urged the National Transitional Council (CNT) to incorporate the Malian diaspora into the 2026 Finance Law.
title_en: CSDM Calls on Mali’s National Transitional Council to Integrate Diaspora in 2026 Finance Law
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 21, 2025 - The High Council of Malians Abroad (CSDM) has urged the National Transitional Council (CNT) to incorporate the Malian diaspora into the 2026 Finance Law.
body_en:
Bamako, December 21, 2025 - The High Council of Malians Abroad (CSDM) has urged the National Transitional Council (CNT) to incorporate the Malian diaspora into the 2026 Finance Law. The appeal aims to mobilize productive investments representing 7% of GDP and to modernize consular services, enhancing the protection and support of citizens living abroad.

excerpt_en: Washington, December 17, 2025 - Former U.S. President Donald Trump signed an executive order prohibiting entry to the United States for nationals of Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger, citing national security concerns.
body_en:
Washington, December 17, 2025 - Former U.S. President Donald Trump signed an executive order prohibiting entry to the United States for nationals of Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger, citing national security concerns. Partial restrictions also apply to Senegal and Côte d’Ivoire, effective January 1, 2026.

The measure could disrupt travel, education, and economic exchanges and strain diplomatic relations. While it reinforces the sovereignty narrative of ESA countries in response to perceived Western interference, analysts warn it could isolate diasporas and worsen socio-economic vulnerabilities if alternative migration pathways are not strengthened.

title: Mali Adopts 2026 Budget, Targets Deficit Reduction and Economic Recovery
excerpt: Bamako, December 10, 2025 - Mali’s National Transitional Council (CNT) has adopted the draft budget law for the 2026 fiscal year, setting total expenditures at 3,578 billion CFA francs, authorities announced on Tuesday.
title_en: Mali Adopts 2026 Budget, Targets Deficit Reduction and Economic Recovery
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 10, 2025 - Mali’s National Transitional Council (CNT) has adopted the draft budget law for the 2026 fiscal year, setting total expenditures at 3,578 billion CFA francs, authorities announced on Tuesday.
body_en:
Bamako, December 10, 2025 - Mali’s National Transitional Council (CNT) has adopted the draft budget law for the 2026 fiscal year, setting total expenditures at 3,578 billion CFA francs, authorities announced on Tuesday.

The new budget forecasts a 10% reduction in the budget deficit compared to the previous year, while remaining in line with the convergence criteria of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU). The government is projecting economic growth of 6.3%, despite ongoing security pressures and climate-related challenges affecting the Sahel.

According to official documents, the 2026 budget prioritizes security, education, and health, sectors considered critical to state reconstruction and improvements in living conditions for the population. Significant allocations to these areas are intended to strengthen national resilience and support inclusive, long-term development.

The adoption of the budget is seen as a signal of increased fiscal discipline and budgetary maturity under the transition authorities. Analysts say it could help bolster confidence among international partners and investors, at a time when Mali is deepening regional coordination within the framework of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES).

title: Mali Launches CFA 312 Billion Domestic Debt Relief to Boost Economic Recovery
excerpt: Bamako, December 8, 2025 - Mali has launched a domestic debt relief program worth 312 billion CFA francs (about US$554 million) aimed at reviving the national economy and easing pressure on local businesses, the…
title_en: Mali Launches CFA 312 Billion Domestic Debt Relief to Boost Economic Recovery
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 8, 2025 - Mali has launched a domestic debt relief program worth 312 billion CFA francs (about US$554 million) aimed at reviving the national economy and easing pressure on local businesses, the…
body_en:
Bamako, December 8, 2025 - Mali has launched a domestic debt relief program worth 312 billion CFA francs (about US$554 million) aimed at reviving the national economy and easing pressure on local businesses, the Ministry of Economy and Finance announced on Sunday.

Speaking in Bamako, Economy and Finance Minister Alousséni Sanou said the disbursement will be rolled out over three months starting December 8, targeting outstanding debts for 2023 and 2024. The plan also covers payments linked to strategic projects, including road and hospital infrastructure, school fees, compensation claims, and support to the defense sector.

The initiative is financed through revenues generated from an audit of the mining sector, and is intended to inject liquidity into the banking system while improving the cash flow of domestic companies.

According to official figures, Mali’s domestic debt has already fallen from nearly 600 billion CFA francs in September 2024 to around 439 billion CFA francs, following cumulative disbursements totaling 1,654 billion CFA francs.

Authorities describe the program as a turning point in the financial management of the Transition, reflecting a move toward greater fiscal discipline and economic sovereignty in line with the objectives of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES).

Economists note that the measure could stimulate economic growth, strengthen investor confidence, and support the private sector, despite persistent security challenges. Analysts from the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund have welcomed the sustained reduction in domestic arrears, which they say could help underpin projected growth of between 5% and 6.3% in 2025, driven mainly by the extractive and agricultural sectors.

title: Mali Launches SDG-Aligned Investment Map to Channel Private Capital into High-Impact Projects
excerpt: Bamako, December 9, 2025 - The Investment Promotion Agency of Mali (API-Mali) has officially launched an interactive investment map aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), a digital…
title_en: Mali Launches SDG-Aligned Investment Map to Channel Private Capital into High-Impact Projects
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 9, 2025 - The Investment Promotion Agency of Mali (API-Mali) has officially launched an interactive investment map aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), a digital…
body_en:
Bamako, December 9, 2025 - The Investment Promotion Agency of Mali (API-Mali) has officially launched an interactive investment map aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), a digital platform designed to steer private capital toward projects with strong social and environmental impact.

According to API-Mali, the tool provides real-time information on investment opportunities across priority sectors such as sustainable agriculture, renewable energy, and infrastructure. The platform will be updated continuously to ensure data reliability, enhance transparency, and strengthen Mali’s attractiveness to both domestic and international investors.

Authorities say the initiative marks a significant step forward in the digitization of investment services in Mali, where access to economic opportunities is often constrained by bureaucratic bottlenecks and regional instability. By centralizing and standardizing investment data, the platform aims to reduce administrative barriers, improve visibility for viable projects, and facilitate decision-making by investors.

Analysts note that the investment map could help limit corruption, promote the inclusion of local small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), and better align private investment with national development priorities, particularly those of the Economic and Social Development Agency (ADES) focused on inclusive growth. Similar digital tools have been highlighted in African Development Bank (AfDB) reports as effective mechanisms for mobilizing sustainable finance.

Technology experts also view the platform as a move toward a more digital and transparent economy, with the potential to increase foreign direct investment (FDI) in a country where internet penetration currently stands at around 35 percent.

However, observers caution that the impact of the initiative may be limited by uneven internet access and cybersecurity risks, which could exclude rural or vulnerable investors unless accompanied by additional investment in digital infrastructure and data protection systems.

Despite these challenges, the launch of the SDG-aligned investment map is widely seen as a strategic signal of Mali’s commitment to sustainable development, innovation, and improved investment governance amid a complex economic and security environment.

title: Mali Unveils National Cybersecurity Framework for 2026-2030
