title_en: Mali Unveils National Cybersecurity Framework for 2026-2030
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 11, 2025 - The Malian government has announced plans to roll out a coordinated national cybersecurity framework covering the 2026-2030 period, aimed at strengthening the protection of critical…
body_en:
Bamako, December 11, 2025 - The Malian government has announced plans to roll out a coordinated national cybersecurity framework covering the 2026-2030 period, aimed at strengthening the protection of critical infrastructure amid a growing threat landscape in cyberspace.

According to official sources, the strategy will focus on safeguarding key sectors including energy, finance, and telecommunications, which authorities describe as increasingly vulnerable to cyberattacks. The framework is expected to integrate prevention, detection, and response mechanisms, while reinforcing institutional coordination across public and private stakeholders.

The plan also draws on regional cooperation within the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) and foresees targeted investments in advanced technologies to enhance digital resilience. Officials say the initiative reflects Mali’s determination to secure its ongoing digital transition at a time when security challenges are no longer confined to the physical domain.

Analysts note that the cybersecurity framework could help protect essential public services, strengthen confidence among investors, and stimulate local technological innovation. By aligning national standards with international best practices, the strategy is also expected to improve Mali’s positioning in the global digital economy, as highlighted by technology-focused platforms such as We Are Tech Africa.

Experts further emphasize that improved cybersecurity governance may play a key role in protecting digital investments, particularly as Mali diversifies its technological partnerships toward new actors, including China and Russia.

While details on implementation and funding are yet to be fully disclosed, the announcement is widely viewed as a strategic milestone in Mali’s efforts to combine sovereignty, security, and economic modernization in an increasingly connected world.

title: Sahel Alliance Moves to Operationalize Confederal Development Bank
excerpt: Bamako, December 11, 2025 - Ministers of Economy and Finance from the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) met in Bamako on Wednesday to advance the operational launch of the AES Confederal Bank for Investment and Development…
title_en: Sahel Alliance Moves to Operationalize Confederal Development Bank
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 11, 2025 - Ministers of Economy and Finance from the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) met in Bamako on Wednesday to advance the operational launch of the AES Confederal Bank for Investment and Development…
body_en:
Bamako, December 11, 2025 - Ministers of Economy and Finance from the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) met in Bamako on Wednesday to advance the operational launch of the AES Confederal Bank for Investment and Development (BCID-AES), a key pillar of the bloc’s strategy for regional economic autonomy.

According to official statements, the bank-formally established on December 11-is designed to finance structuring projects primarily through national resources, with a focus on infrastructure and energy. The meeting follows an expert-level session held in May 2025, which laid the technical groundwork for the institution.

The initiative is seen as a significant step toward deepening economic integration within the AES and reinforcing Mali’s leadership role in shaping the bloc’s financial architecture. By prioritizing domestically mobilized funding, the BCID-AES aims to reduce reliance on international financial institutions while accelerating investment in priority sectors.

Analysts note that, if effectively implemented, the bank could unlock capital for high-impact projects, support inclusive growth, and strengthen investor confidence across the Sahel. The African Development Bank (AfDB) has welcomed the momentum, viewing it as aligned with broader objectives of sovereignty and sustainable development.

While timelines and capitalization details are expected to be clarified in the coming months, officials described the Bamako meeting as a decisive milestone toward making the BCID-AES fully operational.

excerpt_en: Washington, December 15, 2025 - The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has approved the first review of Mali’s Supervised Services Program (SSP).
body_en:
Washington, December 15, 2025 - The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has approved the first review of Mali’s Supervised Services Program (SSP). The program is designed to strengthen macroeconomic policies, enhance governance, and lay the groundwork for a potential future financing agreement.

Malian authorities have reportedly made progress in fiscal management and reducing vulnerabilities, despite ongoing security challenges. This approval signals international confidence in Mali’s economic trajectory and could unlock additional financing, potentially boosting projected growth to 5-6% in 2026, aligned with the Regional Economic Council (RES) fiscal self-sufficiency goals.

Analysts caution that further reforms are needed to mitigate risks stemming from insecurity and dependence on raw materials, ensuring sustainable economic stability.

excerpt_en: Bamako, December 17, 2025 - Mali has unveiled its 2026 airport modernization plan, aiming to transform Bamako into a major West African hub.

Bamako, December 17, 2025 - Mali has unveiled its 2026 airport modernization plan, aiming to transform Bamako into a major West African hub. The program includes the integration of advanced technologies, adherence to ICAO safety standards, and renovation of regional airport infrastructure.

This initiative aligns with the transitional government’s efforts to revitalize transport infrastructure and supports the ESA’s regional integration objectives. Officials say it could attract investment, boost tourism, and enhance trade.

However, analysts caution that ongoing security and financial challenges could delay implementation unless robust partnerships are established to support the program.

excerpt_en: Bamako, December 20, 2025 - Sékou Ibrahim Barry, an agricultural economist, has been appointed head of the Office du Niger, Mali’s key irrigation authority.
body_en:
Bamako, December 20, 2025 - Sékou Ibrahim Barry, an agricultural economist, has been appointed head of the Office du Niger, Mali’s key irrigation authority. His mandate focuses on modernizing 140,000 hectares of irrigated land and supporting local producers, advancing the government’s strategy for agricultural self-sufficiency and a resilient economy within the WAEMU framework.

Officials note that this move could increase rice production, reduce food imports, and promote inclusive growth. Analysts, however, caution that climate risks and ongoing security challenges may impede progress unless additional investments in infrastructure and technology are made.

title: Return of 3 Tons of Gold to Barrick Gold Resolves Major Mining Dispute
excerpt: Bamako, December 15-21, 2025 - A Malian judge has ordered the return of 3 tons of gold (around US$400 million) seized from Barrick Gold at the Loulo-Gounkoto site in January, following a settlement reached last month.
title_en: Return of 3 Tons of Gold to Barrick Gold Resolves Major Mining Dispute
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 15-21, 2025 - A Malian judge has ordered the return of 3 tons of gold (around US$400 million) seized from Barrick Gold at the Loulo-Gounkoto site in January, following a settlement reached last month.
body_en:
Bamako, December 15-21, 2025 - A Malian judge has ordered the return of 3 tons of gold (around US$400 million) seized from Barrick Gold at the Loulo-Gounkoto site in January, following a settlement reached last month. Under the agreement, Barrick accepted US$430 million, and control of the mining complex is expected to be restored this week, ending a two-year dispute over the new mining code.

Four Barrick employees, imprisoned since November 2024, have been released, and international arbitration proceedings have been dropped. Officials say this resolution strengthens investor confidence in Mali’s mining sector and contributes to the goal of raising US$1.2 billion through mining reforms in early 2026, including 500 billion CFA francs already secured by end-2024. Additionally, the settlement increases state revenue via a 35% participation and provisions on gold sales.

title_en: Appointment to AES TV Management Signals Progress in Digital Media
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 17, 2025 - The Minister of Communication, Digital Economy, and Administrative Modernization has appointed five Malians to the management of AES TV, including editor-in-chief Moussa Abdoulaye Papa…
body_en:
Bamako, December 17, 2025 - The Minister of Communication, Digital Economy, and Administrative Modernization has appointed five Malians to the management of AES TV, including editor-in-chief Moussa Abdoulaye Papa Haïdara and technical director Mamadou Guindo. While the move is intended to ensure representation of AES countries, the exclusively Malian appointments have drawn criticism over perceived hegemony.

Officials describe this as a step toward media modernization and the digital economy in the Sahel, promoting sovereign information. On the positive side, it could strengthen regional cohesion through shared content and support technological diversification. However, analysts warn that excluding Burkinabe and Nigerien partners risks internal tensions within the ESA, potentially limiting the channel’s cross-border impact.

title: Bamako Faces Fluctuating Fuel Shortages Amid Security Challenges
excerpt: Bamako, December 15-21, 2025 - Fuel supplies in Bamako remain unstable due to road insecurity, disrupting tanker transport.
title_en: Bamako Faces Fluctuating Fuel Shortages Amid Security Challenges
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 15-21, 2025 - Fuel supplies in Bamako remain unstable due to road insecurity, disrupting tanker transport.
body_en:
Bamako, December 15-21, 2025 - Fuel supplies in Bamako remain unstable due to road insecurity, disrupting tanker transport. According to CECOGEC, the situation has slightly slowed economic activity, worsened by JNIM attacks since December 6, despite a temporary resumption of deliveries.

The crisis is impacting the daily economy by raising transport costs and affecting productive sectors. On the positive side, it highlights the resilience of alternative supply chains. However, without sustainable road security measures, it risks exacerbating inflation and hindering growth, particularly amid ongoing efforts to diversify energy partnerships within the ESA.

title: Mercy Corps Hosts Regional Conference on Gender-Based Violence in the Sahel
excerpt: Tahoua, December 9, 2025 - As part of the Justice and Stability in the Sahel (JASS) program, Mercy Corps convened a regional conference in Bouza, bringing together exemplary husbands and wives from Mali and Niger to…
title_en: Mercy Corps Hosts Regional Conference on Gender-Based Violence in the Sahel
excerpt_en: Tahoua, December 9, 2025 - As part of the Justice and Stability in the Sahel (JASS) program, Mercy Corps convened a regional conference in Bouza, bringing together exemplary husbands and wives from Mali and Niger to…
body_en:
Tahoua, December 9, 2025 - As part of the Justice and Stability in the Sahel (JASS) program, Mercy Corps convened a regional conference in Bouza, bringing together exemplary husbands and wives from Mali and Niger to promote positive masculinity and prevent gender-based violence (GBV).

Funded by the UK’s Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO), the initiative aligns with the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence campaign and aims to mainstream gender equality into regional stability strategies. Organizers emphasized the importance of reshaping cultural norms and empowering communities to reduce social vulnerabilities exacerbated by ongoing conflict in the Sahel.

The program is expected to strengthen community cohesion and contribute to the broader Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) objectives of the JASS program. Independent observers have welcomed its potential to foster long-term behavioral change.

However, experts caution that without strengthened legislative oversight and greater investment in education, the impact of such initiatives may be limited, particularly amid persistent challenges such as the forced displacement of over 400,000 people in Mali.

title: WHO Reports First Smallpox Case in Mali, Urges Heightened Vigilance
excerpt: Bamako, December 10, 2025 - The World Health Organization (WHO) has confirmed Mali’s first reported case of smallpox, detected in November 2025, in its latest multi-country health alert.
title_en: WHO Reports First Smallpox Case in Mali, Urges Heightened Vigilance
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 10, 2025 - The World Health Organization (WHO) has confirmed Mali’s first reported case of smallpox, detected in November 2025, in its latest multi-country health alert.
body_en:
Bamako, December 10, 2025 - The World Health Organization (WHO) has confirmed Mali’s first reported case of smallpox, detected in November 2025, in its latest multi-country health alert.

The report emphasizes heightened risks in border regions with Burkina Faso and Niger and calls for vaccination of vulnerable populations alongside strengthened regional coordination through the Early Warning System.

Health authorities note that ongoing conflict and population displacement in Mali exacerbate the country’s vulnerability to infectious disease outbreaks, highlighting the urgent need for proactive public health measures.

WHO’s alert signals a renewed emphasis on disease surveillance, preparedness, and cross-border cooperation to prevent further spread.

title: NRC Warns of Worsening Humanitarian Crisis in Southern Mali
excerpt: Bamako, December 11, 2025 - The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) has issued a stark warning over the impact of humanitarian aid cuts in Mali, noting that the security crisis is expanding southward.
title_en: NRC Warns of Worsening Humanitarian Crisis in Southern Mali
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 11, 2025 - The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) has issued a stark warning over the impact of humanitarian aid cuts in Mali, noting that the security crisis is expanding southward.
body_en:
Bamako, December 11, 2025 - The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) has issued a stark warning over the impact of humanitarian aid cuts in Mali, noting that the security crisis is expanding southward.

The report details that families are reducing meals, while many children are unable to attend school due to restricted access to basic services. Currently, over 8 million people are in urgent need of assistance.

The NRC emphasizes that insecurity and logistical challenges, including attacks on aid convoys, are compounding the crisis. The organization is calling for immediate and increased funding to address hunger, displacement, and the growing vulnerabilities of affected communities.

This alert underscores the critical link between security and humanitarian access, highlighting the urgent need for coordinated national and international response efforts.

title_en: Mali Partners with UNAIDS to Eliminate HIV in Newborns by 2030
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 20, 2025 - The State of Mali has partnered with UNAIDS to accelerate progress toward the goal of “Zero HIV in Newborns” by 2030, targeting the triple elimination of HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis B.
body_en:
Bamako, December 20, 2025 - The State of Mali has partnered with UNAIDS to accelerate progress toward the goal of “Zero HIV in Newborns” by 2030, targeting the triple elimination of HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis B. A key component of the initiative is to strengthen prenatal care coverage to 95% for pregnant women.

This collaboration underscores Mali’s commitment to improving maternal and child health in line with the African Union’s Sustainable Development Goals. It could substantially reduce mother-to-child transmission, enhancing public health outcomes and promoting equity. However, limited access to care and resources in rural areas may restrict the program’s effectiveness without further investment in health infrastructure.

title_en: Social Crisis at Diamond Cement Mali: 271 Employees Facing Layoffs
excerpt_en: Kayes, December 18, 2025 - Diamond Cement Mali has announced plans to lay off 271 employees due to economic reasons, a decision that has been contested by the union.
body_en:
Kayes, December 18, 2025 - Diamond Cement Mali has announced plans to lay off 271 employees due to economic reasons, a decision that has been contested by the union. The dispute is currently under review by the Labor Directorate, with workers denouncing the move as unjustified.

This situation underscores social tensions in Mali’s industrial sector, linked to broader economic challenges in the Sahel. On one hand, it could prompt reforms to protect employment and maintain social stability. On the other hand, analysts warn that escalating labor disputes may negatively impact local economic growth if effective mediation is not implemented.

title_en: Launch of the 2025 Arts and Culture Biennial: Strengthening Social Cohesion Through Culture
excerpt_en: Timbuktu, December 20, 2025 - Prime Minister Abdoulaye Maïga inaugurated the 2025 Arts and Culture Biennial in Timbuktu, themed “Culture, a Pillar for Building the New Mali.”
body_en:
Timbuktu, December 20, 2025 - Prime Minister Abdoulaye Maïga inaugurated the 2025 Arts and Culture Biennial in Timbuktu, themed “Culture, a Pillar for Building the New Mali.” Running from December 18 to 28, the event showcases Malian traditions and creative expressions as part of the Year of Culture proclaimed by the transitional government.

The biennial aims to promote social cohesion and inclusive development by reinforcing national identity amid ongoing security challenges. It is also expected to stimulate cultural tourism, boost the local economy, and foster unity within the African Union.

However, instability in northern Mali may limit access and the event’s overall impact, highlighting the need for enhanced security measures, especially for vulnerable communities.

excerpt: Bamako, December 18, 2025 - On International Migrants Day, 150 Malians were repatriated to Mali via Niger, in partnership with the International Organization for Migration (IOM).
title_en: Repatriation of 150 Malians in Distress from Algeria and Tunisia: Humanitarian Support for the Diaspora
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 18, 2025 - On International Migrants Day, 150 Malians were repatriated to Mali via Niger, in partnership with the International Organization for Migration (IOM).
body_en:
Bamako, December 18, 2025 - On International Migrants Day, 150 Malians were repatriated to Mali via Niger, in partnership with the International Organization for Migration (IOM). They were welcomed by Minister for Malians Living Abroad and African Integration, Mossa Ag Attaher, and will receive assistance for socio-economic reintegration.

This operation reflects the government’s commitment to supporting Malians in distress abroad, addressing migration vulnerabilities exacerbated by regional crises. It also strengthens national cohesion and could reduce irregular migration flows through reintegration programs.

However, without structural reforms to create local opportunities, the initiative risks failing to tackle root causes of migration, such as unemployment and insecurity.

The events included conferences, workshops, and awareness campaigns engaging young people, justice actors, and civil society to promote transparency and combat economic crime.

This initiative reflects the Transitional Government’s commitment to integrating youth into anti-corruption strategies, particularly in a context where corruption continues to undermine public trust in institutions. Experts note that such engagement could strengthen civic education and help reduce corrupt practices within the public sector, aligning with the objectives of the Economic and Social Action Network (RAS) for good governance.

Independent observers, including Transparency International, welcomed the mobilization, while cautioning that without concrete legal reforms and strengthened oversight institutions such as the Office for the Control of Illicit Enrichment (Oclei), these efforts risk remaining largely symbolic, especially amid persistent allegations of corruption in the mining sector.

title_en: Mali Dismisses Former Bamako Military Region Commander Amid Controversy
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 12, 2025 - Colonel Alpha Yaya Sangaré, former commander of the Bamako military region, has been dismissed from the Malian Armed Forces (FAMA) following his arrest over the publication of a book…
body_en:
Bamako, December 12, 2025 - Colonel Alpha Yaya Sangaré, former commander of the Bamako military region, has been dismissed from the Malian Armed Forces (FAMA) following his arrest over the publication of a book criticizing “abuses committed by the army against civilian populations.”

The move exposes internal tensions within FAMA, where discipline and loyalty are strictly enforced. While it could reinforce cohesion by sanctioning dissenting voices aligned against the Transition’s vision of a unified anti-terror army, analysts warn of risks of increased repression, potential stifling of human rights debates, and international criticism.

Observers also note concerns about balancing national security and transparency, especially amid partnerships with organizations such as Africa Corps, which has faced allegations of employing controversial methods.

body_en:
Bamako, December 13, 2025 - A group of lawyers has filed a case with Mali’s Supreme Court contesting the recent dismissal of officers from the Malian Armed Forces (FAMA). The plaintiffs allege abuse of power and violations of defense rights, requesting both annulment of the dismissals and reinstatement of the affected personnel.

This legal action underscores ongoing tensions between military authority and judicial oversight. Supporters say it could promote transparency and uphold the rule of law, while neutral observers note its significance in protecting the rights of individuals.

However, given Mali’s persistent security challenges, an impartial judicial process will be critical to prevent accusations of bias. Analysts also warn that the case could provoke debate regarding international military partnerships, particularly with Russia.

body_en:
Bamako, December 16, 2025 - In the case of Mohamed Youssouf Bathily, known as Ras Bath, the Indictment Chamber did not order his release but instead referred his case to the Assize Court-a court that has been abolished in Mali, creating significant judicial confusion. Media sources indicate that the case will likely be transferred to the Anti-Cybercrime Unit for prosecution.

This incident underscores the dysfunctions within the Malian judicial system, especially in cases involving public figures critical of the regime.

On the positive side, it could accelerate reforms to clarify judicial procedures and strengthen the rule of law within the AES framework. However, independent analysts warn of the risks of politicized justice, which could prolong arbitrary detentions and invite human rights criticism during the transitional period.

title: Investigation into French Intelligence Agent Detained in Mali

title_en: Investigation into French Intelligence Agent Detained in Mali
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 17, 2025 - Malian authorities have opened an investigation into a French intelligence agent detained in Mali since August on suspicion of espionage.
body_en:
Bamako, December 17, 2025 - Malian authorities have opened an investigation into a French intelligence agent detained in Mali since August on suspicion of espionage. France has condemned the detention as a violation of the Vienna Convention and is intensifying efforts to secure the agent’s release.

The case highlights post-colonial judicial tensions and Mali’s commitment to upholding its judicial sovereignty. On one hand, it demonstrates the application of national law against foreign interference. On the other, analysts warn that without a swift resolution, the situation could strain diplomatic relations and underscores the need for a careful balance between national security and adherence to international norms.

title: ESA Puts Air Defense on Maximum Alert
excerpt: Bamako, December 8, 2025 - The Alliance of Sahel States (ESA) has placed its air and anti-air defense on maximum alert, following instructions from the Heads of State.
title_en: ESA Puts Air Defense on Maximum Alert
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 8, 2025 - The Alliance of Sahel States (ESA) has placed its air and anti-air defense on maximum alert, following instructions from the Heads of State.
body_en:
Bamako, December 8, 2025 - The Alliance of Sahel States (ESA) has placed its air and anti-air defense on maximum alert, following instructions from the Heads of State.

Announced by General Assimi Goïta, President of the Confederation, the measure authorizes the neutralization of any aircraft violating ESA airspace, in line with the December 22, 2024 declaration.

The decision responds to a recent incursion by a Nigerian military aircraft and underscores ESA’s commitment to sovereign territorial security. While the alert strengthens deterrence and regional stability, analysts caution that it may heighten diplomatic tensions with neighboring countries and urge a careful balance between security measures and dialogue.

body_en:
Bamako, December 9, 2025 - JNIM militants launched an attack on a tanker convoy escorted by the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) along the Bougouni-Bamako road, setting several vehicles on fire and causing casualties among soldiers and drivers.

The army swiftly secured the area and called on civilians to report suspicious activity. The incident ends a brief period of relative calm, disrupting fuel supplies from Côte d’Ivoire and Senegal. Analysts note that the attack is part of JNIM’s strategy to isolate Bamako and exacerbate shortages.

While the FAMa’s rapid response helped limit the damage, the incident underscores persistent vulnerabilities in securing key road networks, highlighting the need for strengthened regional partnerships and sustainable logistics solutions to maintain public confidence.

title_en: JNIM Publishes Video Claiming Soumpi Camp Attack
excerpt_en: Timbuktu, December 14, 2025 - JNIM has released a video confirming its takeover of Soumpi camp on November 7, 2025, claiming to have killed over 40 Malian soldiers.
body_en:
Timbuktu, December 14, 2025 - JNIM has released a video confirming its takeover of Soumpi camp on November 7, 2025, claiming to have killed over 40 Malian soldiers.

The footage, released today, shows smoke rising from the camp and field commander Houssein Ghoulam appearing in the sequence, underscoring one of the bloodiest attacks in recent years.

The release highlights the ongoing propaganda efforts of armed groups and the persistent challenges in eradicating jihadist networks in northern Mali.

While it may prompt an intensification of counterterrorism operations within the AES, neutral observers caution about prolonged humanitarian consequences, including forced displacement and vulnerable local populations, urging a balanced approach combining military action with socio-economic initiatives to curb recruitment.

title: Associated Press Investigation: Alleged Abuses by Russian African Corps in Mali
excerpt: Mali, December 18, 2025 - A new Associated Press investigation reports that 34 Malian refugees have described summary executions, beheadings, and sexual violence allegedly committed by the Russian African…
title_en: Associated Press Investigation: Alleged Abuses by Russian African Corps in Mali
excerpt_en: Mali, December 18, 2025 - A new Associated Press investigation reports that 34 Malian refugees have described summary executions, beheadings, and sexual violence allegedly committed by the Russian African…
body_en:
Mali, December 18, 2025 - A new Associated Press investigation reports that 34 Malian refugees have described summary executions, beheadings, and sexual violence allegedly committed by the Russian African Corps-successor to the Wagner Group-during operations conducted alongside the Malian army.

The report traces the evolution of the Russian presence in Mali since 2021. The African Corps, reportedly under the Russian Ministry of Defense, is estimated to deploy up to 2,000 fighters, largely former Wagner personnel. Malian authorities deny the deployment of mercenaries, claiming the individuals are Russian instructors.

These revelations highlight humanitarian challenges and potential human rights violations in counterterrorism operations across the Sahel, compounded by restricted access for journalists and aid workers. On the positive side, the findings could encourage international accountability and bolster demands for greater transparency within the Sahel Economic and Social Agency (SESA). However, analysts warn of possible diplomatic tensions and increased forced displacement without independent verification mechanisms.

title: Diplomatic Consultations on Security Ahead of BAMEX 2026
excerpt: Bamako, December 15, 2025 - Mali’s Ministers of Foreign Affairs and Security convened with the diplomatic corps to discuss preparations for the second International Defense and Security Exhibition (BAMEX 2026)…
title_en: Diplomatic Consultations on Security Ahead of BAMEX 2026
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 15, 2025 - Mali’s Ministers of Foreign Affairs and Security convened with the diplomatic corps to discuss preparations for the second International Defense and Security Exhibition (BAMEX 2026)…
body_en:
Bamako, December 15, 2025 - Mali’s Ministers of Foreign Affairs and Security convened with the diplomatic corps to discuss preparations for the second International Defense and Security Exhibition (BAMEX 2026), scheduled for November 2026. Discussions also addressed ongoing counterterrorism efforts and measures to secure oil supplies.

The initiative aims to strengthen international security partnerships and foster technological innovation. On the positive side, it could attract foreign investment in defense and enhance national resilience. However, analysts caution that persistent security and logistical challenges may limit the exhibition’s impact without stronger engagement from international partners.

The period from December 7 to 21, 2025, underscores a pivotal phase for Mali as it maneuvers through a complex landscape of sovereignty-driven diplomacy, economic restructuring, and persistent security volatility. The transitional authorities have made significant strides in institutionalizing the Alliance of Sahel States (AES), most notably through the operationalization of the Confederation Bank for Investment and Development (BCID-AES) and the symbolic presentation of the flag for the United Force of the Sahel States Alliance (UF-AES). These moves signal a clear intent to achieve regional self-reliance in both finance and defense.

However, this drive for autonomy is being tested by several critical factors:

Security Pressures: Despite successful Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) airstrikes in the Sikasso, Nioro, and Bougouni regions , jihadist groups like JNIM continue to exert pressure through ambushes on vital supply routes and attacks on state infrastructure. The spread of violence into southern Mali remains a growing concern.

Economic Resilience: The adoption of the 2026 budget and the launch of a 312 billion CFA franc debt relief program reflect a commitment to fiscal discipline and the revitalization of the private sector. Yet, fluctuating fuel shortages and labor disputes, such as the layoffs at Diamond Cement Mali, highlight the fragility of the domestic economy.

Governance and Human Rights: The dismissal of Colonel Alpha Yaya Sangaré and the indictment of individuals for "attempted destabilization" illustrate a strict enforcement of military discipline and internal security. Nevertheless, reports of abuses by the Africa Corps and the judicial confusion surrounding the Ras Bath case continue to draw scrutiny from independent observers and international partners regarding the balance between security and civil liberties.

Humanitarian Crisis: The situation remains dire, with the Norwegian Refugee Council warning that over 8 million people are in urgent need of assistance. The detection of the first smallpox case and ongoing aid cuts further exacerbate the vulnerabilities of displaced populations.

In summary, while Mali is successfully building the architectural framework for a sovereign Sahelian bloc, the long-term viability of these initiatives depends on its ability to translate political and military maneuvers into tangible security for its citizens and a stable environment for economic growth.

title: ESA Deepens Institutional Integration at High-Level Ministerial Session
excerpt: OUAGADOUGOU, Burkina Faso - November 26, 2025 - The Alliance of Sahel States (ESA) marked a major step forward in its regional integration project during an extensive ministerial coordination session that brought…
title_en: ESA Deepens Institutional Integration at High-Level Ministerial Session
excerpt_en: OUAGADOUGOU, Burkina Faso - November 26, 2025 - The Alliance of Sahel States (ESA) marked a major step forward in its regional integration project during an extensive ministerial coordination session that brought…
body_en:
OUAGADOUGOU, Burkina Faso - November 26, 2025 - The Alliance of Sahel States (ESA) marked a major step forward in its regional integration project during an extensive ministerial coordination session that brought together the foreign ministers of Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger. The meeting was chaired by Captain Ibrahim Traoré, President of Burkina Faso and current Chair of the ESA, and focused on accelerating the implementation of the confederation’s emerging institutional framework.

One of the most concrete outcomes of the session was the official signing of a memorandum of understanding establishing “ESA Confederation Radio.” The new media platform is envisioned as a strategic tool to counter what officials described as “external narrative dominance” and to strengthen cultural and information sovereignty across the Sahel.

Niger's Minister of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation, and Nigeriens Abroad, Bakary Yaou Sangaré, said the project represents “a sovereign information space enabling the Sahelian peoples to express their own aspirations for development without external mediation.”

On the sidelines of the ministerial session, Minister Sangaré held in-depth bilateral talks with Dr. Khosravinejad Akba, Special Envoy of the Iranian Foreign Minister. Their two-hour meeting focused on technical cooperation in areas such as energy infrastructure, agricultural technology transfer, and pharmaceutical production capacity. Discussions also explored Iranian investment opportunities in Niger’s renewable energy sector, signaling growing interest in diversified partnerships.

title: Niger Reactivates Decentralization Framework to Reinforce National Governance
excerpt: NIAMEY, Niger - November 27, 2025 - After a three-year hiatus, Niger has formally reactivated the Consultation Framework on Decentralization (CCD), reaffirming its central role in guiding local governance reforms.
title_en: Niger Reactivates Decentralization Framework to Reinforce National Governance
excerpt_en: NIAMEY, Niger - November 27, 2025 - After a three-year hiatus, Niger has formally reactivated the Consultation Framework on Decentralization (CCD), reaffirming its central role in guiding local governance reforms.
body_en:
NIAMEY, Niger - November 27, 2025 - After a three-year hiatus, Niger has formally reactivated the Consultation Framework on Decentralization (CCD), reaffirming its central role in guiding local governance reforms. The re-launch took place during a workshop at the Mahatma Gandhi International Conference Center, presided over by Major General Mohamed Toumba, Minister of State for the Interior, Public Security, and Territorial Administration. He was joined by Niamey Regional Governor Assoumane Abdou Harouna and Claudio Tognola, Head of Swiss Cooperation, representing international development partners.

Minister Toumba underscored the government’s strategic vision, noting that decentralization is “not simply an administrative reorganization, but a fundamental societal choice - a governance model that places communities at the heart of public action and national development.”

Technical sessions examined the status of the transfer of competences from central to local authorities, revealing that municipalities currently receive less than 2% of the national budget. Participants recommended a progressive increase to 5% by 2029, aligning the reform with WAEMU’s regional integration targets.

The revitalized reform agenda is organized around four priority pillars:

Clarifying the powers transferred between the central government and local entities.

Establishing sustainable financing mechanisms for local governance.

Reorganizing local planning and development processes.

Significantly strengthening the capacities of local authorities.

Sectoral ministers from Education, Health, Water Resources, and Environment presented detailed progress reports, highlighting advances made to date while acknowledging persistent structural challenges that continue to impede full implementation of the decentralization policy.

title_en: Niger and Italy Deepen Security Cooperation Through Strategic Institutional Dialogue
excerpt_en: NIAMEY, Niger - November 28, 2025 - The Director of the National Center for Strategic and Security Studies (CNESS), Colonel-Major Mahamadou Nouhou Bako, held a three-hour working session with Italy’s Ambassador to Niger, H.E.
body_en:
NIAMEY, Niger - November 28, 2025 - The Director of the National Center for Strategic and Security Studies (CNESS), Colonel-Major Mahamadou Nouhou Bako, held a three-hour working session with Italy’s Ambassador to Niger, H.E. Roberto Orlondo, aimed at advancing bilateral security cooperation and strengthening institutional partnerships.

The meeting outlined several concrete areas of collaboration, including plans to establish permanent communication channels between CNESS and Italy’s Center for Advanced Defense Studies (CASD). Both parties also explored modalities for CNESS to take part in Mediterranean security dialogue forums, extending Niger’s engagement beyond its traditional cooperation frameworks.

Colonel-Major Bako briefed the Italian delegation on the center’s ongoing transformation, emphasizing its ambition to evolve into a “center of excellence for strategic analysis and forward-looking security policy development.” Discussions also touched on shared security challenges-particularly maritime security issues affecting landlocked Sahelian countries and cybersecurity capacity building-reflecting Niger’s expanding partnerships with European nations outside the Francophone sphere.

title_en: WAEMU Coordination Drives Progress in Regional Economic Integration
excerpt_en: NIAMEY, Niger - November 25, 2025 - Prime Minister Ali Mahaman Lamine Zeine participated via secure videoconference in the first extraordinary session of the WAEMU Council of Ministers, held from the regional…
body_en:
NIAMEY, Niger - November 25, 2025 - Prime Minister Ali Mahaman Lamine Zeine participated via secure videoconference in the first extraordinary session of the WAEMU Council of Ministers, held from the regional headquarters of the BCEAO. The four-hour session focused on harmonizing macroeconomic policies, strengthening regional payment systems, and removing barriers to trade facilitation-underscoring Niger’s sustained commitment to West African economic cooperation, despite ongoing political tensions with ECOWAS.

Technical discussions centered on the implementation of the WAEMU Regional Economic Program 2021-2025. Prime Minister Zeine outlined Niger’s priorities, particularly the development of agricultural value chains and the improvement of cross-border infrastructure connectivity.

The session concluded with an agreement to speed up the operationalization of the regional food security reserve mechanism, a measure deemed essential for Sahelian member states facing recurring production instability.

title_en: Accelerating Strategic Development of the Mining Sector Through International Partnerships
excerpt_en: NIAMEY, Niger - Tuesday, November 25, 2025 - The Prime Minister chaired a high-level investment meeting with a delegation from the Dasa Mining Company (SOMIDA), accompanied by the Ministers of Mines and Justice.
body_en:
NIAMEY, Niger - Tuesday, November 25, 2025 - The Prime Minister chaired a high-level investment meeting with a delegation from the Dasa Mining Company (SOMIDA), accompanied by the Ministers of Mines and Justice. At the center of the discussions was a detailed technical review of the uranium mining project stretching between Tchirozérine and Arlit, with strong emphasis on environmental safeguards, community development commitments, and the reinforcement of local content policies.

The SOMIDA delegation-led by CEO Stephan Roman-presented revised project timelines and renewed investment commitments. These updates reflect the government’s broader strategic orientation: accelerating natural resource development through rebalanced partnership models that preserve national interests and ensure greater economic returns for Niger.

Talks culminated in concrete agreements on technology transfer, capacity-building, and workforce nationalization targets. The Minister of Justice underscored the need for strict adherence to contractual obligations, highlighting the importance of robust legal frameworks and effective dispute resolution mechanisms to secure long-term sector stability.

title: Comprehensive Review of the Food Security Partnership
excerpt: NIAMEY, Niger - Thursday, November 27, 2025 - The World Food Programme (WFP) held its annual comprehensive review of the Country Strategic Plan (2023-2025), under the chairmanship of the Minister Delegate for Budget, Mamane Sidi.
title_en: Comprehensive Review of the Food Security Partnership
excerpt_en: NIAMEY, Niger - Thursday, November 27, 2025 - The World Food Programme (WFP) held its annual comprehensive review of the Country Strategic Plan (2023-2025), under the chairmanship of the Minister Delegate for Budget, Mamane Sidi.
body_en:
NIAMEY, Niger - Thursday, November 27, 2025 - The World Food Programme (WFP) held its annual comprehensive review of the Country Strategic Plan (2023-2025), under the chairmanship of the Minister Delegate for Budget, Mamane Sidi. The one-day technical session highlighted major accomplishments, including support to more than 3.8 million beneficiaries through integrated resilience and emergency interventions, the provision of regular school meals to 380,000 children, and the ecological restoration of 300,000 hectares of degraded land.

WFP’s Country Director in Niger, Ms. Kinday Samba, presented a detailed economic analysis demonstrating that sustained investments in land rehabilitation could help the country avoid up to $9.7 billion in humanitarian expenditures by 2055. The review also marked the start of preliminary planning for the next strategic programming cycle (2027-2031), with a strong focus on aligning future interventions with the third pillar of the Republic Refounding Program, which prioritizes strengthening national production systems to advance food and economic sovereignty.

excerpt: NIAMEY, Niger - Wednesday, November 26 to Thursday, November 27, 2025 - Minister of Trade and Industry Abdoulaye Seydou personally led a sweeping 48-hour inspection campaign across service stations in the Niamey region.
title_en: Strengthening Domestic Energy Market Regulation Through Systematic Inspection Campaign
excerpt_en: NIAMEY, Niger - Wednesday, November 26 to Thursday, November 27, 2025 - Minister of Trade and Industry Abdoulaye Seydou personally led a sweeping 48-hour inspection campaign across service stations in the Niamey region.
body_en:
NIAMEY, Niger - Wednesday, November 26 to Thursday, November 27, 2025 - Minister of Trade and Industry Abdoulaye Seydou personally led a sweeping 48-hour inspection campaign across service stations in the Niamey region. The operation included detailed checks on safety compliance, fuel quality control, and price verification at thirteen stations, culminating in the immediate temporary closure of three facilities found to be in violation of national standards.

The Minister underscored that “market regulation is a fundamental function of national sovereignty, ensuring citizens access to essential goods under conditions of safety, affordability, and quality.” This initiative forms part of a broader government strategy to curb informal practices in the energy market and reinforce consumer protection. Similar inspection campaigns are scheduled to extend to regional capitals in the coming weeks.

title: Niger: Uranium Convoys Continue Amid High Tension
excerpt: NIAMEY, Niger - December 3, 2025 - The uranium sector in Niger remains at the center of escalating tensions following the departure of the first convoy from the SOMAÏR site in Arlit on November 27.
title_en: Niger: Uranium Convoys Continue Amid High Tension
excerpt_en: NIAMEY, Niger - December 3, 2025 - The uranium sector in Niger remains at the center of escalating tensions following the departure of the first convoy from the SOMAÏR site in Arlit on November 27.
body_en:
NIAMEY, Niger - December 3, 2025 - The uranium sector in Niger remains at the center of escalating tensions following the departure of the first convoy from the SOMAÏR site in Arlit on November 27. Despite warnings from Orano and prior ICSID rulings, multiple shipments have left northern Niger under heavy military escort, reflecting both the political sensitivity and strategic importance of the material.

Local sources reported that the first convoy traveled the Arlit-Agadez road before continuing to Tahoua, arriving in Abalak on December 1. The convoy was protected by Nigerien security units and accompanied by 31 Russian mercenaries, underscoring the high-risk nature of the transport.

In Niamey, President General Abdourahamane Tiani reaffirmed that the uranium belongs “to the Nigerien people” and that its export does not depend “on anyone’s authorization.” Government sources indicate that Niger is seeking a credible buyer to avoid involvement in nuclear proliferation.

Meanwhile, French company Orano denounced the convoy as “illegal,” claiming it had no knowledge of the cargo’s final destination and emphasizing that the ICSID ruling explicitly prohibited any transfer of uranium stockpiles from Arlit. Orano has reserved the right to pursue legal action, including prosecution.

On the night of December 3, 53 trucks belonging to MB TRANS, a company owned by Baye Mohamed, arrived in Niamey carrying uranium, while an additional 20 trucks owned by gold trader Saleh Boss were reportedly en route. These developments mark a decisive phase in the ongoing standoff over Niger’s uranium exports.

title: President Tiani Visits Saguia Amont Hydro-Agricultural Site
excerpt: NIAMEY, Niger - December 3, 2025 - President General Abdourahamane Tiani inspected the Saguia Amont hydro-agricultural development site near Niamey on Wednesday, highlighting ongoing efforts to boost local food…
title_en: President Tiani Visits Saguia Amont Hydro-Agricultural Site
excerpt_en: NIAMEY, Niger - December 3, 2025 - President General Abdourahamane Tiani inspected the Saguia Amont hydro-agricultural development site near Niamey on Wednesday, highlighting ongoing efforts to boost local food…
body_en:
NIAMEY, Niger - December 3, 2025 - President General Abdourahamane Tiani inspected the Saguia Amont hydro-agricultural development site near Niamey on Wednesday, highlighting ongoing efforts to boost local food production and support farmers.

Welcomed by the Minister of Agriculture and Livestock, the Governor of the Niamey Region, and the Director General of the National Office for Water and Sanitation (ONAH), the President met with 410 farmers to review the rehabilitation of the 105.29-hectare site.

The rehabilitation aims to increase rice yields from 6 to 9 tons per hectare. Works focused on upgrading the pumping system, which includes three pumps with a combined capacity of 540 m³ of water per hour, as well as reinforcing two sections of dikes, the pumping station shelter, 12 km of irrigation and drainage networks, access roads, and housing facilities.

Funded under the national Large-Scale Irrigation Program at a cost of 902,634,016 CFA francs (excluding taxes), the site is now fully operational. Initial estimates post-rehabilitation indicate an expected production of approximately 790 tons of paddy rice, up from 578 tons before the works, while reducing production costs per hectare from 190,000 to 135,558 CFA francs.

President Tiani also toured the rice silo and cooperative headquarters, engaging with producers about the varieties cultivated and the challenges faced. Established in 1973 with Libyan support, the Saguia Amont irrigation scheme remains a critical component of Niamey’s food security and agricultural development strategy, particularly for the city’s 5th district.

title: Strengthening the National Civil Registration System Through a Universal Birth Registration Campaign
excerpt: NIAMEY, Niger - Tuesday, November 25, 2025 - The government, through the Ministry of the Interior and in partnership with UNICEF, has officially launched an ambitious national universal birth registration campaign…
title_en: Strengthening the National Civil Registration System Through a Universal Birth Registration Campaign
excerpt_en: NIAMEY, Niger - Tuesday, November 25, 2025 - The government, through the Ministry of the Interior and in partnership with UNICEF, has officially launched an ambitious national universal birth registration campaign…
body_en:
NIAMEY, Niger - Tuesday, November 25, 2025 - The government, through the Ministry of the Interior and in partnership with UNICEF, has officially launched an ambitious national universal birth registration campaign during a high-level ceremony at the International Conference Center. The initiative seeks to address Niger’s persistently low rates of birth registration, especially in rural and border communities where fewer than 60 percent of children under five possess an official identity document.

The campaign introduces innovative mobile registration units, expanded community outreach mechanisms, and stronger integration with health facilities to ensure maximum coverage. The Ministry stressed that legal identity is “the key to accessing social services, education, and protection from exploitation,” a message with particular resonance for vulnerable children living in conflict-affected areas.

title_en: Implementation of a Comprehensive Strategy for Preventing Gender-Based Violence
excerpt_en: TAHOUA, Niger - Tuesday, November 25, 2025 - The national launch of the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence took place through coordinated ceremonies across multiple regions, underscoring the government’s…
body_en:
TAHOUA, Niger - Tuesday, November 25, 2025 - The national launch of the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence took place through coordinated ceremonies across multiple regions, underscoring the government’s commitment to an integrated, multisectoral strategy aimed at addressing systemic gender inequalities. In Tahoua, Governor Colonel-Major Souleymane Amadou Moussa presided over a major regional event that brought together traditional chiefs, religious leaders, women’s associations, and representatives of the defense and security forces.

The ceremony was highlighted by the inauguration of a new specialized support center for survivors, as well as the establishment of community monitoring committees dedicated to preventing early marriage and sexual violence. Meanwhile, in Tillabéri, Governor Lieutenant-Colonel Maina Boukar framed the campaign as a series of “patriotic actions” essential to national cohesion and development, integrating gender equality into the broader national refoundation agenda.

title_en: Improving the Quality of Education Through Sharing Best Practices
excerpt_en: NIAMEY, Niger - Friday, November 28, 2025 - The Ministry of National Education, Literacy, and the Promotion of National Languages opened a three-day workshop dedicated to sharing best practices from the “Sahel”…
body_en:
NIAMEY, Niger - Friday, November 28, 2025 - The Ministry of National Education, Literacy, and the Promotion of National Languages opened a three-day workshop dedicated to sharing best practices from the “Sahel” educational project at the Espace Soleil d’Afrique. Deputy Secretary General Alhaji Idi Abdou underscored the importance of professional learning communities for teachers, noting their essential role in improving educational outcomes despite persistent security challenges and limited resources.

Participants examined detailed case studies from the project’s implementation regions, which highlighted measurable progress in student retention and learning achievement through locally adapted teaching methodologies. Technical discussions focused on scaling up the most effective interventions and integrating digital learning tools to help mitigate teacher shortages in remote and hard-to-reach areas.

NIAMEY, Niger - Tuesday, November 25, 2025 - Ivorian journalist Serge Mathurin Adou was sentenced to two years in prison for “undermining state security” following publications considered threatening to Burkinabe military authorities. The case underscores increasing coordination among ESA member states in addressing cross-border information security and highlights their strict interpretation of national security laws amid ongoing counterterrorism operations.

Legal analysts note that the ruling reflects the transitional authorities’ efforts to balance press freedom with security imperatives, particularly concerning media coverage of military operations across borders. The case has drawn attention from international press freedom organizations, while government officials maintain that national security remains the overriding concern.

title: Niger-Agadez: 17th Aïr Festival Opens in Iférouane
excerpt: IFÉROUANE, Niger - December 5, 2025 - The 17th edition of the Aïr Festival was officially inaugurated in Iférouane, northern Niger, marking a major cultural milestone for the Sahel region.
title_en: Niger-Agadez: 17th Aïr Festival Opens in Iférouane
excerpt_en: IFÉROUANE, Niger - December 5, 2025 - The 17th edition of the Aïr Festival was officially inaugurated in Iférouane, northern Niger, marking a major cultural milestone for the Sahel region.
body_en:
IFÉROUANE, Niger - December 5, 2025 - The 17th edition of the Aïr Festival was officially inaugurated in Iférouane, northern Niger, marking a major cultural milestone for the Sahel region. The event was opened by Prime Minister and Minister of Economy and Finance, His Excellency Ali Mahamane Lamine Zeine, and attracted participants from across the Sahel.

The ceremony saw the presence of several high-ranking regional officials, including the Prime Minister of Chad, the Burkinabe Prime Minister, and Mali’s Minister of Tourism representing their head of government. Their attendance highlights the festival’s growing regional significance.

Numerous civilian and military dignitaries were also in attendance, including members of Niger’s CNSP (National Committee for the Salvation of the People) and Major General Ibra Boulama Issa, Governor of the Agadez region. Local administrative and traditional authorities actively participated, adding to the event’s prestige and celebratory atmosphere.

This year’s Aïr Festival promises a rich showcase of cultural heritage, traditions, and artistic expression, reaffirming its status as a premier platform for celebrating the Sahel’s diverse cultural identity.

excerpt: Lamu, Kenya - December 2, 2025 - The Director General of the Agadez Urban Municipality, Battalion Commander Assarid Almoustapha, accompanied by the curator of the historic center, Mr.
title_en: Niger-Agadez: Advocating for African Urban Heritage at Lamu Workshop
excerpt_en: Lamu, Kenya - December 2, 2025 - The Director General of the Agadez Urban Municipality, Battalion Commander Assarid Almoustapha, accompanied by the curator of the historic center, Mr.
body_en:
Lamu, Kenya - December 2, 2025 - The Director General of the Agadez Urban Municipality, Battalion Commander Assarid Almoustapha, accompanied by the curator of the historic center, Mr. Ali Salifou, represented Agadez at an international workshop organized by the Organization of World Heritage Cities (OWHC). The workshop gathered managers of African UNESCO World Heritage sites to discuss urban preservation challenges and prepare a collaborative project for the 18th OWHC World Congress in Marrakech in 2026.

During the session, the Agadez delegation highlighted major issues facing the city, including financial constraints, climate change impacts, population pressure, declining tourism, and the deterioration of historic buildings. Concrete actions were proposed, such as raising community awareness, restoring heritage sites, finalizing urban development plans, and mobilizing necessary funding.

A field visit to Lamu’s historic sites allowed participants to observe successful rehabilitation efforts, reinforcing Agadez’s commitment to adapting sustainable practices to its own heritage context.

Concluding the workshop, the Director General made key commitments: adherence to the OWHC urban project, application for active membership by the end of 2025, and advocacy for increased international technical and financial support. A platform for ongoing cooperation among African heritage cities is also planned to facilitate knowledge exchange and collaborative preservation efforts.

title: Niger Strengthens Protection for Journalists and Combats Disinformation
excerpt: Niamey, November 30, 2025 - On the eve of National Press Freedom Day, Minister of Communication Adji Ali Salatou emphasized Niger’s commitment to protecting journalists and fighting disinformation amid a challenging…
title_en: Niger Strengthens Protection for Journalists and Combats Disinformation
excerpt_en: Niamey, November 30, 2025 - On the eve of National Press Freedom Day, Minister of Communication Adji Ali Salatou emphasized Niger’s commitment to protecting journalists and fighting disinformation amid a challenging…
body_en:
Niamey, November 30, 2025 - On the eve of National Press Freedom Day, Minister of Communication Adji Ali Salatou emphasized Niger’s commitment to protecting journalists and fighting disinformation amid a challenging security and geopolitical context.

Minister Salatou warned of a “communication war” orchestrated by certain foreign powers, while reaffirming that press freedom is a legally guaranteed right, to be exercised responsibly and with respect for citizens. “The freedom of journalists ends where that of citizens begins,” he stressed, highlighting the delicate balance between transparency and public safety.

Acknowledging the difficult conditions under which journalists operate, the Minister underscored the State’s pledge to ensure their safety. He also pointed to the growing challenge posed by social media and the rapid spread of disinformation, noting recent measures to strengthen the sector, including a 90% reduction in media tax debt, the establishment of the National Communication Observatory, and a simplified tax regime for media organizations.

Looking ahead, the government intends to further professionalize the media sector through training, improved access to public information, and the promotion of journalistic ethics. Minister Salatou concluded by calling for information to serve as a tool for peace and national progress.

title: Political Detentions in Niger Draw International Attention
excerpt: NIAMEY, Niger - Wednesday, November 26, 2025 - Former President Mohamed Bazoum and his wife Khadija Bazoum have now been in detention for over 865 days, prompting their children to launch an international advocacy…
title_en: Political Detentions in Niger Draw International Attention
excerpt_en: NIAMEY, Niger - Wednesday, November 26, 2025 - Former President Mohamed Bazoum and his wife Khadija Bazoum have now been in detention for over 865 days, prompting their children to launch an international advocacy…
body_en:
NIAMEY, Niger - Wednesday, November 26, 2025 - Former President Mohamed Bazoum and his wife Khadija Bazoum have now been in detention for over 865 days, prompting their children to launch an international advocacy campaign calling for their release. The prolonged detention has become a focal point of concern for Niger’s international partners, particularly European countries and regional organizations.

The government maintains that the detentions are linked to ongoing legal proceedings. However, international human rights organizations increasingly describe the situation as arbitrary detention. Authorities continue to emphasize national judicial sovereignty while facing persistent calls for a resolution through political dialogue.

title: Niger Plans Legal Action Against Orano After Discovery of Radioactive Barrels
excerpt: Niamey, December 2, 2025 - The Nigerien government announced its intention to sue the French mining group Orano following the discovery of 400 barrels containing radioactive core samples in Madaouela, northern Niger.
title_en: Niger Plans Legal Action Against Orano After Discovery of Radioactive Barrels
excerpt_en: Niamey, December 2, 2025 - The Nigerien government announced its intention to sue the French mining group Orano following the discovery of 400 barrels containing radioactive core samples in Madaouela, northern Niger.
body_en:
Niamey, December 2, 2025 - The Nigerien government announced its intention to sue the French mining group Orano following the discovery of 400 barrels containing radioactive core samples in Madaouela, northern Niger.

Speaking at a press conference, Minister of Justice Alio Daouda condemned Orano, describing the company as a “predator that has lost its prey” and criticizing its historical handling of Niger’s uranium sector. “Several million tons of radioactive waste were left exposed to the open air,” the Minister said.

Measurements of the barrels revealed radiation levels between 7 and 10 microsieverts per hour-far exceeding the 0.5 microsievert safety standard. The samples reportedly contain bismuth-207 and chromium X, highly toxic substances capable of contaminating anyone within a 10-meter radius, prompting serious environmental, health, and social concerns.

The Minister emphasized that Niger’s nationalization of its uranium sector in December 2024 and the discovery of the barrels represent a clear breach of responsibility by Orano. The government plans to seek full compensation for damages.

Orano, which has denied involvement in the controversial convoy of uranium, stated it is prepared to take legal measures, including criminal proceedings, to defend its rights. The incident also reportedly violates an ICSID arbitration ruling from September 2025, which prohibited Niger from selling or transferring uranium produced by SOMAIR.

title: ONC Outlines Strategic Reforms to Modernize Media and Protect Journalists
excerpt: Niamey, November 30, 2025 - On National Press Freedom Day, Ibrahim Manzo Diallo, President of the National Communication Observatory (ONC), presented the institution’s new guidelines aimed at modernizing media…
title_en: ONC Outlines Strategic Reforms to Modernize Media and Protect Journalists
excerpt_en: Niamey, November 30, 2025 - On National Press Freedom Day, Ibrahim Manzo Diallo, President of the National Communication Observatory (ONC), presented the institution’s new guidelines aimed at modernizing media…
body_en:
Niamey, November 30, 2025 - On National Press Freedom Day, Ibrahim Manzo Diallo, President of the National Communication Observatory (ONC), presented the institution’s new guidelines aimed at modernizing media regulation and strengthening journalist protection in Niger.

Speaking on Télé Sahel, Diallo highlighted three main reform areas. First, the internal reorganization of the ONC seeks to create a fully operational, modern, and credible regulatory framework capable of addressing the evolving challenges of Niger’s media landscape.

The second focus is on “cleaning up” the media sector by ensuring that public, private, and online outlets operate in compliance with existing regulations. Diallo stressed that the initiative is not intended to restrict media freedom but to promote professionalism, order, and ethical standards.

Finally, the ONC plans to reinforce legal protections for journalists, establish mechanisms for dialogue, and prevent abuses. Special attention will be given to digital media regulation, which Diallo described as “essential” in today’s information environment.

Diallo expressed confidence in the reform process, noting that the ONC is guided by individuals committed to maintaining a responsible media landscape, which he believes will ensure the success of these initiatives.

title: A Year of Injustice: Moussa Tchangari, Symbol of a Silenced Civil Society
excerpt: Niamey, December 3, 2025 - One year ago today, Moussa Tchangari was arrested in Niamey by armed men without a warrant.
title_en: A Year of Injustice: Moussa Tchangari, Symbol of a Silenced Civil Society
excerpt_en: Niamey, December 3, 2025 - One year ago today, Moussa Tchangari was arrested in Niamey by armed men without a warrant.
body_en:
Niamey, December 3, 2025 - One year ago today, Moussa Tchangari was arrested in Niamey by armed men without a warrant.

Since then, the Secretary General of Alternative Espaces Citoyens, a respected and steadfast figure in Nigerien civil society, remains imprisoned in Filingué Prison. Accused of “apology for terrorism” and “undermining national defense,” he has only been questioned twice in ten months, while international organizations such as Amnesty International, the FIDH, and several UN experts denounce his arbitrary and politically motivated detention.

Moussa Tchangari is not unknown. For decades, he has defended human rights, social justice, and the dignity of Nigeriens under all regimes, never yielding to fear or pressure. His career demonstrates remarkable consistency: denouncing abuses, protecting the most vulnerable, and reminding the authorities of their obligations to the people. Today, this commitment has earned him imprisonment, even though he has simply been exercising his role as a vigilant citizen.

Under the transition led by General Abdourahamane Tiani, critical voices appear to have become the primary targets. The government relentlessly attacks men and women recognized for their integrity and civic engagement, while those who plunge the country into insecurity or anarchy benefit from astonishing leniency. This reversal of priorities creates a disturbing climate of arbitrariness, where loyalty to the nation is paradoxically rewarded with prison.

The prolonged imprisonment of Moussa Tchangari illustrates the excesses of a regime that conflates dissent with threats, criticism with treason. By targeting human rights activists rather than actual criminals, the authorities are undermining not only the rule of law but also the trust of the Nigerien people. The immediate and unconditional release of Moussa Tchangari remains, now more than ever, a demand for justice and a democratic imperative.

title: Asymmetric Attacks Highlight Persistent Security Challenges in Tillaberi
excerpt: TILLABERI, Niger - Thursday, November 27, 2025 - Nigerien defense and security forces continue to face sophisticated asymmetric attacks, despite strengthened counterterrorism measures.
title_en: Asymmetric Attacks Highlight Persistent Security Challenges in Tillaberi
excerpt_en: TILLABERI, Niger - Thursday, November 27, 2025 - Nigerien defense and security forces continue to face sophisticated asymmetric attacks, despite strengthened counterterrorism measures.
body_en:
TILLABERI, Niger - Thursday, November 27, 2025 - Nigerien defense and security forces continue to face sophisticated asymmetric attacks, despite strengthened counterterrorism measures. On Thursday, an improvised explosive device struck a military convoy between Torodi and Makalondi, killing four personnel and injuring several others. Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) claimed responsibility for the attack, releasing images through its propaganda channels as part of an information warfare campaign.

This incident follows a complex ambush on Monday, November 24, targeting five military vehicles on the strategic Niamey-Téra road. While security forces have improved their tactical response, successfully minimizing casualties through effective counter-maneuvers, these attacks underscore the ongoing challenges of securing rural transport routes in the region.

Participants stressed the need to balance operational security with the public’s right to accurate information in counterinsurgency operations.

NIAMEY, Niger - Friday, November 28, 2025 - Following the National Community Radio Forum for Inclusive and Responsible Communication (November 25-27, 2025), senior military officials convened with community radio leaders and municipal administrators for a one-day coordination session. The discussions led to the establishment of framework agreements on security alert protocols, the creation of counter-narratives, and standards for responsible crisis reporting.

title: Niger: New Wave of Displacement Hits Téra Amid Rising Insecurity
excerpt: Téra, November 24, 2025 - The commune of Téra in western Niger is facing a fresh wave of displacement, as residents flee escalating threats from armed groups in the surrounding areas.
title_en: Niger: New Wave of Displacement Hits Téra Amid Rising Insecurity
excerpt_en: Téra, November 24, 2025 - The commune of Téra in western Niger is facing a fresh wave of displacement, as residents flee escalating threats from armed groups in the surrounding areas.
body_en:
Téra, November 24, 2025 - The commune of Téra in western Niger is facing a fresh wave of displacement, as residents flee escalating threats from armed groups in the surrounding areas. Already hosting over 50,000 displaced individuals, the town is now struggling to accommodate new arrivals from villages south of the Téra department.

Local sources report that fighters from Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) issued urgent evacuation orders for approximately thirty villages in the Diagourou area, located just ten kilometers from Téra. This region, part of the sensitive “three borders” zone between Niger, Mali, and Burkina Faso, is increasingly targeted by JNIM and Islamic State in the Sahel (ISIS) attacks.

The forced departures have resulted in a massive influx toward Téra, a strategic military hub housing Defense Zone No. 9. Displaced families are living in precarious conditions: many are sleeping outdoors or on undeveloped land, while others are accommodated by local families who are themselves struggling with limited resources.

While exact figures remain unclear, the humanitarian situation is worsening in one of western Niger’s most fragile regions, raising urgent concerns over shelter, food, and basic services for the newly displaced populations.

title: Mr. Moli Hamit, a Toubou trader in Tabarakaten, was violently abducted in broad daylight by a group
excerpt: Mr. Moli Hamit, a Toubou trader in Tabarakaten, was violently abducted in broad daylight by a group of foreigners and taken to an unknown location.
title_en: Mr. Moli Hamit, a Toubou trader in Tabarakaten, was violently abducted in broad daylight by a group
excerpt_en: Mr. Moli Hamit, a Toubou trader in Tabarakaten, was violently abducted in broad daylight by a group of foreigners and taken to an unknown location.
body_en:
Mr. Moli Hamit, a Toubou trader in Tabarakaten, was violently abducted in broad daylight by a group of foreigners and taken to an unknown location. Despite alerts from friends, the local Defense and Security Forces (FDS) did not initiate a search.

Hoping for his safe return, Mr. Hamit’s family reached out to a committee allegedly linked to the kidnappers. Initially promising assistance, the committee ultimately declared itself unable to act. According to unconfirmed sources, Mr. Hamit was reportedly executed, apparently solely due to his ethnic affiliation with the presumed perpetrator.

The situation worsened when, on December 2, 2025, a video surfaced showing the kidnappers brandishing weapons and threatening an entire community. Social media users close to the criminal networks circulated claims accusing the Nigerien army of complicity in Mr. Hamit’s death.

The incident underscores the growing insecurity in northern Niger, where the region’s gold wealth, particularly in Djado and Tabarakaten, has attracted both opportunistic criminal networks and rising ethnic tensions, severely threatening local stability.

Niamey, December 4, 2025 - At least six civilians were killed in Ouro Gueladio, just 30 km from Niamey, in an attack attributed to JNIM, which also left an undetermined number of wounded and missing. This incident marks a further deterioration of the security situation around Niger's capital.

In an official statement, the administrator of the rural commune of Ouro Gueladio offered his condolences to the entire local population, condemning an attack he described as “heinous and barbaric” against peaceful citizens returning from the Youri market.

The administrator prayed for the souls of the victims, asking God to welcome them into Paradise, and wished a speedy recovery to those seriously injured in the attack. He also called on residents to strengthen their collaboration with the Defense and Security Forces, and to scrupulously respect the instructions given, in order to contribute to the protection of the municipality against persistent threats.

title: Niger-Filingué: Two School Principals Murdered and Another Deadly Incursion
excerpt: December 4, 2025 - Two school principals from the Filingué Education Inspectorate were murdered this morning by members of the Islamic State in the Greater Sahara (ISGS).
title_en: Niger-Filingué: Two School Principals Murdered and Another Deadly Incursion
excerpt_en: December 4, 2025 - Two school principals from the Filingué Education Inspectorate were murdered this morning by members of the Islamic State in the Greater Sahara (ISGS).
body_en:
December 4, 2025 - Two school principals from the Filingué Education Inspectorate were murdered this morning by members of the Islamic State in the Greater Sahara (ISGS). The victims, known for their courage and competence, were on their way to the General Assembly of the Federal Council of Commissioners (FCC) in Filingué when they were coldly targeted. Among them was Mr. Abdoulaye Askou, also known as Baba Tandja.

A few hours later, between 10:00 and 11:00 a.m., another terrorist incursion struck the region, this time the village of Maïtalakia. The assailants killed the village chief's son, sowing terror among the inhabitants. During their retreat, the same assailants intercepted and executed the son of the village chief of Sabon Gari, near Toukounous, a locality known as the birthplace of General Tiani.

These attacks demonstrate the continued deadly incursions in the Tillabéri region. Local authorities and security forces are now on high alert to prevent further attacks and protect the exposed civilian population.

excerpt_en: December 4, 2025 - Nighttime clashes erupted Thursday evening in Sella Illimiki, a town south of Bankilaré in the Tillabéri region.

December 4, 2025 - Nighttime clashes erupted Thursday evening in Sella Illimiki, a town south of Bankilaré in the Tillabéri region. According to local sources, self-defense militias, arriving on horseback from the village of Tara (Kokorou commune), stormed the town around 10 p.m., triggering fierce fighting with residents. The hostilities lasted much of the night, resulting in a significant provisional death toll. At least two people were killed, including a militiaman and a villager, and several others were wounded, both civilians and militiamen.

The violence of these clashes reflects the persistent communal tensions in this region, where local rivalries can quickly escalate into deadly incidents. Local authorities remain on high alert and are trying to intervene to restore calm, but the situation remains extremely tense and worrying for the population.
