title: Burkina Faso, EU Review Partnership Actions and Priorities
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 7, 2025 - Senior members of the Burkinabe government on Friday met with a delegation from the European Union and its Member States to review progress under their multilateral partnership and align…
title_en: Burkina Faso, EU Review Partnership Actions and Priorities
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 7, 2025 - Senior members of the Burkinabe government on Friday met with a delegation from the European Union and its Member States to review progress under their multilateral partnership and align…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 7, 2025 - Senior members of the Burkinabe government on Friday met with a delegation from the European Union and its Member States to review progress under their multilateral partnership and align future cooperation with Burkina Faso’s national priorities.

The government delegation was led by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation and Burkinabe Abroad, H.E. Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, alongside the Minister of Security, Divisional Police Commissioner Mahamadou Sana; the Minister of Economy and Finance, Dr. Aboubacar Nacanabo; and the Minister Delegate for Regional Cooperation, Ms. Stella Eldine Kabre/Kaboré. The talks took place on the afternoon of Friday, December 5, in Ouagadougou.

Discussions focused on assessing actions undertaken by the EU delegation to Burkina Faso, measuring progress on existing commitments, and ensuring coherence with government priorities outlined in the Stabilization and Development Action Plan (SDA) 2021-2025.

Chairing the meeting, Minister Traoré said the partnership with the European Union has produced tangible results in key sectors, notably governance, inclusive human development, and community and humanitarian resilience. However, he stressed that major challenges persist, including securing the national territory, restoring state authority, strengthening the resilience of vulnerable communities, and accelerating infrastructure development.

He called for a convergence of visions between Burkina Faso and its European partners to translate shared ambitions into concrete actions, grounded in transparency, mutual trust, and efficiency, in order to support the emergence of a peaceful, resilient, and prosperous country.

The Head of the EU Delegation to Burkina Faso, Ambassador Philippe Bronchain, welcomed the dialogue and reaffirmed the European Union’s commitment to continued engagement with its Sahel partners, particularly Burkina Faso, within a framework of mutually beneficial cooperation.

According to Ambassador Bronchain, the consultations also served as a platform to address differences, with the aim of defining improved prospects for cooperation in socio-economic development, the fight against terrorism and criminal networks, and migration management, while upholding the principles of equality, human values, and mutual respect.

He called for a convergence of visions between Burkina Faso and its European partners to translate shared ambitions into concrete actions, grounded in transparency, mutual trust, and efficiency, in order to support the emergence of a peaceful, resilient, and prosperous country.

The Head of the EU Delegation to Burkina Faso, Ambassador Philippe Bronchain, welcomed the dialogue and reaffirmed the European Union’s commitment to continued engagement with its Sahel partners, particularly Burkina Faso, within a framework of mutually beneficial cooperation.

According to Ambassador Bronchain, the consultations also served as a platform to address differences, with the aim of defining improved prospects for cooperation in socio-economic development, the fight against terrorism and criminal networks, and migration management, while upholding the principles of equality, human values, and mutual respect.

title: SP-APRM Hosts Governance and Sovereignty Roundtable at ENAM

title_en: SP-APRM Hosts Governance and Sovereignty Roundtable at ENAM
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 8, 2025 - The Permanent Secretariat of the African Peer Review Mechanism (SP-APRM) on Saturday held a roundtable discussion on governance, sovereignty, and endogenous development for students of…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 8, 2025 - The Permanent Secretariat of the African Peer Review Mechanism (SP-APRM) on Saturday held a roundtable discussion on governance, sovereignty, and endogenous development for students of the National School of Administration and Magistracy (ENAM), as part of efforts to promote good governance values among future public administrators.

The event took place on Saturday, December 6, and aimed to strengthen trainees’ understanding of the African Peer Review Mechanism (APRM), while raising awareness of the principles of sound political, economic, and social governance, as well as probity and integrity in public service.

The roundtable featured three thematic presentations. An initial session led by the SP-APRM focused on clarifying the institution’s mandate and core activities. Two additional presentations examined issues related to governance, national sovereignty, and endogenous development models.

The opening session was chaired by Ambassador Seydou Sinka, Special Advisor to the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation and Burkinabè Abroad, in the presence of Dr. Jacob Yarassoula Yarabatioula, Director General of ENAM, and Mr. Brahima Ouedraogo, Secretary General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Agricultural Development (MPAD).

In his opening remarks, Ambassador Sinka recalled the process that led to the establishment of Burkina Faso’s self-assessment and governance monitoring mechanism under the APRM framework. He underscored the importance of the mechanism, describing it as a tool designed to “stimulate and promote political, economic, social, and entrepreneurial development based on endogenous values.”

He further noted that the initiative seeks to deepen understanding of the APRM process and to help define the contours of a new vision for development governance rooted in national values and priorities.

According to the Special Advisor, the relevance of the roundtable lies in its contribution to shaping future leaders of the Burkinabe public administration, by instilling a strong sense of responsibility and integrity, and by fostering greater awareness of issues related to sovereignty and good governance.

title: Burkina Faso Ambassador Presents Credentials to Philippine President
excerpt: Manila, December 8, 2025 - Burkina Faso’s newly appointed Ambassador to the Republic of the Philippines, H.E. Ms.
title_en: Burkina Faso Ambassador Presents Credentials to Philippine President
excerpt_en: Manila, December 8, 2025 - Burkina Faso’s newly appointed Ambassador to the Republic of the Philippines, H.E. Ms.
body_en:
Manila, December 8, 2025 - Burkina Faso’s newly appointed Ambassador to the Republic of the Philippines, H.E. Ms. Bibata NEBIE/OUEDRAOGO, has officially assumed her duties after presenting her credentials to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in Manila.

The formal ceremony took place on November 25 at the Malacañan Presidential Palace, marking the beginning of her mandate as Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Burkina Faso to the Philippines. Ambassador NEBIE/OUEDRAOGO is based in Tokyo, Japan, where she holds concurrent accreditation.

A day earlier, on Monday, November 24, 2025, the Burkinabe diplomat had presented her credentials to Mr. Ariel Rodelas Peñaranda, Deputy Secretary and Chief of Protocol at the Philippine Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

According to official sources, the two credential ceremonies provided an opportunity for exchanges between the Ambassador and Philippine authorities on ways to strengthen ties of friendship and cooperation between Burkina Faso and the Republic of the Philippines.

The discussions focused on prospects for enhanced bilateral relations, reflecting the shared commitment of both countries to deepen diplomatic engagement and explore new avenues of cooperation.

title: AES Condemns Unauthorized Nigerian Military Aircraft Overflight
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 8, 2025 - The Confederation of Sahel States (AES) has strongly condemned what it described as a violation of its confederal airspace after a Nigerian Air Force C-130 aircraft was forced to land in…
title_en: AES Condemns Unauthorized Nigerian Military Aircraft Overflight
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 8, 2025 - The Confederation of Sahel States (AES) has strongly condemned what it described as a violation of its confederal airspace after a Nigerian Air Force C-130 aircraft was forced to land in…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 8, 2025 - The Confederation of Sahel States (AES) has strongly condemned what it described as a violation of its confederal airspace after a Nigerian Air Force C-130 aircraft was forced to land in Bobo-Dioulasso, western Burkina Faso, on Monday following an in-flight emergency.

In a press release issued the same day, the AES said the military aircraft, which was carrying two crew members and nine passengers, all military personnel, had been operating in Burkinabe airspace without authorization.

According to the statement, an investigation was immediately opened by the competent Burkinabe authorities after the aircraft’s landing. Preliminary findings established that the plane did not have clearance to overfly Burkina Faso, prompting the Confederation to denounce the incident as a breach of sovereignty.

“The Confederation of Sahel States condemns in the strongest possible terms this violation of its airspace and the sovereignty of its member states,” the statement said.

The AES further described the incident as a hostile act carried out in violation of international law and international civil and military aviation regulations. It added that measures are being taken to ensure the security of confederal airspace, safeguard the sovereignty and territorial integrity of member states, and protect civilian populations.

Acting on instructions from the Heads of State, the AES announced that its air and anti-aircraft defense forces have been placed on maximum alert, in line with the Declaration of the College of Heads of State of December 22, 2024.

Under these directives, AES defense forces are now authorized to neutralize any aircraft found violating the Confederation’s airspace, the statement warned.

title_en: Burkina Faso Ambassador Presents Credentials to Greek President
excerpt_en: Athens, December 9, 2025 - H.E. Ms. Cyrile GANOU/BADOLO, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Burkina Faso to the Hellenic Republic, has officially presented her credentials to President Konstantinos…
body_en:
Athens, December 9, 2025 - H.E. Ms. Cyrile GANOU/BADOLO, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Burkina Faso to the Hellenic Republic, has officially presented her credentials to President Konstantinos Tassoulas of Greece, marking the formal start of her diplomatic mission.

The credential ceremony was held on November 18, 2025, at the Presidential Palace in Athens. During the event, Ambassador GANOU/BADOLO conveyed fraternal greetings from President Ibrahim Traoré of Burkina Faso, as well as from the Burkinabè people, to the Greek head of state and the people of Greece.

In her remarks, the Ambassador highlighted the Burkinabe government’s ongoing efforts to restore national territorial integrity. She also presented Burkina Faso’s economic and cultural potential, underscoring investment and business opportunities available in the country. Ambassador GANOU/BADOLO reaffirmed the authorities’ commitment to diversifying international partnerships, strengthening national sovereignty, and promoting balanced and respectful cooperation aimed at sustainable development.

President Tassoulas welcomed the Ambassador and expressed Greece’s willingness to deepen bilateral relations with Burkina Faso. He identified energy, water resources, infrastructure, and agriculture as priority sectors for enhanced cooperation between the two countries.

It was also noted that on the previous day, Ambassador GANOU/BADOLO had presented copies of her credentials to the Chief of State Protocol at the Greek Ministry of Foreign Affairs, in accordance with diplomatic protocol.

title: Burkina Faso, Morocco Sign 12 Agreements to Deepen Bilateral Cooperation
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 10, 2025 - Burkina Faso and the Kingdom of Morocco have signed 12 new cooperation agreements aimed at strengthening long-standing bilateral relations, following the fifth session of their Joint…
title_en: Burkina Faso, Morocco Sign 12 Agreements to Deepen Bilateral Cooperation
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 10, 2025 - Burkina Faso and the Kingdom of Morocco have signed 12 new cooperation agreements aimed at strengthening long-standing bilateral relations, following the fifth session of their Joint…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 10, 2025 - Burkina Faso and the Kingdom of Morocco have signed 12 new cooperation agreements aimed at strengthening long-standing bilateral relations, following the fifth session of their Joint Commission on Bilateral Cooperation held in Ouagadougou on Wednesday.

The ministerial meeting was co-chaired by Burkina Faso’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, H.E. Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, and Morocco’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, African Cooperation and Moroccans Abroad, H.E. Nasser Bourita. It concluded with the adoption of the session’s minutes, a joint communiqué, and the signing of multiple cooperation instruments.

Among the agreements is a deal on the reciprocal recognition of national driver’s licenses, as well as three cooperation agreements covering labor, security, and civil protection. Six memoranda of understanding were also signed in the fields of agriculture, trade, youth, housing and urban planning, and the exchange of expertise in security and road infrastructure.

In addition, the two sides initialed a framework agreement on scholarships, internships, and the sharing of expertise, along with another framework agreement focused on vocational training.

The holding of the joint commission reflects the shared commitment of President Ibrahim Traoré of Burkina Faso and King Mohammed VI of Morocco to consolidating six decades of friendship and fraternity between the two nations.

“This meeting underscores the strength and depth of the ties that unite our two countries, founded on fraternity, solidarity, mutual respect, and fruitful cooperation,” Minister Bourita said, reaffirming Morocco’s solidarity with Burkina Faso and its support for efforts to preserve territorial integrity, sovereignty, and national security.

For his part, Minister Traoré described the meeting as a concrete expression of South-South cooperation centered on shared development and the affirmation of sovereignty. He praised Morocco’s role in promoting peace and stability, particularly in the Sahel, and highlighted Rabat’s support for the Sahelian Confederation.

The Burkinabe foreign minister expressed hope that the Ouagadougou meeting would accelerate the implementation of commitments made by both parties. The fifth session follows expert-level talks held last October in Ouagadougou. The sixth session of the Joint Commission is scheduled for 2027 in Morocco.

title: Burkina Faso Ambassador Presents Credentials to Cuban President
excerpt: Havana, December 11, 2025 - H.E. Manignan Roxane Adams Medah, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Burkina Faso to the Republic of Cuba, officially assumed her duties on Saturday, December 6, after presenting…
title_en: Burkina Faso Ambassador Presents Credentials to Cuban President
excerpt_en: Havana, December 11, 2025 - H.E. Manignan Roxane Adams Medah, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Burkina Faso to the Republic of Cuba, officially assumed her duties on Saturday, December 6, after presenting…
body_en:
Havana, December 11, 2025 - H.E. Manignan Roxane Adams Medah, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Burkina Faso to the Republic of Cuba, officially assumed her duties on Saturday, December 6, after presenting her credentials to President Miguel Díaz-Canel.

The ceremony took place at the Havana Convention Center, marking a new phase in diplomatic relations between the two countries.

During subsequent discussions, Ambassador Medah conveyed the greetings of President Ibrahim Traoré of Burkina Faso to his Cuban counterpart. President Díaz-Canel expressed gratitude for Burkina Faso’s continued support for Cuba, which has faced a long-standing economic, commercial, and financial blockade imposed by the United States since 1962.

Ambassador Medah stated that, under instructions from the Burkinabe head of state, this support would be reinforced and a renewed momentum given to bilateral cooperation. While current cooperation focuses mainly on health and higher education, she noted that collaboration would be expanded into additional sectors in the coming years.

Following the ceremony, the Ambassador laid a wreath at the José Martí Memorial, honoring Cuba’s national hero and a central figure in the country’s struggle for independence. This year marks the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Burkina Faso and Cuba.

Burkina Faso’s embassy in Havana, opened in 1984, is accredited to approximately 20 countries.

title: Burkina Faso Hosts Second Press and Diplomacy Day to Engage Media on Foreign Policy Challenges
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 12, 2025 - The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation and the Burkinabè Diaspora on Friday held the second edition of Press and Diplomacy Day, aimed at strengthening journalists’…
title_en: Burkina Faso Hosts Second Press and Diplomacy Day to Engage Media on Foreign Policy Challenges
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 12, 2025 - The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation and the Burkinabè Diaspora on Friday held the second edition of Press and Diplomacy Day, aimed at strengthening journalists’…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 12, 2025 - The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation and the Burkinabè Diaspora on Friday held the second edition of Press and Diplomacy Day, aimed at strengthening journalists’ understanding of the strategic challenges and choices shaping Burkina Faso’s diplomacy.

Organized through the Directorate of Communication and Press Relations (DCRP), the event brought together media professionals in Ouagadougou to discuss key diplomatic issues in a context marked by security challenges and shifting geopolitical alignments.

The opening ceremony was presided over by the Secretary General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Yiriguoin Hermann Toe, who underscored the central role of the media in explaining and contextualizing the country’s diplomatic orientation.

The discussions focused on several themes, including the dynamics and prospects of the AES, the outcomes of efforts to diversify Burkina Faso’s international partners, and the role of the Burkinabè diaspora in national development. According to organizers, these exchanges were intended to help journalists better grasp the diplomatic implications of political decisions taken to assert national sovereignty and preserve the dignity of the population.

“For these choices to be accepted, information must be accurate, clear, and accessible. That is the true nobility of your mission as journalists,” Ambassador Toe said in his opening address.

He added that the objective of the initiative is to help foster “an informed, lucid, and constructive public opinion,” which he described as essential to the country’s transformation, in line with the vision of President Ibrahim Traoré.

For her part, Ms. Wendata Nathalie Kaoré, Director of Communication and Press Relations, said the Press and Diplomacy Day also serves as a platform to strengthen cooperation between diplomatic actors and the national media. She expressed hope that the exchanges would encourage greater media engagement in supporting the ministry’s diplomatic actions.

The second edition of the event was also marked by direct exchanges between the Minister of Foreign Affairs, H.E. Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, and journalists, providing an opportunity for open dialogue on Burkina Faso’s foreign policy priorities.

title: Burkina Faso Foreign Minister Holds Dialogue with Journalists on Diplomatic Priorities
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 13, 2025 - Burkina Faso’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation and Burkinabè Abroad, H.E.
title_en: Burkina Faso Foreign Minister Holds Dialogue with Journalists on Diplomatic Priorities
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 13, 2025 - Burkina Faso’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation and Burkinabè Abroad, H.E.
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 13, 2025 - Burkina Faso’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation and Burkinabè Abroad, H.E. Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, on Friday held an extensive exchange with media professionals as part of the second edition of Press Day - Diplomacy.

The meeting, which took place on December 12, brought together around 20 Burkinabè journalists for an open discussion on key foreign policy issues, including bilateral and multilateral cooperation, regional integration, and the mobilization of the Burkinabè diaspora.

According to participants, the discussions focused on Burkina Faso’s overall diplomatic orientation, the challenges and prospects of the AES Confederation, evolving cooperation with the Russian Federation and other strategic partners, the strengthening of ties with neighboring and African countries, as well as the internal functioning of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Minister Traoré said Burkina Faso is undergoing a process of radical transformation and renewal of its diplomatic relations, in line with the principles of the People’s Progressive Revolution. He reaffirmed President Ibrahim Traoré’s determination to build partnerships based on mutual respect and shared benefits.

Within this framework, he noted, Burkina Faso has consolidated its partnership with Russia while expanding cooperation with other strategic partners. On the AES Confederation, the minister highlighted achievements and the synergy of actions carried out by the three member states to strengthen the bloc.

He also pointed to efforts by the authorities and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to enhance Burkina Faso’s international standing, ensure the country’s voice is heard globally, and challenge persistent stereotypes.

The exchange was described by participants as a constructive and candid dialogue, reflecting a shared commitment to transparency and mutual understanding between public authorities and the media. Minister Traoré praised the work of journalists and pledged to further develop platforms for regular engagement with the press.

The Press Day - Diplomacy initiative is organized by the Directorate of Communication and Press Relations of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, with the objective of strengthening collaboration between Burkinabè diplomats and the national media.

Minister Traoré praised the work of journalists and pledged to further develop platforms for regular engagement with the press.

The Press Day - Diplomacy initiative is organized by the Directorate of Communication and Press Relations of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, with the objective of strengthening collaboration between Burkinabè diplomats and the national media.

title_en: Burkinabè Diaspora in Greece Supports Presidential Initiative “Faso Mêbo”
excerpt_en: Athens, December 14, 2025 - The Association of Burkinabè Nationals in Greece (ARBG) has donated €2,135 (approximately 1,400,465 CFA francs) to the Faso Mêbo presidential initiative.

Athens, December 14, 2025 - The Association of Burkinabè Nationals in Greece (ARBG) has donated €2,135 (approximately 1,400,465 CFA francs) to the Faso Mêbo presidential initiative. The funds were raised through a crowdfunding campaign among association members and friends of Burkina Faso.

The contribution was handed to Her Excellency Cyrille Ganou Badolo, Ambassador of Burkina Faso to Greece, who was present to present her credentials. The Ambassador expressed deep gratitude, highlighting the diaspora’s commitment to Burkina Faso’s development and the strengthening of ties between its members and their homeland.

During the meeting, the Ambassador also raised awareness about national expectations and values that every Burkinabè should embody abroad. The embassy team informed citizens about solidarity and unity, vital for cohesion within the community, and assisted in gathering concerns and facilitating administrative and consular procedures.

This is not the first contribution of the ARBG to national development: in 2024, the association donated €1,535 (1,006,895 CFA francs) to the Patriotic Support Fund, reinforcing its role as a dedicated partner in building a resilient and united Burkina Faso.

title: Burkina Faso and Oman Strengthen Bilateral Ties During High-Level Visit
excerpt: Muscat, December 15, 2025 - Burkina Faso and the Sultanate of Oman reaffirmed their commitment to deepening bilateral cooperation during a friendly working visit by the Burkinabè Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional…
title_en: Burkina Faso and Oman Strengthen Bilateral Ties During High-Level Visit
excerpt_en: Muscat, December 15, 2025 - Burkina Faso and the Sultanate of Oman reaffirmed their commitment to deepening bilateral cooperation during a friendly working visit by the Burkinabè Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional…
body_en:
Muscat, December 15, 2025 - Burkina Faso and the Sultanate of Oman reaffirmed their commitment to deepening bilateral cooperation during a friendly working visit by the Burkinabè Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation, and Burkinabè Abroad to Muscat on December 14, 2025.

During the visit, Minister Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré met with His Excellency Sayyid Badr Albusaidi, Omani Minister of Foreign Affairs, as well as Mr. Qais Bin Mohammed Al Yousef, Omani Minister of Trade, Industry, and Investment Promotion.

The two sides highlighted a new phase of collaboration, agreeing to establish technical teams and exchange delegations to explore strategic areas of cooperation. Key sectors identified include agriculture, mining, investment, trade, cultural and academic exchanges, telecommunications, tourism, and media, aimed at fostering mutual understanding and facilitating partnerships between the populations of both countries.

The ministers also discussed trade and investment, with Minister Traoré presenting Burkina Faso’s potential to attract Omani investors and emphasizing Ouagadougou’s strategic location in West Africa. They stressed the importance of connecting the Chambers of Commerce of both nations to accelerate business collaboration.

Additional agreements under consideration include visa exemptions for official passport holders and political consultations between the Ministries of Foreign Affairs of Burkina Faso and Oman.

Diplomatic relations between the two countries were first established on October 5, 1981, and the ongoing exchanges signal a renewed commitment to long-term partnership. The visit follows an Omani delegation’s trip to Ouagadougou in August 2025, highlighting a mutual desire to expand cooperation in economic, cultural, and social spheres.

Oman, located on the Arabian Peninsula, boasts significant economic and strategic potential, including natural gas and renewable energy resources, efficient logistics, infrastructure, and a growing cultural and tourism sector, making it a valuable partner for Burkina Faso’s development objectives.

title: Burkina Faso Holds 3rd Consultation Framework to Strengthen Regional Cooperation
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 16, 2025 - The Minister Delegate for Regional Cooperation, Ms.
title_en: Burkina Faso Holds 3rd Consultation Framework to Strengthen Regional Cooperation
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 16, 2025 - The Minister Delegate for Regional Cooperation, Ms.
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 16, 2025 - The Minister Delegate for Regional Cooperation, Ms. Bêbgnasgnan Stella Eldine KABRE/KABORE, launched the 3rd Consultation Framework with leaders of regional and sub-regional organizations accredited to Burkina Faso on Tuesday, December 16, 2025.

This initiative, organized by the Ministry of Regional Cooperation, is designed to facilitate dialogue between Ministry officials and regional and sub-regional organization leaders, focusing on aligning national development initiatives with regional programs.

The theme of the consultation was: “Contribution of Presidential Initiatives to the Endogenous Development of Burkina Faso.” In her opening remarks, Ms. KABRE/KABORE praised the commitment of organizations to strengthening Burkina Faso’s resilience and development. She described the meeting as a “privileged forum for dialogue, mutual listening, and synergy” to better integrate national projects with regional programs.

Representing the regional and sub-regional organizations, Mr. Gaafar Rizgallah welcomed the framework, highlighting that it demonstrates the government’s dedication to inclusive development and shared responsibility. He stressed that strong partnerships based on trust and shared objectives allow for the implementation of development initiatives meeting international standards.

The consultation provided an opportunity to review organizational interventions, explore new avenues for collaboration, and engage in direct dialogue between the Minister Delegate and the representatives.

In addition, a fundraising event for the Faso Mêbo initiative was held during the meeting, further reinforcing the commitment of regional and sub-regional actors to national development projects and the mobilization of the Burkinabè diaspora and partners.

During the meeting, Mr. Ouane presented WFP’s new operational plan for Burkina Faso, emphasizing a participatory and inclusive approach that involves government stakeholders in its development. The meeting reflects Burkina Faso’s commitment to strengthening dialogue and coordination with international partners, particularly in the context of ongoing challenges affecting food security and national development.

Ouagadougou, December 17, 2025 - His Excellency Fahad Aldosari, Ambassador of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to Burkina Faso, concluded his five-year tenure with a farewell visit to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation, and Burkinabe Abroad on December 16, 2025.

During the visit, Ambassador Aldosari expressed his gratitude to Minister Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, the Minister Delegate for Regional Cooperation, and the Ministry staff for their support, noting that their collaboration facilitated his diplomatic work and helped strengthen bilateral ties.

“The collaboration with stakeholders at the Ministry has been fruitful. It allowed me to develop my diplomatic skills and advance joint initiatives,” the Ambassador said, affirming Saudi Arabia’s continued commitment to dynamic cooperation with Burkina Faso.

Minister Traoré praised Ambassador Aldosari for his personal dedication, which has reinforced partnerships in sectors such as health, education, and humanitarian aid, and wished him continued success in his future endeavors.

Ambassador Aldosari assumed his post in Burkina Faso in 2021, leaving behind a legacy of strengthened cooperation and mutual understanding between the two nations.

excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 17, 2025 - In a formal agreement signed on Wednesday, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation, and Burkinabe Abroad and the President of the High Council for Communication (CSC)…
title_en: Burkina Faso Grants 94.0 FM Frequency to Radio “Daandé Liptako”
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 17, 2025 - In a formal agreement signed on Wednesday, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation, and Burkinabe Abroad and the President of the High Council for Communication (CSC)…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 17, 2025 - In a formal agreement signed on Wednesday, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation, and Burkinabe Abroad and the President of the High Council for Communication (CSC) officially granted the 94.0 FM frequency to Radio du Sahel, known as Radio “Daandé Liptako.”

The Minister of Foreign Affairs described the signing as a logical continuation of the station's recent launch and commended Minister of Communication Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo for his support. He emphasized that the new radio station would provide the AES Confederation with a platform to produce content that counters misinformation and fosters cohesion and peace.

The President of the CSC, Wendingoudi Louis Modeste Ouédraogo, highlighted that Radio Daandé Liptako embodies the aspirations and struggles of the AES population. He added that the station will broadcast from Ouagadougou, with programming relayed to Niamey and Bamako, and stressed compliance with technical standards and equipment requirements as part of the agreement.

The frequency is granted for a renewable three-year period, and the station is set to be officially launched during the AES Heads of State Summit on December 22-23, 2025, in Bamako, Mali.

title: Burkina Faso-Nigeria Meeting: Nigeria Issues Official Apology for Airspace Incident
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 17, 2025 - President Ibrahim Traoré of Burkina Faso met with Nigerian Foreign Minister Yusuf Maitama Tuggar on Wednesday, during the latter’s official visit to Ouagadougou.
title_en: Burkina Faso-Nigeria Meeting: Nigeria Issues Official Apology for Airspace Incident
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 17, 2025 - President Ibrahim Traoré of Burkina Faso met with Nigerian Foreign Minister Yusuf Maitama Tuggar on Wednesday, during the latter’s official visit to Ouagadougou.
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 17, 2025 - President Ibrahim Traoré of Burkina Faso met with Nigerian Foreign Minister Yusuf Maitama Tuggar on Wednesday, during the latter’s official visit to Ouagadougou.

Minister Tuggar conveyed a message of solidarity and fraternity from Nigerian President Ahmed Bola Tinubu and addressed an incident in which a Nigerian military C-130 transport plane landed in Burkina Faso on December 8, 2025, without overflight authorization. Nigeria acknowledged procedural irregularities and issued a formal apology for the violation of Burkinabe airspace.

The Nigerian Foreign Minister also distanced his government from remarks by a Nigerian political figure alleging mistreatment of Nigerian soldiers in Burkina Faso and reiterated his country’s sincere apologies.

The discussions further focused on bilateral cooperation and regional security, with Minister Tuggar commending Burkina Faso’s efforts to ensure the safety of the aircraft occupants and praising the country’s ongoing fight against terrorism.

Burkina Faso emphasized the importance of strengthened regional collaboration to address common security threats. The Confederation of Sahel States condemned the airspace violation and reaffirmed that its air defenses remain on high alert to protect sovereignty and territorial integrity.

Ouagadougou, December 18, 2025 - The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation, and Burkinabe Abroad, through its Bureau of Interpretation and Translation (BIT), marked International Translation Day on December 17, 2025.

This year’s theme, “Translators and Interpreters: Key Actors in Communication, Linguistic Allies,” reflects the critical role of language professionals in diplomacy and international cooperation.

The ceremony was presided over by Ambassador Dieudonné Désiré Sougouri, Chief of Staff to the Minister of Foreign Affairs, who highlighted the essential contribution of translators and interpreters to the smooth conduct of diplomatic exchanges. He encouraged staff to strengthen their skills, integrate technological innovations, and maintain high standards of excellence.

Ms. Maïmouna Yaguibou, representing the Bureau of Interpretation and Translation, reaffirmed the commitment of her team to continuously improve translation and interpretation practices to facilitate communication and international cooperation.

The commemorative day included discussions on the ethics and professional standards of translation and interpretation, as well as reflections on the challenges faced by language professionals in diplomatic contexts.

title: Burkina Faso Marks 25th International Migrants Day, Highlights Migrants’ Role in Development
excerpt: Bobo Dioulasso, December 18, 2025 - The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation, and Burkinabè Abroad, through the Directorate General for Burkinabè Abroad and in partnership with the International…
title_en: Burkina Faso Marks 25th International Migrants Day, Highlights Migrants’ Role in Development
excerpt_en: Bobo Dioulasso, December 18, 2025 - The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation, and Burkinabè Abroad, through the Directorate General for Burkinabè Abroad and in partnership with the International…
body_en:
Bobo Dioulasso, December 18, 2025 - The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation, and Burkinabè Abroad, through the Directorate General for Burkinabè Abroad and in partnership with the International Organization for Migration (IOM), commemorated the 25th International Migrants Day on Thursday in Bobo Dioulasso, Guiriko Region.

The official ceremony was presided over by the Governor of Guiriko Region, representing Minister Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré. This year’s theme, “Migration in the Service of Cultural Diversity, Social Inclusion, and Economic Development,” emphasized the contributions of migrants to the socioeconomic and cultural development of their countries of origin, transit, and destination.

Ambassador Michel Somma, Director General for Burkinabè Abroad, described the theme as a call for states to facilitate the reception, integration, and well-being of migrants, while David Coomber, Head of Mission for IOM in Burkina Faso, stressed the importance of promoting social reintegration for returning migrants.

During the event, migrant representative Aboubacar Guindo expressed gratitude for national support and urged further measures to protect migrants from abuse, exploitation, and mistreatment.

Highlighting Burkina Faso’s proactive approach, the Governor noted initiatives including free visas for Africans holding valid passports, a national migration plan, and the creation of a national migration observatory.

The celebration featured a panel discussion on migration policies, a football match between foreign communities and returning Burkinabè migrants, testimonials, and a screening of films highlighting Burkinabè realities, underlining the government’s commitment to inclusive and sustainable development through migration.
body_fr:
Bobo Dioulasso, December 18, 2025 - The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation, and Burkinabè Abroad, through the Directorate General for Burkinabè Abroad and in partnership with the International Organization for Migration (IOM), commemorated the 25th International Migrants Day on Thursday in Bobo Dioulasso, Guiriko Region.

The official ceremony was presided over by the Governor of Guiriko Region, representing Minister Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré. This year’s theme, “Migration in the Service of Cultural Diversity, Social Inclusion, and Economic Development,” emphasized the contributions of migrants to the socioeconomic and cultural development of their countries of origin, transit, and destination.

Ambassador Michel Somma, Director General for Burkinabè Abroad, described the theme as a call for states to facilitate the reception, integration, and well-being of migrants, while David Coomber, Head of Mission for IOM in Burkina Faso, stressed the importance of promoting social reintegration for returning migrants.

During the event, migrant representative Aboubacar Guindo expressed gratitude for national support and urged further measures to protect migrants from abuse, exploitation, and mistreatment.

Highlighting Burkina Faso’s proactive approach, the Governor noted initiatives including free visas for Africans holding valid passports, a national migration plan, and the creation of a national migration observatory.

The celebration featured a panel discussion on migration policies, a football match between foreign communities and returning Burkinabè migrants, testimonials, and a screening of films highlighting Burkinabè realities, underlining the government’s commitment to inclusive and sustainable development through migration.

title: Burkina Faso’s New Ambassador to Gabon Presents Credentials to President Oligui Nguema
excerpt: Libreville, December 19, 2025 - His Excellency Issa Boro, newly appointed Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Burkina Faso to the Gabonese Republic, officially presented his credentials to President Brice…
title_en: Burkina Faso’s New Ambassador to Gabon Presents Credentials to President Oligui Nguema
excerpt_en: Libreville, December 19, 2025 - His Excellency Issa Boro, newly appointed Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Burkina Faso to the Gabonese Republic, officially presented his credentials to President Brice…
body_en:
Libreville, December 19, 2025 - His Excellency Issa Boro, newly appointed Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Burkina Faso to the Gabonese Republic, officially presented his credentials to President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema at the Palais de la Rénovation in Libreville on Wednesday, December 17, 2025.

During the ceremony, Ambassador Boro conveyed the fraternal greetings of Burkina Faso’s President, Captain Ibrahim Traoré, to the Gabonese Head of State. President Oligui Nguema praised the strong diplomatic relations and cooperation between the two countries and reaffirmed his support for Burkina Faso in the fight against terrorism, commending the courage and resilience of the Burkinabè people.

The discussions highlighted prospects for enhancing bilateral cooperation, particularly in political, economic, cultural, multilateral, and vocational training sectors. President Oligui Nguema emphasized the need for Burkinabè expertise in agriculture and livestock to boost local production and invited the Burkinabe private sector to invest in Gabon. He also pledged to increase the number of Gabonese students receiving vocational training in Burkina Faso’s higher education institutions.

Ambassador Boro expressed gratitude for the Gabonese President’s support and reaffirmed his commitment to revitalizing strategic cooperation and promoting public-private partnerships for the endogenous development of both countries.

title: AES Confederation: First Confederal Session of the Council of Ministers Opens in Bamako
excerpt: Bamako, December 20, 2025 - The Koulouba Palace hosted the opening of the inaugural confederal session of the Council of Ministers of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) on Saturday, December 20, 2025.
title_en: AES Confederation: First Confederal Session of the Council of Ministers Opens in Bamako
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 20, 2025 - The Koulouba Palace hosted the opening of the inaugural confederal session of the Council of Ministers of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) on Saturday, December 20, 2025.
body_en:
Bamako, December 20, 2025 - The Koulouba Palace hosted the opening of the inaugural confederal session of the Council of Ministers of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) on Saturday, December 20, 2025. The session was chaired by General Assimi Goïta, Head of State of Mali and President of the AES Confederation, and brought together ministers from Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger.

In his opening remarks, President Goïta described the session as a preparatory step for the second meeting of the College of Heads of State, scheduled for December 22-23 in Bamako. He recalled that the Council of Ministers, as outlined in Article 12 of the Constitutive Treaty signed in Niamey on July 6, 2024, forms one of the three pillars of AES governance, alongside the College of Heads of State and the future Confederal Parliament.

The session will focus on key issues, including the progress report on the first-year roadmap, additional protocols on defense, diplomacy, and development, and provisions governing confederal parliamentary sessions. Adoption of these documents will complete the institutional framework of the Confederation.

President Goïta emphasized that the AES mission is to become a platform for “emancipation, freedom, and true independence”, driven by the resources and ingenuity of the Sahelian peoples. “Our three states have made the sovereign choice to join forces to build a stable and peaceful space, conducive to the development and full flourishing of our people,” he declared.

He also condemned the “economic and media terrorism” directed at AES countries by certain international actors, stating that such pressures only strengthen the Confederation’s resolve to pursue its sovereign path on the African and international stage.

The Head of State paid tribute to the defense and security forces of Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger for their commitment “at the risk of their lives,” and commended the courageous peoples of the AES, recognizing them as the true source of the Confederation’s legitimacy.

Looking beyond the Sahel, President Goïta highlighted regional unity: “West Africa is united by a centuries-old history, shared culture, and common geography. Our peoples are naturally called upon to live together, in mutual respect, solidarity, and fraternity.”

Economy and Tech.

title: Burkina Faso Finance Ministry Holds HIV/AIDS and Syphilis Awareness and Screening Campaign
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 8, 2025 - The Ministry of Economy and Finance has stepped up efforts to promote employee health by organizing an HIV/AIDS and syphilis awareness and screening campaign at the Institute of Public…
title_en: Burkina Faso Finance Ministry Holds HIV/AIDS and Syphilis Awareness and Screening Campaign
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 8, 2025 - The Ministry of Economy and Finance has stepped up efforts to promote employee health by organizing an HIV/AIDS and syphilis awareness and screening campaign at the Institute of Public…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 8, 2025 - The Ministry of Economy and Finance has stepped up efforts to promote employee health by organizing an HIV/AIDS and syphilis awareness and screening campaign at the Institute of Public Finance of Burkina Faso.

The initiative, held on Friday, December 5, was led by the ministry’s Human Resources Department in partnership with the SOS Sang association and the Directorate General of Taxes. It forms part of the ministry’s broader strategy to contribute actively to the fight against major epidemic diseases and to safeguard the well-being of its workforce.

During the campaign, participants took part in awareness sessions focusing on the modes of transmission and prevention of HIV/AIDS and syphilis. Free, anonymous, and confidential testing services were also provided on site, allowing staff to learn their serological status in a secure and supportive environment.

Organizers emphasized the importance of early screening, highlighting that knowing one’s health status is essential for timely and effective medical care. The event was conducted under the slogan “Getting tested is a good start for your health.”

Through this initiative, the Ministry of Economy and Finance reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening prevention and awareness actions, while encouraging responsible health practices among public sector employees.

title: Burkina Faso Presents 2024 EITI Report Highlighting Transparency and Extractive Sector Reforms
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 9, 2025 - A delegation from the Steering Committee of the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI) of Burkina Faso, led by Chairman Vieux Abdoul Rachid Soulama, officially presented the…
title_en: Burkina Faso Presents 2024 EITI Report Highlighting Transparency and Extractive Sector Reforms
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 9, 2025 - A delegation from the Steering Committee of the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI) of Burkina Faso, led by Chairman Vieux Abdoul Rachid Soulama, officially presented the…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 9, 2025 - A delegation from the Steering Committee of the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI) of Burkina Faso, led by Chairman Vieux Abdoul Rachid Soulama, officially presented the 2024 EITI Report, titled “Transparency in Action: Reforms for Sustainable Development”, to Minister of Economy and Finance Dr. Aboubakar Nacanabo on Tuesday. The handover marks a key milestone in strengthening governance and accountability in Burkina Faso’s extractive industries.

The 2024 report builds on progress achieved in the management of the country’s mining sector, presenting updates to the legislative and regulatory framework and providing an overview of the macroeconomic context, which reflects a recovery in economic activity and the sector’s contributions to national development.

Notably, the report includes new disclosures, publishing for the first time the costs of mining extraction and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, enabling a more comprehensive analysis of both the economic and environmental performance of the sector.

For this reporting cycle, the EITI-BF Steering Committee focused on enhancing data quality and reliability, ensuring traceability of financial flows between companies, government, and local authorities, integrating recent legislative reforms, and documenting the economic, social, and environmental impacts of extractive activities.

Minister Nacanabo praised the EITI Permanent Secretariat and all stakeholders for the quality and rigor of their work, welcoming the report as a strategic tool to highlight the extractive sector’s contributions to Burkina Faso’s sustainable development and to reinforce transparency and good governance practices in the sector.

title: Burkina Faso Reviews Peacebuilding Fund Projects to Strengthen Strategic Interventions
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 9, 2025 - The Steering Committee for Peacebuilding Fund (PBF) projects in Burkina Faso held its second ordinary session of 2025 on Tuesday, marking a key transition from the Emergency Program for…
title_en: Burkina Faso Reviews Peacebuilding Fund Projects to Strengthen Strategic Interventions
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 9, 2025 - The Steering Committee for Peacebuilding Fund (PBF) projects in Burkina Faso held its second ordinary session of 2025 on Tuesday, marking a key transition from the Emergency Program for…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 9, 2025 - The Steering Committee for Peacebuilding Fund (PBF) projects in Burkina Faso held its second ordinary session of 2025 on Tuesday, marking a key transition from the Emergency Program for the Sahel (PUS-BF) to the new National Strategy for Territorial Resilience and Stabilization. The session, chaired by the Minister of Economy and Finance and represented by the Governor of Kadiogo, provided an opportunity to assess past progress and set strategic priorities for future interventions.

Between 2017 and 2024, the PBF mobilized approximately 33 billion CFA francs to support 27 projects across Burkina Faso. These initiatives focused on three main pillars:

Strengthening trust between the population and the State;

Building social resilience and promoting active participation of women and youth;

Fostering peaceful, inclusive, and sustainable conflict management.

As of November 15, 2025, the implementation of these projects achieved 84.4% of physical targets and 79% of financial objectives, reflecting significant progress on the ground.

According to Maurice Azonnankpo, Acting UN Resident Coordinator in Burkina Faso, the Fund’s interventions have yielded tangible results. These include supporting government measures against money laundering and terrorist financing, mobilizing the agricultural mechanization brigade to cultivate 200 hectares, and establishing 669 savings groups, of which 530 have been equipped with savings management tools.

The meeting also provided a framework to align new projects with local realities, ensuring interventions are more effective, relevant, and capable of addressing the evolving challenges of peacebuilding, resilience, and stabilization in Burkina Faso.

title: Confederal Bank for Investment and Development Launched to Boost AES Economic Integration
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 12, 2025 - The President of the Transition and President of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), General Assimi Goïta, on December 11 met with the Ministers of Economy and Finance of Burkina…
title_en: Confederal Bank for Investment and Development Launched to Boost AES Economic Integration
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 12, 2025 - The President of the Transition and President of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), General Assimi Goïta, on December 11 met with the Ministers of Economy and Finance of Burkina…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 12, 2025 - The President of the Transition and President of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), General Assimi Goïta, on December 11 met with the Ministers of Economy and Finance of Burkina Faso, who, alongside representatives from Mali and Niger, presented the results of technical preparations for the launch of the Confederal Bank for Investment and Development (BCID-AES).

The ministers, led by Dr. Aboubakar Nacanabo, announced a key milestone: the validation and signing of the BCID-AES statutes, officially establishing the bank. This strategic institution is designed to mobilize sovereign resources and finance projects of high regional importance.

Road infrastructure and access to remote areas,

Private sector projects aligned with national priorities.

Capital commitments from the three member states, combined with a planned confederal tax, have allowed the BCID-AES to enter its operational phase. The next steps include appointing the bank’s administrators and launching a campaign to raise additional funds.

President Goïta emphasized the institution’s strategic importance, stating that the BCID-AES will be the most effective tool for promoting independence and advancing economic development within the AES region.

title: Burkina Faso Begins Drafting New National Development Plan 2026-2030
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 12, 2025 - The Secretary General of the Ministry of Economy and Finance, Vieux Abdoul Rachid Soulama, chaired a meeting of the technical committee responsible for developing Burkina Faso’s National…
title_en: Burkina Faso Begins Drafting New National Development Plan 2026-2030
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 12, 2025 - The Secretary General of the Ministry of Economy and Finance, Vieux Abdoul Rachid Soulama, chaired a meeting of the technical committee responsible for developing Burkina Faso’s National…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 12, 2025 - The Secretary General of the Ministry of Economy and Finance, Vieux Abdoul Rachid Soulama, chaired a meeting of the technical committee responsible for developing Burkina Faso’s National Development Plan 2026-2030 on Friday.

The session brought together secretaries general from various ministries and several observer members to review the preliminary draft of the plan. This process follows an extensive period of data collection, analysis, and nationwide consultations, which laid the groundwork for the country’s next five-year planning framework.

The exercise is particularly timely, as the National Development Plan 2021-2025 is set to expire at the end of the year. Under the law governing development planning, a new national framework must be prepared every five years, taking into account Burkina Faso’s current context, which is shaped by the challenges of sovereignty, resilience, and endogenous development promoted by the People’s Progressive Revolution (RPP).

The technical committee, led by the Ministry of Economy and Finance, is tasked with reviewing and refining the draft before submitting it to the Steering and Monitoring Committee, chaired by the Prime Minister. During the meeting, participants provided feedback and proposed adjustments to the tools, mechanisms, and implementation strategies of the future plan.

The preliminary draft outlines an ambitious vision to make Burkina Faso a sovereign and prosperous nation grounded in sustainable development and its own national strengths. The central objective of the 2026-2030 plan is to promote inclusive economic and social progress, underpinned by patriotism, national sovereignty, and a climate of peace.

title: TIKTO Community Radio Officially Launches in Téma-Bokin, Passoré Province
excerpt: Passoré, December 13, 2025 - The Minister of Communication, Culture, Arts, and Tourism, Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo, took part in the inauguration of the TIKTO community radio station in Téma-Bokin, Passoré Province, on Friday.
title_en: TIKTO Community Radio Officially Launches in Téma-Bokin, Passoré Province
excerpt_en: Passoré, December 13, 2025 - The Minister of Communication, Culture, Arts, and Tourism, Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo, took part in the inauguration of the TIKTO community radio station in Téma-Bokin, Passoré Province, on Friday.
body_en:
Passoré, December 13, 2025 - The Minister of Communication, Culture, Arts, and Tourism, Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo, took part in the inauguration of the TIKTO community radio station in Téma-Bokin, Passoré Province, on Friday. The event was held under the patronage of Louis Modeste Ouédraogo, President of the High Council for Communication, and attended by the Minister in charge of Promotion of National Languages, Jacques Sosthène Dingara, as well as the station’s founder, Yacouba Jacob Barry.

In his address, the President of the High Council for Communication called on stakeholders to practice self-regulation, emphasizing that responsible media is essential for social cohesion.

Minister Ouédraogo congratulated the station’s founder, highlighting that TIKTO, meaning “solidarity” in the Moorish language, should serve as a symbol of community values and social unity. He stressed the strategic role of community media in promoting recovery, stability, and national progress.

The minister outlined the four core missions of community media:

Mobilizing citizens to support local development and civic engagement.

He also recalled the vision of President Ibrahim Traoré for a sovereign, resilient, and dignified Burkina Faso, urging the media to act as a vector of reliable information, collective hope, and national transformation. “The inauguration of Radio TIKTO marks the beginning of a vision, a hope, and a collective commitment,” the minister said.

Founder Yacouba Jacob Barry expressed gratitude for the support of national authorities and emphasized that Radio TIKTO will position itself as a patriotic media outlet, promoting local initiatives, national talent, and innovative solutions aligned with government priorities.

Radio TIKTO broadcasts on 102.10 FM, covering approximately 18 surrounding localities in the Passoré region.

Ouagadougou, December 15, 2025 - The Minister of Economy and Finance, Aboubakar Nacanabo, inaugurated the 3rd National Academy of the Green Economy on Monday, December 15, 2025.

Held under the patronage of Ousmane Bougouma, President of the Transitional Legislative Assembly, the three-day forum ran from December 15 to 17 and was themed: “Green Transition in Burkina Faso: Challenges and Acceleration Strategies in a Context of National Rebuilding.” The event provided a platform to explore how the ecological transition can drive economic growth, environmental sustainability, and societal well-being.

Minister Nacanabo highlighted that the green economy represents a strategic opportunity for Burkina Faso to generate value, create decent employment, foster local innovation, and reconcile economic development with social justice and environmental protection. He called on all stakeholders to leverage the ecological transition as a catalyst for development, resilience, and harmony between citizens and the natural environment.

title: Burkina Faso’s Economy Shows Strong Growth and Positive Indicators, IMF Reports
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 16, 2025 - Technical Advisor Souleymane Nabole, representing the Minister of Economy and Finance, chaired a presentation of the IMF Regional Economic Outlook for Sub-Saharan Africa, October 2025…
title_en: Burkina Faso’s Economy Shows Strong Growth and Positive Indicators, IMF Reports
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 16, 2025 - Technical Advisor Souleymane Nabole, representing the Minister of Economy and Finance, chaired a presentation of the IMF Regional Economic Outlook for Sub-Saharan Africa, October 2025…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 16, 2025 - Technical Advisor Souleymane Nabole, representing the Minister of Economy and Finance, chaired a presentation of the IMF Regional Economic Outlook for Sub-Saharan Africa, October 2025 edition, titled “Staying Firm”, at the Higher Institute of Population Sciences (ISSP) of Joseph Ki-Zerbo University. The event was organized by the IMF Resident Representative in Burkina Faso.

The report highlighted Burkina Faso as a favorable case, benefiting from ambitious reforms aimed at mobilizing domestic resources and enhancing public spending management. Investments across key sectors, particularly agriculture, have boosted national production and supported economic activity.

According to the IMF, Burkina Faso’s economic growth reached nearly 5% in 2024, with projections exceeding 6% for 2025. Inflationary pressures remain low, with 0.5% inflation in 2024 and deflation expected in 2025. The fiscal outlook is also encouraging, with the public deficit projected at around 3%, potentially below the WAEMU threshold by 2027.

The IMF Regional Economic Outlook provides a semi-annual analysis of sub-Saharan Africa’s economic situation, evaluating recent developments, challenges, government initiatives, and regional priorities for sustainable economic management.

title: Ouagadougou-Bobo-Dioulasso Highway Officially Launched Under President Traoré
excerpt: Bobo-Dioulasso, December 16, 2025 - President of Burkina Faso, Captain Ibrahim Traoré, officially inaugurated the construction of the Ouagadougou-Bobo-Dioulasso highway on Tuesday afternoon, marking a major milestone in…
title_en: Ouagadougou-Bobo-Dioulasso Highway Officially Launched Under President Traoré
excerpt_en: Bobo-Dioulasso, December 16, 2025 - President of Burkina Faso, Captain Ibrahim Traoré, officially inaugurated the construction of the Ouagadougou-Bobo-Dioulasso highway on Tuesday afternoon, marking a major milestone in…
body_en:
Bobo-Dioulasso, December 16, 2025 - President of Burkina Faso, Captain Ibrahim Traoré, officially inaugurated the construction of the Ouagadougou-Bobo-Dioulasso highway on Tuesday afternoon, marking a major milestone in the country’s infrastructure development. The project, long anticipated by the Burkinabè population, aims to enhance connectivity between the two largest cities.

The four-lane (2x4) highway forms part of the Faso Mêbo Presidential Initiative, designed to improve access to urban and remote areas. Built to modern standards with environmental considerations, the infrastructure will significantly boost mobility and support regional development.

Fully state-funded, the project has been allocated at least 200 billion CFA francs for 2026, as confirmed by President Traoré. He urged residents along the route to actively participate, emphasizing that citizen engagement is key to the project’s success.

Beyond this strategic corridor, the government plans additional regional highways, including the Koudougou-Yako road, which will now be upgraded to an expressway. President Traoré underscored the broader vision: connecting regional capitals to each other and integrating Burkina Faso through a modern road network to stimulate economic growth and national cohesion.

title: Burkina Faso: 2026 Finance Law Nears Submission to Transitional Legislative Assembly
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 18, 2025 - The draft 2026 Finance Law is approaching its final stage in the Transitional Legislative Assembly (ALT).
title_en: Burkina Faso: 2026 Finance Law Nears Submission to Transitional Legislative Assembly
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 18, 2025 - The draft 2026 Finance Law is approaching its final stage in the Transitional Legislative Assembly (ALT).
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 18, 2025 - The draft 2026 Finance Law is approaching its final stage in the Transitional Legislative Assembly (ALT).

Following consultations with various ministries and institutions, and after the arbitration by the Finance and Budget Committee (COMFIB), a key step was taken on Thursday, December 18, 2025.

Minister of Economy and Finance Aboubakar Nacanabo, accompanied by a ministry delegation, held a working session with COMFIB members to review and adopt the committee’s report.

The initial draft Finance Law for the 2026 fiscal year, along with the COMFIB report, will now be submitted to the ALT plenary session for review and adoption, marking a decisive step toward implementing Burkina Faso’s 2026 budgetary and economic priorities.

title: Burkina Faso: President Traoré Inaugurates Burkina Cajou Cashew Processing Plant
excerpt: Bobo-Dioulasso, December 20, 2025 - The President of Burkina Faso, Captain Ibrahim Traoré, officially inaugurated the Burkina Cajou cashew nut processing plant on Saturday, marking a major step in the country’s…
title_en: Burkina Faso: President Traoré Inaugurates Burkina Cajou Cashew Processing Plant
excerpt_en: Bobo-Dioulasso, December 20, 2025 - The President of Burkina Faso, Captain Ibrahim Traoré, officially inaugurated the Burkina Cajou cashew nut processing plant on Saturday, marking a major step in the country’s…
body_en:
Bobo-Dioulasso, December 20, 2025 - The President of Burkina Faso, Captain Ibrahim Traoré, officially inaugurated the Burkina Cajou cashew nut processing plant on Saturday, marking a major step in the country’s industrial development.

Situated in the Bobo 2010 industrial zone, Burkina Cajou was founded by Ms. Masso So/Traoré, whose vision of processing cashew nuts locally rather than exporting raw materials has now become a reality with government support.

President Traoré highlighted the state’s involvement: “She presented her project to us, which was facing difficulties, and we decided to support it with public funds.” The project received 25% support from the Burkinabe Council for Agricultural Sectors, the Dumu Ka Fa Fund, the Burkinabe Fund for Economic and Social Development (FBDES), and the Commercial Bank of Burkina Faso (BCB).

The plant, equipped with modern technology, has a processing capacity of 150,000 tons of cashew nuts per year and represents a total investment of 9.743 billion CFA francs, creating an estimated 1,700 direct and indirect jobs.

Minister of Industry, Trade, and Handicrafts, Serge Gnaniodem Poda, stressed the strategic importance of the cashew sector for Burkina Faso’s economy. President Traoré encouraged domestic processing, stating that the government stands ready to support exporters returning to local production, promoting industrial growth and employment opportunities for young Burkinabè.

title: Burkina Faso Reviews Draft Law on Paid Leave and Commemorative Days
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 8, 2025 - The Minister of Public Service, Labor, and Social Protection, Mathias Traoré, held a working session on Monday with members of the Commission on General Institutional Affairs and Human…
title_en: Burkina Faso Reviews Draft Law on Paid Leave and Commemorative Days
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 8, 2025 - The Minister of Public Service, Labor, and Social Protection, Mathias Traoré, held a working session on Monday with members of the Commission on General Institutional Affairs and Human…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 8, 2025 - The Minister of Public Service, Labor, and Social Protection, Mathias Traoré, held a working session on Monday with members of the Commission on General Institutional Affairs and Human Rights (CAGIDH) to review the draft law on paid leave and commemorative days in Burkina Faso.

The meeting, chaired by MP Linda Gwladys Ouédraogo, President of CAGIDH, was attended by the minister’s staff and representatives from the Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, responsible for institutional relations. The purpose of the session was to refine the draft before it is submitted for plenary review.

During the presentation, Minister Traoré highlighted that the adoption of the law would help enable the Burkinabè people to work more effectively while reinforcing the country’s goals of endogenous development and national sovereignty. Among the main innovations, the draft eliminates the paid holiday entitlement for the day following a public holiday that falls on a Sunday.

The bill also reclassifies key national observances: the popular uprising of January 3, the proclamation of independence on August 5, and National Martyrs’ Day on October 31 as days of commemoration and remembrance. Additionally, May 15 is designated as a day honoring customs and traditions, reflecting the secular nature of the State.

Following detailed debates and article-by-article review, the draft law will be submitted in the coming days for adoption during a plenary session of the Transitional Legislative Assembly.

title: Burkina Faso Holds 2025 Session of Public Vocational Training Institutions Committee in Tenkodogo
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 8, 2025 - The Ministry of Public Service, Labor, and Social Protection (MFPTPS) convened the 2025 session of the Committee of Public Vocational Training Institutions (EFPE Committee) on December…
title_en: Burkina Faso Holds 2025 Session of Public Vocational Training Institutions Committee in Tenkodogo
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 8, 2025 - The Ministry of Public Service, Labor, and Social Protection (MFPTPS) convened the 2025 session of the Committee of Public Vocational Training Institutions (EFPE Committee) on December…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 8, 2025 - The Ministry of Public Service, Labor, and Social Protection (MFPTPS) convened the 2025 session of the Committee of Public Vocational Training Institutions (EFPE Committee) on December 8-9 in Tenkodogo, Nakambé region. The session was organized through the Permanent Secretariat for the Coordination of Vocational Training Institutions and the Strengthening of Public Expertise (SP-CEFP-VEP).

The meeting focused on examining the implementation of recommendations from the EFPE 2025 Forum, evaluating the effectiveness of the 2025-2026 academic year, improving tools such as the statistical yearbook and EFPE dashboard, and validating mechanisms for evaluating teaching staff and academic performance.

A central goal of the session was to harmonize and standardize procedures within the EFPEs, including monitoring forum recommendations, organizing civil service examinations, conducting merit-based recruitment, managing waiting lists, and certifying trainees upon completion of their programs.

At the opening, Mr. Boubacar Ouédraogo, Director General of INFPE, expressed hope that the forum would continue to serve as a platform for knowledge exchange, sharing experiences, and consolidating best practices.

According to Mr. Ousmane David Zanné, Permanent Secretary of SP-CEFP-VEP, the 2025 Forum produced three major recommendations and a resolution aimed at strengthening pedagogical and administrative governance in the EFPEs. Key measures include developing a framework for civil servant professional development, providing supervision for temporary teachers, and harmonizing methodologies for professional dissertations.

The Committee session brought together senior officials, EFPE focal points, and the directors general of the AGRE and the Civil Service, continuing an annual tradition of collaborative governance and institutional strengthening for Burkina Faso’s vocational training system.

title: ENAM Graduates 1,290 Trainees in 2023-2025 Class, Prime Minister Names Cohort “Sovereignty”
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 9, 2025 - The National School of Administration and Magistracy (ENAM) officially awarded diplomas to its 2023-2025 graduating class, comprising 1,290 trainees, in a ceremony held on Tuesday in…
title_en: ENAM Graduates 1,290 Trainees in 2023-2025 Class, Prime Minister Names Cohort “Sovereignty”
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 9, 2025 - The National School of Administration and Magistracy (ENAM) officially awarded diplomas to its 2023-2025 graduating class, comprising 1,290 trainees, in a ceremony held on Tuesday in…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 9, 2025 - The National School of Administration and Magistracy (ENAM) officially awarded diplomas to its 2023-2025 graduating class, comprising 1,290 trainees, in a ceremony held on Tuesday in Ouagadougou.

The event was presided over by Prime Minister Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouedraogo, with the Minister of Public Service, Labor, and Social Protection, Mathias Traoré, other government officials, and dignitaries in attendance. The Prime Minister named the graduating cohort “Sovereignty”, reflecting the importance of national service and responsibility.

Minister Traoré highlighted the significance of the graduates in fulfilling state needs and pledged to accelerate their integration into relevant ministries and institutions. He encouraged the trainees to become “progressive and patriotic revolutionaries”, guiding Burkina Faso toward a better future through endogenous development, and to uphold the values of integrity, ethics, and professionalism.

ENAM Director General Dr. Jacob Yarabatioula noted that the class spans P, A, B, and C cycles, covering 19 programs and 53 sections across the central institution and regional institutes, achieving a 100% success rate. He expressed gratitude to the Board of Directors and the Scientific Council for their support.

The ceremony’s patron, El Hadji Moussa Kouanda, urged graduates to serve the state with integrity and efficiency, warning against opportunism and corruption. “Just as energy flows to provide light, ensure that public service flows efficiently everywhere,” he advised.

Class representative Pascal Tiendrebeogo pledged that the graduates would carry the spirit of their cohort throughout their professional journeys.

The event included the presentation of diplomas and awards to top graduates, recognition certificates for the sponsor and the Georges Namoano Academy, and a guided tour of ENAM’s new media library. Additionally, ENAM inaugurated new facilities, including a digital media library, modern amphitheater, multi-sports field, renovated school façade, and a paved access road.

The graduation marks a major milestone in preparing competent and patriotic professionals to serve Burkina Faso’s public administration.

title: Guiriko Commemorates Burkina Faso’s 65th Independence Anniversary, Honoring 302 Citizens
excerpt: Bobo-Dioulasso, December 12, 2025 - The Guiriko region celebrated the 65th anniversary of Burkina Faso’s independence on Thursday, December 11, under the theme: “Sacrifice of our martyrs, flame of our resistance…
title_en: Guiriko Commemorates Burkina Faso’s 65th Independence Anniversary, Honoring 302 Citizens
excerpt_en: Bobo-Dioulasso, December 12, 2025 - The Guiriko region celebrated the 65th anniversary of Burkina Faso’s independence on Thursday, December 11, under the theme: “Sacrifice of our martyrs, flame of our resistance…
body_en:
Bobo-Dioulasso, December 12, 2025 - The Guiriko region celebrated the 65th anniversary of Burkina Faso’s independence on Thursday, December 11, under the theme: “Sacrifice of our martyrs, flame of our resistance: together for total and assured sovereignty.”

The ceremony was presided over by Regional Governor Mariama Konaté, in the presence of Minister of Public Service, Labor, and Social Protection Mathias Traoré, and Secretary General of the Government and Council of Ministers Ousmane Ouattara.

During the event, 302 individuals were formally recognized by the nation through official decorations for their contributions. Governor Konaté paid tribute to the armed forces, highlighting their courageous operations over the past year in areas previously considered hostile, and emphasized that defending national sovereignty is a collective responsibility of all Burkinabè citizens.

“This must be reflected in each of our decisions and actions,” she said, echoing the call of President Ibrahim Traoré for unity in the pursuit of sovereignty. She reaffirmed that the People’s Progressive Revolution, proclaimed on April 2, 2025, represents a societal vision to break dependencies and ensure Burkina Faso masters its own destiny.

Governor Konaté urged Guiriko residents to fully commit to the ongoing movement for complete sovereignty, emphasizing that it is “neither a facade nor mere rhetoric: it is a daily struggle and a shared responsibility.”

Minister Mathias Traoré congratulated the honorees and called on the population to actively contribute to national sovereignty. “On behalf of the government, we attended this commemorative ceremony in Guiriko at the invitation of the governor. It was a solemn occasion marked by acts of great significance,” he stated.

The event reflected a strong message of patriotism, unity, and commitment to Burkina Faso’s independence and national sovereignty.
body_fr:
Bobo-Dioulasso, December 12, 2025 - The Guiriko region celebrated the 65th anniversary of Burkina Faso’s independence on Thursday, December 11, under the theme: “Sacrifice of our martyrs, flame of our resistance: together for total and assured sovereignty.”

The ceremony was presided over by Regional Governor Mariama Konaté, in the presence of Minister of Public Service, Labor, and Social Protection Mathias Traoré, and Secretary General of the Government and Council of Ministers Ousmane Ouattara.

During the event, 302 individuals were formally recognized by the nation through official decorations for their contributions. Governor Konaté paid tribute to the armed forces, highlighting their courageous operations over the past year in areas previously considered hostile, and emphasized that defending national sovereignty is a collective responsibility of all Burkinabè citizens.

“This must be reflected in each of our decisions and actions,” she said, echoing the call of President Ibrahim Traoré for unity in the pursuit of sovereignty. She reaffirmed that the People’s Progressive Revolution, proclaimed on April 2, 2025, represents a societal vision to break dependencies and ensure Burkina Faso masters its own destiny.

Governor Konaté urged Guiriko residents to fully commit to the ongoing movement for complete sovereignty, emphasizing that it is “neither a facade nor mere rhetoric: it is a daily struggle and a shared responsibility.”

Minister Mathias Traoré congratulated the honorees and called on the population to actively contribute to national sovereignty. “On behalf of the government, we attended this commemorative ceremony in Guiriko at the invitation of the governor. It was a solemn occasion marked by acts of great significance,” he stated.

The event reflected a strong message of patriotism, unity, and commitment to Burkina Faso’s independence and national sovereignty.
