title_en: Burkina Faso: Ministry of Public Service Launches Major Promotion Campaign for Civil Servants and Retirees
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 15, 2025 - The Ministry of Public Service, Labor, and Social Protection, through its Directorate General of the Public Service, launched a major promotion campaign on Monday for civil servants…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 15, 2025 - The Ministry of Public Service, Labor, and Social Protection, through its Directorate General of the Public Service, launched a major promotion campaign on Monday for civil servants eligible for retirement.

The initiative, in line with Article 90 of Law No. 081-2015/CNT of November 24, 2015, will benefit approximately 3,000 civil servants eligible for retirement between 2020 and 2025.

Process pending promotion applications for active civil servants.

Regularize administrative situations related to promotions.

Handle retirement applications for employees eligible in the first half of 2026.

Process integration and reclassification applications for trainees recently graduated from vocational training schools.

This operation reflects the government’s commitment to accelerating and simplifying career management for civil servants.

It builds on the recent decentralization of career management procedures to regional directors, a reform launched on December 10, 2025, which produced its first results on December 15 in all regions, demonstrating tangible progress in public service administration.

title: Burkina Faso: Council of Ministers Adopts Five Decrees Reforming Civil Service Professions
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 17, 2025 - During its ordinary session held on Wednesday, December 17, 2025, under the chairmanship of President Captain Ibrahim Traoré, the Council of Ministers adopted five decrees aimed at…
title_en: Burkina Faso: Council of Ministers Adopts Five Decrees Reforming Civil Service Professions
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 17, 2025 - During its ordinary session held on Wednesday, December 17, 2025, under the chairmanship of President Captain Ibrahim Traoré, the Council of Ministers adopted five decrees aimed at…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 17, 2025 - During its ordinary session held on Wednesday, December 17, 2025, under the chairmanship of President Captain Ibrahim Traoré, the Council of Ministers adopted five decrees aimed at modernizing and better structuring civil service professions.

The decrees, under the oversight of the Ministry of Public Service, Labor, and Social Protection, revise previous regulations to align with the Interministerial Directory of State Professions (RIME).

Renames the occupational family "Social Education" to "Social Assistance".

Social Education Assistant → Social Affairs Assistant (Categories B & C)

Social Education Advisor → Social Affairs Administrator (Category A)

Introduces provisions for secondment of probationary civil servants applicable across civil service positions.

Integrates specialist veterinarian (Category P) in the "Veterinary Diagnosis and Care" family.

Renames Medical Biologist → Medical Biology Engineer.

Ceases recruitment for Clinical Psychologist positions.

Introduces Assistant in Economics and Development (Category B).

Integrates the Industrial Development family with positions: Senior Technician in Industrial Engineering (B) and Industrial Engineer (A).

Gradually eliminates the Statistical Engineer position (A) within the Statistics and Demography family.

Human Resources and Administration Management → Human Resources Management

Corresponding adjustments for assistants and advisors across categories A, B, and C.

Creates Hydrogeological Works Engineer (Category A) in the Hydrogeology family.

Establishes the Drilling Workshop occupational category with positions from technical agent (C) to design engineer (A).

These reforms aim to streamline career paths, modernize job classifications, and improve public sector human resource management, ensuring civil service roles are clearly defined and aligned with current institutional needs.

title_en: Burkina Faso: Labor Inspectors Embrace New Methodological Guide; CNSS Wins Interdepartmental Cup
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 18, 2025 - The Ministry of Public Service, Labor, and Social Protection (MFPTPS) organized a two-day workshop on December 18-19, 2025, to introduce labor inspectors and controllers to the…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 18, 2025 - The Ministry of Public Service, Labor, and Social Protection (MFPTPS) organized a two-day workshop on December 18-19, 2025, to introduce labor inspectors and controllers to the innovations in the revised methodological guide.

Chaired by Stella Zoungrana Somé, Director General of Labor, the event brought together central-level labor stakeholders. Ms. Zoungrana highlighted that the guide, updating the 2011 edition, is not merely a reference but a practical tool providing structured procedures, guidance, and methods for inspection, advisory, conciliation, and investigative missions. Participants reviewed the guide’s innovations, shared experiences, and explored ways to strengthen Burkina Faso’s labor inspection system.

In parallel, the Interdepartmental Cup and Affiliated Structures of MFPTPS concluded on December 18 at the National School of Administration and Magistracy (ENAM). The tournament, returning after more than ten years, featured ten teams representing various departments.

The National Social Security Fund (CNSS) faced the Human Resources and Information Systems Directorate (DRH-DSI) in the final. After a draw in regulation time, CNSS won on penalties.

Minister Mathias Traoré praised the competition for fostering camaraderie, solidarity, discipline, and patriotism, aligning with President Captain Ibrahim Traoré’s vision to promote well-being and excellence among Burkinabè citizens. Awards were presented to players and coaching staff, while the Minister also paid tribute to the armed forces for their tireless service.

This dual event highlighted the Ministry’s commitment to modernizing labor oversight while promoting team spirit, health, and motivation among civil servants.

title: Burkina Faso Reviews Government Parliamentary Activities for 2024-2025

title_en: Burkina Faso Reviews Government Parliamentary Activities for 2024-2025
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 8, 2025 - The Minister of Justice and Human Rights, responsible for relations with institutions, Edasso Rodrigue Bayala, inaugurated a seminar focused on reviewing the Government’s parliamentary…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 8, 2025 - The Minister of Justice and Human Rights, responsible for relations with institutions, Edasso Rodrigue Bayala, inaugurated a seminar focused on reviewing the Government’s parliamentary activities for the years 2024 and 2025.

Organized by the Directorate General for Relations with Institutions (DGRI), the session aims to raise awareness of DGRI’s role, promote the operational mechanisms of the Transitional Legislative Assembly (ALT), and compile a consolidated review of two years of parliamentary sessions.

In his opening remarks, Minister Bayala highlighted the strategic importance of the seminar:"This consultation framework is an excellent opportunity to get to know each other better and to exchange views with all stakeholders on the missions of my ministry in its relations with institutions, the missions of the legislative body, and to address the difficulties that hinder relations between the Government and the legislative body."

Over the two-day session, parliamentarians and representatives from key institutions will analyze the progress of parliamentary activities, identify challenges, and propose actionable solutions. A summary report will be produced at the conclusion of the seminar.

The initiative seeks to strengthen effective, transparent, and results-oriented institutional partnerships within Burkina Faso’s public sector.

body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 9, 2025 - The Secretary General of the Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, Harouna Kadio, received the finalist delegation of the ENAM (National School of Administration and Magistracy) Football Cup, highlighting the Ministry’s commitment to promoting sports excellence and cohesion within the judiciary.

The delegation, led by Daouda Mande from the 30th graduating class of student magistrates, presented the trophy won at the Maracana tournament organized by ENAM, which trains Burkina Faso’s administrative and judicial elite.

Addressing the team, Secretary General Kadio congratulated the competitors for their performance, emphasizing that the victory reflects unity, cohesion, and a strong sense of duty within the judiciary."This trophy proves one thing: when the judiciary is united, we are invincible and capable of achieving great victories," he stated.

The football team, representing ENAM’s judicial section, expressed gratitude for the Ministry’s support of sports initiatives and its role in promoting well-being and team spirit in the workplace. They reaffirmed their commitment to using sports as a means of enhancing the image and values of the judiciary.

The ENAM judiciary section comprises trainee judges, court clerks, and judicial interpreters. The tournament, held from April 24 to November 29, 2025, brought together ten clubs competing on ENAM’s multi-sports field, fostering talent, discipline, and camaraderie among participants.

title: Burkina Faso Celebrates Human Rights Night 2025 with Advocacy and Recognition
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 10, 2025 - The Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, responsible for relations with institutions (MJDHRI), marked Human Rights Night 2025, a flagship event in the country’s International Human…
title_en: Burkina Faso Celebrates Human Rights Night 2025 with Advocacy and Recognition
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 10, 2025 - The Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, responsible for relations with institutions (MJDHRI), marked Human Rights Night 2025, a flagship event in the country’s International Human…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 10, 2025 - The Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, responsible for relations with institutions (MJDHRI), marked Human Rights Night 2025, a flagship event in the country’s International Human Rights Day celebrations. The theme for this year was: “Human Rights: Essential to Our Daily Lives.”

The ceremony, chaired by Secretary General Harouna Kadio, representing the Minister, brought together technical and financial partners, civil society organizations, students, human rights defenders, and Ministry staff.

In her remarks, Zeinab Hamza Diaby, Resident Representative of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR), emphasized that human rights are “a living ideal that we defend every day.”

Secretary General Kadio thanked the Ministry’s partners for their ongoing support and highlighted the theme’s relevance, noting that human rights are “the very essence of our lives,” encompassing daily efforts to ensure dignity, peace, and fulfillment for all citizens. He also acknowledged the sacrifices of the National Armed Forces, Internal Security Forces, and Volunteers for the Defense of the Homeland, whose efforts help restore Burkina Faso’s territorial integrity.

Kadio urged all human rights advocates to go beyond merely denouncing injustices and to become agents of change, fostering peace, social cohesion, and community resilience.

The evening featured a video recap of commemorative activities, testimonials from defenders of human rights, artistic performances, and the presentation of awards for the human rights advocacy competition. Six top universities received promotional items, certificates, and cash prizes, while the two winning teams each received a laptop. The team from Thomas Sankara University was particularly recognized, receiving 75,000 CFA francs alongside other awards.

Human Rights Night 2025 offered a platform for dialogue, celebration, and recognition, reaffirming Burkina Faso’s commitment to promoting and protecting fundamental rights, even amid ongoing security challenges.

title: Burkina Faso Authorities Address Yargatenga Chieftaincy Crisis, Stress Peace and Justice
excerpt: Tenkodogo, December 12, 2025 - The Public Prosecutor’s Office of the Tenkodogo High Court issued an official statement following violent clashes on November 8, 2025, between rival groups linked to the Yargatenga…
title_en: Burkina Faso Authorities Address Yargatenga Chieftaincy Crisis, Stress Peace and Justice
excerpt_en: Tenkodogo, December 12, 2025 - The Public Prosecutor’s Office of the Tenkodogo High Court issued an official statement following violent clashes on November 8, 2025, between rival groups linked to the Yargatenga…
body_en:
Tenkodogo, December 12, 2025 - The Public Prosecutor’s Office of the Tenkodogo High Court issued an official statement following violent clashes on November 8, 2025, between rival groups linked to the Yargatenga chieftaincy in the village of Hornogho. The incident left seven people injured, including one by gunshot, and caused significant property damage.

In response, authorities launched an immediate investigation to identify those responsible and ensure justice. On November 23, 2025, a mediation session led by the Minister of Security facilitated initial de-escalation, resulting in the suspension of arrests while investigations continued.

However, tensions resurfaced on December 7, 2025, when a defamation and incitement to hatred complaint was filed against Mr. Adama Guindaogo on Facebook, prompting the reopening of the investigation.

On December 12, 2025, Mr. Guindaogo was charged with flagrant offenses and placed in pretrial detention. He is scheduled to appear before the criminal court on December 18, 2025.

The Prosecutor emphasized that no one is above the law, calling on all parties to act with responsibility, restraint, and respect for social cohesion. He reaffirmed that terrorism remains a shared threat and that any acts undermining national unity will be prosecuted with the utmost rigor.

Niamey, December 12, 2025 - The official opening of the 2025-2026 judicial year in Niger took place Friday at the Mahatma Gandhi International Conference Center in Niamey, presided over by His Excellency General Abdourahmane Tiani, President of the Republic of Niger and Head of State.

Representing Burkina Faso, Minister of Justice and Human Rights, Keeper of the Seals, Mr. Edasso Rodrigue Bayala, attended the ceremony on behalf of President Captain Ibrahim Traoré. The event brought together Nigerien dignitaries, including Prime Minister and Minister of Economy and Finance Ali Mahaman Lamine Zeine, members of the National Committee for the Salvation of the People (CNSP), government officials, presidents of national institutions, heads of diplomatic missions, international organizations, magistrates, and other distinguished guests.

During the event, President Tiani granted a private audience to Minister Bayala, highlighting the close judicial and diplomatic ties between Burkina Faso and Niger, as well as their shared commitment to regional cooperation and rule of law.

title: Digital Justice in Burkina Faso: Enhancing Transparency, Speed, and Efficiency Through e-Services
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 12, 2025 - The Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, responsible for relations with institutions, showcased the impact of digitalization on Burkina Faso’s judicial services in a press visit…
title_en: Digital Justice in Burkina Faso: Enhancing Transparency, Speed, and Efficiency Through e-Services
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 12, 2025 - The Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, responsible for relations with institutions, showcased the impact of digitalization on Burkina Faso’s judicial services in a press visit…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 12, 2025 - The Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, responsible for relations with institutions, showcased the impact of digitalization on Burkina Faso’s judicial services in a press visit organized by the Directorate of Communication and Press Relations. The tour highlighted new platforms including electronic criminal justice, communication permits, and RCCM (Register of Commerce and Companies) derivative documents.

Journalists first visited the Ouaga I High Court, where the electronic Burkinabè nationality certificate platform has received 48,931 applications as of December 11, 2025, generating 24,465,500 FCFA in state revenue. Of these, 37,336 certificates were issued, while 10,144 (27.16%) were rejected, mostly due to non-compliant or poorly scanned documents. Staff emphasized submitting authentic, clear documents and avoiding fraudulent attempts.

The tour continued at the central office for electronic criminal records, which has handled 418,241 applications, issuing 393,574 records and rejecting 23,596 (5.99%). Rejections were mainly caused by inaccurate birthplaces, occupations, or poorly scanned documents. The office maintains a database of 30,343 convicted individuals and 1,018 recorded offenses, ensuring accuracy and transparency.

Officials highlighted that these platforms, covering 11 regional courts for nationality certificates, streamline procedures, enhance traceability, and build public trust. The initiative reflects Burkina Faso’s commitment to modernizing the justice system while emphasizing the responsibility of users to provide correct, legible, and authentic documentation.

Through these digital tools, the Ministry seeks to make judicial services faster, more transparent, and reliable, reinforcing citizens’ confidence in public institutions and advancing the country’s broader modernization agenda.

title: Ouagadougou Court of Appeal Swears in 20 New Magistrates
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 12, 2025 - Twenty newly appointed magistrates officially joined Burkina Faso’s judiciary this Friday during a swearing-in ceremony at the Ouagadougou Court of Appeal.
title_en: Ouagadougou Court of Appeal Swears in 20 New Magistrates
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 12, 2025 - Twenty newly appointed magistrates officially joined Burkina Faso’s judiciary this Friday during a swearing-in ceremony at the Ouagadougou Court of Appeal.
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 12, 2025 - Twenty newly appointed magistrates officially joined Burkina Faso’s judiciary this Friday during a swearing-in ceremony at the Ouagadougou Court of Appeal.

Presided over by Adama Nana, President of the Court of Appeal, the ceremony took place in the presence of Adama Ouedraogo, President of the High Council of the Judiciary (CSM), and several senior magistrates. Each magistrate solemnly declared:

"I swear to faithfully and diligently fulfill my duties, to exercise them with absolute impartiality and respect for the law, to respect professional secrecy, and to conduct myself in all things as a worthy and loyal servant of justice."

The President of the Court emphasized the legal necessity of this oath, marking it as a mandatory step for all magistrates assuming judicial positions. Attorney General Pingrédewindé Désiré Sawadogo underlined the importance of rigor, integrity, and responsibility as guiding principles for the new magistrates. He encouraged them to support ongoing reforms aimed at humanizing the judicial system, including the implementation of community service as an alternative to imprisonment.

Following the ceremony, the magistrates were declared fit to serve and will assume their duties across multiple jurisdictions, including the High Courts of Ouaga II, Koudougou, Manga, Léo, Ziniaré, Kaya, Pô, Yako, Ouahigouya, Kongoussi, Djibo, and the Koudougou Labor Court, serving as judges or deputy prosecutors.

This induction reinforces Burkina Faso’s commitment to strengthening its judiciary and promoting professional and ethical judicial service across the nation.

Ouagadougou, December 12, 2025 - The hearing for the case of YE Yaké Camille and others began on Friday, December 12, 2025, at the Ouaga I High Court, with the Criminal Chamber sitting as the Economic and Financial Chamber.

The court adjourned the proceedings to Monday, December 15, 2025, at 9:00 a.m., when the trial will officially commence before the 1st Chamber of the Economic and Financial Chamber.

This case follows the earlier high-profile trial of Teignan Hamidou and others. Defendants in the current proceedings, including former minister Laure ZONGO/HIEN, face charges of embezzlement of public funds, complicity in embezzlement, illicit enrichment, and money laundering.

The upcoming hearings will provide a detailed examination of the alleged facts, adhering to the principles of transparency and judicial rigor that guide the Burkinabè legal system.

title: Burkina Faso: 20 Years of CIMDH and High Council of the Judiciary Strengthen Human Rights and Justice
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 15, 2025 - Burkina Faso marked the 20th anniversary of the Interministerial Committee on Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law (CIMDH), launching a series of commemorative activities from…
title_en: Burkina Faso: 20 Years of CIMDH and High Council of the Judiciary Strengthen Human Rights and Justice
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 15, 2025 - Burkina Faso marked the 20th anniversary of the Interministerial Committee on Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law (CIMDH), launching a series of commemorative activities from…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 15, 2025 - Burkina Faso marked the 20th anniversary of the Interministerial Committee on Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law (CIMDH), launching a series of commemorative activities from December 15 to 18, 2025. The ceremony, held under the high patronage of the Minister of Justice and Human Rights, underscores the committee’s role as a strategic framework for coordinating government action on human rights and international humanitarian law since its creation in 2005.

Speaking on behalf of the Minister, Seidou Ouédraogo emphasized that this milestone goes beyond symbolism. Under the theme, “CIMDH: What reforms are necessary for an endogenous appropriation of human rights values and international humanitarian law?”, he called for reforms to strengthen the institution, bring human rights closer to citizens, and integrate them into Burkina Faso’s cultural and social realities.

The commemoration program includes conferences, roundtables, a documentary exhibition, reforestation initiatives, donation distributions for injured personnel, and civic and sporting activities, reflecting a commitment to public engagement and human dignity. Professor Alkassoum Maïga moderated the inaugural conference, setting the stage for discussions on adapting CIMDH to the context of the progressive popular revolution.

Justice and Judicial Sovereignty: Customary Law in Focus

On the same day, President Captain Ibrahim Traoré, Guarantor of Judicial Independence, chaired the first statutory meeting of 2025 of the High Council of the Judiciary (CSM). The session emphasized the importance of justice as a pillar of the Republic amid ongoing reforms, security challenges, and geopolitical upheavals.

The Council examined two key reports: one on the performance evaluation of lower courts to enhance efficiency, and another on “Traditional Justice in Building a Judicial System for the People: The Contribution of Customary Law”, highlighting the need to strengthen local conflict resolution mechanisms.

Following Burkina Faso’s withdrawal from the International Organisation of La Francophonie (OIF), the CSM announced the suspension of its participation in Francophone judicial networks, citing institutional coherence and sovereignty.

President Ouédraogo presented the Council’s annual activity report, reaffirming the judiciary’s commitment to an independent, effective, and nationally grounded justice system, aligned with the principles of the progressive popular revolution.

This dual initiative reflects Burkina Faso’s determination to consolidate human rights, judicial sovereignty, and citizen-centered governance.

title: Burkina Faso Advances Digital Justice with Launch of Three Online Platforms
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 15, 2025 - The Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, responsible for relations with institutions, has taken a major step toward a modern, accessible, and citizen-centered judicial system with the…
title_en: Burkina Faso Advances Digital Justice with Launch of Three Online Platforms
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 15, 2025 - The Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, responsible for relations with institutions, has taken a major step toward a modern, accessible, and citizen-centered judicial system with the…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 15, 2025 - The Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, responsible for relations with institutions, has taken a major step toward a modern, accessible, and citizen-centered judicial system with the official launch of three digital platforms on Monday, December 15.

The ceremony was held under the high patronage of Prime Minister Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouedraogo, represented by Minister of State Émile Zerbo, and was presided over by Minister of Justice and Human Rights Edasso Rodrigue Bayala, co-chaired by Minister of Digital Transition, Posts and Electronic Communications, Aminata Zerbo/Sabane.

justice-penale.gov.bf - enabling citizens to file and track complaints online, ensuring transparency and traceability in judicial procedures.

e-permis-commeniuer.gov.bf - allowing relatives of incarcerated individuals to apply for visitation permits online.

e-acte-rcm.gov.bf - providing online access to RCCM documents, including extracts, registration certificates, and certificates of good standing.

These tools are designed to reduce administrative burdens, shorten court delays, and enhance access to justice, while supporting business productivity by streamlining legal procedures.

The Prime Minister’s representative emphasized that digitalization is crucial for modernizing Burkina Faso’s judicial system, reinforcing the government’s commitment to transparency, efficiency, and citizen empowerment.

A symbolic official click marked the integration of these platforms into daily judicial operations, signaling a new era where Burkinabe citizens can interact with the justice system anytime, anywhere.

title: Burkina Faso Commemorates 20 Years of CIMDH with Focus on Human Rights and International Credibility
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 16, 2025 - Burkina Faso continues to celebrate the 20th anniversary of the Interministerial Committee on Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law (CIMDH), with a roundtable discussion…
title_en: Burkina Faso Commemorates 20 Years of CIMDH with Focus on Human Rights and International Credibility
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 16, 2025 - Burkina Faso continues to celebrate the 20th anniversary of the Interministerial Committee on Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law (CIMDH), with a roundtable discussion…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 16, 2025 - Burkina Faso continues to celebrate the 20th anniversary of the Interministerial Committee on Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law (CIMDH), with a roundtable discussion emphasizing the theme: “Preserving Burkina Faso’s image and international credibility through respect for human rights and obligations under international humanitarian law.”

The event is chaired by Minister of Justice Edasso Rodrigue Bayala, President of the CIMDH, represented by Technical Advisor Julie Rose Ouedraogo. In her opening remarks, she highlighted the importance of balancing operational imperatives with adherence to national and international standards, a responsibility that spans the State, the Defense and Security Forces (FDS), the Volunteers for the Defense of the Homeland (VDP), and all actors involved in Burkina Faso’s security efforts.

The anniversary program combines strategic reflection with civic and solidarity activities. Upcoming initiatives include tree planting and visits to wounded FDS and VDP personnel, coupled with the distribution of donations, demonstrating the CIMDH’s ongoing human and social commitment.

Established on February 23, 2005, the CIMDH reaffirms its dedication to reform and adaptation, positioning itself as a strategic instrument for the progressive popular revolution, the protection of human dignity, and the promotion of Burkina Faso’s international standing.

This milestone underscores Burkina Faso’s continued focus on integrating human rights and international humanitarian law into its governance and security framework.

title: Burkina Faso Strengthens Human Rights Monitoring Through Targeted Training Program
excerpt: Koudougou, December 16, 2025 - The Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, responsible for relations with institutions (MJDHRI), through its Directorate General of Human Rights (DGDH), has launched a three-day training…
title_en: Burkina Faso Strengthens Human Rights Monitoring Through Targeted Training Program
excerpt_en: Koudougou, December 16, 2025 - The Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, responsible for relations with institutions (MJDHRI), through its Directorate General of Human Rights (DGDH), has launched a three-day training…
body_en:
Koudougou, December 16, 2025 - The Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, responsible for relations with institutions (MJDHRI), through its Directorate General of Human Rights (DGDH), has launched a three-day training session for members of the Consultation, Monitoring, and Early Warning Framework on Human Rights Violations.

The program focuses on human rights principles, the human rights-based approach (HRA), and the mandate of the United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR). It is designed to enhance constructive dialogue among stakeholders and ensure continuous monitoring and evidence-based reporting of alleged human rights violations in contexts of insecurity and violence.

The opening ceremony was presided over by Secretary General Harouna Kadio, represented by Project Manager Mathias Sam, who emphasized the strategic importance of human rights promotion and protection for Burkina Faso. “This is an important step for Burkina Faso,” he noted, underscoring that the effectiveness of the Consultation Framework depends on members’ mastery of technical monitoring tools.

Over the course of the training, participants from various ministries and departments aim to strengthen operational capacities, improve early-warning mechanisms, and enhance coordination across institutions.

This initiative reflects a joint commitment by the MJDHRI and OHCHR to build a robust, accountable, and well-equipped national human rights protection system, rooted in the principles of human dignity and accountability.

Ouagadougou, December 16, 2025 - Inmates at the Ouagadougou Detention and Correction Center (MACO) are benefiting from a free kidney disease screening campaign organized by the nephrology department of Tengandogo University Hospital Center (CHU).

title: Burkina Faso Honors 140 Justice Officials for Excellence and Public Service
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 17, 2025 - The Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, responsible for relations with institutions, presented honorary awards today to 140 officials across all categories within the justice sector.
title_en: Burkina Faso Honors 140 Justice Officials for Excellence and Public Service
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 17, 2025 - The Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, responsible for relations with institutions, presented honorary awards today to 140 officials across all categories within the justice sector.
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 17, 2025 - The Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, responsible for relations with institutions, presented honorary awards today to 140 officials across all categories within the justice sector.

The ceremony was presided over by Minister of Justice Edasso Rodrigue Bayala and attended by the President of the Constitutional Council, government members, senior judicial and administrative officials, former ministers of justice and human rights, and numerous colleagues and friends of the awardees.

Minister Bayala paid tribute to the Defense and Security Forces (FDS) and Volunteers for the Defense of the Homeland (VDP) who fell in the line of duty in 2025, stating, “These medals are not mere decorations; they bear witness to the recognition of an entire nation for the integrity and excellence of public service.”

The honorary awards were distributed as follows:

Order of the Horse: 12 recipients (10 Knights and 2 Officers)

Order of Merit of Burkina Faso: 58 Knights

Medals of Honor for Prison Security: 35, including one posthumous award and one awarded to a legal entity

Minister Bayala also highlighted the Ministry’s achievements, particularly the FASO MEEBO initiative, which mobilized over 22.6 million CFA francs from judicial stakeholders and legal professionals, reflecting their commitment beyond the courts toward national development.

Closing the ceremony, Minister Bayala emphasized that these awards mark the beginning of a renewed drive to modernize Burkina Faso’s judicial system and ensure fair and effective access to justice for all citizens.

The session, which ran from December 16 to 18, 2025, was part of the roadmap to enhance the operational effectiveness of the Framework following its recent evaluation.

The training also provided a platform to review previous cases, discuss the functioning of the Framework, and strengthen coordination mechanisms.

title: Burkina Faso Strengthens Conflict Prevention Through UNOPREGEC National Convention
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 19, 2025 - The 2025 Ordinary Statutory Session of the National Council of the National Observatory for Prevention and Community Conflict Management (ONAPREGECC) took place today in Ouagadougou.
title_en: Burkina Faso Strengthens Conflict Prevention Through UNOPREGEC National Convention
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 19, 2025 - The 2025 Ordinary Statutory Session of the National Council of the National Observatory for Prevention and Community Conflict Management (ONAPREGECC) took place today in Ouagadougou.
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 19, 2025 - The 2025 Ordinary Statutory Session of the National Council of the National Observatory for Prevention and Community Conflict Management (ONAPREGECC) took place today in Ouagadougou.

Chaired by Minister of Justice Edasso Rodrigue Bayala and co-chaired by Chief of Staff Bépoadi Sinini, the session gathered statutory members, directors of regional observatories, and technical and financial partners.

The meeting provided an opportunity to assess the national conflict prevention mechanism and analyze trends in community conflicts amid a challenging security and social context.

In his opening remarks, the Minister’s representative highlighted ONAPREGECC’s strategic role as a national early warning and mediation system, supporting communities in preventing and peacefully resolving conflicts. He praised the resilience of the population, the dedication of local actors, and the bravery of the Defense and Security Forces and Volunteers for the Defense of the Homeland, stressing that resilience must be actively nurtured.

The results presented were encouraging: 561 community conflicts were reported, with 345 resolved by September 30, 2025, reflecting the increasing effectiveness of ONAPREGECC’s regional branches.

The National Council approved the 2025 activity report, reviewed the implementation of 2024 recommendations, and built on lessons learned from successful mediations.

This session underscores Burkina Faso’s commitment to strengthening local conflict governance, consolidating early warning mechanisms, and promoting inclusive, sustainable solutions, contributing to social cohesion and lasting peace.

title: Burkina Faso Launches First Prison Arts and Crafts Fair to Promote Inmate Reintegration
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 19, 2025 - The first edition of the Burkina Faso Prison Arts and Crafts Fair (FAUCA-BF) officially opened today under the presidency of Minister of Justice and Human Rights, Edasso Rodrigue Bayala.
title_en: Burkina Faso Launches First Prison Arts and Crafts Fair to Promote Inmate Reintegration
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 19, 2025 - The first edition of the Burkina Faso Prison Arts and Crafts Fair (FAUCA-BF) officially opened today under the presidency of Minister of Justice and Human Rights, Edasso Rodrigue Bayala.
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 19, 2025 - The first edition of the Burkina Faso Prison Arts and Crafts Fair (FAUCA-BF) officially opened today under the presidency of Minister of Justice and Human Rights, Edasso Rodrigue Bayala.

Held under the patronage of Sabila Sawadogo, Divisional Inspector of Penitentiary Security and Director General of the Penitentiary Administration, and supported by Commander Ismaël Sombie and Serge Gnaniodem Poda, the fair aims to highlight the skills of inmates while promoting their professional development and social reintegration.

Scheduled from December 19 to 22, 2025 at the National Museum, the fair features exhibitions, sales, roundtables, artistic performances, and a food area, creating a space for dialogue between the prison system and civil society.

In his opening remarks, Minister Bayala emphasized that prisons should serve as spaces for learning, responsibility, and social reintegration. He underscored that FAUCA-BF reflects the government’s reformist vision, combining respect for human rights with effective preparation for inmates’ return to society.

“These individuals are now an integral part of the system,” he said, highlighting the fair as a demonstration of the modern, humane, and productive governance of the prison system.

Admission is free, with the event open daily from 8:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m., offering the public a unique opportunity to discover the talents of inmates and engage with Burkina Faso’s ongoing prison reform initiatives.

The visit showcased artwork produced by wounded soldiers during the “Heroes' Workshop,” a visual arts training program held from August 28 to October 15, 2025.

The program, aimed at reconverting retiring members of the Defense and Security Forces, enabled 62 participants to acquire both theoretical knowledge and practical skills essential for careers in agriculture and livestock farming.

Colonel-Major Yamba Léonard Oûoba, Secretary General of the MDAC, chaired the ceremony and highlighted the initiative as part of the ministry’s broader policy to support retired personnel, helping them build productive, sustainable, and socially valuable livelihoods in promising sectors.

This training underscores Burkina Faso’s commitment to ensuring that veterans are equipped for post-service careers, contributing to both their personal development and national economic growth.

Burkina Faso, December 20, 2025 - The Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM/GSIM) group released a 5-minute video from Camp Abou Adam, addressing the nation in Moorish and Fulani.

In the footage, the speaker claims that JNIM includes members from all ethnic groups in the Sahel and emphasizes that the group does not discriminate. The video also declares the group’s current objective is to overthrow President Ibrahim Traoré, whom it blames for the hardships faced by the Burkinabe population.

This release forms part of JNIM’s ongoing media and propaganda campaign amid persistent security challenges in Burkina Faso.

Conclusion: A Period of Strategic Transformation and Resilience

The reporting period from December 07 to 21, 2025, underscores a pivotal moment in Burkina Faso’s journey toward national sovereignty and regional integration. Under the leadership of President Ibrahim Traoré, the government has intensified its "radical transformation" of diplomatic relations, shifting toward partnerships based on mutual respect and shared benefits

Regional Integration and the AES: The inaugural confederal session of the Council of Ministers in Bamako and the launch of the Confederal Bank for Investment and Development (BCID-AES) represent major milestones in consolidating the Confederation of Sahel States as a platform for "emancipation, freedom, and true independence".

Diplomatic Diversification: Burkina Faso has significantly broadened its international engagement, presenting credentials in countries as varied as the Philippines, Greece, Cuba, and Gabon. The signing of 12 new agreements with Morocco further illustrates a commitment to South-South cooperation centered on shared development.

Sovereignty and Security: The government took a firm stance on territorial integrity, notably in its response to the Nigerian military aircraft incident, while also engaging in high-level diplomacy to resolve the matter through an official apology from Nigeria. Despite persistent security challenges from groups like JNIM, the state continues to prioritize national territorial restoration.

Governance and Internal Reforms: Significant strides were made in public administration, including the modernization of civil service roles and the review of the National Development Plan for 2026-2030. Initiatives like the "Faso Mêbo" presidential project have successfully mobilized support from both the diaspora and international organizations.

Transparency and Human Rights: The presentation of the 2024 EITI Report and various human rights training sessions highlight an ongoing effort to strengthen accountability and the protection of fundamental rights within the national framework.

In summary, this fortnight reflects a nation actively redefining its role on the global stage while simultaneously reinforcing its internal governance and regional alliances to build a more "peaceful, resilient, and prosperous" future

title: Burundi Faces an Unwelcome New Neighbor After Fall of Uvira, Senator Says
excerpt: Bujumbura, December 15, 2025 - Burundian Senator Evode Uwizeyimana has warned that Burundi must come to terms with the AFC/M23, following the capture of Uvira in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, or risk sliding…
title_en: Burundi Faces an Unwelcome New Neighbor After Fall of Uvira, Senator Says
excerpt_en: Bujumbura, December 15, 2025 - Burundian Senator Evode Uwizeyimana has warned that Burundi must come to terms with the AFC/M23, following the capture of Uvira in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, or risk sliding…
body_en:
Bujumbura, December 15, 2025 - Burundian Senator Evode Uwizeyimana has warned that Burundi must come to terms with the AFC/M23, following the capture of Uvira in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, or risk sliding into a strategic and economic dead end.

Speaking on Burundi National Television, Uwizeyimana said the takeover of Uvira places Burundi in a difficult position, urging authorities to seek an understanding with the group now controlling the city. “Not doing so would expose Burundi to problems without solutions,” he cautioned.

The senator stressed Uvira’s strategic and economic importance, describing it as both a former hub for anti-M23 operations and a key center of trade for Burundi. He noted that defeated forces from Goma and Bukavu, including Wazalendo fighters, had regrouped there, making the city a prime target.

Uwizeyimana warned that continued M23 advances could isolate Burundi, leaving it with limited access routes and threatening cross-border commerce vital to Bujumbura’s economy. He also raised concerns over Burundian troops still stranded in the highlands of South Kivu, arguing that their withdrawal would require negotiations with the M23.

According to the senator, the capture of Uvira was unrelated to the Washington peace agreement between Rwanda and the DRC and followed months of military preparation by the AFC/M23 amid stalled negotiations.

In response to the takeover, Burundi closed the Kavimvira and Vugizo border posts with the DRC, adding to existing border closures with Rwanda, further underscoring the growing regional strain.

title: Nduhungirehe Accuses International Community of Ignoring FARDC Airstrikes
excerpt: December 15, 2025 - Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Amb. Olivier Nduhungirehe, has criticized the international community for what he described as silence over airstrikes carried out by the…
title_en: Nduhungirehe Accuses International Community of Ignoring FARDC Airstrikes
excerpt_en: December 15, 2025 - Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Amb. Olivier Nduhungirehe, has criticized the international community for what he described as silence over airstrikes carried out by the…
body_en:
December 15, 2025 - Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Amb. Olivier Nduhungirehe, has criticized the international community for what he described as silence over airstrikes carried out by the Congolese army in areas controlled by the AFC/M23.

Reacting on his X (formerly Twitter) account, Nduhungirehe said Sukhoi-25 aircraft and FARDC drones bombed the Rwitsankuku area on the morning of December 15, killing civilians, notably in Banyamulenge-inhabited villages in South Kivu.

He accused Western countries of failing to condemn what he called repeated and deliberate attacks on densely populated areas, while reacting only when the AFC/M23 retaliates and later withdraws.

Air and drone strikes in Banyamulenge areas have intensified in recent days following the defeat of Burundian, FARDC, Wazalendo and FDLR forces in the Rusizi Valley.

title: Cardinal Ambongo Calls for Inclusive Dialogue After M23 Seizure of Uvira
excerpt: Kinshasa December 14, 2025 - The Archbishop of Kinshasa, Cardinal Fridolin Ambongo, has renewed calls for an inclusive national dialogue following the capture of Uvira by the AFC/M23.
title_en: Cardinal Ambongo Calls for Inclusive Dialogue After M23 Seizure of Uvira
excerpt_en: Kinshasa December 14, 2025 - The Archbishop of Kinshasa, Cardinal Fridolin Ambongo, has renewed calls for an inclusive national dialogue following the capture of Uvira by the AFC/M23.
body_en:
Kinshasa December 14, 2025 - The Archbishop of Kinshasa, Cardinal Fridolin Ambongo, has renewed calls for an inclusive national dialogue following the capture of Uvira by the AFC/M23. Speaking at the close of the 15th plenary assembly of the Association of Episcopal Conferences of Central Africa (ACEC), he urged Congolese leaders to address the root causes of the conflict in eastern DRC.

Cardinal Ambongo questioned the effectiveness of the Washington Agreement signed on December 4 between Presidents Félix Tshisekedi and Paul Kagame, noting that Uvira fell under occupation less than a week later. He warned against peace initiatives that exclude Congolese voices and legitimize the exploitation of the country’s resources.

Emphasizing that “peace remains possible,” he endorsed the CENCO-ECC social pact as a credible path toward lasting peace and coexistence in the DRC and the Great Lakes region.

excerpt: The United States is considering sanctions and other diplomatic measures to enforce the Washington peace agreement between the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Rwanda, US Ambassador Lucy Tamlyn said on Monday…
title_en: US Considers Sanctions as Violence Undermines Washington Peace Deal
excerpt_en: The United States is considering sanctions and other diplomatic measures to enforce the Washington peace agreement between the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Rwanda, US Ambassador Lucy Tamlyn said on Monday…
body_en:
The United States is considering sanctions and other diplomatic measures to enforce the Washington peace agreement between the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Rwanda, US Ambassador Lucy Tamlyn said on Monday, December 15, in Kinshasa.

Speaking at a press conference, Tamlyn reaffirmed Washington’s commitment to the accord, warning that all available tools-including bilateral and multilateral actions-are under review to ensure compliance. She expressed US disappointment over the renewed violence in eastern DRC, which erupted a day after the agreement was signed, and pointed to Rwanda’s responsibility.

Tamlyn said the fall of Uvira, South Kivu’s provisional capital, does not reflect a failure of the US-sponsored initiative, stressing that President Donald Trump remains personally engaged in efforts to restore peace.

Meanwhile, the UN Secretary-General has strongly condemned the latest AFC/M23 offensive in several parts of South Kivu, including Uvira, and called for an immediate and unconditional ceasefire, warning of the risk of wider regional escalation.

title: Tshisekedi in Luanda Amid Renewed Violence in Eastern DRC
excerpt: President Félix Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) arrived in Luanda, Angola, on Sunday, December 14, for a working visit, according to several sources.
title_en: Tshisekedi in Luanda Amid Renewed Violence in Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: President Félix Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) arrived in Luanda, Angola, on Sunday, December 14, for a working visit, according to several sources.
body_en:
President Félix Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) arrived in Luanda, Angola, on Sunday, December 14, for a working visit, according to several sources.

The visit is reportedly aimed at reviving the Luanda process, a regional diplomatic initiative to restore peace in eastern DRC, amid continued violence in the Kivu region linked to the M23 armed group. According to Le Potentiel, the talks seek to reinforce regional mediation efforts.

Other sources say Tshisekedi met with Angolan President João Lourenço to discuss bilateral cooperation and regional peace and security in Central Africa.

The visit comes days after the DRC-Rwanda peace agreement, signed on December 4, 2025, in Washington, under US mediation. Despite the accord, fighting has intensified, with the AFC/M23, allegedly backed by Kigali, seizing several towns in South Kivu, including the strategic city of Uvira.

title: AFC/M23 Facilitates Return of Over 500 Burundians from Uvira
excerpt: Uvira, December 14, 2025 - The AFC/M23 coalition has assisted more than 500 Burundian nationals to return home from Uvira, days after they were stranded by fighting and the closure of the Kavimvira and Vugizo border…
title_en: AFC/M23 Facilitates Return of Over 500 Burundians from Uvira
excerpt_en: Uvira, December 14, 2025 - The AFC/M23 coalition has assisted more than 500 Burundian nationals to return home from Uvira, days after they were stranded by fighting and the closure of the Kavimvira and Vugizo border…
body_en:
Uvira, December 14, 2025 - The AFC/M23 coalition has assisted more than 500 Burundian nationals to return home from Uvira, days after they were stranded by fighting and the closure of the Kavimvira and Vugizo border crossings by Burundi.

The returnees, many of them traders who had been working in South Kivu, said they were trapped in Uvira after the rebels entered the city on December 9. “I was stuck because of the fighting. Sometimes we had to hide. I am happy to return safely,” one Burundian said at the Kavimvira crossing.

Another returnee, identified as Mugenzi, said dozens of Burundian businesspeople faced similar difficulties and stressed that the move was a temporary return, pending security developments.

AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the operation followed discussions with Burundian authorities, arguing that the group had not closed the border. “These are our fellow Africans. Our border is open, but Burundi’s is closed. We asked them to open it for humanitarian reasons,” he said.

Meanwhile, more than 20,000 Congolese civilians who fled to Burundi following the fall of Uvira remain unable to return, as Burundian authorities have kept the border closed.

title: Burundi Deploys Troops and Heavy Weapons Near Rwandan Border as Tensions Rise
excerpt: Bujumbura, December 15, 2025 - Burundi has intensified its military presence along the Rwandan border, deploying troops, heavy weapons, and combat equipment amid escalating regional tensions linked to the conflict in…
title_en: Burundi Deploys Troops and Heavy Weapons Near Rwandan Border as Tensions Rise
excerpt_en: Bujumbura, December 15, 2025 - Burundi has intensified its military presence along the Rwandan border, deploying troops, heavy weapons, and combat equipment amid escalating regional tensions linked to the conflict in…
body_en:
Bujumbura, December 15, 2025 - Burundi has intensified its military presence along the Rwandan border, deploying troops, heavy weapons, and combat equipment amid escalating regional tensions linked to the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

According to security sources, Burundian forces have reinforced positions in Busoni commune, Butanyerera province, near the Gasenyi-Nemba border, with senior military officials confirming the deployment of heavy artillery to counter potential threats from Rwanda. Additional troops have been transported to military camps, including the 411th camp in Mutwenzi, while night patrols by police and Imbonerakure youth have increased in border areas.

Security measures have also tightened in Bujumbura Province (former Cibitoke), where Burundian forces reportedly fired shells toward Kamanyola, in South Kivu. These strikes preceded AFC/M23 advances across the Rusizi Valley, reaching Uvira on Lake Tanganyika.

Before the UN Security Council, Burundi accused Rwanda of backing the AFC/M23, while residents near the border report growing fear of a possible interstate conflict. “We sleep dressed, ready to flee,” one local resident said.

Multiple sources further report a significant influx of weapons, including combat drones, with around 30 trucks delivering arms to the Mukoni military base in recent weeks-fueling concerns that Burundi is preparing for a wider confrontation.

title: South Kivu: Sukhoi-25 Jets and Drones Strike Banyamulenge Areas
excerpt: South Kivu, December 15, 2025 - Warplanes and drones have carried out a series of airstrikes on areas inhabited by the Banyamulenge community in South Kivu province, causing civilian deaths and injuries, according to…
title_en: South Kivu: Sukhoi-25 Jets and Drones Strike Banyamulenge Areas
excerpt_en: South Kivu, December 15, 2025 - Warplanes and drones have carried out a series of airstrikes on areas inhabited by the Banyamulenge community in South Kivu province, causing civilian deaths and injuries, according to…
body_en:
South Kivu, December 15, 2025 - Warplanes and drones have carried out a series of airstrikes on areas inhabited by the Banyamulenge community in South Kivu province, causing civilian deaths and injuries, according to opposition politician Moïse Nyarugabo.

Nyarugabo said the first drone strike hit the Rugezi area in Fizi territory at around 5:00 p.m. on December 15. Shortly afterward, a Sukhoi-25 fighter jet bombed Rwitsankuku, before continuing its attacks on Gahwera and Mikenke.

“These strikes killed many civilians and left others wounded,” Nyarugabo said, adding that a similar Sukhoi-25 attack had already targeted Rwitsankuku on the morning of December 14.

According to him, the aircraft and drones involved are believed to belong to Burundi. He called for accountability, urging that those who ordered the strikes - including pilots and airbase controllers - be held responsible.

The air and drone attacks have intensified since last week, following the defeat of Burundian, FARDC, Wazalendo and FDLR forces by the AFC/M23 in the Rusizi Valley, further deepening fears of a widening regional conflict.

title: Walikale: FDLR Burns Village, Four Killed
excerpt: Walikale, December 15, 2025 - The FDLR armed group burned down an entire village in the Tuonane area of Waloa Loanda, in Walikale territory, North Kivu, killing four people and forcing residents to flee to nearby…
title_en: Walikale: FDLR Burns Village, Four Killed
excerpt_en: Walikale, December 15, 2025 - The FDLR armed group burned down an entire village in the Tuonane area of Waloa Loanda, in Walikale territory, North Kivu, killing four people and forcing residents to flee to nearby…
body_en:
Walikale, December 15, 2025 - The FDLR armed group burned down an entire village in the Tuonane area of Waloa Loanda, in Walikale territory, North Kivu, killing four people and forcing residents to flee to nearby villages.

Local sources say an FDLR fighter known as “General Mudayongwa” ordered residents to leave land he claimed to have purchased from local authorities-an allegation the community denies. After villagers refused, FDLR fighters torched homes and attacked the area.

Two members of the Mai-Mai Kifuafua group were among those killed during clashes involving small arms and heavy weapons.

The attack comes despite commitments in the June 27 DRC-Rwanda peace agreement to dismantle the FDLR. A UN experts’ report released December 8 said the group continues to operate, with elements of the Congolese army still cooperating with it.

title: More Than 30 Dead in Boat Capsizing on the Kwango River
excerpt: At least 30 people have died after a wooden boat (baleinière) capsized on Saturday, December 13, on the Kwango River, near Bolo village, in Bagata territory, Kwango province.
title_en: More Than 30 Dead in Boat Capsizing on the Kwango River
excerpt_en: At least 30 people have died after a wooden boat (baleinière) capsized on Saturday, December 13, on the Kwango River, near Bolo village, in Bagata territory, Kwango province.
body_en:
At least 30 people have died after a wooden boat (baleinière) capsized on Saturday, December 13, on the Kwango River, near Bolo village, in Bagata territory, Kwango province.

According to National Assembly member Gary Sakata, who spoke on Monday to Radio Okapi, most of the victims were teachers traveling to Bandundu to collect their salaries. Several passengers are still reported missing, and the exact cause of the accident has not yet been established.

The boat was carrying more than 100 passengers along with around 700 sacks of maize and cassava, coming from the villages of Kingukukapayi, Kusu, and Fambondo. It reportedly hit an obstacle, causing it to capsize and resulting in the loss of all luggage.

Some passengers were also traveling to Bandundu to prepare for end-of-year celebrations, Sakata added.

The tragedy follows a similar incident on the Kwango River in September 2024, when another boat capsized, killing 12 people and leaving several others injured or missing.
